yoruba: Àgbéré àwòdì ní ńní òun ó jẹ ìgbín.
english_literal: It is an overreaching kite that proposes to eat snails.
interpretation_gold: Know your limits.

yoruba: A kì í kórira ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n ká finá bọ ahéré.
english_literal: One does not so hate the bush rat that one sets one's farm hut alight.
interpretation_gold: One should not destroy oneself simply to get at one's enemy.

yoruba: A kì í bọ òrìṣà lójú ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n; bó bá dalẹ́ a máa tú pẹpẹ.
english_literal: One does not sacrifice to a god in the presence of a house rat; otherwise, when night falls it invades the rafter shelves.
interpretation_gold: Do not do things that might constitute temptation to others.

yoruba: Àrí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, baálé ilé yọkun lémú.
english_literal: Something-seen-but-unmentionable, the man of the house walks around with mucus dripping from his nose.
interpretation_gold: When a venerable person acts like a fool, few dare tell him so.

yoruba: Àwòrò tí a ò bá lù kì í luni.
english_literal: A priest one does not hit does not hit one.
interpretation_gold: A person who wants to be respected must respect others.

yoruba: Àpárá ńlá, ìjà ní ńdà.
english_literal: Excessive ribbing unfailingly leads to a fight.
interpretation_gold: Jokes should know limits.

yoruba: À-jẹ-tán, à-jẹ-ì-mọra, ká fi ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá jẹun ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
english_literal: Eating-absolutely-everything, eating-with-abandon, eating with all ten fingers is unworthy of human beings.
interpretation_gold: People should not be slaves to food.

yoruba: Aláṣejù, pẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ńtẹ́; àṣéjù, baba àṣetẹ́.
english_literal: The immoderate person easily finds disgrace; immoderation is the father of disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation brings disgrace.

yoruba: Arọ̀lẹ̀kẹ̀ ò rọ bàtà; gbẹ́dó-gbẹ́dó ò rọ ojúgun.
english_literal: The bead maker cannot fashion a shoe; the mortar carver cannot manufacture a shinbone.
interpretation_gold: People should stick to what they are qualified to do.

yoruba: A kì í gbọ́n tó Báyìí-ni-ngó-ṣe-ǹkan-àn-mi.
english_literal: One cannot be as wise as “Thus-will-I-do-my-thing.”
interpretation_gold: Never impose your preferences on other people in their own affairs.

yoruba: A-bèèrè kì í ṣìnà.
english_literal: He who asks the way does not lose his way.
interpretation_gold: One should admit one's weaknesses.

yoruba: À ńgé e lọ́wọ́, ó ḿbọ òrùka.
english_literal: His hand is being severed, yet he is slipping on a ring.
interpretation_gold: The person has been judged undeserving of a hand; it is an affront, therefore, for him or her to adorn his or her fingers-an indication of heedlessness.

yoruba: Àjàjà ṣoge àparò, abàyà kelú.
english_literal: The uncharacteristically spruced up partridge swells its chest.
interpretation_gold: The nouveau riche always goes to extremes in consumption.

yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ sọ̀rọ̀ méjì, ọ́ fìkan purọ́; ó ní nígbàtí òún lu ọmọ òun lábàrá, òún já a léèékánná pàtì.
english_literal: The leper said two things, one of them being a lie; he said after he had struck his child with his palm, he also pinched him severely with his nails.
interpretation_gold: One fools only oneself when one claims to have done the impossible.

yoruba: Àrífín ilé ò jẹ́ ká jẹ òròmọ adìẹ.
english_literal: Fear of losing face within one's home dissuades one from eating day-old chicks.
interpretation_gold: A person who would retain his esteem among his peers must not act beneath himself or herself.

yoruba: Àbúrò rẹ ńdáṣọ fún ọ, o ní o ò lo elékuru; ta ní ńlo alákàrà?
english_literal: Your junior brother (or sister) buys clothing for you, and you say you will not wear anything with bean-grits patterns; who has the right to opt for clothing with a bean-fritter patterns?
interpretation_gold: One should act in accordance to one's station in life.

yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ olè, aboyún ńdáhùń; odiidi èèyàn ló gbé pamọ́.
english_literal: We speak of stealing and a pregnant woman intervenes; she herself is concealing a whole person.
interpretation_gold: Her condition makes her guilty of concealment.

yoruba: A kì í peni lákọ ẹran ká ṣorí bòró.
english_literal: One does not enjoy the designation “He Goat” and yet sport a smooth (horn-less) head.
interpretation_gold: A person should live up to his/her billing.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà kì í ṣe lágbalàgba.
english_literal: An elder should not behave in an unbecoming manner.
interpretation_gold: One should behave according to one's status.

yoruba: A kì í mọ́ egbò fúnra ẹni ká sunkún.
english_literal: One does not treat one's own sore and yet cry from the pain.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's own pain threshold.

yoruba: Àbọ̀ ejò kì í gbé isà.
english_literal: Half a snake does not live in a burrow.
interpretation_gold: One should act according to one's circumstances.

yoruba: Aláǹgbá kì í lérí àti pa ejò.
english_literal: A lizard does not boast that it will kill a snake.
interpretation_gold: People should not propose what they cannot accomplish.

yoruba: A kì í fi gbèsè sọ́rùn ṣọ̀ṣọ́.
english_literal: One does not carry debt around one's neck and live like a dandy.
interpretation_gold: One should discharge one's obligations before one indulges in extravagance.

yoruba: Ajá kì í gbó níbojì ẹkùn.
english_literal: A dog does not bark in the leopard's lair.
interpretation_gold: One must defer to one's superiors.

yoruba: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn ní ńsọ pé irú òun ò sí; irúu rẹ̀-ẹ́ pọ̀ ó ju ẹgbàágbèje lọ.
english_literal: Only an imbecile says there is no one else like himself; the likes of him are many more than several thousands.
interpretation_gold: There is no one the likes of whom the world has never seen.

yoruba: Àáyá yó níjọ́ kan, ó ní ká ká òun léhín ọ̀kánkán.
english_literal: The Colobus monkey ate its fill one day, and asked that his front teeth be knocked out.
interpretation_gold: Excessive happiness made the animal careless.

yoruba: Àgbà tí kò lẹ́sẹ̀ nílẹ̀ a lọ́gbọ́n nínú.
english_literal: An elder that has no substance should have cunning.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limitations and how to compensate for them.

yoruba: A-wọ̀lú-má-tẹ̀ẹ́, ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀ ló mọ̀.
english_literal: One-who-enters-a-town-and-maintains-his/her-reputation does because he/she knows his/her place.
interpretation_gold: Self-knowledge guarantees one's reputation.

yoruba: Àbá ni ikán ńdá; ikán ò lè mu òkúta.
english_literal: The termite is only striving; it can never eat a rock.
interpretation_gold: Termites may make their tunnels on a rock; the rock will be safe.

yoruba: A kì í fi pàtàkì bẹ́ èlùbọ́; ẹní bá níṣu ló ḿbẹ́ ẹ.
english_literal: One does not come by yam-flour because of one's importance; only people who have yams can make yam flour.
interpretation_gold: One cannot eat one's importance.

yoruba: Àgbàrá ba ọ̀nà jẹ́, ó rò pé òún tún ọ̀nà ṣe.
english_literal: The rain flood ruins the path believing that it is repairing it.
interpretation_gold: Ignorance or incompetence in tackling a task often leads to unintended results.

yoruba: Àìsí-ńlé ẹkùn, ajá ńgbó.
english_literal: The leopard being away from home, the dog barks.
interpretation_gold: When the master is away the minion will strut.

yoruba: Àgbààgbà ìlú ò lè péjọ kí wọn ó jẹ ìfun òkété, àfi iyán àná.
english_literal: The elders of the town will not assemble and eat the intestines of a bush-rat, only stale pounded yams.
interpretation_gold: People should behave in ways that befit their station.

yoruba: Ahọ́n ni ìpínnlẹ̀ ẹnu.
english_literal: The tongue is the border of the mouth.
interpretation_gold: There is a limit to everything.

yoruba: Aláṣọ-kan kì í ná ànárẹ.
english_literal: A person who has only one set of clothing does not bargain until he is wet.
interpretation_gold: A person with meagre resources should husband them judiciously.

yoruba: Àgbà tó bú ọmọdé fi èébú-u rẹ̀ tọrọ.
english_literal: An elder who insults a youth makes a present of his own insult.
interpretation_gold: Only those who show respect for others may expect respect in return.

yoruba: Aláàńtètè: ó jí ní kùtùkùtù ó ní òun ó dàá yànpọ̀n-yànpọ̀n sílẹ̀.
english_literal: The cricket arises in the morning and vows to perform wonders.
interpretation_gold: The puny person's boasts are always empty.

yoruba: Adìẹ funfun ò mọ ara ẹ̀ lágbà.
english_literal: The white chicken does not recognize itself as an elder.
interpretation_gold: One should act one's age always.

yoruba: Àgbà tó fi ara-a rẹ̀ féwe lèwe ḿbú.
english_literal: It is an elder who delivers himself unto youths that the youth will insult.
interpretation_gold: If one wants to be respected, one should respect oneself.

yoruba: Àlémú ò yẹ àgbà; àgbà kì í ṣe ohun àlémú.
english_literal: To be pursued does not become an elder; an elder does not cause himself to be pursued.
interpretation_gold: Elders should always behave in ways that would cause them no disgrace.

yoruba: Ajá rí epo kò lá; ìyá-a rẹ̀ẹ́ ṣu ihá bí.?
english_literal: The dog sees palm-oil but does not lick it; did its mother excrete palm-nut pericarp?
interpretation_gold: One should not be unreasonably squeamish.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà akàn tó kó sí garawa yègèdè, ojú tì í.
english_literal: The elderly crab that enters into a bucket; it is thoroughly disgraced.
interpretation_gold: One should avoid potentially disgraceful actions.

yoruba: Abùléra ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n; ó ní ọjọ́ tí ológbò-ó ti bí òun ò ìtí-ì dá a ní báríkà.
english_literal: Mouse-that-does-not-know-its-place; it says that since the day the cat delivered (a baby) it has not gone to offer congratulations.
interpretation_gold: Never forget your vulnerabilities and limitations.

yoruba: A-ṣe-bọ̀rọ̀kìnní-má-kìíyè-sábíyá, gbogbo abíyá dọ́ṣẹ.
english_literal: He-who-lives-in-style-but-pays-no-attention-to-his-armpits, both armpits are taken over with foamy filth.
interpretation_gold: Attention to detail is integral to good character or breeding.

yoruba: Àjátì àwọ̀n ní ńkọ́ òrofó lọ́gbọ́n.
english_literal: It is a loosely hung net that teaches the fruit pigeon a lesson.
interpretation_gold: The careless, imprudent person has his/her nemesis waiting for him/her.

yoruba: A kì í bá ọba pàlà kí ọkọ́ ọba má ṣàn-ánni lẹ́sẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not share a farm boundary with a king without getting one's feet gashed by the king's hoe.
interpretation_gold: One should be cautious in dealing with people in authority.

yoruba: Aláṣejù ajá ní ńlépa ẹkùn.
english_literal: It is an overreaching dog that chases leopards.
interpretation_gold: One should not challenge people one cannot match.

yoruba: À ńwọ́nà àti fi aṣiwèrè sílẹ̀, ó ní bí a bá dé òkè odò ká dúró de òun.
english_literal: People are scheming to shake an imbecile from their company, and he asks that they wait for him on reaching the bank of the river.
interpretation_gold: If people are seeking ways of getting rid of a person, that person should not lay down his conditions for remaining with them.

yoruba: A kì í lé èkúté ilé ẹni ká fọwọ́ ṣẹ́.
english_literal: One does not shoosh the mouse in one's house and break one's hand.
interpretation_gold: One should be safe from hazards in one's own home.

yoruba: Aláìnítìjú lọ kú sílé àna-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: A shameless person goes to die in his relative-in-laws' house.
interpretation_gold: One should never demean oneself with unbecoming actions.

yoruba: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀yọ màrìwò, ó ní òun ó kan ọ̀run; àwọn aṣáájúu rẹ̀-ẹ́ ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ rí?
english_literal: The newly emerged palm frond says it will touch the sky; did those that came before it do so?
interpretation_gold: Ambition should be tempered with realism.

yoruba: Adígbọ́nránkú ńfikú ṣeré.
english_literal: Death-feigning-beetle flirts with death.
interpretation_gold: If one persists in flirting with disaster, disaster is liable to befall one.

yoruba: Aáyán fẹ́ jó; adìẹ ni ò jẹ́.
english_literal: The cockroach would dance; it is the chicken that does not allow.
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of the previous entry.

yoruba: A kì í gbọ́n tó ẹni tí ńtannijẹ.
english_literal: One is never as wise as the person deceiving one.
interpretation_gold: The deceiver always has the advantage of the dupe.

yoruba: Àìsí-ńlé ológbò, ilé dilé èkúté.
english_literal: The cat being away from home, the house becomes a domain for mice.
interpretation_gold: People will take advantage of any relaxation of supervision.

yoruba: Àkàtàm̀pò ò tó ìjà-á jà; ta ní tó mú igi wá kò ó lójú?
english_literal: The bow cannot fight, but who dares confront it with a stick?
interpretation_gold: A stick is no match for a bow.

yoruba: Ara okó ní òún gbọ́ fínrín fínrín; ta ló sọ fun bí kò ṣe ará ile?
english_literal: The bush dweller says he heard a rumour; who told him, if it was not a town dweller?
interpretation_gold: People should not presume to instruct those who know better than they.

yoruba: Àgbà tó torí ogójì wọ ìyẹ̀wù; igbawó ò tó ohun à-mú-ṣèyẹ.
english_literal: The elder who escapes into his inner chamber because of forty cowries: two hundred cowries are not enough for casual spending.
interpretation_gold: One must act as one's station demands.

yoruba: Àgbà kì í fàárọ̀ họ ìdí kó má kan funfun.
english_literal: A grown person does not scratch his buttocks in the early morning without showing some whiteness.
interpretation_gold: Improper behaviour brings disgrace.

yoruba: A kì í bínú orí ká fi fìlà dé ìbàdí.
english_literal: One does not get angry with one's head and therefore use one's cap to cover one's buttocks.
interpretation_gold: Do not cut your nose to spite your face.

yoruba: A kì í kọ́ àgbàlagbà pé bó bá rún kó rún.
english_literal: One does not teach an elder that what has been crushed should remain crushed.
interpretation_gold: An elder should know when a matter should end.

yoruba: À-jẹ-pọ̀ ni tàdán.
english_literal: Eating-until-vomiting is the trait of the bat.
interpretation_gold: An observation on a being with no self-restraint. This could also be a wish that a person does not benefit from something he/she has appropriated.

yoruba: Àgbà kì í wà lọ́jà kórí ọmọ titun wọ́.
english_literal: An elder is not present at a market and permit a child's head to rest askew.
interpretation_gold: Elders must not permit untowards happenings in their presence.

yoruba: Àgbà ìmàle kì í káṣọ kọ́rùn.
english_literal: A muslim elder does not throw a sheet over his shoulder for clothing.
interpretation_gold: One should behave as is proper for one's position.

yoruba: Adìẹ́ tó ṣu tí kò tọ̀, ara-a rẹ̀ ló kù sí.;
english_literal: The chicken that shits and does not piss retains the rest in its body.
interpretation_gold: Self-deprivation hurts the person concerned, not anyone else.

yoruba: À-fà-tiiri ni tìyàwó; bí a bá fà á tí kò tiiri, ó ní ohun tó ńṣe é.
english_literal: Resisting-while-being-pulled is the proper behavior for a bride; if she is pulled and she does not resist, something is the matter with her.
interpretation_gold: However eager the bride, she must appear coy and shy; one should behave with decorum appropriate to one's position.

yoruba: Àkísà-á mọ ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀, ó gbé párá jẹ́.
english_literal: The rag knows its place; it remains quietly on the rafters.
interpretation_gold: A person of low standing should not call attention to himself or herself.

yoruba: A kì í gbọ́n tó “Èmi-lóni-í.”
english_literal: One cannot be as wise as “I-am-the-owner.”
interpretation_gold: One should not presume to know as much about something as the owner.

yoruba: Àgbà ajá kì í bàwọ̀jẹ́.
english_literal: A grown dog does not deface its skin.
interpretation_gold: Decorum goes with age.

yoruba: Àgbà-ìyà tí ńmùkọ ọ̀níní, ó ní nítorí omi gbígbóná orí-i rẹ̀ ni.
english_literal: Worthless elderly person who is eating corn gruel worth one tenth of a penny, he says he only wants the hot water on top of it.
interpretation_gold: One should act according to the demands of one's status.

yoruba: We saw other trees in the bush before we settled on ọ̀mọ̀
interpretation_gold: One should never presume to be the only possible answer to every challenge.

yoruba: Àgbà tí kò nítìjú, ojú kan ni ìbá ní; ojú kan náà a wà lọ́gangan iwájú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: An elder without self-respect might as well have only one eye, that one eye being in the center of his forehead.
interpretation_gold: Shamelessness does not become an elder.

yoruba: A kì í yàgò fún “Mo gun ẹṣin rí o!”
english_literal: One does not get out of the way for “I used to ride a horse!”
interpretation_gold: People should not expect to live on past glory.

yoruba: A kì í mọ ọ̀nà ọgbà ju ọlọ́gbà lọ; ẹní múni wá là ńtẹ̀lé.
english_literal: One does not presume to know the way to or around a garden better than the owner of the garden; one always follows the person who brought one.
interpretation_gold: Never presume to have a better knowledge of a matter than has the person most intimately involved.

yoruba: Àì-kúkú-joye, ó sàn ju, “Ẹnuù mi ò ká ìlú” lọ.
english_literal: Not-assuming-the-position-of-ruler-at-all is far better than, “My word is not heeded by the people.”
interpretation_gold: A person who does not assume a responsibility is better off than a person who takes it on and fails to fulfill it.

yoruba: A sìnkú tán, alugbá ò lọ́ ó fẹ́ ṣúpó ni?
english_literal: The funeral is over, but the calabash beater does not take his leave; does he want to inherit a wife?
interpretation_gold: This proverb has the same import as, A kúnlẹ̀, a pàgbò . . .

yoruba: Àkíìjẹ́ mú òrìṣà níyì.
english_literal: Refusal-to-acknowledge-salutations enhances the god's dignity.
interpretation_gold: Distancing oneself from ordinary people lends one prestige.

yoruba: Aládàá lo làṣẹ àro.
english_literal: It is the owner of the machete who exercises authority over mutual laborers.
interpretation_gold: One yields authority to one's host, or the owner of the property.

yoruba: Akú, nkò ní omitooro-o rẹ̀ ẹ́ lá; àìkú, nkò níí pè é rán níṣẹ́.
english_literal: Dead, I will not eat its broth; alive, I will not send it on an errand.
interpretation_gold: One needs pay no mind to a person who can in no way affect one's fortune.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà tó ńgun ọ̀pẹ, bó bá já lulẹ̀ ó dọ̀run.
english_literal: An elder who climbs palm-trees: if he crashes from the tree he will find himself in heaven.
interpretation_gold: An elder should know better than to climb palm-trees; one should not court danger.

yoruba: Àì-lápá làdá ò mú; bí a bá lápá, ọmọ owú to-o gégi.
english_literal: It is a deficiency of biceps that blunts the machete; if one has strong biceps one can cut trees with a cudgel.
interpretation_gold: One should not blame one's deficiencies on one's tools.

yoruba: A kì í gbé sàráà kọjá-a mọ́ṣáláṣí.
english_literal: One does not carry alms beyond the mosque.
interpretation_gold: Excess brings disgrace.

yoruba: A kì í fini joyè àwòdì ká má lè gbádìẹ.
english_literal: One cannot be given the title “eagle” and yet be incapable of snatching chickens.
interpretation_gold: One should be able to live up to expectations.

yoruba: Aláṣejù, baba ojo.
english_literal: The immoderate person, greatest of cowards.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation is a cloak for cowardice.

yoruba: Aṣọ tó kuni kù ní ńjẹ́ gọgọwú.
english_literal: Whatever clothing one is left with is one's best.
interpretation_gold: One makes the most of what one has.

yoruba: À-sẹ́-kú làgbàlagbà ńsẹ́ ọ̀ràn.
english_literal: Denying-until-death is the way a venerable person denies a matter.
interpretation_gold: One must never admit to doing something unworthy of one's position.

yoruba: À-gbàbọ̀-ọ ṣòkòtò, bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a ṣoni; rẹ́múrẹ́mú ni ohun ẹni ḿbani mu.
english_literal: Borrowed trousers: if they are not too tight around the legs, they will be too loose; one's own things fit one exactly.
interpretation_gold: Borrowed articles are never like one's own.

yoruba: Àpárá ńlá ni iná ńdá; iná ò lè rí omi gbéṣe.
english_literal: The fire is being most overbearing; there is nothing fire can do to water.
interpretation_gold: This entry has the same application as the preceding one.

yoruba: Ajá kì í rorò kó ṣọ́ ojúlé méjì.
english_literal: A dog is never so fierce that it can guard two doorways.
interpretation_gold: One cannot serve two masters simultaneously.

yoruba: Agbára wo ló wà lọ́wọ́ igbá tó fẹ́ fi gbọ́n omi òkun?
english_literal: What strength does the calabash have at its disposal that makes it attempt to scoop up all the water in the ocean?
interpretation_gold: People should not overreach.

yoruba: A-dìtan-mọ́ èsúó; ó ní èkùlù ló bí ìyá òun.
english_literal: The red-flanked duiker, desperate to claim relationship, says that its mother was born of a crested duiker.
interpretation_gold: Never make preposterous claims of kinship.

yoruba: À ḿbáni mú adìẹ à ńforúnkún bó; bọ́wọ́ bá ba òkókó, a ò ní fún aládìẹ?
english_literal: One helps to catch a chicken and scrapes one's knees; having laid one's hands on the chick will one not hand it over to the owner?
interpretation_gold: One should not be overzealous in helping others, especially when no benefit will accrue to one from the effort.

yoruba: Ajá ò gbọdọ̀ dé mọ́ṣáláṣí ìkókò ṣàlùwàlá.
english_literal: A dog dares not go to a wolf's mosque to make ablutions.
interpretation_gold: One should not exceed one's station.

yoruba: Àfòpiná tó fẹ́ paná-a súyà: ẹrán pọ̀ sí i.
english_literal: The moth (that) tries to put out the barbecue fire: the meat becomes more plentiful.
interpretation_gold: A person who foolishly attempts dangerous tasks courts destruction.

yoruba: Àgbéré laáyán gbé tó ní òun ó jòó láàárín adìẹ.
english_literal: The cockroach overreaches itself when it says it will dance in the company of chickens.
interpretation_gold: The chickens will eagerly peck it to death.

yoruba: A kì í pe ìyàwó kó kan alárẹnà.
english_literal: One does not summon the wife and so involve the go-between.
interpretation_gold: People should mind their own business.

yoruba: A-ṣúra-mú ò tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: A person who is mindful of his/her image is not easily disgraced.
interpretation_gold: People take one as one presents oneself.

yoruba: A kì í dákẹ́ ká ṣìwí; a kì í wò sùn-ùn ká dáràn.
english_literal: One does not keep quiet and yet misspeak; one does not silently contemplate the world and yet get into trouble.
interpretation_gold: A careful and cautious person seldom gets into trouble.

yoruba: Àjàpá ní òun tí ìbá só ló sùn yí, bẹ́ẹ̀ni ẹní bá sùn kì í só.
english_literal: Tortoise argues that it that might have farted is sound asleep, and, surely, those that sleep do not fart!
interpretation_gold: Some defenses are so transparent as to be frivolous.

yoruba: A kì í ní agbára kékeré ṣe èkejì.
english_literal: One does not offer to second a combatant in spite of one's negligible strength.
interpretation_gold: Never attempt more than you have the power to accomplish.

yoruba: Ajá kì í lọ ságinjù lọ ṣọdẹ ẹkùn.
english_literal: A dog does not go into the wild to hunt a leopard.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt feats one is unqualified to accomplish.

yoruba: A kì í ní ọ̀kánjúwà ká mọ̀; ará ilé ẹni ní ńsọ fúnni.
english_literal: One does not know that one has covetousness; it is one's kin who so inform one.
interpretation_gold: Often, only those close to one can recognize one's flaws and alert one to them.

yoruba: Àjàpá ńlọ sájò, wọ́n ní ìgbà wo ni yó dèé, ó ní ó dìgbàtí òún bá tẹ́.
english_literal: Tortoise set out on a journey and it was asked when it would return; it replied that it would be after it had earned disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Certain people will not change course until they are disgraced.

yoruba: Afọ́jú tó dijú, tó ní òún sùn, ìgbàtí kò sùn ta ló rí?
english_literal: The blind person who shuts his eyes and says he is asleep, when he was not asleep whom did he see?
interpretation_gold: The deceiver deceives him/herself.

yoruba: Amùrín ò sunwọ̀n, ó yí sáró.
english_literal: The lizard is not good-looking to start with, and it slips into indigo dye.
interpretation_gold: A person who has enough flaws should not seek ways to add to them.

yoruba: Aáyán ati eèràá ṣígun, wọ́n ní àwọ́n ńlọ mú adìẹ àlọ la rí, a ò rábọ̀.
english_literal: Cockroach and ant make ready for war and say they are off to capture chicken; we see their departure, but not their return.
interpretation_gold: Never forget your limitations.

yoruba: Ajá mọ ìgbẹ́; ẹlẹ́dẹ̀-ẹ́ mọ àfọ̀; tòlótòló mọ ẹni tí yó yìnbọn ìdí sí.
english_literal: A dog knows excrement; a pig knows a mud pit; a turkey knows to whom to direct its fart.
interpretation_gold: People should know who are their peers and who are not.

yoruba: Aláṣejù tí ńpọkọ ní baba.
english_literal: Overzealous wife that calls her husband “father.”
interpretation_gold: The wife who calls her husband “father” carries respect beyond reasonable limits; one should not be overzealous in one's observance of proprieties.

yoruba: Alákòró kì í sá fógun.
english_literal: A wearer of a battle-helmet does not flee from war.
interpretation_gold: A warrior does not run from battle.

yoruba: Afínjú-u póńpólà, ogé kun osùn láìwẹ.
english_literal: Unusual-fashionable-person, the preener anoints herself with camwood without taking a bath.
interpretation_gold: Cleanliness should be more than a matter of appearance.

yoruba: A rí èyí rí ni tonílé; a ò rí èyí rí ni tàlejò; bónílé bá ní ká jẹ ẹ́ tán, àlejò a ní ká jẹ ẹ́ kù.
english_literal: “Its likes have been seen before,” is what the host says; “No one has ever seen its likes before,” is what the guest says; if the host says that we should empty the plate, the guest should argue for leaving a little.
interpretation_gold: A host might minimize his hospitality, but the guest should praise it; if the host is lavish, the guest should not be greedy.

yoruba: A-dá-má-lè-ṣe àdàbà tí ńdún bẹ̀m̀bẹ̀.
english_literal: Start-something-it-cannot-finish dove that makes bombastic noises.
interpretation_gold: Bombast often masks fickleness.

yoruba: Àgó tó gbó ṣáṣá, ẹ̀bìtí pa á, áḿbọ̀sì olóósè a-bara-kùọ̀kùọ̀.
english_literal: The nimble, sprightly rat fell victim to the trap, how much more the sluggish, sickly mouse.
interpretation_gold: If the green wood is consumed, the dry wood has no prayer.

yoruba: Àpárá ńlá nikán ńdá; ikán ò lè mu òkúta.
english_literal: The termite is being most overbearing; a termite cannot eat a rock.
interpretation_gold: Certain people do not know their place; certain people are beyond the reach of their adversaries.

yoruba: À ḿbẹ̀rù alájá, ajá ṣebí òun là ḿbẹ̀rù.
english_literal: One shows deference to the dog's owner, and the dog thinks the deference is to it.
interpretation_gold: A person who has a powerful patron mistakenly believes that the respect he enjoys from others is due to his or her own qualities, whereas it is reflected from the patron.

yoruba: Aaka ò gbé ọ̀dàn; igbó ní ńgbé.
english_literal: The hedgehog does not live in the grassland, only in the forest.
interpretation_gold: Certain things are proper; certain things are not.

yoruba: Àgbà tí kò mọ ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀ lodò ńgbé lọ́.
english_literal: It is an elder who does not know his limitations that is washed away by a river.
interpretation_gold: Elders who cannot swim will be cautious near rivers.

yoruba: A kì í bẹ̀rù ikú bẹ̀rù àrùn ká ní kí ọmọ ó kú sinni.
english_literal: One does not so fear death and disease that one asks that one's child die before one.
interpretation_gold: One should not be more concerned with saving oneself than with saving one's dependents.

yoruba: A kì í fi ìka ro etí, ká fi ro imú, ká wá tún fi ta ehín.
english_literal: One does not use one's finger to clean one's ear passages, use it to pick one's nose, and then use it to pick one's teeth.
interpretation_gold: One should always behave with decorum.

yoruba: Àgbéré lẹyẹ ńgbé; kò lè mu omi inú àgbọn
english_literal: The bird only attempts the impossible; it cannot drink the milk in a coconut.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limits.

yoruba: À ńjá ìbàǹtẹ́ ẹ̀ lẹ́hìn, ó ńjá tará iwájú.
english_literal: His loincloth is being stripped from behind, yet he is stripping those of the people ahead of him.
interpretation_gold: Attacks on him do not stop him from belaboring his enemies.

yoruba: Àpọ́nlé ni “İyá-a Káà”; ìyá kan ò sí ní káà tí kò lórúkọ.
english_literal: Calling a person “Mother of the Compound” is only a mark of respect; there is no mother in the compound who does not have a name.
interpretation_gold: People in a position of respect should not forget that respect can be withdrawn.

yoruba: A gbé gàárì ọmọ ewurẹ ńrojú; kì í ṣe ẹrù àgùntàn.
english_literal: We lift a saddle and the goat (kin) scowls; it is no burden for a sheep.
interpretation_gold: The goat has no cause to scowl, because no one will condescend to ride it anyway.

yoruba: Àjàpá ní kò sí oun tó dà bí oun tí a mọ̀ ọ́ṣe; ó ní bí òún bá ju ẹyìn sẹ́nu, òun a tu èkùrọ́ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: Tortoise says there is nothing quite like expertise in one's calling; it says if it puts a palm-fruit into its mouth, it spits out a palm-nut.
interpretation_gold: Nothing succeeds like expertise.

yoruba: Àgbà kì í ṣorò bí èwe.
english_literal: An elderly person does not perform rituals like a youth.
interpretation_gold: The elder's performance should be commensurate with his station and status.

yoruba: Àgùnbánirọ̀ ní ńfojúdini.
english_literal: It is the person taller than another who shows no respect for the other.
interpretation_gold: Even in a company, each person should know his/her relative station.

yoruba: Abùlàǹgà kì í ṣasán; bíyàá ò lọ́rọ̀, baba a lówó lọ́wọ́.
english_literal: The arrogant person is not arrogant for nothing; if his mother is not wealthy, his father must be rich.
interpretation_gold: There is, or should be, some basis for one's strutting.

yoruba: Ajá tún padà sí èébì-i rẹ̀.
english_literal: The dog returns to its vomit.
interpretation_gold: To accept what one has once rejected is to lose face.

yoruba: Àì-lè-jà ni à ńsọ pé “Ojúde baba-à mi ò dé ìhín.”
english_literal: It is inability to fight that prompts one to say, “My father's front yard does not extend this far.”
interpretation_gold: A coward will find any excuse to avoid a just fight.

yoruba: Àfi ohun tí a kì í tà lọ́jà lẹrú kì í jẹ.
english_literal: The only thing a slave cannot eat is something not available in the market.
interpretation_gold: A slave has no choice.

yoruba: Àṣá kì í rà kádìẹ gbé kòkòrò dání.
english_literal: When a kite hovers, a chicken does not hang on to an insect.
interpretation_gold: When a great danger threatens, one does not wait for small favors.

yoruba: A-binú-fùfù ní ńwá oúnjẹ fún a-binú-wẹ́rẹ́-wẹ́rẹ́.
english_literal: A volatile-tempered person secures food for a mild-tempered person.
interpretation_gold: Whatever good fortune might have been meant for the volatile person will wind up in the lot of the mild-mannered person.

yoruba: À-bí-ì-kọ́; à-kọ́-ì-gbà; òde ló ti ńkọ́gbọ́n wálé.
english_literal: A-child-that-was-never-taught-how-to-behave; a-child-that-was-taught-but-that-refused-to-heed-instruction; it is from outside the home that he will learn wisdom.
interpretation_gold: Look well to your child's upbringing.

yoruba: Àì-mọ̀-kan, àì-mọ̀-kàn ní ḿmú èkúté-ilé pe ológbò níjà.
english_literal: It is severe ignorance that prompts a mouse to challenge a cat to a fight.
interpretation_gold: Never taunt an adversary you cannot handle.

yoruba: Àlejò kì í pìtàn ìlú fónílé.
english_literal: The visitor does not recount the history of the town for the host.
interpretation_gold: Never presume to know more than the custodian of knowledge.

yoruba: A di gàárì sílẹ̀ ewúrẹ́ ńyọjú; ẹrù ìran rẹ̀ ni?
english_literal: We prepare the saddle, and the goat presents itself; is it a burden for the lineage of goats?
interpretation_gold: Goats that know their place do not offer their backs to be saddled.

yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ rí wèrè, ó kán lùgbẹ́.
english_literal: The leper sees a mad person and dashes into the bush.
interpretation_gold: A person who should be ostracized ostracizes others.

yoruba: Ara-àìbalẹ̀, olórí àrùn.
english_literal: Restlessness, father of all diseases.
interpretation_gold: No disease is greater than hyper-action.

yoruba: A fi ọ́ jọba ò ńṣàwúre o fẹ́ jẹ Ọlọ́run ni?
english_literal: You have been crowned a king, and yet you make good-luck charms; would you be crowned God?
interpretation_gold: Being crowned a king is about the best fortune a mortal could hope for.

yoruba: A kì í bínú ààtàn ká dalẹ̀ sígbẹ̀ẹ́.
english_literal: One does not get angry with the rubbish dump and discard one's rubbish into the bush.
interpretation_gold: One should not act in unreasonable and harmful ways because of anger.

yoruba: Àjànàkú ò tu lójú alájá; o-nígba-ajá ò gbọdọ̀ tọ́pa erin.
english_literal: The elephant does not break and run at the sight of dogs; a person with two hundred dogs dares not stalk an elephant.
interpretation_gold: Two hundred dogs are no match for an elephant.

yoruba: A kì í jẹ oyè ẹnu ọ̀nà kalẹ́.
english_literal: One does not bear the title of gatekeeper even until night time.
interpretation_gold: As one advances in age, so should one's responsibilities advance in gravity and importance.

yoruba: A pè ọ́ lọ́mọ erín-màgbọn ò ńyọ̀; ìwọ pàápàá ló mì í?
english_literal: You are described as the child of the elephant that swallows coconuts, and you rejoice; are you the one who swallows coconuts?
interpretation_gold: The description honors the father, not the person being addressed.

yoruba: Àbúrò kì í pa ẹ̀gbọ́n nítàn.
english_literal: The younger person does not give the older person history lectures.
interpretation_gold: One should not exceed one's station.

yoruba: À-tẹ́-ẹ̀-ká ni iyì ọlọ́lá; sálúbàtà ni iyì ọlọ̀tọ̀; bá a bá gbéra lágbèéjù ọba ni wọ́n ńfini íṣe
english_literal: Spreading-the-mat-without-rolling-it-back-up is the mark of the wealthy; sandals are the mark of the illustrious; if one sings one's praise too loudly one is liable to be made a king.
interpretation_gold: People take one as one presents oneself.

yoruba: Afínjú wọ ọjà ó rìn gbẹndẹ́kẹ ọ̀bún wọ ọjà ó rìn ṣùẹ̀ṣùẹ̀; ọ̀bùn ní ó ru ẹrù afínjú relé.
english_literal: The fashionable person enters the market and walks in a leisurely manner; the filthy person enters the market and walks in a sluggish manner; it is the filthy person that will carry the fashionable person's load to the house for him or her.
interpretation_gold: Good breeding confers great advantages.

yoruba: A kì í mú oko lọ́nà ká ṣèmẹ́lẹ́; tajá tẹran ní ḿbúni.
english_literal: One does not farm a plot by the road and neglect its care; every dog and goat would ridicule one.
interpretation_gold: Never expose yourself to insult by behaving badly in public view.

yoruba: Àgbéré-e ṣìgìdì tó ní ká gbé òun sójò; bí apá ti ńya nitan ńya; kidiri orí ò lè dá dúró.
english_literal: The overreaching mud idol that asked to be put in the rain; as the arms fell off, so did the thighs; the rounded head could not support itself.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limitations.

yoruba: Aláṣọ-kan kì í ṣeré òjò.
english_literal: A person who has only one set of clothing does not play in the rain.
interpretation_gold: See the preceding entry.

yoruba: Aṣọ à-fọ̀-fún ò jẹ́ ká mọ olówó.
english_literal: Clothes washed clean make identifying the rich person impossible.
interpretation_gold: A poor person who looks to his or her appearance looks rich.

yoruba: A ní ká wá ẹni tó lẹ́hìn ká fọmọ fún, abuké ní òun rèé; ti gànnàkù ẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀ là ńwí?
english_literal: One seeks a person with a prominent back as suitor for one's daughter, and the humpback presents himself; who spoke of protruding back?
interpretation_gold: The expression that translates as “prominent back” is an idiom meaning a proud pedigree. The humpback makes a rather embarrassing mistake.

yoruba: À-wín-ná-wó ò yẹni; à-gbà-bọ̀-ọ ṣòkòtò ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn; bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a dòrògí; ohun ẹni ní ńyẹni.
english_literal: Borrowing-money-to-spend does not speak well of one; borrowed trousers do not become a person; if it is not tight around the legs it is difficult to remove; it is one's thing that fits one.
interpretation_gold: One should not live beyond one's means.

yoruba: A kì í gbọ́ “Lù ú” lẹ́nu àgbà.
english_literal: One never hears “Beat him/her up” in the mouth of an elder.
interpretation_gold: Elders resolve disputes; they do not goad disputants on.

yoruba: Akórira ò ní ǹkan; ọ̀dùn ò sunwọ̀ fún ṣòkòtò.
english_literal: An overly squeamish person owns nothing; raffia cloth is no good for trousers.
interpretation_gold: Excessive squeamishness renders one helpless and destitute.

yoruba: A kì í jayé ọba ká ṣu sára.
english_literal: One does not so luxuriate in one's majesty that one shits on oneself.
interpretation_gold: Lack of moderation and decorum will bring disgrace to even the most elevated person.

yoruba: Adití ò gbọ́, “Yàgò!”
english_literal: The deaf does not hear,“Make way!”
interpretation_gold: Cautionary words are lost on reckless people.

yoruba: À-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, baálé ilé ṣu sápẹ.
english_literal: Something-seen-but-unmentionable, the man of the house shits in the sauce-pan.
interpretation_gold: When an illustrious person does the unmentionable, no one dares speak.

yoruba: Aáyán fẹ gẹṣin; adìẹ ni ò gbà fún un.
english_literal: The cockroach would ride a horse; it is the chicken that does not allow.
interpretation_gold: A cockroach that stirs in the presence of a chicken is as good as dead.

yoruba: Aáyán kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ erin; èèyàn kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ irò.
english_literal: A cockroach does not trip an elephant; a human being does not trip a chimpanzee.
interpretation_gold: One should not take on adversaries one cannot match.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà tó wẹ̀wù àṣejù, ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó fi rí.
english_literal: An elder who wears the garment of immoderation will find disgrace because of it.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation brings disgrace.

yoruba: A kì í kọ ẹlẹ́ṣin ká tún lọ fẹ́ ẹlẹ́sẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not divorce a horse rider and go marry a pedestrian.
interpretation_gold: One should ever progress, never regress.

yoruba: A kì í pẹ̀lú ọ̀bọ jáko.
english_literal: One does not join a monkey in roaming the bush.
interpretation_gold: Do not join others in their madness.

yoruba: Àkùkọ̀ adìẹ́ fi dídájí ṣàgbà; ó fi ṣíṣu-sílẹ̀ ṣèwe.
english_literal: The rooster shows its maturity by its early rising; it shows its lack of maturity by defecating on the floor.
interpretation_gold: Nobody is free of some blemish.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà kì í yọ ayọ̀-ọ kí-ló-báyìí-wá?
english_literal: An elder does not rejoice in a manner that would provoke, “What brought all this about?”
interpretation_gold: Moderation and decorum in everything.

yoruba: À-jókòó-àì-dìde, à-sọ̀rọ̀-àì-gbèsì, ká sinni títí ká má padà sílé, àì-sunwọ̀n ní ńgbẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀.
english_literal: Sitting-without-getting-up, speaking-without-waiting-for-responses, walking people on their way and not turning back, unpleasantness is what they breed.
interpretation_gold: Excess and self-forgetfulness in anything bring unpleasant results.

yoruba: it is a sagacious person that eats kolanut; it is someone not squeamish about what he eats that eats awùsá.
interpretation_gold: People are what they eat; each to his/her own taste.

yoruba: Àfòpiná tó ní òun ó pa fìtílà, ara ẹ̀ ni yó pa.
english_literal: The moth that attempts to kill (put out) the oil lamp will kill itself.
interpretation_gold: It is unwise to take on an adversary one knows can destroy one.

yoruba: Àì-jọnilójú lọ́sàn-án ní ḿmúni jarunpá luni lóru.
english_literal: Lack of regard for a person during the day makes one kick the person during the night as one tosses restlessly in sleep.
interpretation_gold: Familiarity breeds contempt.

yoruba: Ajá tó ńlépa ẹkùn, ìyọnu ló ńwá.
english_literal: A dog that chases a leopard is seeking trouble.
interpretation_gold: One should not overreach oneself.

yoruba: Ayọ̀ àyọ̀jù làkèré fi ńṣẹ́ nítan.
english_literal: It is excessive rejoicing that breaks the frog's thigh.
interpretation_gold: Immoderate happiness breeds unhappiness.

yoruba: Àgbà tí yó tẹ̀ẹ́, bó fárí tán, a ní ó ku járá ẹnu.
english_literal: An elder courting disgrace, after his head has been shaved he says, “Now, how about shaving the beard (as a gratuity)?”
interpretation_gold: One should know how far one may go before one suffers disgrace.

yoruba: Alátiṣe ní ḿmọ àtiṣe ara-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: The person who must settle his/her affair knows best how he/she plans to go about doing so.
interpretation_gold: One should not second guess others, or try to make their decisions for them.

yoruba: Without having a wife a person spares oóyọ́
interpretation_gold: The vegetable is used in stews, and stews are for wives to cook.

yoruba: Àgbà kì í ṣerée kí-ló-bá-yìí-wá?
english_literal: An elderly person does not engage in the type of play that provokes the comment, “What brought all this about?”
interpretation_gold: Elders should show decorum.

yoruba: A kì í yàgò fún ẹlẹ́ṣin àná.
english_literal: One does not get out of the way for a person who rode a horse yesterday.
interpretation_gold: Past glory avails little in the present.

yoruba: Àṣejù baba àṣetẹ́; ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńgbẹ̀hìn àṣejù; àgbàlagbà tó wẹ̀wù àṣejù ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó fi rí.
english_literal: Lack of moderation is the father of disgrace; disgrace comes of immoderation; a grown person who clothes himself in immoderation will find disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation leads to disgrace.

yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀ẹ́ ní òun ò lè fún wàrà, ṣùgbọ́n òún lè yí i dànù.
english_literal: The leper says he may not be able to squeeze out milk, but he can spill it.
interpretation_gold: Even feckless people can cause some damage.

yoruba: A-báni-gbé kì í yáná; a-bọ̀rìṣà kì í sun òtútù; ẹyin gẹ́gẹ́ kì í gbé àwùjọ́; ilé kannáà ni wọ́n kọ́ fún àwọn mẹ́tẹ̀ẹ̀ta.
english_literal: A guest does not warm himself by the fire; a priest or priestess does not sleep in the cold; a delicate egg does not live in a crowd; the same house was built for all three.
interpretation_gold: Know yourself and your place.

yoruba: Àgbá òfìfo ní ńpariwo; àpò tó kún fówó kì í dún.
english_literal: It is an empty barrel that is noisy; a sack full of money makes no sound.
interpretation_gold: Empty barrels make the most noise.

yoruba: A kì í mọ̀-ọ́ rò bí ẹlẹ́jọ́.
english_literal: One never knows how to present it like the owner of the case.
interpretation_gold: No one can know better than the person itself where it hurts most and what relief is needed.

yoruba: A kì í dàgbà má làáyà; ibi ayé bá báni là ńjẹ ẹ́.
english_literal: One does not become an adult and yet lack courage; one lives life as it finds one.
interpretation_gold: One should do what is fitting for one's station in life.

yoruba: A kì í dá ọwọ́ lé ohun tí a ò lè gbé.
english_literal: One does not lay one's hands on a load one cannot lift.
interpretation_gold: One should not overreach.

yoruba: À ńwá ẹni tí a ó fọmọ fún, olòṣì ńyọjú.
english_literal: We seek a person to give a child to (in marriage) and a worthless person presents himself.
interpretation_gold: People should know their place and not over-rate themselves.

yoruba: Àgbà tó mọ ìtìjú kì í folè ṣeré.
english_literal: An elder who is wary of disgrace will not play at stealing.
interpretation_gold: Anything that smacks of stealing will disgrace an elder.

yoruba: Aláṣọ àlà kì í jókòó sísọ̀ elépo.
english_literal: A person dressed in white does not sit at the stall of a palm-oil seller.
interpretation_gold: One should not expose oneself to abuse or danger.

yoruba: A léṣu sílẹ̀ páńdọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ já lù ú; èlé mbénì?
english_literal: We group yams in lots and the fruit of the sausage tree drops among them; does it count as complement to a lot, or as gratuity?
interpretation_gold: The fruit might look somewhat like a yam, but it does not belong with yams.

yoruba: Àìsí èèyàn lóko là ḿbá ajá sọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: It is the absence of people on the farm that brings one to conversing with a dog.
interpretation_gold: But for unfortunate circumstances one would not deign to associate with certain people.

yoruba: A-bánijẹun-bí-aláìmọra, ó bu òkèlè bí ẹ̀gbọ́n ìyá ẹ̀.
english_literal: He-who-eats-with-one-without-self-restraint; he breaks off morsels like his mother's senior.
interpretation_gold: When eating in company one should be restrained. A man eating with the child of his younger sister need show no such restraint.

yoruba: Adìẹ ò bí yọyọ kú yọ̀.
english_literal: A chicken does not give birth to a multitude of chicks and die of the exertion.
interpretation_gold: Children should not be the death of their parents.

yoruba: A kì í kó èlé ṣẹ̀ṣọ́.
english_literal: One does not live fashionably on borrowed money.
interpretation_gold: Live within your means.

yoruba: Àpọ́nlé ni “Fọ́maàn”; ẹnìkan ò lè ṣe èèyàn mẹ́rin.
english_literal: Calling a person a foreman is only a mark of respect; nobody can be four men.
interpretation_gold: People whose positions earn them respect should not forget themselves, or people would forget their positions.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà kì í wẹwọ́ tán kó ní òun ó jẹ si.
english_literal: An elder does not wash his hand and then decide to eat more.
interpretation_gold: An elder should know his mind.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá dáṣọ lé aṣọ, a kì í pe ọ̀kan lákìísà.
english_literal: If one has not acquired one garment after another, one does not call one a rag.
interpretation_gold: One may not disdain an old tool until one is able to replace it.

yoruba: Bí eegbọ́n bá ṣo ayínrín nímú, adìẹ kọ́ ni yó ja.
english_literal: If a tick clings to a fox's nose, it is not a chicken that will remove it.
interpretation_gold: The prey is not the one one sends to minister to a predator.

yoruba: Bí a bá ńgúnyán, kòmẹsẹ̀ á yọ.
english_literal: If one prepares pounded yams, the uninvited should depart.
interpretation_gold: The well-bred visitor should make his/her exit when the hosts turn to intimate affairs.

yoruba: Bí a bá fi inú wénú; iwọ là ńjẹ.
english_literal: If we compare notes with others, we wind up eating bile.
interpretation_gold: Comparing fortunes with others is liable to leave a bitter taste in one's mouth.

yoruba: Bí a bá ti lè ṣe là ńwí; a kì í yan àna ẹni lódì.
english_literal: One admits to one's limits; one does not cease speaking to one's relatives-in-law.
interpretation_gold: One should not let one's inability to fulfil a formal obligation prevent one from fulfilling essential obligations.

yoruba: Bí ìlàrí bá fẹ́ tẹ́, a ní kí lọba ó ṣe?
english_literal: When a courtier seeks disgrace, he asks, “What can the king do?”
interpretation_gold: If one does not show respect for one's patron, one courts disgrace.

yoruba: Bí iná bá dun ọbẹ̀, a dá ọ̀rọ̀ sọ.
english_literal: If the fire gets at the stew, the stew will burst into speech.
interpretation_gold: If the excitement is strong enough, coyness disappears.

yoruba: Bí a bá ti mọ là ńdé; a-láì-lẹ́ṣin kì í dé wọ̀nwọ̀n.
english_literal: One arrives according to one's worth; a horseless person does not arrive with the noise of hoofs and stirrups.
interpretation_gold: One should act according to one's worth.

yoruba: Bí ojú kò bá rí, ẹnu kì í sọ nǹkan.
english_literal: If the eye does not see, the mouth says nothing.
interpretation_gold: The mouth can tell only what the eye sees.

yoruba: Bí òfé ti ńfò la ti ḿmọ̀ ọ́ lákọ ẹyẹ.
english_literal: It is by its flight that the parrot proves itself a formidable bird.
interpretation_gold: One shows one's quality through one's accomplishments.

yoruba: Bí a bá dàgbà à yé ogun-ún jà.
english_literal: When one becomes old, one stops warring.
interpretation_gold: An elder should leave off things that are a mark of youth.

yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá gun òkè àgbà, ó ńláti gbọ́n.
english_literal: If a child ascends the height of maturity, he/she must become wise.
interpretation_gold: Wisdom goes with age.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá ṣèké, a kì í fi ẹ̀tẹ́ kú.
english_literal: If one has not been false, one does not die in disgrace.
interpretation_gold: One's honesty is one's vindication.

yoruba: Bí ayá bá mojú ọkọ, alárìnnà a yẹsẹ̀.
english_literal: When the wife has got to know the husband, the marriage broker makes way.
interpretation_gold: Once one's task is done, one removes oneself.

yoruba: Bí ayé bá ńyẹni, ìwà ìbàjẹ́ là ńhù.
english_literal: If life is being good to one, one is liable to act disgracefully.
interpretation_gold: Prosperity breeds temptations to misbehave.

yoruba: Bí ọ̀lẹ́ ò lè jà, a lè kú tùẹ̀.
english_literal: If a lazy man cannot fight, he should be able to die disgracefully.
interpretation_gold: A person who cannot defend his rights should yield to death.

yoruba: Bí ẹlẹ́bọ ò bá pe ẹni, àṣefín ò yẹni.
english_literal: If the person offering a sacrifice does not invite one, intruding is not proper for one.
interpretation_gold: It is bad form to intrude into other people's affairs.

yoruba: Bí ojú kò bá ti olè, a ti ará ilé ẹ̀.
english_literal: If the thief feels no shame, members of his household should.
interpretation_gold: A person's disgrace must concern his relatives.

yoruba: Bí olóde ò kú, òdee rẹ̀ kì í hu gbẹ́gi.
english_literal: If the owner of a yard does not die, his yard is not overgrown with wild grass.
interpretation_gold: If one does not die one is able to look after one's affairs.

yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá ńṣe ọmọdé, àgbà a máa ṣe àgbà.
english_literal: When a child is being a child, an elder must remain an elder.
interpretation_gold: One should not permit other people's misbehavior to deflect one from the proper course.

yoruba: Bí ojú bá rí, ẹnu a dákẹ́.
english_literal: When the eyes see, the mouth remains quiet.
interpretation_gold: The mouth does not reveal everything the eyes see.

yoruba: Bí Ọlọ́run ò ṣe ẹni ní baba, à fi ìyànjú ṣe bí àgbà.
english_literal: If God does not make one a father, one strives to act like an elder.
interpretation_gold: Even if one has no influence, one strives to act responsibly.

yoruba: Bẹbẹlúbẹ ò ì tíì débẹ̀; ibẹ̀ ló ḿbọ̀.
english_literal: The busybody is not there yet; but he is on his way.
interpretation_gold: There is no keeping a nosy person off others' affairs.

yoruba: Bí eegbọ́n bá so mọ́ ajá lẹ́nu, akátá là ńní kó já a?
english_literal: If a tick fastens on to a dog's mouth, does one ask a jackal to dislodge it?
interpretation_gold: A person of great substance is not asked to minister to a person of no substance.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá tó baba ọmọọ́ ṣe, a kì í pe alákàrà.
english_literal: If one lacks the wherewithal to act like a father to a child, one does not summon the seller of bean fritters.
interpretation_gold: If one has no means of offering hospitality, one should not invite visitors.

yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá fẹ́ ṣìṣe àgbà, ọjọ́ orí-i rẹ̀ ò níí jẹ́.
english_literal: If a youth attempts to act like an elder, his age will stop him.
interpretation_gold: A youth does not have what it takes to be an elder.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá lè dá Tápà, Tápà kì í dáni.
english_literal: If one cannot throw a Nupe man in a wrestling match, he should not throw one.
interpretation_gold: If one fails, one should at least avoid disgrace.

yoruba: Bí a bá tọ̀ sílé, onípò a mọ ipò.
english_literal: If someone wets the bed, each person should know where he or she slept.
interpretation_gold: In the event of a crime, the guilty should not attempt to shift the blame to others.

yoruba: Bí a bá ti mọ là ńkú; olongo kì í kú tìyàntìyàn.
english_literal: One dies according to one's weight; the robin does not die and make a resounding noise “on hitting the ground.”
interpretation_gold: One acts according to one's worth.

yoruba: Bí kò sí tọ̀bùn èèyàn, ta ni ìbá jí lówùúrọ̀ tí kò bọ́jú ṣáṣá?
english_literal: But for a person of filthy habits, who would wake in the morning and not wash his or her face clean?
interpretation_gold: Antisocial people betray themselves by their habits.

yoruba: Bí ọjọ́ ewúrẹ́ bá pé, a ní kò sí ohun tí alápatàá lè fi òun ṣe.
english_literal: When a goat's day “to die” arrives, it says there is nothing a butcher can do to it.
interpretation_gold: A person who does not recognize and heed danger courts death.

yoruba: Bí baálẹ̀-ẹ́ bá ńtàkìtì, òrógi là ḿbá ẹmẹsẹ̀.
english_literal: If the chief is turning somersaults, the messenger should be found standing erect.
interpretation_gold: The great may indulge themselves, but the lowly must keep their heads.

yoruba: Bí mo bá torí oko kú ng ó rò fáhéré; bí mo bá torí ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ kú ng ó rò fódò; bí mo bá torí alábàjà òkíkí kú, ng ó rò fórí-ì mi.
english_literal: If I die on account of a farm, I will lay my case before the hut; if I die on account of bananas, I will lay my case before the river; if I die on account of the famous woman with facial scarification, I will lay my case before my head.
interpretation_gold: Were I to die for a woman, the forces ordering my fortune would know why.

yoruba: Bí òkú fẹ̀, bí kò fẹ̀, ká bi ọmọ olókùú léèrè.
english_literal: Whether the corpse is distended or is not, one should ask the heir of the dead.
interpretation_gold: Only those most intimately concerned know the close truths of an affair, and should be asked about them.

yoruba: Bí ọmọdé ńlérí bébé, tí kò ní baba, ti baba là ńṣe.
english_literal: If a child brags a great deal, but has no father, one acts the part of a father.
interpretation_gold: One should not deal too harshly with a child who has no one to direct him or her.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá lọ sóko irọ́, a kì í pa á mọ́ni.
english_literal: If one does not go to the farm of lies, lies are not told against one.
interpretation_gold: If one does not lay oneself open to lies, one is not lied about.

yoruba: Bí èèyán bá ní kò sí irú òun, àwọn ọlọgbọ́n a máa wòye.
english_literal: If a person says there is no one like him/her, wise people maintain a contemplative silence.
interpretation_gold: A person who thinks he/she is peerless fools no one but him/herself.

yoruba: Bí àgbà kò bá ṣe ohun ẹ̀rù, ọmọdé kì í sá.
english_literal: If an elder does not do something fearful, the youth do not flee.
interpretation_gold: Youth responds to age according to how age acts.

yoruba: Bí ẹkùn ò bá fẹ̀, èse là ńpè é.
english_literal: If a leopard does not act mighty, one refers to it as a cat.
interpretation_gold: A person who acts beneath his station loses some respect.

yoruba: Bí olóúnjẹẹ́ bá rojú à fi àìjẹ tẹ́ ẹ.
english_literal: If the owner of the food is reluctant to share, one disgraces him by refusing to eat.
interpretation_gold: The best way to treat a miser is to refuse anything from him.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá tíì jókòó, a kì í nasẹ̀.
english_literal: If one has not yet sat down, one does not stretch one's legs out.
interpretation_gold: Until one has thoroughly secured one's position, relaxation is premature.

yoruba: Bí ó di ọdún mẹ́ta tí ẹkùn-ún ti ńṣe òjòjò, olugbe la ó ha rán lọ bẹ̀ ẹ́ wò?
english_literal: If it has been three years since the leopard took ill, is it a monkey that one sends to ask its condition?
interpretation_gold: Even though one may be down on one's luck, there are yet certain propositions one would consider insulting.

yoruba: Bí ojú onílé bá mọ tíntín, tí ojú àlejòó tó gbòǹgbò, onílé ní ńṣe ọkọ àlejò.
english_literal: Even though the host's eyes are tiny, and the guest's eyes are huge, it is the host who holds sway over the guest.
interpretation_gold: The host is lord over the guest.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá tó ìyà-á kọ̀ tí à ńkọ̀ ọ́, àjẹkún ìyà là ńjẹ.
english_literal: If one lacks the means to reject suffering and attempts to reject it, one's suffering simply multiplies.
interpretation_gold: Whoever cannot defend himself or herself must learn forebearance.

yoruba: Bí àjànàkú ò bá rí ohun gbémì, kì í ṣe inú gbẹndu sọ́dẹ.
english_literal: Unless an elephant had swallowed something, it would not turn its bloated stomach to the hunter.
interpretation_gold: Unless a person has some resource to rely on, he or she does not tempt fate.

yoruba: Babaaláwo kì í bèrè ẹbọ àná.
english_literal: The diviner does not ask for yesterday's sacrifice.
interpretation_gold: One should not demean oneself by demanding piddling favors.

yoruba: Bí ajá rójú ẹkùn, a pa rọ́rọ́.
english_literal: When the dog sees the eyes of the leopard, it keeps very still.
interpretation_gold: In the presence of one's betters, one keeps one's place.

yoruba: Bí a ó ti tó kì í jẹ́ ká hùwà búburú; bí a ó ti mọ kì í jẹ́ ká hùwà rere.
english_literal: The heights one will reach keeps one from evil deeds; the ordained limit to one's greatness keeps one from doing good deeds.
interpretation_gold: A person's achievements are enhanced or limited by the person's character.

yoruba: Bí a bá ḿbá ọmọdé jẹun lóko, gànmùganmu imú ẹni ní ńwò.
english_literal: If one eats with a youth on the farm he stares at the protrusion of one's nose.
interpretation_gold: Too much familiarity with youth breeds contempt.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá tíì lè kọ́lé, àgọ́ là ńpa.
english_literal: If one is yet unable to build a house, one makes a tent.
interpretation_gold: One should neither overreach oneself, nor refrain from striving.

yoruba: Dìgbòlugi-dìgbòlùùyàn ò jẹ́ ká mọ ajá tòótọ́.
english_literal: The mad dog, and the person who behaves like a mad dog, both make it impossible for one to know the real dog.
interpretation_gold: He who acts like a dog makes himself the equal of a dog.

yoruba: Dídákẹ́ lerín dákẹ́; àjànàkú ló lẹgàn.
english_literal: The elephant has only chosen to remain silent; to the elephant belongs the forest.
interpretation_gold: The mighty need not proclaim their importance.

yoruba: Èmi ìwọ̀fà, ìwọ ìwọ̀fà, o ní babá ní ká gbowó wá; o dá tìrẹ sílẹ̀ ná?
english_literal: I am a pawn, you are a pawn, and you tell me the creditor sent you to collect his money; have you repaid yours?
interpretation_gold: Whoever will correct others should first take care of his/her own failings.

yoruba: Eégún wọlé, ó ní òun ò rí Ejonto; Ejontó ní, “Àkísà ni, àbí kíní wọlé?”
english_literal: The masquerader enters a house and claims he did not see Ejonto; Ejonto asked, “Is that a rag that entered the house, or what?”
interpretation_gold: A person who disregards one earns one's disregard.

yoruba: Eégún pẹ́ lóde, ó fètè òkè dáhùn; wọ́n ní, “Baba kú àbọ̀,” ó ní, “Hì ìì.”
english_literal: The masquerader stayed too long on parade and is reduced to speaking with his upper lip. They said, “Welcome, father,” and he responded, “He-e-e-e.”
interpretation_gold: A person who has disgraced himself speaks softly.

yoruba: Èèyàn bí ọ̀bọ lọ̀bọ ńya láṣọ.
english_literal: Only people like monkeys have their clothing torn by monkeys.
interpretation_gold: Those who consort with undesirables are liable to have their reputation soiled.

yoruba: Èmí dákọ okòó, ìwọ́ dákọ okòó, ò ńpèmí ní mùkọ-mùkọ.
english_literal: I bought twenty cowries worth of corn pap and you bought twenty cowries worth of corn pap, and you call me a corn pap addict.
interpretation_gold: One should not criticize others for flaws that are also one's lot.

yoruba: Èèyàn ò ríbi sùn, ajá ńhanrun.
english_literal: Humans have no place to sleep, and a dog is snoring.
interpretation_gold: A Lowly person lays claim to what his/her betters lack.

yoruba: Èrò ọ̀nà ni yó ròhìn ọkà tó gbó.
english_literal: It is people who use the path that will spread the word about mature corn.
interpretation_gold: A noteworthy accomplishment need not advertise itself.

yoruba: Ejò kì í ti ojú Ààrẹ gun ọgbà lọ.
english_literal: A snake does not escape over the fence while a warrior
interpretation_gold: One does not permit disaster on one's watch; one must live up to the expectations of one's position.

yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ ò wí pé òun ò ṣọmọ àgùntàn; àgùntàn ló wí pé òun ò ṣọmọ ewúrẹ́.
english_literal: The goat did not say it was not sired by the sheep; it was the sheep that said it was not sired by the goat.
interpretation_gold: The goat would like to associate with the sheep; but the sheep would not associate with the goat; “superior” people reject association with “inferior” people; not the other way around.

yoruba: Èsúrú yam
interpretation_gold: A person who does not know his or her place soon suffers disgrace.

yoruba: Epo ni mo rù; oníyangí má ba tèmi jẹ́.
english_literal: It is palm oil that I am carrying; sandman, do not ruin my fortune.
interpretation_gold: I am cautiously going about my own business; let no one bring trouble my way.

yoruba: Èwo ló tó ẹ̀kọ-ọ́ gbà nínú ewé ìrúgbàá?
english_literal: Which among the leaves of the locust-bean tree is adequate to receive corn-loaf?
interpretation_gold: Certain feats are beyond certain people; people should not presume to do things beyond their capabilities.

yoruba: Erin kì í fọn kọ́mọ-ọ rẹ̀ ó fọn.
english_literal: An elephant's trumpeting is never answered by its young's trumpeting.
interpretation_gold: Lowly people should not emulate illustrious ones.

yoruba: Ewújù tí yóò tú ọ̀pẹ: gbogbo ehín ẹ̀ ni yóò kán tán.
english_literal: The cane-rat that attempts to uproot a palm-tree will lose all its teeth in the attempt.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt a task for which one is not qualified.

yoruba: Eegun àjànàkú: ó há ìkokò lẹ́nu.
english_literal: An elephant's bone: it sticks in the wolf's mouth.
interpretation_gold: A person has overreached him/herself and is paying the price of folly.

yoruba: Eégún ò na obìnrin lágọ̀; obìnrín tú kíjìpá ìdí-i rẹ̀, ó fi na eégún.
english_literal: The masquerader did not hit a woman with his shroud, but the woman unwraps her home-woven wrapper and hits the masquerader with it.
interpretation_gold: A person is fortunate to have been overlooked by trouble, but he/she goes to deliberately provoke it.

yoruba: Eegbọ́n so mọ́ àyìnrín lẹ́nu, a ní kí adìẹ wá yán an jẹ; adìẹ́ mọ̀ pé òun náà oúnjẹ àyìnrín.
english_literal: A tick fastens on a fox's mouth and a chicken is asked to peck it off; the chicken, though, knows that it itself is food for a fox.
interpretation_gold: One wastes one's time inviting others to endanger themselves.

yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ kì í bíni ká lọ sísọ̀ àgùntàn lọ jẹ̀.
english_literal: If sired by a goat, one does not go foraging in the realm of sheep.
interpretation_gold: One should keep to one's proper company.

yoruba: Èèyàn tí ò nítìjú ojú kan ni ìbá ní; a gbórín a tó tẹṣin.
english_literal: A shameless person deserves to have only one eye, that one as large as a horse's.
interpretation_gold: Human endowments are wasted on graceless people.

yoruba: Fálànà gbọ́ tìrẹ, tara ẹni là ńgbọ́.
english_literal: Falana, look to your own affairs; one's attention should be focused first on one's own affairs.
interpretation_gold: People should keep their noses out of others' affairs.

yoruba: Fáàárí ọ̀bọ ò ju inú ìgbẹ́ lọ.
english_literal: The monkey's showing off is limited to the confines of the forest.
interpretation_gold: One may be esteemed in one's locality and be quite unknown in another.

yoruba: Gànràn-gànràn ò yẹ ẹni a bí ire.
english_literal: Unrestrained and thoughtless behavior does not befit a well-born person.
interpretation_gold: One should behave in a manner that reflects well on one's family.

yoruba: Gbọ̀n-ọ́n-gbọ̀n-ọ́n kan ò sí, àfi ẹni tó bá ńti ara ẹ̀.
english_literal: There is no cause for staggering about, except for the person pushing himself/herself.
interpretation_gold: Some people make more trouble for themselves than others can ever make for them.

yoruba: “Gbà mí, gbà mí!” ò yẹ àgbà; àgbà kì í ṣe ohun àlémú.
english_literal: “Save me, save me!” does not become an elder; an elder should not do something that will make him the object of pursuit.
interpretation_gold: One should behave in a manner that befits one's station.

yoruba: “Gbà mí, gbà mí!” ò yẹ eégún; “ẹran ńlémi bọ̀” ò yẹ ọdẹ.
english_literal: “Save me, save me!” does not befit a masquerader; “An animal is chasing me!” does not befit a hunter.
interpretation_gold: One should act in ways that become one's station.

yoruba: “Gba wèrè,” “Ng ò gba wèrè” lọjà-á fi ńhó.
english_literal: “Accept imputation of imbecility,” “I will accept no imputation of imbecility” is the explanation for market noise.
interpretation_gold: One may have no means of avoiding insult from others, but it is always in one's power to reject insults.

yoruba: “Gbà jẹ” ò yẹ àgbà.
english_literal: “Take this and eat it” does not become an elder.
interpretation_gold: It better becomes an elder's to give than to go begging.

yoruba: Gbogbo ọ̀rọ̀ ní ńṣojú èké.
english_literal: The busybody is privy to all matters.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing the busybody will say he/she does not know about.

yoruba: Ìyàwó tó na ọmọ ọbàkan, ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ gbọ́.
english_literal: The wife who whips a relative of her husband is asking for stern rebuke.
interpretation_gold: One should not engage in inappropriate actions.

yoruba: Ibi tí a bá pè lórí, a kì í fi tẹlẹ̀.
english_literal: Whatever one names as the head, one does not tread the floor with it.
interpretation_gold: Never misuse or abuse your prized possessions or attributes.

yoruba: Ìbọ́n dídá olówó ló ní kíwọ̀fà rín rín rín kó sọ àdá nù.
english_literal: It is the master's engaging in silly antics that affords the pawn the opportunity to laugh so hard that he tosses his cutlass away.
interpretation_gold: If the person in charge behaves irresponsibly, then those over whom he/she has charge have an excuse for irresponsible behavior also.

yoruba: Ìjàlọ ò lè gbé òkúta.
english_literal: The brown ant cannot lift a boulder.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt a task that is beyond one's capability.

yoruba: Ìwọ̀n eku nìwọ̀n ìtẹ́; olongo kì í gbé tìmùtìmù.
english_literal: The measure of the rat is the measure of the nest; a robin does not live on a cushion.
interpretation_gold: One should cut one's garment according to one's size.

yoruba: Irú aṣọ ò tán nínu àṣà.
english_literal: The likeness of a particular type of cloth is not lacking among those in fashion.
interpretation_gold: No one has a monopoly of certain qualities.

yoruba: Iná ńjó ògiri ò sá, ó wá ńgbá gẹẹrẹ gẹẹrẹ sómi.
english_literal: Fire burns and the wall does not run from it; now it moves threateningly towards water.
interpretation_gold: A person who is powerless against others should not make threatening moves.

yoruba: Ihò wo lèkúté ńgbé tó ní iṣẹ́ ilé ńdíwọ́?
english_literal: What sort of hole does the rat live in that makes him say that household work preoccupied it?
interpretation_gold: One should not oversell oneself.

yoruba: Idà ahun la fi ńpa ahun.
english_literal: It is with its own sword that one kills the tortoise.
interpretation_gold: Each person carries his/her own bane around with him/her.

yoruba: ba ilé àgbà jẹ́.
english_literal: Trading insults brings ruin to an elder's home.
interpretation_gold: An elder who fails to maintain harmony among the members of his household will see it destroyed.

yoruba: Ilé kì í jó kí oorun kun ojú.
english_literal: A house does not burn and fill the eyes with sleep.
interpretation_gold: One must not ignore grave matters.

yoruba: Ibi tí a ti mú ọ̀lẹ ò kúnná; ibi tí a ti mú alágbáraá tó oko-ó ro.
english_literal: The place where a lazy person was apprehended bears no marks; the place where a powerful man was apprehended is broad enough to plant a farm.
interpretation_gold: A worthy person, even if eventually vanquished, will leave signs of powerful resistance behind.

yoruba: Ilè-ni-mo-wà kì í jẹ̀bi ẹjọ́.
english_literal: “I-was-in-my-home” is never the guilty party in a dispute.
interpretation_gold: One does not get into trouble by minding one's own business.

yoruba: Ìjokòó ẹni ní ḿmúni da ewé ẹ̀kọ nù.
english_literal: How one sits causes one to carry the leaves used to wrap corn-meal to the dump.
interpretation_gold: People treat one the way one presents oneself.

yoruba: Ìṣẹ̀ ò ti ibìkan mú ẹni; ìyà ò tibìkan jẹ èèyàn; bí o bá rìnrìn òṣì, bí o bá ojú ìṣẹ́ wọ̀lú, igbá-kúgbá ni wọn ó fi bu omi fún ẹ mu.
english_literal: Destitution does not attach to one at a particular place; suffering does not attack a person at a particular place; if one walks like a wretch into a town, if one looks like a loser when one enters a town, it is with a miserable calabash that the people will offer one water to drink.
interpretation_gold: People treat one the way one presents oneself.

yoruba: Ìgbà tí ṣìgìdìí bá fẹ́ ṣe eré ẹ̀tẹ́ a ní kí wọ́n gbé òun sójò.
english_literal: When the clay statue hankers for disgrace it asks to be placed in the rain.
interpretation_gold: A person who so forgets himself/herself and overreaches himself/herself will wind up in disgrace.

yoruba: Inú burúkú làgbà ńní, àgbà kì í ní ojú burúkú.
english_literal: An unpleasant inside is what a venerable elder should have; a venerable elder should not have an unpleasant mien.
interpretation_gold: One should not permit the way one really feels to push one into unseemly behavior.

yoruba: Ipa ọgbẹ́ ní ńsàn; ipa ohùn kì í sàn.
english_literal: The wound left by a cutlass may heal, but the wound left by speech does not heal.
interpretation_gold: Injury inflicted through speech is impossible to heal.

yoruba: Igúnnugún bà lé òrùlé; ojú tó ilé ó tó oko.
english_literal: The vulture perches on the roof; its eyes see the homestead as well as the farm.
interpretation_gold: Said of a busybody whose eyes get into everything.

yoruba: Ìdí méjèèjìí tó olúwa rẹ̀-ẹ́ jókòó.
english_literal: The two buttocks are sufficient for their owner to sit on.
interpretation_gold: One should be satisfied with one's own resources.

yoruba: Ìpàkọ́ onípàkọ́ là ńrí; eniẹlẹ́ni ní ńrí tẹni.
english_literal: One sees only other peoples' occiputs; only others can see one's own.
interpretation_gold: One usually pays closer attention to other people's faults than to one's own, while others are quite aware of one's faults.

yoruba: Ibi tí a pè lórí ní ńhurun.
english_literal: The part one names the head is the one that grows hair.
interpretation_gold: One should act in accordance to one's station.

yoruba: Ìbàjẹ́ ọjọ́ kan ò tán bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: The disgrace one incurs in one day does not disappear that soon.
interpretation_gold: Reputations are easy to destroy but most difficult to repair.

yoruba: Ibi tí a fi iyọ̀ sí ló ńṣomi sí.
english_literal: Salt dampens only the place where it is placed.
interpretation_gold: One should confine one's activities to the proper arena.

yoruba: Ilé kì í jó kí baálé ilé tàkakà.
english_literal: A house does not burn while the landlord lounges with indifference.
interpretation_gold: One must not ignore matters of grave concern to one.

yoruba: Idà ńwó ilé ara ẹ̀ ó ní òún ḿba àkọ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: The sword is destroying its own home, and it says it is ruining the scabbard.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person whose actions will eventually recoil on him/her, even though the person thinks that he/she is hurting others.

yoruba: Ìgbà wo ni Mákùú ò níí kú? Mákùú ò mọ awo ó ḿbú ọpa; Mákùú ò mọ ìwẹ̀ ó ḿbọ́ sódò.
english_literal: When will (or how can) Maku avoid the danger of dying? Maku does not know the mysteries of the cult yet he joins in its vows; Maku does not know how to swim and yet he jumps into the river.
interpretation_gold: A person who will not cooperate in safeguarding himself/herself frustrates the efforts of others.

yoruba: Ìjọba ńpè ọ́ o ní ò ḿmu gààrí lọ́wọ́; ta ní ni ọ́, ta ní ni omi tí o fi ḿmu gààrí?
english_literal: The government summons you and you say you are busy eating cassava grains soaked in water; who owns you, and who owns the water with which you are eating the cassava?
interpretation_gold: When the law summons, one has no option but to heed the summon.

yoruba: The likeness of an elephant is not scarce in Alọ.
interpretation_gold: Nobody is one of a kind.

yoruba: Ibi tí a ti ńpìtàn ká tó jogún, ká mọ̀ pé ogún ibẹ̀ ò kanni.
english_literal: Where one must recite genealogies in order to establish one's claim to inheritance, one should know that one really has no claim to patrimony there.
interpretation_gold: One need not go to great lengths to establish one's claim if it is legitimate.

yoruba: Ìpéǹpéjú ò ní enini; àgbàlagbà irùngbọ̀n ò ṣe òlòó.
english_literal: The eyelashes do not make dew; a venerable old beard does not behave like an ingenue.
interpretation_gold: Some habits are fitting for one's station, while others are not.

yoruba: Ìsáǹsá ò yọ ẹ̀gún; ìsáǹsá kì í káwo ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: The fugitive does not stop to pull a thorn “from his/her feet”; the fugitive does not stop to clear dinner dishes.
interpretation_gold: A person who has committed a crime would not wait around to be caught.

yoruba: Ibi tí ayé bá ẹni ni a ti ńjẹ ẹ̀.
english_literal: Where life catches up with one, there one lives it.
interpretation_gold: One lives according to the conditions one finds oneself in.

yoruba: Ìwà ní ńjọ oníwà lójú.
english_literal: Character is always remarkable (or good) in the opinion of its owner.
interpretation_gold: One naturally approves of one's own character.

yoruba: Ibi tí a fi ara sí lara ńgbé.
english_literal: Wherever one situates the body, there it inhabits.
interpretation_gold: One should confine oneself and one's activities to the appropriate spheres.

yoruba: Ìwọ̀fà ní ḿmú ìwọ̀fà jó.
english_literal: A pawned person always dances with a pawned person.
interpretation_gold: People should know who share their station and confine their dealings with them.

yoruba: Ìrẹ́jẹ ò sí nínúu fọ́tò; bí o bá ṣe jókòó ni o ó bàá ara-à rẹ.
english_literal: There is no cheating in photography; it is just as you sit that you will find your image.
interpretation_gold: One's public perception depends ultimately on one's self-presentation.

yoruba: Ìjàkùmọ̀ kì í rin ọ̀sán, ẹni a bí ire kì í rin òru.
english_literal: The wild cat never roams in daylight; a well-bred person does not wander around in the night time.
interpretation_gold: People who care about their reputation should stay away from questionable actions.

yoruba: Jẹ́jẹ́ leégún àgbà ńjó.
english_literal: Sedately is the way an elderly masquerader dances.
interpretation_gold: Grown-up people should behave in a decorous manner.

yoruba: Kò rà, kò lówó lọ́wọ́, ó ńwú tutu níwájú onítumpulu.
english_literal: He does not buy, he has no money, yet he sits sulkily before the seller of bean fritters.
interpretation_gold: Said of people reluctant to accept the fact that they cannot have what they wish.

yoruba: Kékeré lọ̀pọ̀lọ́ fi ga ju ilẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: The toad is only slightly taller than the earth.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who behave as though they are superior to others while they have little reason to believe so.

yoruba: Kò sí ẹni tó dùn mọ́ àfi orí ẹni.
english_literal: There is no one pleased “by one's success” except one's head.
interpretation_gold: Few people genuinely wish that one should succeed.

yoruba: Kí ni orí ńṣe tí èjìká ò lè ṣe? Èjìká ru ẹrù ó gba ọ̀ọ́dúnrún; orí ta tiẹ̀ ní ogúnlúgba.
english_literal: What can the head do that the shoulder cannot do? The shoulder carried a load and earned three hundred cowries; the head sold its own for two hundred and twenty cowries.
interpretation_gold: If a person has more power and standing than one, one should not be foolish enough to think the person cannot accomplish what one has accomplished.

yoruba: Kí ni ó yá àpọ́n lórí tó fiṣu síná tó ńsúfèé pé “bí a ti ńṣe ni inú ḿbí wọn”?
english_literal: What has the bachelor to feel superior about, such that while he is roasting yams he is whistling the song, “What one does fills them with jealousy”?
interpretation_gold: Said of people who are arrogant even though they have no basis for pride.

yoruba: Ká wí ogún, ká wí ọgbọ̀n, “Ng ò fẹ́, ng ò gbà” laṣiwèré fi ńpẹ̀kun ọ̀ràn.
english_literal: Whether one speaks twenty times or speaks thirty times, “I do not like it, and I will not accept it” is how the imbecile ends the discussion.
interpretation_gold: The incorrigible person will never listen to reason.

yoruba: Ká ríni sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ò dàbí-i ká sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ká gbà.
english_literal: Having people to advise one is nothing like knowing how to take advice.
interpretation_gold: Nobody can help anyone who will not help himself or herself.

yoruba: Ká ríni lóde ò dàbí-i ká báni délé.
english_literal: To see a person in the streets is not the same as going home with the person.
interpretation_gold: To really know a person one must see the person where he/she lives.

yoruba: Kò-sí-nílé kì í jagun ẹnu tì.
english_literal: He-was-not-at-home never fails to prove his valor with his mouth.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who vows that had he been around when something happened he would have performed wonders.

yoruba: Ká wí fún ẹni ká gbọ́; ká sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ká gbà; kà bèrè ọnà lọ́wọ́ èrò tó kù lẹ́hìn kàyè baà lè yẹni.
english_literal: If one is spoken to one should listen; if one is advised one should heed the advice; one should seek direction from straggling wayfarers in order than one's life might be pleasant.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to heed advice, and it is wise to seek direction from those who have greater experience than one does.

yoruba: Ká wí ká gbà ló yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
english_literal: To heed advice is what best becomes a human being.
interpretation_gold: One should heed advice.

yoruba: Kàkà kí àgbò ké, àgbò a kú.
english_literal: Rather than cry out, the ram will die.
interpretation_gold: A grown man must know how to hide his pain.

yoruba: Kí ni apárí ńwá ní ìsọ̀ onígbàjámọ̀?
english_literal: What does a bald man want in the stall of the barber?
interpretation_gold: One should stay out of places where one has no business.

yoruba: Kí ni ìbá mú igún dé ọ̀dọ̀-ọ onídìrí?
english_literal: What would take the vulture to the stall of the hair dresser?
interpretation_gold: One should stay away from places where one has no business.

yoruba: Kàkà ká dọ̀bálẹ̀ fún Gàm̀bàrí, ká rọ́jú ká kú.
english_literal: Rather than prostrate oneself in homage or obeisance to a Hausa person, one should rather die.
interpretation_gold: An expression of Yoruba superciliousness towards the Hausa.

yoruba: Kàkà kí iga akàn ó padà sẹhìn, a kán.
english_literal: Rather than bend backwards, the crab's claws will break.
interpretation_gold: Death is to be preferred to retreat.

yoruba: Kí ni onígbá ńṣe tí aláwo ò lè ṣe?
english_literal: What is the calabash owner doing that the china plate owner cannot do?
interpretation_gold: Whatever one can accomplish, those better placed or better endowed than one can accomplish also.

yoruba: Kíjìpá laṣọ ọ̀lẹ; òfì laṣọ àgbà; àgbà tí ò ní tòfì a rọ́jú ra kíjìpá.
english_literal: Durable hand-woven cloth is the material for shiftless people; loom-woven cloth is the material for the elders; whichever elder cannot afford loom-woven cloth should strive for durable hand-woven cloth.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot have the perfect thing, one should strive to have at least something.

yoruba: Kí ni àǹfàníi kẹ̀tẹ̀kẹ̀tẹ̀ lára kẹ́tẹ́kẹ́tẹ́ à-gùn-fẹsẹ̀-wọ́lẹ̀?
english_literal: What is the point of bragging on account of an ass which when one rides on it one's feet drag on the ground?
interpretation_gold: It is pointless to make too much of a virtually worthless thing.

yoruba: Kò sí mi lájọ àjọ ò kún: ara ẹ̀ ló tàn jẹ.
english_literal: Without-me-in-an-assembly-the-assembly-is-not-complete deceives only himself/herself.
interpretation_gold: Whoever thinks he or she is indispensable is self-deceived.

yoruba: Kí ẹrú mọ ara ẹ̀ lẹ́rú; kí ìwọ̀fà mọ ara ẹ̀ níwọ̀fà; kí ọmọlúwàbí mọ ara ẹ̀ lẹ́rú Ọlọ́run ọba.
english_literal: Let the slave know him/herself as a slave; let the pawn know him/herself as a pawn; let the well born person know him/herself as the child of God.
interpretation_gold: Everybody should know himself/herself and his/her station in the scheme of things.

yoruba: Kó-tán-kó-tán lajá ńlá omi.
