english_literal: Swiftly-consumed-swiftly-consumed is the way a dog laps up water.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who attack good things with excessive greed.

yoruba: Ká wí fúnni ká gbọ́; ká sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ká gbà; à-wí-ìgbọ́, à-gbọ́-ìgbà ní ńfi igbá àdánù bu omi mu.
english_literal: If one is spoken to one should listen; if one is advised one should accept the advice; refusal to listen to speech and refusal to accept advice leads to using the calabash of deprivation as a drinking cup.
interpretation_gold: Refusal to heed advise leads to deprivation.

yoruba: Kàkà kí bàbá ran ọmọ ní àdá bọ oko, oníkálukú a gbé tiẹ̀.
english_literal: Rather than the father carrying the son's cutlass home from the farm, each will carry his own.
interpretation_gold: People may withhold their respect from one, but one should not abet their insolence.

yoruba: Kì í dọwọ́-ọ baba kó ló di ọwọ́ ọmọ.
english_literal: Responsibility does not devolve on the father only for him to say it is his son's duty.
interpretation_gold: An elder must do his/her duty and not shove it on the youth.

yoruba: Kí ni wọ́n ti ńṣe Àmọ́dù nÍlọrin? Ewúrẹ́ ńjẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
english_literal: What use do the people of Ilorin have for Ahmadu? Even goats are so named.
interpretation_gold: Said to express the overabundance of some commodity being discussed.

yoruba: Kàkà kí kìnìún ṣe akápò ẹkùn, ọlọ́dẹ a mú ọdẹ ẹ̀ ṣe.
english_literal: Rather than the lion serving as carrier for the leopard, each will hunt separately.
interpretation_gold: One would rather leave a company that remain in it and be subordinate to those one considers inferior.

yoruba: Labalábá fi ara ẹ̀ wẹ́yẹ, kò lè ṣe ìṣe ẹyẹ.
english_literal: The butterfly likens itself to a bird, but it cannot do what a bird can do.
interpretation_gold: Attempts to emulate those better endowed and qualified than oneself always prove futile.

yoruba: Lékèélékèé ò yé ẹyin dúdú; funfun ni wọ́n ńyé ẹyin wọn.
english_literal: Cattle egrets never lay black eggs; only white eggs do they lay.
interpretation_gold: Only certain types of behavior are suitable for people in certain positions.

yoruba: fara wé àgbàdo.
english_literal: Ash mixed with water likens itself to indigo dye, but it cannot do what the dye can do; the large red bean likens itself to corn.
interpretation_gold: One should know better than to attempt to overreach one's capabilities.

yoruba: Lágbájá ìbá wà a di ìjímèrè; ẹni tó bá níwájú di oloyo?
english_literal: Were So-and-So alive he would transform himself into a brown monkey; did the person who preceded him ever transform himself into any kind of monkey?
interpretation_gold: One should not make excessive claims when there is no basis for them.

yoruba: One does not wear ẹtù
interpretation_gold: Not every person is made for greatness.

yoruba: Láká-ǹláká ò ṣéé fi làjà; ọmọ eégún ò ṣéé gbé ṣeré.
english_literal: A limp is no great asset for a person wishing to stop a fight; a masquerader's child is no easy playmate.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limits and also what one would be ill advised to attempt.

yoruba: Mélòó lÈjìgbò tí ọ̀kan ẹ̀ ńjẹ́ Ayé-gbogbo?
english_literal: How large a community is Ejigbo that one of its settlements is named Ayegbogbo “The whole world”?
interpretation_gold: One should be modest in one's claims.

yoruba: “Mo yó” ńjẹ́ “mo yó,” “mo kọ̀” ńjẹ́ “mo kọ̀”; jẹun ǹṣó, àgbà ọ̀kánjúwà ni.
english_literal: “I am full” means “I am full”; “I decline” means “I decline”; eating with abandon, that is the father of all greediness.
interpretation_gold: One should not accept every invitation to the table.

yoruba: Mo dàgbà tán èwé wù mí.
english_literal: Having grown old I miss youthfulness.
interpretation_gold: One does not appreciate one's youth until one has lost it.

yoruba: Mànàmáná ò ṣéé sun iṣu.
english_literal: Lightning is no good for roasting yams.
interpretation_gold: Many instances of boasting lack the substance to back them.

yoruba: “Mo mọ̀-ọ́ gùn” lẹṣin ńdà.
english_literal: “I am an expert horseman” is usually the one thrown by a horse.
interpretation_gold: Assuming that one knows it all it causes one grief.

yoruba: Má tẹ̀ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ oníle, má tẹ̀ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àlejò; lọ́wọ́ ara ẹni la ti ńtẹ́.
english_literal: Save face with members of your household and save face with complete strangers, such a person loses face with himself/herself.
interpretation_gold: A person too careful about his/her reputation will end up losing regard for himself/herself. Some situations call for doing away with decorum.

yoruba: “Mo mọ̀wọ̀n ara-à mi” kì í ṣẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ èébú.
english_literal: “I am jealous of my dignity” does not hurl insults at others.
interpretation_gold: A person who wishes to maintain his dignity must not by his/her actions invite insults.

yoruba: Mo dàgbà mo dàgó, aré ọmọdé ò tán lójúù mi.
english_literal: I have become old and wise, but childish play has not ceased to appeal to me.
interpretation_gold: There is something of the youth that lingers even in age.

yoruba: “Mo gbọ́n tán, mo mọ̀ràn tán” kì í jẹ́ kí agbọ́n lóró bí oyin.
english_literal: “I am all-wise, I am all-knowing” kept the wasp from having as much venom as the bee.
interpretation_gold: Whoever will not listen to instruction will learn nothing.

yoruba: Màlúù ò lè lérí níwájú ẹṣin.
english_literal: A cow may not boast in the presence of a horse.
interpretation_gold: One should acknowledge and defer to those better able than oneself.

yoruba: “Mo mọ̀-ọ́ gún, mo mọ̀-ọ́ tẹ̀” niyán ewùrà-á fi ńlẹ́mọ.
english_literal: “I know how to pound and I know how to marsh” is what causes pounded yam made with wateryam to be lumpy.
interpretation_gold: Knowing it all can be disastrous.

yoruba: “Mo dára, mo dára,” àìdára ní ńpẹ̀kun ẹ̀.
english_literal: “I am beautiful, I am beautiful!” has ugliness as its conclusion.
interpretation_gold: Whoever is infatuated with his or her attractiveness will end up being despised by all.

yoruba: N:láńlá lọmọ abuké ńdá: ó ní “Ìyá, ìyá, òun ó pọ̀n.”
english_literal: The humpback's child has presented a formidable dilemma: he cries, “Mother, mother, carry me on your back!”
interpretation_gold: A dependent who demands of one what one cannot provide is intent on showing one up.

yoruba: Nígbàwo làpò ẹkùn-ún di ìkálá fọ́mọdé?
english_literal: Since when did a tiger-hide sac become a thing a child uses to harvest okro?
interpretation_gold: People should not presume to lay claim to things or functions that are far beyond their station.

yoruba: “Ng óò gba owó-ò mi lára ṣòkòtò yìí”; ìdí làgbàlagbà ńṣí sílẹ̀.
english_literal: “I will get my money's worth out of these trousers”; the grown man only winds up exposing his bare buttocks to the world.
interpretation_gold: One should not insist on squeezing every last once of use out of a perishable article.

yoruba: Nígbàtí à ńto ọkà a ò to ti ẹmọ́ si.
english_literal: When we were stacking the corn we did not stack some for the brown rat.
interpretation_gold: People should keep their hands off other people's property unless they have been asked to help themselves.

yoruba: Nígbàtí o mọ̀-ọ́ gùn, ẹṣin ẹ-ẹ́ ṣe ṣẹ́ orókún?
english_literal: Since you claim to be a seasoned rider, how come your horse has gone lame?
interpretation_gold: An expert does not produce flawed goods.

yoruba: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó dínwó aró, kò yẹ atọ̀ọ́lé.
english_literal: It is fitting for everybody to bargain to reduce the cost of dyeing clothes, but not the bed wetter.
interpretation_gold: The person in desperate need of a thing cannot afford to be finicky.

yoruba: Olóbìnrin kan kì í pagbo ìja.
english_literal: A person who has only  one wife does not form a circle for a fight.
interpretation_gold: A person who does not have enough helping hands should not embark on ventures that are too ambitious.

yoruba: Ohun tí eèrá bá lè gbé ní ńpè ní ìgànnìkó.
english_literal: Whatever the ant is able to carry is what it says is its full measure.
interpretation_gold: One should match one's desires to what one can afford.

yoruba: Ó bọ́ lọ́wọ́ iyọ̀ ó dòbu.
english_literal: Salt loses its good quality and becomes like saltpeter.
interpretation_gold: A person who has been written off loses all regard.

yoruba: O dájú dánu, o ò mọ ẹ̀sán mẹ́sàn-án.
english_literal: Your eyes flinch not and your mouth is unstoppable, but you do not know nine times nine.
interpretation_gold: Too much mouth often indicates too little substance.

yoruba: Olówó ní ḿbá ọlọ́rọ̀-ọ́ rìn; ẹgbẹ́ ní ḿbá ẹgbẹ́ ṣeré.
english_literal: It is a rich person that keeps company with a wealthy person; only people of equal standing play together.
interpretation_gold: One should associate with one's equals.

yoruba: Ohun tí wèré fi ńse ara ẹ̀, ó pọ̀ ju ohun tó fi ńṣẹ ọmọ ẹlòmíràn lọ.
english_literal: What the imbecile does to himself is far worse than what he does to others.
interpretation_gold: Said what a person intending to injure others in fact does himself or herself greater injury.

yoruba: Oúnjẹ ọmọ kékeré a máa wọ àgbà nínú; òrùka ọmọ kékeré ni kì í wọ ágbá lọ́wọ́.
english_literal: A youth's food can enter the stomach of an elder; it is only a youth's ring that cannot slip unto an elder's finger.
interpretation_gold: An elder may take advantage of the youth in certain respects, but in some others an elder must respect his status.

yoruba: Ó bọ́ lọ́wọ́ oṣù ó dàràn-mọ́jú.
english_literal: The moon loses its esteem and shines all night long.
interpretation_gold: A person who overstays his/her welcome ceases to be valued.

yoruba: Ohun méjì ló yẹ Ẹ̀ṣọ́: Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà, ó lé ogun; Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà ó kú sógun.
english_literal: Only two things are proper for a warrior: the warrior goes to war and drives the enemy off; the warrior goes to war and dies in battle.
interpretation_gold: One should not act in a way that is not proper or becoming.

yoruba: Olójúkan kì í tàkìtì òró.
english_literal: A one-eyed person does not attempt standing somersaults.
interpretation_gold: One should limit one's ambition to one's capability.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fàbúrò ẹni ṣaya.
english_literal: One should not become so desperate that one takes one's younger sister as wife.
interpretation_gold: Desperation should not preempt propriety.

yoruba: Olówó ní ńjẹ iyán ẹgbàá.
english_literal: It is a rich person that eats pounded yams worth two thousand cowries.
interpretation_gold: One's level of consumption is a reflection of the depth of one's pocket.

yoruba: O kò mọ ẹ̀wà lóńjẹ à-jẹ-sùn.
english_literal: You do not know what black eyed peas are like for dinner.
interpretation_gold: Addressed to a person who is not mindful of the repercussions of his/her behavior.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká pọ́n léhín.
english_literal: One's circumstances do not so deteriorate that one becomes red in teeth.
interpretation_gold: Adverse circumstances should not keep one from attending to essential matters.

yoruba: Ohun tó yẹni ló yẹni; okùn ọrùn ò yẹ adìẹ.
english_literal: Whatever is becoming for a person is what is becoming; a noose is not becoming for a chicken.
interpretation_gold: One should always confine one's actions to those that are proper and becoming.

yoruba: Owó ẹ̀yẹ ò sú ẹni-í san; tọ̀ràn ni ò súnwọ̀n.
english_literal: People have no difficulty paying the money for glorious events; it is the money for trouble that is unpleasant to pay.
interpretation_gold: The trouble one goes into for honorable purposes are really a pleasure, not so the trouble to extricate oneself from problems.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọnni ká fàkísà bora.
english_literal: One should never be so benighted that one covers oneself in rags.
interpretation_gold: Despite adverse circumstances, one should strive to maintain one's dignity.

yoruba: Ojú iná kọ́ lewùrà ńhurun.
english_literal: It is not in the presence of the flame that water-yam grows hair.
interpretation_gold: One dares not strut when one's bane is around.

yoruba: Olóyè kékeré kì í ṣe fáàárí níwájú ọba.
english_literal: A minor chief should not act garrulously in the presence of a king.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's station and act accordingly.

yoruba: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó sọ pé “Ọlọ́run a-ṣèkan-má-kù,” kò yẹ akúkó.
english_literal: Everyone can justifiably say, “God, who has left nothing undone,” but not a eunuch.
interpretation_gold: People should not act as though they are unaware of their flaws.

yoruba: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; onílẹ̀kẹ̀ ìbá gbowo, ko rọ́rùn fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ so.
english_literal: The person with goitre offers a ridiculously low price for beads; were the beads seller to accept her offer she would have no neck to string the beads around.
interpretation_gold: One can always find a ruse to get one out of embarrassing situations.

yoruba: Ò ńjàgbọ̀nrín èṣín lọ́bẹ̀, o ní o ti tó tán.
english_literal: You are reduced to eating last year's antelope in your stew, and yet you claim to have attained the height of good fortune.
interpretation_gold: A hard-up person who claims to be prosperous deceives him/herself.

yoruba: Olómele kì í sọ pé igi yó dàá lóde lọ́la.
english_literal: The omele drummer does not vow that there will be an earth-shaking performance on the morrow.
interpretation_gold: If one has no say, one should avoid making projections or promises.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́n baálé ilé kó fọwọ́ gbálẹ̀ ilé ẹ̀.
english_literal: A head of a household is never so hard up that he sweeps his compound with his bare hands.
interpretation_gold: However desperate one might be, there are certain things one must not stoop to do.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́n ẹdun kó dẹni ilẹ̀; ìṣẹ́ kì í ṣẹ́ igún kó di ojúgbà adìẹ.
english_literal: The colobus monkey is never so reduced in circumstances that it becomes a land-hugging creature; the vulture is never so badly off that it becomes the equal of a chicken.
interpretation_gold: No matter one's misfortune one should maintain one's dignity.

yoruba: “Òru ò molówó” nIfá tí à ńdá fún “Ìwọ ta nìyẹn?”
english_literal: “The dark of night knows not who is a wealthy person” is the oracle one delivers to “Who might that be?”
interpretation_gold: Night-time wanderers should be prepared for indignities.

yoruba: Òkété pẹ̀lú ọmọ ẹ̀-ẹ́ di ọgbọọgba sínú ihò; nígba tí ìyá ńfehín pàkùrọ́, ọmọ náà ńfehín pa pẹ̀lú.
english_literal: The giant bush rat and its child become equals in their hole; the mother cracks palm-nuts with its teeth, and the child does the same thing.
interpretation_gold: Too much familiarity makes comrades of people who are quite distant from each other in standing.

yoruba: Odò kékeré lalákàn-án ti lè fọ́ epo; bó bá di àgàdàm̀gbá tán, odò a gbé alákàn lọ.
english_literal: It is only in a small stream that the crab can make its oil; when it becomes huge and swift the river sweeps the crab away.
interpretation_gold: When times are easy there is little one cannot attempt.

yoruba: Ojú ò ti oníṣègùn, ó ní àna òun ńkú lọ.
english_literal: The medicine man lacks all shame, he announces that his parent-in-law is dying.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot do what is expected of one, one should at least not broadcast one's shame.

yoruba: Orí awọ là ḿbágbà.
english_literal: It is on the hide that one finds the elder.
interpretation_gold: One should always live up to what others expect of one.

yoruba: Orí àgbà-á níyì, ó sàn ju orí àgbà-á fọ́ lọ.
english_literal: The-elderly-person's-head-deserves-respect is better than The-elderly-person's-head-is-damaged.
interpretation_gold: An elder who enjoys respect is better off than one who is insulted by others.

yoruba: O ru ládugbó ò ńrerá; kí ni ká sọ fẹ́ni tó ru Òrìṣà-a Yemọja?
english_literal: Because you are carrying a huge pot you strut; what would one say to the person carrying the divinity Yemoja?
interpretation_gold: Never assume to be more important than you are, especially when there are really more important people around.

yoruba: Òní, ẹtú jìnfìn, ọ̀la, ẹtú jìnfìn; ẹtu nìkan lẹran tó wà nígbó?
english_literal: Today, the antelope falls into the ditch; tomorrow, the antelope falls into the ditch; is the antelope the only animal in the forest?
interpretation_gold: If a person is the only one misfortune always visits, there is probably something the person is doing to invite it.

yoruba: Ogun tí olójúméjìí rí sá ni olójúkan-án ní òún ńlọ jà.
english_literal: The war that the two-eyed person saw and fled is the same the one-eyed person vows he will join.
interpretation_gold: A comment on overreaching people who attempt feats that have defeated their betters.

yoruba: Ohun tí kò tó okòó kì í jẹ àgbà níyà.
english_literal: A thing that is not worth the least amount of money should not prove a hardship for an elder.
interpretation_gold: One should not be defeated by insignificant problems.

yoruba: Ojú àlejò la ti ńjẹ gbèsè; ẹ̀hìn-in ẹ̀ là ńsan án.
english_literal: It is in a visitor's presence that one gets into debt; it is in her absence that one repays the debt.
interpretation_gold: One does not estimate how much hospitality is costing one until the visitor has departed.

yoruba: Orogún ìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dáṣọ fún ọ o ní kò balẹ̀; mélòó nìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dá fún ọ tó fi kú?
english_literal: Your mother's co-wife made a garment for you and you complain that it is not long enough; how many did your mother make for you before she died?
interpretation_gold: People dependent on charity should rather be grateful than difficult to please.

yoruba: Oǹpè ní ńfa ọlá; òjípè kì í fa ọlá.
english_literal: It is the person who does the summoning that assumes airs; the person subject to summons does not assume airs.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's place, especially in the company of more illustrious people.

yoruba: Ó di ọjọ́ alẹ́ kábuké tó mọ̀ pé iké kì í ṣọmọ.
english_literal: It will not be until the end of days before the humpback realizes that a hump is not a child.
interpretation_gold: People seldom learn wisdom until it is too late.

yoruba: Ojú baba ara; awọ́n bí ojú; aṣòró dà bí àgbà.
english_literal: The eye, father of the body; nothing is as valuable as the eye; nothing is as difficult to achieve as the status of elder.
interpretation_gold: The status of elder is most precious, and most difficult to achieve.

yoruba: Onífunra àlejò tí ńtètè ṣe onílé pẹ̀lẹ́.
english_literal: The excessively attentive visitor “who” extends hospitality greetings to the host.
interpretation_gold: One should not assume other people's functions.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́n òkú ọ̀run kó ní kí ará ayé gba òun.
english_literal: A dead person cannot be so desperate as to appeal to a living person for deliverance.
interpretation_gold: However bad one's circumstances might be, one should use good sense in determining where one can turn for help.

yoruba: Òtòlò-ó jẹ, òtòlò-ó mu, òtòlò-ó fẹsẹ̀ wé ẹsẹ̀ erin.
english_literal: The water-buck ate, the water-buck drank, the water-buck compared its limbs to an elephant's.
interpretation_gold: Satiation leads to excess.

yoruba: Ohun tí à ńtà là ńjẹ; kì í ṣe ọ̀rọ̀ oní-kẹrosíìnì.
english_literal: What one sells is what one eats; that does not apply to the kerosene seller.
interpretation_gold: One should be mindful of the peculiarities of one's situation.

yoruba: Oníbàjẹ́ ò mọra; oníbàjẹ́ ńlọ sóko olè ó mú obìnrin lọ; ọkọ́ kó akọṣu, ìyàwó kó ewùrà.
english_literal: The shameless person does not know what is fitting; the shameless person is off to raid a farm, and he takes his wife along; the husband steals staple yams, the wife steals wateryams.
interpretation_gold: A man who involves his family in his questionable ventures has sunk to the lowest depths.

yoruba: Oòrùn, kó tìẹ wọ̀ ká má bàá Ọlọ́jọ́ wí.
english_literal: Sun, go set so one does not blame the owner of the day.
interpretation_gold: Subordinates should not behave in a manner that would bring their superior to disrepute.

yoruba: Olówó jẹun jẹ́jẹ́; òtòṣì jẹun tìpà-tìjàn; òtòṣì tí ḿbá ọlọ́rọ̀ rìn, akọ ojú ló ńyá.
english_literal: The rich man eats slowly and at leisure; the poor person eats fast and with anxiety; the poor man who keeps company with a wealthy man is exceeding his station.
interpretation_gold: One should keep to comrades whose station is similar to one's.

yoruba: Pẹ̀lẹ́ larẹwà ńrìn; jẹ́jẹ́ lọmọ ọlọ́jà ńyan.
interpretation_gold: Gently and carefully is the best manner to take life.

yoruba: Pátápátá alágbẹ̀dẹ ò ju ilé àrọ lọ.
english_literal: The most one can expect of the blacksmith is confined to the smithy.
interpretation_gold: There is a limit to a person's bragging.

yoruba: Pamí-nkú obìnrín ṣorí bẹmbẹ sọ́kọ.
english_literal: A masochistic woman hardens her head against her husband.
interpretation_gold: Obstinacy only invites harsh punishment.

yoruba: Pẹ̀lẹ́-pẹ̀lẹ́ nijó àgbà; ara gbogbo ló di àkísà tán.
english_literal: An elderly person's manner of dancing must be very gentle, because the whole body has become worn to a rag.
interpretation_gold: Elderly people should not over-exert themselves.

yoruba: San là ńrìn; ajé ní ḿmúni pá kọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: Straight and upright is the way one would walk; it is money that forces one to sneak about.
interpretation_gold: When one is in debt, one's freedom of movement is compromised.

yoruba: Sesere ńdá gọ́ọ́bú; oníkamẹ́sàn-án ńgbé ṣíbí.
english_literal: The insignificant thing is attempting an earth-shaking feat; the person with only nine fingers is lifting a spoon.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person overreaching.

yoruba: Sún mọ ọ̀hún, sún mọ́ ìhín! Bí a bá kan ògiri ilé-e baba ẹni, ṣe là ńdúró gbọin-gbọin.
english_literal: Move away, move over here! When one moves until one is against the walls of one's father's house, one stands steadfast.
interpretation_gold: There must be a limit to how much one will back down before enemies.

yoruba: Ta ní ńjẹun tájá ńjùrù?
english_literal: At whose dinner table is the dog wagging its tail?
interpretation_gold: Said to tell off people who make their presence felt when they should rather make themselves scarce.

yoruba: Ta ní ńjájá ní mọ́ṣáláṣí?
english_literal: What would a dog be doing in a mosque?
interpretation_gold: Said to tell off people who are not wanted in a company.

yoruba: Tòlótòló mọ ẹni tó ńyìnbọn ìdí sí.
english_literal: The turkey knows towards whom it farts.
interpretation_gold: People must be careful how to choose the people they presume to approach with familiarity.

yoruba: Tẹ̀tẹ̀ kì í tẹ́.
english_literal: Spinach is never disgraced.
interpretation_gold: May one never know disgrace.

yoruba: “Ta ní ḿbẹ níbẹ̀?” làgbẹ́ fi ńsán ìbàǹtẹ́ wọ̀lú.
english_literal: “Who is there whose opinion matters?” is the attitude that makes the farmer come into town dressed only in a loin cloth.
interpretation_gold: People who make a spectacle of themselves show no regard for others.

yoruba: Wọ́n ńpe gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nà ẹyẹ àkókó ńyọjú.
english_literal: The call goes out for a carpenter and the woodpecker presents itself.
interpretation_gold: One should not think too much of one's capabilities.

yoruba: Wèrè èèyàn ní ńwípé irú òun ò sí; irú ẹ̀ẹ́ pọ̀ ó ju ẹgbàágbèje lọ.
english_literal: Only an imbecile asserts that there is none like him or her; his or her likes are numerous, numbering more than millions.
interpretation_gold: No one is incomparable.

yoruba: “Yan àkàrà fún mi wá ká jìjọ jẹ ẹ́”: àìtó èèyàn-án rán níṣẹ́ ní ńjẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
english_literal: “Go buy bean fritters for me so we can eat them together”: that spells uncertainly about one's right to send the person concerned on an errand.
interpretation_gold: People in authority should not be tentative in asserting their authority.

yoruba: Ẹni tí kò lè gbé eèrà, tí ńkùsà sí erin, títẹ́ ní ńtẹ́.
english_literal: A person who lacks the strength to lift an ant but rushes forward to lift an elephant ends in disgrace.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's capabilities and limit oneself to what one can accomplish.

yoruba: Ẹní dádé ti kúrò lọ́mọdé.
english_literal: The person who wears a crown has outgrown childhood.
interpretation_gold: A high office carries high responsibilities with it.

yoruba: Ṣàgbà-ṣàgbà ò níí sé àgbà títí láí.
english_literal: The elderly person who acts his proper part will always be respected as an elder.
interpretation_gold: If responsible people wish to be retain people's respect they must always act like elders.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ìbá hùwà ipá ò hùwà ipá; ẹni tí ìbá hùwà ẹ̀lẹ̀ ò hu ẹ̀lẹ̀; ọ̀kùn tó nígba ọwọ́, tó nígba ẹsẹ̀ ńhùwà pẹ̀lẹ́.
english_literal: The person one would expect to be reckless is not reckless; the person one would expect to be cautious is not cautious; the millipede with two hundred arms and two hundred legs behaves very gently.
interpretation_gold: Even though one has a great deal of weight, one should still tread lightly.

yoruba: Ẹ̀yá ló bí mi, ẹkùn ló wò mí dàgbà, ológìnní gbà mí tọ́; bí kò sẹ́ran lọ́bẹ̀ nkò jẹ.
english_literal: I was born of a monkey; I was raised by a leopard, I was adopted by a cat; if there is no meat in the stew I will not eat it.
interpretation_gold: I will not act in a way inconsistent with my upbringing.

yoruba: “Ẹ fà á wọlé” ló yẹ ẹlẹ́ṣin.
english_literal: “Lead it into the stable” is what becomes a horseman.
interpretation_gold: To be able to afford a horse but not a groom is something of a disgrace.

yoruba: Ọ̀gẹ̀gẹ́ ò lẹ́wà; lásán ló fara wéṣu.
english_literal: The poisonous cassava has no attraction; it resembles a yam only in vain.
interpretation_gold: No imitation can be as good as the real thing.

yoruba: Ṣágo ḿbúgò, ó ló ṣẹnu gbáṣọ́rọ́.
english_literal: The demijohn insults the bottle, saying the latter has a long snout.
interpretation_gold: It is silly to pick a blemish one shares as the basis for insulting others; the pot should not call the kettle black.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a fẹ́ yàtọ̀ sí ẹni tó ní kò sí irú òun.
english_literal: A person one loves is different from a person who says there is no one like him/herself.
interpretation_gold: One's worth is more a matter of what other people think of one than what one thinks of oneself.

yoruba: Ẹyẹ akòko-ó ní òún le gbẹ́ odó; ta ní jẹ́ fi odó akòko gúnyán jẹ?
english_literal: The woodpecker boasts that it can carve a mortar; who ever used a mortar carved by the woodpecker to make pounded yam?
interpretation_gold: The puny person's best efforts cannot amount to much.

yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n kan ò ta kókó omi sáṣọ; ọ̀mọ̀ràn kan ò mọ oye erùpẹ̀ ilẹ̀.
english_literal: No wise man ever ties water in a knot in his cloth; no knowledgeable person can tell the number of grains of sand on the earth.
interpretation_gold: There are certain feats that are beyond even the most accomplished of men.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a gbé gun ẹlẹ́dẹ̀, ìwọ̀n ni kó yọ̀ mọ; ẹni tó gẹṣin, ilẹ̀ ló ḿbọ̀.
english_literal: The person whom people have seated on a pig should moderate his or her strutting; even a horse rider will eventually come down to earth.
interpretation_gold: One should not let one's good fortune go to one's head; circumstances do change.

yoruba: Ọwọ́ àìdilẹ̀ ní ńyọ koríko lójú àna ẹ̀.
english_literal: Idle hands are the ones obliged to remove grass specks from their in-law's eyes.
interpretation_gold: People who are unemployed can expect to be asked to perform all sorts of belittling tasks.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ò mẹ̀yẹ.
english_literal: A pig does not know what is becoming.
interpretation_gold: Some people do not know fitting behavior.

yoruba: Ẹ̀gbọ́n ṣíwájú ó so aṣọ kọ́; àbúrò-ó kẹ́hìn ó wẹ̀wù; bí a ò mọ̀lẹ, ọ̀lẹ ò mọ araa rẹ̀?
english_literal: The elder walks in front, a loincloth draped over his shoulder; the younger walks behind, wearing a garment; if people cannot tell which one is shiftless, does he not know himself?
interpretation_gold: The shiftless person cannot hide his shiftlessness either from himself or from others.

yoruba: Ẹni tí kò tó gèlètè kì í mí fìn-ìn.
english_literal: A person who is not huge in stature does not breathe heavily.
interpretation_gold: One should match one's strutting to one's accomplishment.

yoruba: Ọbẹ̀ kì í gbé inú àgbà mì.
english_literal: A stew does not slush around once inside an elder.
interpretation_gold: An elder should know how to keep confidences.

yoruba: Ẹni à bá tà ká fowó-o rẹ̀ ra àtùpà: ó ní òun à-jí-tanná-wò-lóru.
english_literal: A person who should be sold for money to purchase a lamp boasts that he is one-people-light-lamps-to-admire-at-night.
interpretation_gold: A person most unwanted in a company regards himself/herself as the soul of the party.

yoruba: Ọ̀wọ́n là ńra ògo, ọ̀pọ̀ là ńra ọ̀bùn, iyekíye là ńra ìmẹ́lẹ́.
english_literal: Honor is always bought dear, filthiness cheap, and idleness at an indifferent price.
interpretation_gold: Nothing is more difficult to come by than honor.

yoruba: Ẹni tí à ńwò láwò-sunkún ńwo ara-a rẹ̀ láwò-rẹ́rìnín.
english_literal: A person whose appearance moves one to tears is moved to laughter by his own appearance.
interpretation_gold: The miserable person has no notion of his own miserableness.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a ò fẹ́, àlọ́ ò kàn án.
english_literal: A person whose company is not desired gets no turn at riddling.
interpretation_gold: A person not wanted in a group should not press his or her rights.

yoruba: Ẹni tó tijú tì í fún ara-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: The person who is self-aware protects his or her own reputation thereby.
interpretation_gold: Good character benefits the owner more than others.

yoruba: Ọ̀nà ọ̀fun ò gba egungun ẹja.
english_literal: The throat cannot accommodate fish-bone.
interpretation_gold: Everybody and everything has some limitation.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ àgbà-á kú sàn ju ọjọ́ àgbà-á tẹ́.
english_literal: The day an elder dies is far better than the day an elder is disgraced.
interpretation_gold: Death is preferable to disgrace.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ bọ̀tí-bọ̀tí ò yẹ àgbàlagbà.
english_literal: Speech like drunken babble does not befit a venerable person.
interpretation_gold: Responsible adults should be very careful about what they say.

yoruba: Ọ̀yájú-u baálé ní ńpàdé ìbòsí lọ́nà.
english_literal: It is a reckless home owner who is met with alarms when he ventures outside.
interpretation_gold: A patriarch who misbehaves earns disgrace.

yoruba: Ẹ̀rúkọ́ ńṣe bí ọkọ́.
english_literal: The haft of the hoe is behaving like a hoe.
interpretation_gold: A certain person is putting on airs to which he or she is not entitled.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ kan ṣoṣo là ńtẹ́; ojoojúmọ́ lojú ńtini.
english_literal: It takes one day only for one to disgrace oneself; the shame is a daily affair.
interpretation_gold: Fleeting indiscretion have lasting effects.

yoruba: Ọ̀ràn ò dun ọmọ ẹṣin; a mú ìyá ẹ̀ so, ó ńjẹ oko kiri.
english_literal: Problems make hardly any impression on the foal of a horse; its mother is tied down but it grazes nonchalantly about.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who show no concern for the afflictions of those close to them.

yoruba: Ẹni tí kò rí ayé rí ní ńsọ pé kò sẹ́ni tó gbọ́n bí òun.
english_literal: It is a person with limited experience of life who thinks there is none as wise as he.
interpretation_gold: No wise person claims he or she is the best there is.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ tí alákàn-án ti ńṣepo, kò kún orùbà.
english_literal: In all the days the crab has been making oil, it has not filled a pot.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who have labored long but have nothing to show for all their effort.

yoruba: Ẹran kí la ò jẹ rí? Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ báni lábàtà ó ba búrúbúrú.
english_literal: What sort of meat is it, the likes of which one has never tasted? A toad comes upon one at the swamp and cowers in fright.
interpretation_gold: A person for whom one has no use wastes his or her time if he or she goes to great lengths to hide from one.

yoruba: Ẹyẹ tó fi ara wé igún, ẹ̀hìn àdìrò ní ńsùn.
english_literal: Whatever bird emulates the vulture will find itself behind the cooking hearth.
interpretation_gold: People who have everything to lose should not emulate those who have nothing to lose.

yoruba: Ẹ̀gbẹ̀rì ò mọ̀ pé arẹwà kì í gbé ẹ̀kú; gbogbo ehín kin-kìn-kin lábẹ́ aṣọ.
english_literal: The novice does not know that a good-looking person does not wear a masquerade; all his perfectly white teeth are concealed beneath the cloth.
interpretation_gold: It is a foolish person who conceals his or her endowments.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ńpàfọ̀, ó rò pé òún ńṣoge.
english_literal: The pig wallows in mud, but thinks it is being a dandy.
interpretation_gold: People who lack good judgement are never aware of their own misbehavior.

yoruba: Ọ̀bún ríkú ọkọ tìrànmọ́; ó ní ọjọ́ tí ọkọ òún ti kú òun ò fi omi kan ara.
english_literal: The filthy person takes advantage of her husband's death for blame; she says since her husband died she has not violated her person with water.
interpretation_gold: Shiftless people will latch on any excuse to shirk duties.

yoruba: Ẹ̀ṣọ́ kì í gba ọfà lẹ́hìn; iwájú gangan ní ńfi-í gba ọgbẹ́.
english_literal: A palace guard does not receive arrows on his back; he suffers wounds only on his front.
interpretation_gold: One must act in a manner that befits one's station.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ kan là ḿbàjẹ́, ọjọ́ gbogbo lara ńtini.
english_literal: Only one day brings disgrace to a person; the shame is felt every day.
interpretation_gold: The thoughtless act of a moment mars one's reputation for a long time.

yoruba: Ẹni à ńgbé gẹ̀gẹ̀ ni yó ba ara-a rẹ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: It is the person who is revered that will disgrace himself or herself.
interpretation_gold: People who are placed on pedestals have ample opportunities to topple themselves.

yoruba: Ọmọ onílẹ̀ á tẹ̀ ẹ́ jẹ́jẹ́.
english_literal: The owner of the earth treads gently on it.
interpretation_gold: Responsible people do not always do as they can, but behave as is proper.

yoruba: Ẹni à bá tà ká fowó-o rẹ̀ ra àdá: ó ní ìyà àdá ńjẹ òun.
english_literal: A person who should be sold for money to purchase a machete bemoans his lack of a machete.
interpretation_gold: A person who is only most grudgingly tolerated in a company complains about his lack of privileges.

yoruba: Ọmọ àì-jọbẹ̀-rí tí ńja epo sáyà.
english_literal: A child new to eating stews: he shows himself by dripping palm-oil on his chest.
interpretation_gold: Upstarts will betray themselves by their misuse of their new-found fortune.

yoruba: Ẹni à bá tà ká fowó-o rẹ̀ ra èbù: ó ní èlé òún kó ọ̀ọ́dúnrún.
english_literal: A person one would sell for money to purchase quartered yams for planting: he claims that he has enough earnings to buy three hundred yam pieces.
interpretation_gold: A person considered worthless and expendable makes claims to equal rights.

yoruba: Ọmọdé dáwọ́tilẹ̀, ó ní òún tó ọ̀bọ; bó tó ọ̀bọ, ó tó gẹ̀gẹ̀ àyàa ẹ̀?
english_literal: A child rests his hand on the earth and claims it is as big as a monkey “read chimpanzee”; even if the child is as big as a monkey, is its chest as big as the monkey's?
interpretation_gold: Equality is more than mere physical resemblance.

yoruba: “Ọjọ́ tí mo ti ḿbọ̀ ng ò rírú ẹ̀ rí”: olúwa ẹ̀-ẹ́ mọ ìwọ̀n ara ẹ̀ ni.
english_literal: “In all the days I have walked this earth I have never seen the like”: that person knows his place.
interpretation_gold: If one knows one's place one will be spared humiliation.

yoruba: Ẹ jẹ́ ká mí, ẹ jẹ́ ká simi; èèyàn ní ńfìdí èèyàn jókòó; èèyàn ìbá ṣe bí Ọlọ́run kò níí jẹ́ ká mí.
english_literal: Let us breathe, leave us in peace; the fashion is for people to sit on their behinds; were humans in the position of God they would not permit people to breathe.
interpretation_gold: People are wont to be too full of their authority; it is a good thing they have less power over others than God does.

yoruba: Ọ̀ṣìn ò lè mú àwòdì òkè; Bámidélé lọ̀ṣín lè mú.
english_literal: The fish-eagle cannot catch the kite flying on high; it can only catch Bamidele.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who will confront only weaklings rather than people who match them in strength.

yoruba: Ọ̀mùtí gbàgbé ìṣẹ́, alákọrí gbàgbé ọ̀la.
english_literal: The drunkard ignores his misery; the ill-fated person forgets tomorrow.
interpretation_gold: Irresponsible people often indulge themselves instead of taking care of their pressing problems.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá ńdáṣọ fún kì í ka èèwọ̀.
english_literal: The person who is clothed by others does not list what he will not wear.
interpretation_gold: Those who depend on the charity of others must be satisfied with whatever they can get.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a lè gbé kì í dawọ́.
english_literal: A person who can be lifted does not hang limp.
interpretation_gold: There is no point in resisting the irresistible.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà alágbaà ní ńgarùn wo eégún.
english_literal: It is an insatiable chief of the masqueraders cult that stands on tiptoes to watch a performing masquerader.
interpretation_gold: It is unseemly to be too greedy, especially when everything is at one's disposal anyway.

yoruba: Ọkùnrin kì í ké, akọ igi kì í ṣoje.
english_literal: A man does not cry; hardwood does not ooze sap.
interpretation_gold: Fortitude is the mark of a man.

yoruba: Ẹyẹ ò lè rí omi inú àgbọn bù mu.
english_literal: A bird cannot get at the liquid inside a coconut to drink.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt the impossible.

yoruba: Ẹni à bá fi sóko kó dàparò, ó ní òun ẹni ilé.
english_literal: The person one would leave on the farm hoping he would become a partridge boasts that he is the indispensable presence of the household.
interpretation_gold: An unwanted person believes himself to be indispensable.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ ò dùn lẹ́nu ìyá olè.
english_literal: Speech is not pleasant in the mouth of the mother of a thief.
interpretation_gold: There is little a miscreant can say that will impress people.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́ẹ́fà kì í lọ ẹẹ́fàa rẹ̀ ká sọ pé o di ìjẹfà tí a ti jẹun.
english_literal: When a person proclaims the loss of six articles, one does not respond by saying one has not eaten in six days.
interpretation_gold: If one can offer no help to a person in trouble, one should not complicate the person's plight.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́ ńlọ ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́, o ní “Ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀ta ni àbí ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́gbẹ̀fà?”; èwo lo gbé níbẹ̀?
english_literal: A person says he has lost an unspecified amount of money, and you ask if the amount is five hundred cowries or eleven hundred cowries; which amount did you steal?
interpretation_gold: A person who is too inquisitive about other people's affairs raises suspicions about his or her motives.

yoruba: Ṣàkì ńṣe bí ọ̀rá, egungun ńṣe bí ẹran.
english_literal: The tripe presents itself as fat; the bone presents itself as meat.
interpretation_gold: One should not pretend to be what one is not.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ wo ló wà lẹ́nu alaṣọ pípọ́n?
english_literal: What sort of speech can there be in the mouth of the person whose clothes are brown from dirt?
interpretation_gold: People with blemishes should keep a low profile.

yoruba: Ẹ̀bìtì ẹnu ò tàsé.
english_literal: The mouth-trap never misses.
interpretation_gold: The mouth easily accomplishes even impossible feats.

yoruba: Ẹni tó tan ara-a rẹ̀ lòrìṣà òkè ńtàn: àpọń tí ò láya nílé, tó ní kí òrìṣà ó bùn un lọ́mọ.
english_literal: It is the person who deceives himself that the gods above deceive: a bachelor who has no wife at home but implores the gods to grant him children.
interpretation_gold: It is self-deceit to expect the gods to do everything for one, when one has not lifted a finger on one's behalf.

yoruba: Ẹní bá dẹ ojú-u rẹ̀ sílẹ̀ á rímú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: Whoever gazes downwards with will see his or her nose.
interpretation_gold: Whoever comports himself or herself indecorously will be disgraced.

yoruba: Ọ̀ṣọ́ ọlọ́ṣọ̀ọ́ ò yẹni; ṣòkòtò àgbàbọ̀ ò yẹ́ ọmọ èèyàn.
english_literal: One never looks good in other people's finery; borrowed trousers do not fit the borrower.
interpretation_gold: One should not be a habitual borrower.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a ò fẹ́ nílùú kì í jó lójú agbo.
english_literal: A person not welcome in the town does not take a turn in the dancing circle.
interpretation_gold: A person not wanted in a group should keep a low profile.

yoruba: Ẹ̀wọ̀n tó tó ọ̀pẹ ò tó-ó dá erin dúró; ìtàkùn tó ní kí erin má ròkè ọ̀dàn, tòun terin ní ńlọ.
english_literal: A chain as thick as a palm-tree cannot stop an elephant; the vine that proposes to stop the elephant from going to the grassland will go with the elephant.
interpretation_gold: Whoever attempts to stop an irresistible force will be swept along by it.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà àgbà ní ńsọ ara ẹ̀ dèwe.
english_literal: It is an avaricious elder that turns himself into a child.
interpretation_gold: An elder who cannot control his appetite asks to be treated like a child.

yoruba: Ẹnìkan kì í jẹ́ “Àwá dé.”
english_literal: Nobody is entitled to say, “Here we come.”
interpretation_gold: However mighty, a person is still only one person.

yoruba: Ọ̀sán pọ́n o ò ṣán ẹ̀kọ; oòrún kan àtàrí o ò jẹ àmàlà; àlejò-ó wà bà ọ ní ìyẹ̀tàrí oòrùn o ò rí ǹkan fún un; o ní “Njẹ́ ng ò níí tẹ́ lọ́wọ́ ẹ̀ báyìí”? O ò tíì tẹ́ lọ́wọ́ ara ẹ, ká tó ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ wá wípé o ó tẹ̀ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ ẹlòmíràn tàbí o ò níí tẹ́?
english_literal: The sun rises and you do not eat corn meal; the sun moves directly overhead and you do not eat yam-flour meal; a visitor arrives for you when the sun is just past the overhead position and you have nothing to entertain him with; and you ask, “Am I not in danger of being disgraced in his eyes”? Aren't you already disgraced in your own eyes? Never mind whether you may be disgraced in others' eyes or not.
interpretation_gold: What one thinks of oneself is every bit as important as what others think of one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ohun-olóhun tọrẹ bí kò ṣe tẹni.
english_literal: One does not make a gift of someone else's property when it is not one's own.
interpretation_gold: Never be too free with other people's property.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá èṣín ò mọdẹ.
english_literal: A dog born a year ago does not know how to hunt.
interpretation_gold: One learns from experience and maturity.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ààyá bọ́ sílẹ̀, ó bọ́ sílé.
english_literal: The Colobus monkey jumps to the ground; it runs for home.
interpretation_gold: When danger lurks, the wisest course is to run for safety.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi idà pa ìgbín.
english_literal: One does not use a sword to kill a snail.
interpretation_gold: Remedies should be commensurate with the problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi àì-mọ̀-wẹ̀ mòòkùn.
english_literal: One does not dive under water without knowing how to swim.
interpretation_gold: Never engage in a project for which you lack the requisite skills.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka ọmọ fún òbí.
english_literal: One does not enumerate children for the parents.
interpretation_gold: Do not presume to know better than those most intimately involved.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpọ́n dògí ó ṣàrò.
english_literal: When a bachelor becomes old, he makes his own cooking fire.
interpretation_gold: One should make provisions for the future in one's youth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbókan là ńrọ́ Ifá adití.
english_literal: It is with full voice volume that one recites divination verses for the deaf.
interpretation_gold: One cannot be too subtle with the daft.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbùkún layé gbà.
english_literal: The world accepts only adding on.
interpretation_gold: Supplement rather than deplete.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í dá ẹrù ikùn pa orí.
english_literal: One does not weigh the head down with a load that belongs to the belly.
interpretation_gold: Responsibilities should rest where they belong.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbẹ̀jẹ ò korò nílé ńlá.
english_literal: Pumpkin is never bitter in a big household.
interpretation_gold: When one is in need, one cannot be too choosy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ́ rí aláásáà, ó pa ìyẹ́ mọ́.
english_literal: The chicken sees the snuff seller and enfolds its wings.
interpretation_gold: When one sees potential danger approaching, one should take precautions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpà èèyàn ò mọ̀ pé ohun tó pọ̀-ọ́ lè tán.
english_literal: A wastrel does not know that what is plentiful can be used up.
interpretation_gold: A wastrel knows no thrift.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ogun dán ẹ̀ṣọ́ wò.
english_literal: One does not tease a warrior by saying there is a war (or an invasion.)
interpretation_gold: Do not play with a loaded and primed gun.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláṣedànù tí ńfajá ṣọdẹ ẹja.
english_literal: A wastrel “who” uses a dog to stalk fish.
interpretation_gold: It is folly to employ an impossible tool for a given task.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbọn kì í ṣe oúnjẹ ẹyẹ.
english_literal: Coconut is no food for birds.
interpretation_gold: Some things and some people are immune to some types of danger; one should not attempt the impossible.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í duni lóyè ká fọ̀nà ilé-e Baálẹ̀ hanni.
english_literal: One does not compete with another for a chieftaincy title and also show the way to the king's house to the competitor.
interpretation_gold: A person should be treated either as an adversary or as an ally, not as both.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbá kì í di òtítọ́; ojo ni kì í jẹ́ ká dá a.
english_literal: Plans do not automatically bear fruit; only the faint-hearted do not make plans.
interpretation_gold: While plans may never bear fruit, people should still make them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àìpé, “Tìrẹ nìyí” ní ḿbí ayé nínú.
english_literal: Neglect to say, “Here is your's” is what incites the earth's anger.
interpretation_gold: Failure to take account of people's possible influence on one's affairs incites their anger. As long as one assumes humility, people will let one be.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbàtì àlàpà; a bà á tì, a bá a rẹ́.
english_literal: Unfinished abandoned wall: unable to master it, one befriends it.
interpretation_gold: One reconciles oneself to matters one cannot control.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣòroójà bí ìjà ọjà; onítìjú ò níí sá; ẹni tí ńnà án ò níí dáwọ́ dúró.
english_literal: Difficult-to-fight as the fight of the market place; the self-conscious person will not run, and the person beating him up will not stop.
interpretation_gold: Too much concern with appearances exposes one to occasional inconveniences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-sìnkú-àì-jogún, òṣì ní ńtani.
english_literal: Burying-the-dead-without-sharing-in-the-inheritance leads one to poverty.
interpretation_gold: One should have something to show for one's efforts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlejò tó bèèrè ọ̀nà kò níí sọnù.
english_literal: A stranger who asks the way will not get lost.
interpretation_gold: One should be willing to admit one's ignorance and seek direction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbẹ́ àwòrán gàgàrà ká má fi ọwọ́ ẹ ti nǹkan.
english_literal: One does not carve a tall statue without resting its hand on something.
interpretation_gold: Everybody needs some support.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjímú kì í tí.
english_literal: The task one takes on waking in the morning does not flounder.
interpretation_gold: The task to which one gives the highest priority does not suffer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹran ikún gbọn ti àgbọ̀nrín nù.
english_literal: One does not brush off antelope meat with squirrel meat.
interpretation_gold: Never prefer something of little value to something of great value.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi owó du oyè-e alágbára.
english_literal: One does not rely on money to contest a chieftaincy reserved for the strong.
interpretation_gold: Money won't buy everything.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-wí-fúnni-kó-tó-dáni, àgbà òmùjà ni.
english_literal: He-who-alerts-one-before-he-throws-one is a past master of wrestling.
interpretation_gold: One would be wise to avoid adversaries confident enough to show their hands beforehand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ńyan lóko, aláìlóye-é ní ó jọ pẹ́pẹ́yẹ.
english_literal: The tortoise struts on the farm, the senseless person says it resembles a duck.
interpretation_gold: It is indeed a fool that cannot discern the obvious.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú oko mú ẹjọ́ kí ọ̀kan má yẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not opt to work on the farm and also opt to go argue one's case and avoid neglecting one or the other.
interpretation_gold: One cannot do two mind-absorbing tasks at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláǹtakùn, bí yóò bá ọ jà, a ta ká ọ lára.
english_literal: When the spider wants to engage an enemy, it spins its web around it.
interpretation_gold: The attentive person can detect signs of hostility before it occurs. Also, one makes good preparations before embarking on a venture.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ, kàgbo wàrà; ọjọ́ ńlọ.
english_literal: Nursing mother, make the herbal decoction in good time; the day is waning.
interpretation_gold: Attend to duties in time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í tijú bá baálé ilé jẹ akátá; bó bá mú, ìwọ náà a mú tìẹ.
english_literal: One should not be too embarrassed to eat a jackal with one's host; as he helps himself, one also helps oneself.
interpretation_gold: Never be too bashful to adopt the ways of the people among whom you find yourself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ayé ńlọ, à ńtọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: The world goes forth, and we follow.
interpretation_gold: One lives according to what life confronts one with.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í jẹ “Mo fẹ́rẹ̀-ẹ́” lọ́bẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not eat “I almost” in a stew.
interpretation_gold: What one missed narrowly, one cannot enjoy at all.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtàrí ìbá ṣe ìkòkò ká gbé e fún ọ̀tá yẹ̀wò; a ní ó ti fọ́ yányán.
english_literal: If one's head was a pot and one gave it to an enemy to inspect, he would say it was irretrievably broken.
interpretation_gold: An enemy is not one to trust with one's destiny.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbójú-u fífò lé adìẹ àgàgà; a kì í gbójú-u yíyan lé alágẹmọ.
english_literal: One should not expect flight from the flightless chicken; one should not expect striding from a chameleon.
interpretation_gold: To expect the impossible is to delude oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ìrànà ní ńṣíwájú òkú.
english_literal: It is the votive herald-chicken that precedes a dead person.
interpretation_gold: Matters must be attended to in their proper sequence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ́ purọ́ mọ́mọ-ọ rẹ̀ jẹun.
english_literal: The nursing mother lies against her child to secure food.
interpretation_gold: One uses every ruse available to one in the interest of one's well-being.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí ẹ́ni ranni lẹ́rù ká yọké.
english_literal: One does not find helpers willing to help with one's load and yet sprout a hump on one's back “from carrying too heavy a load”.
interpretation_gold: Always avail yourself of offered help.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi iná sórí òrùlé sùn.
english_literal: One does not go to bed while there is a fire on one's roof.
interpretation_gold: Better take care of problems before relaxing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbàká labiyamọ ńgbàjá mọ́ ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: It is completely and securely that a mother (bearing her child on her back) supports the child with a strip of cloth.
interpretation_gold: One must be thorough in discharging one's responsibility.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìtìjú kárùn.
english_literal: One does not because of shyness expose oneself to a disease.
interpretation_gold: Never be too shy to speak out on your own behalf.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Akọ̀pẹ Ìjàyè ò gbọ́ tiẹ̀, ó ní ogún kó Agboroode.
english_literal: The palm-wine tapper of Ijaye: instead of looking to his own affairs says Agboroode has been destroyed by invaders.
interpretation_gold: The wise person learns from others' misfortunes instead of gawking at them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ obìnrin, a ní ká sọ́ bàrà ká lọ gbin bàrà sódò; ta ní máa báni pa á?
english_literal: We speak of women and someone suggests that we hedge our words and go plant water melon by the stream; who will help in harvesting it?
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àwítẹ́lẹ̀ ní ńjẹ́ ọmọ́ gbẹ́nà; ọmọ kì í gbẹ́nà lásán.
english_literal: Previous-instruction enables a child to understand coded speech; a child does not naturally understand codes.
interpretation_gold: A clever child reflects the instruction he/she has received.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ohun sọ́wọ́ búra.
english_literal: One does not hide something in one's hand and yet swear [that one knows nothing about it].
interpretation_gold: It is foolish to tempt fate; the dishonest exposes himself/herself to the possibility of discovery.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “À ńjùwọ́n” ò ṣéé wí lẹ́jọ́; ìjà ìlara ò tán bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: “We are driven by envy of them” is a bad case to make; a quarrel spawned by jealousy is not easy to settle.
interpretation_gold: Quarrels whose causes cannot be openly admitted will not readily end.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkó balẹ̀, ó fi gbogbo ara kígbe.
english_literal: Àko hit the ground and cried out with its whole body.
interpretation_gold: A person who needs help should not be coy in asking.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A lé tẹ̀m̀bẹ̀lẹ̀kun jìnnà bí ẹnipé kó bọ́ jù sígbó.
english_literal: One chases conspiracy away, as though one would have it disappear into the bush.
interpretation_gold: No one should want anything to do with conspiracy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi oko sin fún ìwọ̀fà.
english_literal: One does not hide the farm from the pawned worker.
interpretation_gold: It does not make sense to prevent a servant one has hired from doing what one hired him to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ará ọ̀run ò ṣẹ́tí aṣọ.
english_literal: Natives of heaven do not sew their hems.
interpretation_gold: The uninitiated do not know the customs of a place.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpà-á fi ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá bọ ẹnu; àpà, a-bìjẹun-wọ̀mù-wọ̀mù.
english_literal: The wastrel puts all ten fingers into his mouth; wastrel, a-person-who-eats-with-abandon.
interpretation_gold: A wastrel is immoderate in his feeding.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahún dùn;kò tóó jẹ fúnni.
english_literal: Tortoise meat is delicious, but there is not enough of it to make a meal.
interpretation_gold: One should husband one's resources wisely.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Apajájẹẹ́ ní ẹ̀rù adìẹ ḿba òun.
english_literal: The-person-who-kills-and-eats-dogs claims to be afraid of chickens.
interpretation_gold: A hardened criminal pretends to have scruples about mere peccadillos.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi àgbà sílẹ̀ sin àgbà.
english_literal: One does not leave one elder sitting to walk another elder part of his way.
interpretation_gold: One should not slight one person in order to humor another.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-gbọ́n-léwe ni à-dàgbà-di-wèrè.
english_literal: Lack-of-wisdom-in-youth is imbecility in adulthood.
interpretation_gold: The man turns out just as the child was; the grown person acquires his traits in childhood.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́n-ọn òo lọrùn ò ti wọ òun mọ́.
english_literal: Tortoise says that since the day it learned the trick of saying yes its neck has ceased to shrink.
interpretation_gold: One who says yes to every request avoids a great many arguments.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í wà nínú ìṣẹ́ ká perin tọrẹ.
english_literal: One does not wallow in poverty and yet kill an elephant for public distribution.
interpretation_gold: Always live according to your circumstances.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fá orí lẹ́hìn olórí.
english_literal: One does not shave a head in the absence of the owner.
interpretation_gold: One does not settle a matter in the absence of the person most concerned.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbò dúdú kọjá odò ó di funfun.
english_literal: The black ram crosses the river and becomes white.
interpretation_gold: Propitious events can drastically change a person's fortunes for the better.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ejò sórí òrùlé sùn.
english_literal: One does not go to bed while a snake is on the roof.
interpretation_gold: Never let down your guard while danger still lurks.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ò lórúnkún ẹjọ́.
english_literal: A chicken has no knees for cases.
interpretation_gold: One should steer clear of actionable behavior.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahún ńre àjò, ó gbé ilé-e rẹ̀ dání.
english_literal: Tortoise embarks on a journey and takes his house with it.
interpretation_gold: One's dearest possessions deserve one's closest attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlejò bí òkété là ńfi èkùrọ́ lọ̀.
english_literal: It is a visitor like a giant rat to whom one offers palm-nuts.
interpretation_gold: One should approach other people as their stations dictate.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ní kò sí oun tó dà bí oun tí a mọ̀ ọ́ṣe; ó ní bí òún bá ńrìn lóko ẹ̀pà, ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan a máa bọ́ sóun lẹ́nu.
english_literal: Tortoise says there is nothing quite like what one knows how to do; it says when it walks through a peanut farm, peanuts keep popping one by one into its mouth.
interpretation_gold: When one does what one is a true expert at doing, it seems like performing magic.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; a ní, “Alákàá ẹgbàá, a-biṣu-wọ̀rọ̀-wọ̀rọ̀-lóko, a-bàgbàdo-tàkì-tàkì-lẹ́gàn”; ó ní, “Ọlọ́dẹ ló kú, tàbí ìnájà?”
english_literal: We recite someone's praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; we say, “He of the two hundred granaries, he whose yams are plentiful on the farm, he whose corn is abundant in the fields,” and the person asks, “Is the dead person a hunter, or a trader?”
interpretation_gold: A person for whom everything must be spelled out, a person who cannot make deductions from the most obvious hints, is daft indeed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣe fáàárí itọ́ dídà sọ́mọ a-kú-wárápá.
english_literal: One does not drool in jest in the presence of the child of an epileptic.
interpretation_gold: Never make fun of afflicted people by mimicking their affliction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkísà aṣọ la fi ńṣe òṣùká.
english_literal: A rag is what one uses as a carrying pad.
interpretation_gold: One's most valuable possessions are not for careless use.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alákìísà ní ńtọ́jú abẹ́rẹ́ tòun tòwú.
english_literal: It is the owner of rags who makes sure that needle and thread are available.
interpretation_gold: Each person looks after his/her own interests.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara kì í rọni ká ṣẹ́gi ta.
english_literal: If one has the wherewithal to live a life of ease, one does not gather firewood for sale.
interpretation_gold: When one has found success, one does not persist in grubbing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ta bàbà a fowó-o bàbà ra bàbà.
english_literal: We sell guinea-corn, and with the guinea-corn money we buy guinea corn.
interpretation_gold: This variant of the previous entry suggests that for all one's efforts and exertions one has not significantly altered one's circumstances.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sọ̀kò-sádìẹ-igba, òkò ní ńsọ tí ilẹ̀-ẹ́ fi ńṣú.
english_literal: One-who-throws-stones-at-two-hundred-chickens will be engaged in stone throwing until nightfall.
interpretation_gold: Tackling a job with inadequate tools makes the job interminable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-jí-má-bọ̀ọ́jú, tí ńfi ojú àná wòran.
english_literal: A-person-who-rises-in-the-morning-without-washing-his-face, one who sees things with yesterday's eyes.
interpretation_gold: A person who does not keep his eyes peeled for developments is ever behind times.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú ọmọ oǹdọ́pọ̀ dè.
english_literal: One does not chain the child of a person who offers too low a price for one's wares.
interpretation_gold: It is not a crime to make an offer that might be unacceptable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣòwò méjì kẹ́ran má jẹ ọ̀kan.
english_literal: One does not engage in two trades without having one consumed by goats.
interpretation_gold: One cannot effectively manage two enterprises at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ò ṣéé fi rúná.
english_literal: The palm of the hand is not good for stoking fires.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt difficult tasks without the proper resources.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Atẹ́gùn ò ṣéé gbé.
english_literal: The wind is impossible to carry.
interpretation_gold: Certain propositions are unrealizable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í múlé móko kọ́kan má yẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not devote oneself to the home and devote oneself to the farm and not wind up neglecting one of them.
interpretation_gold: One cannot go in two opposite directions at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajàkàṣù ò mọ̀ bí ìyàn-án mú.
english_literal: The person who eats large helpings does not care that there is a famine.
interpretation_gold: Greed knows no thrift.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣọ funfun òun àbàwọ́n kì í rẹ́.
english_literal: White cloth and stains are not friends.
interpretation_gold: A person of good breeding does not associate with an ill-bred person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìgbín sọ̀kò sórìṣà.
english_literal: One does not throw a snail at a god.
interpretation_gold: Service to the worthy should be performed with decorum, not with insult.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í yin ọmọdé lójú ara ẹ̀; ìfàsẹ́hìn ní ńkángun ẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not praise a child in his presence; only backsliding results.
interpretation_gold: Children should not be praised too highly; they should always be made aware that they can be even better.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Arìngbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni yó mùú oyè délé; asárétete ò róyè jẹ.
english_literal: The person who walks casually is the one who will bear a title home; the person who runs fast has no title to show for his efforts.
interpretation_gold: The spoils do not necessarily go to those who exert themselves most.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ayé ò ṣé-é finú hàn; bí o lọ́gbọ́n, fi síkùn ara-à rẹ.
english_literal: The world does not deserve to be trusted; if you have a store of wisdom, keep it in you.
interpretation_gold: People of the world are not reliable; whatever wisdom one wishes to pass on one should reserve for one's own use.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbọ́ ẹjọ́ẹnìkan dájọ́.
english_literal: One does not deliver a verdict after hearing only one side.
interpretation_gold: Justice requires impartiality and a full hearing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A dẹ́bọ fún igúnnugún, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún àkàlà, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún ẹyẹlé, ẹyẹlé gbẹ́bọ, ó rúbọ.
english_literal: A sacrifice was prescribed for the vulture, but it refused to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the ground-hornbill, but it declined to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the pigeon, and it gathered the prescribed materials and made the sacrifice.
interpretation_gold: The vulture and the ground-hornbill are unfortunate in comparison with the pigeon, because they did not carry out the prescribed sacrifice.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alágbàfọ̀ kì í bá odò ṣọ̀tá.
english_literal: A washerman does enter harbor a grudge with the river.
interpretation_gold: One does not turn one's back on one's means of livelihood.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú ìbọn tetere.
english_literal: One does not hold a gun carelessly.
interpretation_gold: Always be careful in handling dangerous matters.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹ́kù là ńmayo.
english_literal: Leaving-remnants is the indicator of satiation.
interpretation_gold: How one lives will show how well off one is.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mọ ọkọ ọmọ ká tún mọàlè-e rẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not acknowledge the husband for one's child and also acknowledge her illicit lover.
interpretation_gold: Never betray trust or connive at betraying it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀-tọ́-ọtí-wò okùn-un bàǹtẹ́ já; bí a bá mu àmuyó ńkọ́?
english_literal: One taste of wine and the belt snaps; what would happen in the event of drunkenness?
interpretation_gold: One should match the response to the stimulus.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abẹ́rẹ́ tó wọnú òkun ò ṣéé wá.
english_literal: A needle that drops into the ocean defies finding.
interpretation_gold: Some tasks are hopelessly impossible to accomplish.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-sọ̀rọ̀ ní ńmú ẹnu rùn.
english_literal: It is abstention from speaking that makes the mouth smell.
interpretation_gold: One should always say one's piece in a discussion.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Afẹ́fẹ́ ńda ológìì láàmú; oníyẹ̀fun rọra.
english_literal: The wind is making life difficult for the seller of liquid corn starch; corn flour seller, you had better watch out!
interpretation_gold: When those better situated than one are defeated, one must be prepared for tough times.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbé ẹran erin lérí ká máa fẹsẹ̀ wa ihò ìrẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not carry elephant meat on one's head and dig cricket holes with one's big toe.
interpretation_gold: If one is blessed with plenty, one should not keep chasing after trifles.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjò kì í dùn kónílé má relé.
english_literal: The journey is never so pleasant that the traveler does not return home.
interpretation_gold: The traveler should never forget his or her home.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alákatam̀pòó ṣe bí ọ̀bọ ò gbọ́n; ọ̀bọ́ gbọ́n; tinú ọ̀bọ lọ̀bọ́ ńṣe.
english_literal: The person with the cross-bow thinks that the monkey is not clever; the monkey is clever, but it is following its own strategy.
interpretation_gold: It matters nothing if one is derided, as long as one knows what one is doing and why.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-pẹ́-ẹ́-jẹ kì í jẹ ìbàjẹ́.
english_literal: A person who waits patiently for a long time before eating will not eat unwholesome food.
interpretation_gold: Those who are patient will have the best of things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláàárù kì í ru ẹṣin.
english_literal: The porter cannot carry a horse.
interpretation_gold: Certain tasks are impossible of accomplishment.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-rìn-fàà-lójú-akẹ́gàn, a-yan-kàṣà-lojú-abúni, abúni ò lówó nílé ju ẹnu-u rẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: One-who-saunters-in-front-of-detractors, one-who-struts-before-abusers, those who abuse one have no money at home, only their mouths.
interpretation_gold: One's best course is to ignore detractors and insulters; all they have is their mouths.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-roko, àì-rodò tí ńṣápẹ́ fún eégún jó.
english_literal: Not-going-to-the-farm, not-going-to-the-river that claps for masqueraders to dance.
interpretation_gold: It is an idler who makes music for masqueraders to dance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ní ẹgbàá nílé wá ẹgbàá ròde.
english_literal: One does not have a thousand cowries (or six pence) at home and go chasing abroad for a thousand cowries.
interpretation_gold: Only the promise of a greater fortune should tempt one to neglect what one already has.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka oyún inú kún ọmọ ilẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not count a fetus among living children.
interpretation_gold: Never count your chickens before they are hatched.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àwòdì òkè tí ńwo ìkaraun kọ̀rọ̀, kí ni yó fìgbín ṣe?
english_literal: The hawk in the sky eyes the snail-shell slyly; what will it do with a snail.
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's time on a task one cannot master.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Amùṣùà àgbẹ̀ tí ńgbin kókò.
english_literal: A wastrel farmer that plants cocoyams.
interpretation_gold: It is a wastrel farmer that plants cocoyams.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹsílẹ̀-ẹ gbèsè tí ò jẹ́ kí ẹgbẹ̀fà tóó ná.
english_literal: Long-standing debt, that makes twelve hundred cowries insufficient to spend.
interpretation_gold: Existing debts eat new fortunes away.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjànàkú kúrò lẹ́ran à ńgọ dé.
english_literal: The elephant is not among the ranks of animals one lies in ambush for.
interpretation_gold: The wise person puts some distance between himself and an elephant, or a formidable adversary.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá tí ò létí ò ṣé-é dẹ̀gbẹ́.
english_literal: A dog without ears is no good for stalking prey.
interpretation_gold: A person who cannot be instructed is useless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ká-ìgbá-tà-á náwó ikú.
english_literal: He-who-plucks-the-African-locustbean-tree-seeds-to-sell spends death's money.
interpretation_gold: Whoever engages in a dangerous venture more than earns his/her pay.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sùn jẹ́rìí ìdí.
english_literal: One cannot be asleep and also be able to vouch for one's anus.
interpretation_gold: Assert only those things you know for certain.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara ẹ̀ lara ẹ̀: ṣòkòtò ọlọ́pàá.
english_literal: A little bit of it is a little bit of it: the policeman's short pants.
interpretation_gold: Leave nothing to waste, for one can always find some use for the smallest remnant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbá ẹni tó yọ̀bẹ mú.
english_literal: One does not grab hold of a person who has pulled a knife.
interpretation_gold: Prudence and caution are imperative in dealing with dangerous people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi aṣọ ṣèdìdí yọwó.
english_literal: One does not leave cloth in a bundle while bargaining over it.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to know what one is negotiating to buy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹ̀jẹ̀ ìbálé pa tírà; alákoto ò bí abo ọmọ.
english_literal: One does not smear blood (from a woman's deflowering) on a Muslim charm; a de-virgined woman does not give birth to a “female” child.
interpretation_gold: One must not do the forbidden if one does not expect trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọ̀rọ̀ sílẹ̀ gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: One does not ignore one matter to attend to another matter.
interpretation_gold: Every obligation deserves attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àfẹ́ẹ̀rí kan ò ju ká rí igbó ńlá bọ́ sí lọ; ẹbọ kan ò ju ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn lọ; “Òrìṣá gbé mi lé àtète” kan ò ju orí ẹṣin lọ.
english_literal: There is no disappearing trick better than the availability of a dense forest to disappear into; there is no sacrifice more efficacious than having many people on one's side; there is no “The gods have elevated me” that is higher than the back of a horse.
interpretation_gold: Practical and realistic moves are more reliable than mysterious expectations.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbọ̀ṣẹ́ kì í ṣe iṣẹ́ òòjọ́; iṣẹ́-ẹ baba ẹni ní ńgbani lọ́jọ́ gan-an.
english_literal: Spare-time work is no profession; it is an assignment from one's father that takes all of one's day.
interpretation_gold: One does not waste one's time on trifles or hobbies.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Amọ̀nà èṣí kì í ṣe amọ̀nà ọdúnnìí.
