english_literal: The person who knew the way last year does not necessarily know the way this year.
interpretation_gold: The person whose knowledge does not grow with the times soon becomes ignorant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A fún ọ lọ́bẹ̀ o tami si; o gbọ́n ju ọlọ́bẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: You are given some stew and you add water; you must be wiser than the cook.
interpretation_gold: Adding water is a means of stretching stew. A person who thus stretches the stew he or she is given would seem to know better than the person who served it how much would suffice for the meal.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-fasẹ́-gbèjò ńtan ara-a rẹ̀ jẹ.
english_literal: He-who-would-collect-rain-water-in-a-sieve deceives himself.
interpretation_gold: The shiftless person hurts himself more than others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣọ tá a bá rí lára igún, ti igún ni.
english_literal: Whatever cloth one finds on the vulture belongs to it.
interpretation_gold: The vulture may lack feathers, but it does not borrow from other birds.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọlá jẹ iyọ̀.
english_literal: One does not consume salt according to one's greatness.
interpretation_gold: Too much of a good thing can be dangerous.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìyá ẹní dákú ṣeré.
english_literal: One does not as a joke say one's mother has collapsed.
interpretation_gold: Never trifle with serious matters.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àṣàyá kì í jẹ́ kí ọmọ ọ̀yà ó gbọ́n.
english_literal: Roughhousing keeps the young of the cane rat from learning wisdom.
interpretation_gold: A person who takes life as a jest does not learn to be wary.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ti ojú ogun wẹ́fọ́n.
english_literal: One does not wait until the heat of the battle to start looking for palm-leaf midrib.
interpretation_gold: Always make your preparations well ahead of the event.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbà ṣoore má wo bẹ̀.
english_literal: Elder, do a favor and remove your eyes from it.
interpretation_gold: Do not advertize your acts of kindness, or pointedly await acknowledgment of them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í wá aláṣọ-àlà nísọ̀ elépo.
english_literal: One should not look for a white-clad person in the stall of palm-oil sellers.
interpretation_gold: One should know the likely places to look for whatever one seeks.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgùntàn ò jí ní kùtùkùyù ṣe ẹnu bọbọ.
english_literal: A sheep does not wake in the morning and droop its mouth.
interpretation_gold: One should not dawdle in the morning.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sọrọ ìkọ̀kọ̀ lójú olófòófó.
english_literal: One does not discuss secret matters in the presence of a tattler.
interpretation_gold: Be careful with your secrets.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹkù làgbẹ̀ ńtà.
english_literal: It is the leavings from his table that the farmer sells.
interpretation_gold: One takes care of one's needs before one disposes of the excess.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka igún mọ́ ẹran jíjẹ.
english_literal: One does not list vultures among edible meats.
interpretation_gold: Certain things one does not stoop to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn ní ńgbèjà ìlú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: Only an imbecile gets into a fight in defence of his town.
interpretation_gold: A town's cause is no business of any one individual.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńgba òròmọ adìẹ lọ́wọ́ ikú, ó ní wọn ò jẹ́ kí òun jẹ̀ láàtàn.
english_literal: One struggles to save the chick from certain death, and it complains that one is preventing it from foraging at the dump.
interpretation_gold: Chicks foraging at the dump are easy prey for kites.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Awọ ẹnu ò ṣéé ṣe ìlù.
english_literal: The skin of the mouth cannot be used to fashion a drum.
interpretation_gold: Employ the proper materials for the task in hand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí ewé nílẹ̀ ká fọwọ́ fámí.
english_literal: One does not see leaves lying about and scoop up feces with one's bare hand.
interpretation_gold: Take advantage of whatever aids are available to you.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá tó lè sáré là ńdẹ sí egbin.
english_literal: It is a swift dog that one sends after a Kobe antelope.
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of Ajá ti erée rẹ̀ẹ́ bá dánilójú . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àdó gba ara ẹ̀ tẹ́lẹ̀, ká tó fi oògùn sí?
english_literal: Could the small gourd save itself, before we put charms into it?
interpretation_gold: Do not seek protection from a helpless person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá ti eré-e rẹ̀ẹ́ bá dánilójú là ńdẹ sí ehoro.
english_literal: It is a dog in whose speed one has faith that one sics at a hare.
interpretation_gold: One entrusts important tasks only to those one can trust.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtònímòní ò tó àtànọ́mànọ́.
english_literal: All-day-long is no match for since-yesterday.
interpretation_gold: The person who has endured since yesterday takes precedence over the person who has endured all day.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọ̀nà odò han ikún.
english_literal: One does not show the squirrel the way to the river.
interpretation_gold: Telling someone what he or she already knows is silly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A fọwọ́ mú ajá o lọ, a ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ńfi ìka méjì pè é.
english_literal: We grab a dog with the hands and it escapes; thereafter we beckon it with two fingers.
interpretation_gold: If both hands cannot detain a dog, two fingers from a distance will not bring it to where it escaped from.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ta bàbà, a fowó-o bàbà ra baba.
english_literal: We sell guinea-corn, and with the copper coins we redeem the old man.
interpretation_gold: With what one has one seeks one's goals.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá là bá kí; èse ò pẹran fúnni jẹ.
english_literal: One should rather commend the dog; the cat does not kill meat for one to eat.
interpretation_gold: Assign commensurate values to your assets.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-ṣe-sílẹ̀ làbọ̀wábá; ẹni tó ṣu sílẹ̀ á bọ̀ wá bá eṣinṣin.
english_literal: What-is-put-aside is what-is-there-to-find; he who puts excrement aside will return to find flies.
interpretation_gold: One reaps what one sows.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá tó gbé iyọ̀, kí ni yó fi ṣe?
english_literal: A dog that swipes salt, what will it do with it?
interpretation_gold: Do not expend your effort on senseless ventures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ṣoore-jókòó-tì-í, bí aláìṣe ni.
english_literal: A-person-who-does-a-favor-and-squats-by-it is like a-person-who-has-done-no-favor.
interpretation_gold: One should not dwell on what favor one has done.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹ̀tẹ̀ sílẹ̀ pa làpálàpá.
english_literal: One does not ignore leprosy to treat a rash.
interpretation_gold: More serious problems deserve more immediate attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣoore tán ká lóṣòó tì í.
english_literal: One does not do a favor and then camp by it.
interpretation_gold: Having done some good, do not hang around to compel gratitude.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbá ní ńdi òtítọ́; ojo ni kì í jẹ́ ká da.
english_literal: Attempts result in achievement; it is faint-heartedness that keeps one from making an effort.
interpretation_gold: Without striving, one accomplishes nothing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sin àlè kọjá odò; ohun tí ńṣe ọṣẹ́ ò tó ǹkan.
english_literal: One does not walk one's secret lover across a river; the causes of huge disasters are usually insignificant in themselves.
interpretation_gold: If one is engaged in a dangerous venture, one should not also cast discretion to the wind.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi olórí ogun ṣe ìfagun.
english_literal: One does not position the commander of the army at the rear of the column.
interpretation_gold: The best foot is the one to put forward.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sá fún àjíà ká dìgbò lu eégún.
english_literal: One does not run from the herald of the masquerader and collide with the masquerader himself.
interpretation_gold: Never court a greater disaster in an attempt to avert a minor one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rán ọ̀lẹ wo ojú ọjọ́ àárọ̀.
english_literal: One does not send a shirker to go see what the morning looks like outside.
interpretation_gold: Never rely on the advice of people who have a vested interest in the matter being considered.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọ̀nà ikùn han ọ̀fun.
english_literal: One does not show the throat the way to the stomach.
interpretation_gold: Do not presume to know better than the expert.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í kọ ọmọ-ọ́ bí ká sọ ọ́ ní Èwolódé?
english_literal: One does not so resent having a child that one names it What-is-this-that-has-happened?
interpretation_gold: Childbirth is always a happy event.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbé ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sọnù ká tún bèrè-e jàǹto.
english_literal: One does not throw a toad away and inquire after its young.
interpretation_gold: Commiseration after injury is hypocritical.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláǹtakùnún takùn sí ìṣasùn, ṣíbí gbọludé.
english_literal: The spider has woven its web in the sauce-pan; the spoon takes a holiday.
interpretation_gold: In the absence of the proper tools, one cannot fault the laborer for being idle.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í lọ́mọ lẹ́hin kọ oúnjẹ.
english_literal: One does not have children at one's rear and yet refuse food.
interpretation_gold: No amount of anger or distress should keep one from looking after one's dependents.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbé odò jiyàn-an ọṣẹ́ hó tàbí kò hó.
english_literal: One does not sit by a river and argue whether the soap will foam or will not foam.
interpretation_gold: Where the claim can be put to the test, verbal argument is foolish.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À nfọ̀tún tẹ́ní, à ńfòsì tú ṣòkòtò, obìnrín ní a kò bá òun gbọ́ tọmọ.
english_literal: One spreads a mat with the right hand while removing one's pants with the left hand; yet the woman complains that one is not helping her quest for a child.
interpretation_gold: Some people are incapable of recognizing and acknowledging favors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sáré-lówó ḿbẹ lọ́nà ogun; A-pọ̀ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ḿbẹ lọ́nà èrò; Bó-pẹ́-títí-ng-ó-là ḿbẹ lábà, ó ńjẹ ẹ̀sun iṣu.
english_literal: He-who-hurries-after-riches is on his way to battle; He-who-has-in-abundance is off on his travels; Sooner-or-later-I-will-be-rich is back in his hut, eating roasted yams.
interpretation_gold: Wealth comes to those who exert themselves, not to those who wait for it to find them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í wíjọ́ọ wíwò ká jàre.
english_literal: One does not complain about being looked at and be vindicated.
interpretation_gold: One should not complain that other people are doing what one is also doing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í du orí olórí kí àwòdì gbé tẹni lọ.
english_literal: One does not fight to save another person's head only to have a kite carry one's own away.
interpretation_gold: One should not save other's at the cost of one's own safety.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ti ojú on-íka-mẹ́sàn-án kà á.
english_literal: One does not count the fingers of a person who has only nine in his/her presence.
interpretation_gold: One must be discreet in speaking about other people's flaws and deformities.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-fàtẹ́lẹwọ́-fanná kì í dúró.
english_literal: He-who-carries-live-coals-in-his-palm does not tarry.
interpretation_gold: A person who has a pressing problem has no time for socializing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹ́gbà ni ti kọ̀ǹkọ̀.
english_literal: Croaking-in-relays is the mark of frogs.
interpretation_gold: It is in the nature of sheep to follow and to lack initiative.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara kì í tu ẹni káká, kí ara ó roni koko, ká má leè jíkàkà dÍfá.
english_literal: One cannot be so much at ease, or so much in pain, that one cannot wake early to consult the oracle.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one's condition, one does what one must do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í pa igún, a kì í jẹ igún, a kì í fi igún bọrí.
english_literal: One does not kill the vulture; one does not eat the vulture; one does not offer the vulture as a sacrifice to one's head.
interpretation_gold: Certain behaviors are beyond the pale.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sọ́-ẹ̀hìnkùlé ba araa rẹ̀ nínú jẹ́; ohun tó wuni là ńṣe nílé ẹni.
english_literal: He-who-spies-on-others-from-behind-their-walls upsets himself; one does as one pleases in one's home.
interpretation_gold: What one does in the privacy of one's home is nobody's business.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahun-ún wọnú orù, ó ku àtiyọ.
english_literal: Tortoise has entered into a narrow-necked pot; now, getting out is a problem.
interpretation_gold: One should consider the possible consequences of one's actions before one acts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àyangbẹ ẹjá dùn; ṣùgbọ́n kí la ó jẹ kẹ́já tó yan?
english_literal: Dry smoked fish is delicious, but what is one to eat before the fish is smoked?
interpretation_gold: While one must look to the future, one must also take care of the present.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlùsì ẹsẹ̀ tí ńfa koríko wọ̀lú.
english_literal: Disaster-causing legs that drag weeds into town.
interpretation_gold: It is a person who will bring disaster on others who behaves like the wayward foot that drags weeds into town.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-gbà-bọ́ ò di tẹni.
english_literal: A foster child does not become one's own child.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing like having one's own.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ elégédé, obìnrín ḿbèrè ohun tí à ńsọ, a ní ọ̀rọ̀ ọkùnrin ni; bí a bá kó elégédé jọ, ta ni yó sè é?
english_literal: We are discussing pumpkins, a woman asks what we are discussing, and we respond that it is men's talk; after we have gathered the pumpkins, who will cook them?
interpretation_gold: The woman, certainly. There is no point in excluding her from a matter that will eventually involve her anyway.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abẹ́rẹ́ ò ṣéé gúnyán.
english_literal: A needle cannot be used to make pounded yams.
interpretation_gold: Some tools are inadequate for some tasks.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjànàkú ò ṣéé rù.
english_literal: The elephant is impossible to carry.
interpretation_gold: Some tasks are impossible to accomplish.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbá alágẹmọ lòrìṣà ńgbà.
english_literal: The gods heed what chameleon proposes.
interpretation_gold: One should heed the advice of trusted friends and advisers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-tọrọ-ohun-gbogbo-lọ́wọ́-Ọlọ́run kì í kánjú.
english_literal: The-seeker-of-all-things-from-God does not yield to impatience.
interpretation_gold: The supplicant must be patient for an answer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbàdo kì í ṣe èèyàn;ta ní ńrí ọmọ lẹ́hìn eèsún?
english_literal: The maize plant is not a human being; who ever saw children on the back of elephant grass?
interpretation_gold: One should not overestimate the value of things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í pé kí òṣìkà ṣe é ká wò ó.
english_literal: One does not dare a wicked person to do his worst.
interpretation_gold: Never tempt evil people to do their evil.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-jókòó-àì-fẹ̀hìntì, bí ẹní nàró ni.
english_literal: Sitting-without-leaning-the-back-against-something is like standing.
interpretation_gold: Never do things by half measures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A rí i lójú, a mọ̀ ọ́ lẹ́nu; òṣòwò oṣẹ kì í pọ́n-wọ́-lá.
english_literal: One can tell by looking, and one can tell by taste; a soap seller does not lick her fingers.
interpretation_gold: Soap is recognizable as soap, and anyone who has ever tasted it knows that one does not lick fingers caked with soap. Each trade has its don'ts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi oníjà sílẹ̀ ká gbájúmọ́ alápẹpẹ.
english_literal: One does not leave the person one has a quarrel with and face his lackey.
interpretation_gold: Focus rather on your main problem, not a side-show.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; ó ńgbọ́, “Ikú mẹ́rù, Ọ̀pàgá, a-biṣu-ú-ta-bí-òdòdó, a-lábà-ọkà, a-roko-fẹ́yẹ-jẹ”; ó ní, “Àgbẹ̀ ló kú, tàbí ọ̀nájà?”
english_literal: We recite someone's praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; he hears, “Death takes a renowned man, a titled man, whose yams spread like petals, who possesses barns of corn, whose fields are a bounty for birds,” and he asks, “Is the dead man a farmer or a trader?”
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: 337. Àgbàlagbàá ṣenú kẹrẹndẹn; èyí tó máa ṣe ḿbẹ níkùn-un rẹ̀.
english_literal: An elder shows a smooth belly to the world; but what he will do is known to him.
interpretation_gold: Be a person of thought and action, not of words.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Arúgbó oǹdágbèsè, ó ní mélòó ni òun óò dúró san níbẹ̀?
english_literal: The old person who incurs debt, he says how much of it will he be around to pay?
interpretation_gold: A person whose days are numbered can afford to freely take on long-term obligations.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àfòmọ́ ńṣe ara-a rẹ̀, ó ní òún ńṣe igi.
english_literal: The creeper is destroying itself, but it thinks it is destroying its host.
interpretation_gold: The host's death will be the parasite's death.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ní kọ́mọ má kùú, o ní kò jọ bàbá kò jọ ìyá.
english_literal: We strive to keep a child from dying, and you say he resembles neither the father nor the mother.
interpretation_gold: The person addressed has his or her priorities reversed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ara ẹni ṣe oògun alọ̀kúnná.
english_literal: One does not use oneself as an ingredient in a medicine requiring that the ingredients be pulverized.
interpretation_gold: Self-preservation is a compulsory project for all.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbà òṣìkà ńgbin ìyà sílẹ̀ de ọmọọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A wicked elder sows suffering for his children.
interpretation_gold: One's character often affects the fortunes of one's children.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláàjàá gbé e sókè, o ní, “Kó ṣẹ!”; o mọ̀ bí ibi lówí tàbí ire?
english_literal: The wielder of the incantation rattle lifts it, and you respond, “May it be so!”; do you know if he has invoked good or evil?
interpretation_gold: One should be certain about what is happening before one intervenes or becomes involved.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sọ-aré-dìjà ní ńjẹ̀bi ẹjọ́.
english_literal: One-who-turns-play-into-a-fight is always guilty.
interpretation_gold: One should take a jest in the spirit of jest.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í pa asínwín ilé, nítorí ọjọ́ tí tòde yó bàá wá sílé.
english_literal: One does not kill the imbecile within one's home, because of the day when the one from outside might visit one.
interpretation_gold: One should cultivate one's own madness; one might need it to combat others' madness.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgádágodo ò finú han ara-a wọn.
english_literal: Padlocks do not share their secrets with one another.
interpretation_gold: Some secrets one should not divulge to others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka ilé òrìṣà kún ìlú.
english_literal: One does not count a god's grove as part of the town.
interpretation_gold: Do not list questionable items as part of your wealth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpàkòmọ̀rà, tí ńgẹṣin lórí àpáta.
english_literal: A-shiftless-person-who-knows-not-what-things-cost rides a horse on rocks.
interpretation_gold: A person who has no part in paying for a thing is seldom careful in using it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkámọ́ ẹkùn-ún níyọnu.
english_literal: A cornered leopard poses problems.
interpretation_gold: One should be wary of what prey to stalk.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ kì í rìn kó ṣánwọ́ ahá.
english_literal: A nursing mother does not venture away from home without a cup.
interpretation_gold: She must be prepared to nurse the baby.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-wí-ìgbọ́, àfọ̀-ọ̀-gbọ́ tí ńfi àjèjé ọwọ́ mumi.
english_literal: He-who-will-not-listen-to-talk, he-who-will-not-listen-to-counsel, who drinks water with the bare hand.
interpretation_gold: The obstinate child drinks with the bare hand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A bímọ kò gbọ́n, a ní kó má ṣàá kú; kí ní ńpa ọmọ bí àìgbọ́n?
english_literal: A child lacks wisdom, and some say that what is important is that the child does not die; what kills more surely than lack of wisdom?
interpretation_gold: A foolish child is not much better than a dead child.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí adìẹ nílẹ̀ ká da àgbàdo fún ajá.
english_literal: One does not see chickens about and throw one's corn to the dog.
interpretation_gold: Always direct help where it will be appreciated and where it will do some good.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í léku méjì ká má pòfo.
english_literal: One does not chase two rats and avoid coming up with nothing.
interpretation_gold: Never try to go in two directions at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A leper must not wait for a bearer of abrasive leaves (eépín
interpretation_gold: Know your weaknesses.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ṣòwò-ọṣẹ kì í pa owó ńla.
english_literal: A trader in soap does not make big money.
interpretation_gold: One's success cannot exceed one's enterprise.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣe fáàárí ẹ̀ṣẹ́ dídì sọ́mọ adẹ́tẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not flaunt one's ability to make a fist in the face of a leper's child.
interpretation_gold: Never make fun of people because of their affliction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ayé ò ṣé-é bá lérí; wọ́n lè ṣeni léṣe.
english_literal: The world is not a thing to exchange threats with; it can inflict disaster on one.
interpretation_gold: Be wary in dealing with the world.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ò lè ti ìwòyí sunkún ehín.
english_literal: Chicken cannot at this late date bemoan its lack of teeth.
interpretation_gold: Everything at its proper time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í bọ́ sínú omi tán ká máa sá fún òtútù.
english_literal: One does not enter into the water and then run from the cold.
interpretation_gold: Precautions are useful only before the event.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í peni lólè ká máa gbé ọmọ ẹran jó.
english_literal: One does not suffer the reputation of being a thief and yet go seeking to dance with kids (baby goats).
interpretation_gold: It is foolish to behave in ways that will confirm people's evil opinion of one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn lòjò ìgboro ńpa.
english_literal: It is an imbecile who is soaked in the rain in the middle of a town.
interpretation_gold: Only an imbecile ignores a refuge when one is available.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-mọwọ́-ọ́-wẹ̀ ni àì-bágbà-jẹ; ọmọ tó mọwọ́-ọ́ wẹ̀ á bágbà jẹ.
english_literal: Not-knowing-how-to-wash-one's-hands is not-eating-with-elders; a person who knows how to wash his hands will eat with elders.
interpretation_gold: To qualify to live in society, one must learn the social graces.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Awo aláwo la kì í dá lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: It is another person's divination that one does not repeat.
interpretation_gold: One might not put oneself out for others, but one will for oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-fi-tiẹ̀-sílẹ̀-gbọ́-tẹni-ẹlẹ́ni, ọ̀gànjọ́ ni wọ́n ńsìnkú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: He-who-neglects-his-own-affairs-to-care-for-others'-affairs, it is in the middle of the night that his burial is carried out.
interpretation_gold: Do not sacrifice your self-interest to take care of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Asínwín ní òun ó ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní kó má ti iná bọlé; ó ní òun ó sáà ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní bó bá tiná bọlé àwọn ó sọ ọ́ si; ó ní ìyẹn kẹ̀ ìkan.
english_literal: The imbecile said he would torch the house; he was asked not to torch the house; he said he certainly would torch the house; he was told that if he torched the house he would be thrown in it; he said, “That casts the matter in a different light.”
interpretation_gold: Even an imbecile becomes sane when his life is at stake.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ ní òún sẹ́ ọ̀ràn kan de àwọn ará ilé òun; ó ní bí òún bá lọ sídàálẹ̀, wọn ò jẹ́ fi kàn-ìn-kàn-ìn òun wẹ̀.
english_literal: The leper says that he trusts his relatives on a certain matter; he says when he goes on a journey, they would not dare use his sponge to wash themselves.
interpretation_gold: People have a knack for skirting dangerous or distasteful situations.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adánilóró fagbára kọ́ni.
english_literal: He who disappoints one teaches one to be more resourceful.
interpretation_gold: Once disappointed or injured, one learns to be self-reliant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-bayé-jẹ́ kò ṣéé fìdí ọ̀ràn hàn.
english_literal: A treacherous person is not someone to tell profound matters to.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's secrets from treacherous people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpèmọ́ra là ńpe Tèmídire.
english_literal: It is in furtherance of one's own fortune that one calls the name Temidire.
interpretation_gold: Each person must advance his or her own interests.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjòjí lójú, ṣùgbọ́n kò fi ríran.
english_literal: A stranger has eyes, but they do not see.
interpretation_gold: A stranger's eyes are blind to the intricacies of his new surroundings.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ́ ṣọwọ́ kòtò lu ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A nursing mother cups her palm to strike her child.
interpretation_gold: Discretion is the better part of discipline.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Atipo ò mọ erèé; ó ní, “Bàbá, mo réwé funfun lóko.”
english_literal: Atipo does not recognize beans, he says, “Father, I saw white leaves on the farm.”
interpretation_gold: Ignorance is a curse.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọkùnrín réjò, tóbìrín pa á, à ní kéjò má ṣáà lọ.
english_literal: If a man sees a snake, and a woman kills it, what matters is that the snake does not escape.
interpretation_gold: One should not be a stickler about roles.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ojú ọmọdé ò tó ìtàn, a bá àwígbọ́.
english_literal: If a youth's eyes do not witness a story, they should be good for hearsay.
interpretation_gold: If one does not witness something, one learns from those who did.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí iṣẹ́ kò pẹ́ ẹni, a kì í pẹ́ iṣẹ́.
english_literal: If a task does not delay one, one does not drag it out.
interpretation_gold: Tasks that are easy should be finished promptly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá torí iṣu jẹ epo, à torí epo jẹṣu.
english_literal: If one does not eat oil because of yams, one will eat yams because of oil.
interpretation_gold: If one does not perform a duty because one likes it, one performs it because it is the right thing to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Like proverbs, like proverbs are the pronouncements of Ifá.
interpretation_gold: The most profound speech is indirect and subtle.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ní mọ̀, ọ̀mọ̀ràn a mọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: If one says “Know,” the knowledgeable will know it.
interpretation_gold: The perceptive person can detect meaning in the slightest of signs.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ṣe ohun ńlá, à fi èpè gba ara ẹni là.
english_literal: If one has committed a great offense, one frees oneself by swearing (innocence).
interpretation_gold: One's greatest duty is one's self-preservation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá gbé ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sọ sínú omi gbígbóná, ká tún gbé e sọ sí tútù, kì í mọ èyí tó sàn.
english_literal: If one does not throw a toad into hot water, and then throw it into cold water, it does not know which is better.
interpretation_gold: It takes a change in circumstances to make one appreciate one's good fortune.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò ránni sọ́jà, ọjà kì í ránni sílé.
english_literal: If one does not send a message to the market, the market does not send a message to one at home.
interpretation_gold: Unless one makes an effort, one cannot expect rewards.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé kọ iyán àná, ìtàn la ó pa fún un.
english_literal: If a child refuses yesterday's pounded yams, it is stories one treats the child to.
interpretation_gold: A person who boycotts a meal or some entitlement simply deprives him/herself of some benefits.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Bùn mi níṣu kan” kì í ṣáájú “Ẹkú oko òo.”
english_literal: “Give me one yam” does not precede “Greetings to you on the farm.”
interpretation_gold: One does not ask a favor of, or transact any business with any person without first exchanging pleasantries with the person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọlọgbọ́n bá ńfi wèrè se iṣu, ọ̀mọ̀ràn a máa fi gègé yàn án.
english_literal: If a wise person is cooking yams in an insane way, a knowing person picks them with stakes.
interpretation_gold: If a person tries to mislead one, one finds one's own direction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí kókó bá dáni, a kì í jẹ orí ìmàdò; bí a bá jẹ orí ìmàdò, a kì í lọ sí àwùjọ póńpó; bí a bá lọ sí àwùjọ póńpó, ìwọ̀n ara ẹni là ńmọ̀.
english_literal: (If one is tripped by a protruding object one should not eat a wart-hog's head; if one eats a wart-hog's head, one should not go to a gathering of cudgels; if one goes to a gathering of cudgels, one should know one's place and act accordingly.
interpretation_gold: If unforseen circumstances force one to engage in risky behavior, one should be that much more careful.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bímọ rí, a kò ha rọ́mọ lẹ́hìn adìẹ?
english_literal: If one has never had a child, has one not seen chicks flocking after chickens?
interpretation_gold: Children are no novelty that any person does not know about.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá rántí ọjọ́ kan ìbálé, ká rántí ọjọ́ kan ìkúnlẹ̀ abiyamọ, ká rántí kan abẹ́ tí ńtani lára.
english_literal: If one remembers the day of (the loss of) virginity, one should also remember the day of a woman's delivery, and one should remember the vagina that smarts.
interpretation_gold: As one takes one's pleasures, one should be mindful of the pains that make them possible.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí Ọlọ́run-ún bá ti fọ̀tá ẹni hanni, kò lè pani mọ́.
english_literal: Once God has revealed one's enemy to one, he can no longer kill one.
interpretation_gold: Knowledge neutralizes dangers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá rí èké, à ṣebíèèyàn rere ni; à sọ̀rọ̀ ságbọ̀n a jò.
english_literal: When one sees a devious person one mistakes him for a good person; one talks into a basket and it leaks.
interpretation_gold: It is easy to mistake a bad person for a good person, and to place one's trust in that person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ilú bá dá sí méjì, tọba ọ̀rún là ńṣe.
english_literal: If the town is split into two, one does the will of the heavenly king.
interpretation_gold: If there is a division in one's group, one takes the side God would favor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá kìlọ̀ fólè, ká kìlọ̀ fóníṣu ẹ̀bá ọ̀nà.
english_literal: As one warns the thief, one should also warn the owner of the wayside yams.
interpretation_gold: The offender and the tempter both deserve blame.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá fi ọwọ́ ọ̀tún na ọmọ, à fi ọwọ́ òsì fà á mọ́ra.
english_literal: If one whips a child with the right hand, one embraces it with the left.
interpretation_gold: A child deserving punishment yet deserves love.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí alẹ́ kò lẹ́, òòbẹ̀ kì í fò.
english_literal: If night does not fall, the house bat does not fly.
interpretation_gold: All actions must await their auspicious moments.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá gbọ́n ju àparò oko ẹni lọ, a kì í pa á.
english_literal: If one is not more clever than the partridge on one's farm, one cannot kill it.
interpretation_gold: To succeed one must be more clever than one's adversary.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé ò bá rí oko baba ẹlòmíràn, a ní kò sí oko baba ẹni tó tó ti baba òun.
english_literal: If a youth has never seen another person's father's farm, he says no body's father's farm is as large as his father's.
interpretation_gold: Until one has seen other people's great accomplishments, one is overly impressed by one's own.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá ṣubú a wo iwájú; bí àgbá bá ṣubú a wo ẹ̀hìn.
english_literal: When a youth falls he looks ahead; when an elder falls he looks behind.
interpretation_gold: The youth is mindful of what his superiors think of him, while the elder is mindful of what the young think of him.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí eré bí eré, àlàbọrùn-ún dẹ̀wù.
english_literal: Like play, like play, the makeshift cape became a dress.
interpretation_gold: Imperceptibly, a stop-gap arrangement has become the status quo.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọ̀rán bá pẹ́ nílẹ̀, gbígbọ́n ní ńgbọ́n.
english_literal: If a problem remains long enough, it becomes clever.
interpretation_gold: If one keeps at it long enough, one will find the solution for any problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá dúpẹ́ ore àná, a rí tòní gbà.
english_literal: If a child expresses gratitude for yesterday's favor, he will receive today's.
interpretation_gold: The grateful person encourages others to do him more favors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá jẹ̀wọ́ tán ẹ̀rín là ńrín; bí a bá yó tán orun ní ńkunni.
english_literal: After a joke one gives way to laughter; after satiation one gives way to sleep.
interpretation_gold: The action should match the occasion.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá rí òwúrọ̀, alẹ́ ńkọ́?
english_literal: Although one has seen the morning, what about night time?
interpretation_gold: Nobody should be judged until he or she has reached the end of his or her days.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ régérégé bá ro ẹjọ́-ọ tirẹ̀ tán, kó rántí pé ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ mẹ́kí á rí rò.
english_literal: After the person with smooth cheeks has stated his or her case, he or she should remember that the person with blemished cheeks will have something to say.
interpretation_gold: The person who looks good owing to the efforts of his or her subordinates should remember that they also deserve some credit.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ojú bá mọ́, olówò a gbówò; ọ̀rànwú a gbé kẹ́kẹ́; ajagun a gbé apata; àgbẹ̀ a jí tòun tòrúkọ́; ọmọ ọdẹ a jí tapó tọrán; ajíwẹṣẹ a bá odò omi lọ.
english_literal: When day breaks, the trader takes up his trade; the cotton spinner picks up the spindle; the warrior grabs his shield; the farmer gets up with his hoe; the son of the hunter arises with his quiver and his bows; he-who-wakes-and-washes-with-soap makes his way to the river.
interpretation_gold: When morning comes, everybody should embark on something useful.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò ṣe ọdẹ rí, a kò lè mọ ẹsẹ̀-ẹ kò-lọ-ibẹ̀un.
english_literal: If one has never hunted, one would not know the tracks of “it-did-not-go-that-way.”
interpretation_gold: One is an ignoramus in a trade that is not one's own.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí o bá já ng ó so ọ́, kókó yó wà láàárín-in rẹ̀.
english_literal: “If you break I will retie you”; there will be a knot in it.
interpretation_gold: Something repaired is seldom the same as something unspoilt.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí obìnrin ò bá gbé ilé tó méjì, kì í mọ èyí tó sàn.
english_literal: If a woman has not lived in at least two homes, she never knows which is better.
interpretation_gold: Unless one has tasted some adversity, one does not appreciate one's good fortune.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá rádànán, à fòòbẹ̀ ṣẹbọ.
english_literal: If one cannot find a bat, one sacrifices a housebat.
interpretation_gold: One makes do with what one can find.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí túlàsí bá di méjì, ọ̀kan là ḿmú.
english_literal: When emergencies number two, one concentrates on one.
interpretation_gold: One concentrates on one problem at a time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọ̀bùn ò mọ èrè, a mọ ojú owó.
english_literal: If the filthy person does not know profit, he should know his capital.
interpretation_gold: If a person cannot improve a matter, he should not worsen it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí àrùn búburú bá wọ̀lú, oògùn búburú la fi ńwò ó.
english_literal: If a terrible epidemic descends on a town, it is confronted with a terrible medicine.
interpretation_gold: One matches the medicine to the disease.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ikún bá jẹ, bí ikún bá mu, ikún a wo oòrùn alẹ́.
english_literal: When the squirrel has eaten, when the squirrel has drunk, the squirrel looks at the setting sun.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one does, one should mind the passing of time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọwọ́ ò bá ṣeé ṣán, à ká a lérí.
english_literal: If the arms cannot be swung, one carries them on one's head.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot do as one would, one does what one can.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọ́ bá jágbọ́n-ọn kíkú, ìyá ẹ̀ a jágbọ́n-ọn sísin.
english_literal: If a child learns the trick of dying, his mother should learn the trick of burying.
interpretation_gold: One should learn to meet wiles with wiles.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá ḿbẹ́ igi, àgbàlagbà a máa wo ibi tí yó wòó sí.
english_literal: If a youth is felling a tree, an elder will be considering where it will fall.
interpretation_gold: Unlike the youth, the elder is mindful of consequences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ilẹ̀-ẹ́ bá laná, ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ á fò gun igi.
english_literal: If the earth catches fire, the toad will hop on a tree.
interpretation_gold: If one's position becomes untenable, one seeks refuge elsewhere.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọ́ bá jágbọ́n-ọn kíké, ìyá-a rẹ̀ a jágbọ́n-ọn rírẹ̀ ẹ́.
english_literal: If a child learns the trick of crying, the mother learns the trick of consoling him or her.
interpretation_gold: One must be ready to adapt to cope with any situation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ojú bá rí ọ̀rọ̀, a wò ó fín.
english_literal: When the eyes come upon a matter, they must look hard and well.
interpretation_gold: Imperfect understanding of a matter causes difficulties.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá sọ̀rọ̀ tán, ẹrín là ńrín; bí a bá yó tán orun ní ńkunni.
english_literal: When one is done discussing a matter one laughs, when one is satiated sleep claims one.
interpretation_gold: When a matter has been taken care of, one turns one's attention in the appropriate direction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí òrìṣá bá mú ẹlẹ́hìn, kí abuké máa múra sílẹ̀.
english_literal: If the gods take a person with a protruding back, the humpback should make ready.
interpretation_gold: If a person like one suffers a certain fate, one is at risk.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ńsunkún, à máa ríran.
english_literal: While one weeps, one can still see.
interpretation_gold: However accommodating one is, one should never take leave of one's good judgement.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí igí bá wó lu igi, tòkè là ńkọ́ gbé.
english_literal: If trees fall atop one another, one removes the topmost one first.
interpretation_gold: One should attend to affairs according to their urgency.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọ́ bá yó, a fikùn han baba.
english_literal: When a child is full, he shows his stomach to his father.
interpretation_gold: When one accomplishes one's goals, one feels like celebrating; also, one should show one's appreciation to one's benefactor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Báyìí là ńṣe” níbìkan, èèwọ̀ ibòmínìn.
english_literal: “This is what we do” in one place is taboo in another.
interpretation_gold: Different people, different ways.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí apá ò ká àràbà, apá lè ká egbò ìdí-i rẹ̀.
english_literal: If the arms cannot encompass the silk-cotton tree, they may encompass its root.
interpretation_gold: If one is no match for the father, one may be more than a match for the child.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ránni níṣẹ́ ẹrú, à fi jẹ́ tọmọ.
english_literal: If one is sent on an errand like a slave, one carries it out like a freeborn.
interpretation_gold: The well-bred person removes the flaws in a message sent through him, or a task given him to perform.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ta ará ilé ẹni lọ́pọ̀, a kì í rí i rà lọ́wọ̀n-ọ́n mọ́.
english_literal: If one sells a member of one's household cheap, one will not be able to buy him back at a great value.
interpretation_gold: Once one has besmirched the name of a person one is close to, one cannot later wipe it clean.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí olósùn-ún bá lọ osùn, ara-a rẹ̀ ní ńfi dánwò.
english_literal: When the camwood powder seller grinds the powder, she tests it on her own body.
interpretation_gold: One tries one's remedy on one's self before offering it to others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Baba-ìsìnkú ò fọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ sọfà; alábàáṣe ńfọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ kówó.
english_literal: The executor does not pawn his child; his helper pawns his own.
interpretation_gold: The obligated person holds back, while the helper risks his all.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Baálẹ̀ àgbẹ̀-ẹ́ ní òun ò ní nǹkan-án tà lọ́run, kí owó ọkà òún ṣáà ti pé.
english_literal: The chief of farmers says he has nothing to go to heaven to sell; all he cares about is fair payment for his corn.
interpretation_gold: If one does not ask for too much, one will not have to die to get it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Like proverbs, like proverbs one plays the ògìdìgbó music;
interpretation_gold: Only the wise can follow subtle discourses.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí nǹkán bá tán nílẹ̀, ọmọ ẹbọ a bọ́ síjó, àwọn tó wà níbẹ̀ a múra àti lọ.
english_literal: At the conclusion of a ceremony the acolyte commences to dance, and the onlookers prepare to make their exit.
interpretation_gold: One should not hang around after one's business is done.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá rígún a ò gbọdọ̀ ṣebọ; bí a ò bá rí àkàlà a ò gbọdọ̀ ṣorò.
english_literal: If we cannot find a vulture we may not offer a sacrifice; if we cannot find a ground hornbill we may not carry out a ritual.
interpretation_gold: Nothing can be accomplished in the absence of the requisite materials.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí kò bá tíì rẹ ìjà, a kì í là á.
english_literal: If a fight is not yet spent, one does not intervene to end it.
interpretation_gold: One cannot end a fight that is not yet willing to end.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Baálé àìlọ́wọ̀ ni àlejò àìlọ́wọ̀.
english_literal: An unsolicitous host makes for a visitor with no deference.
interpretation_gold: The visitor responds according to his reception.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dà-á-sílẹ̀-ká-tun-pín, ogún ijọ́un, a ò pín in re.
english_literal: The recent throw-it-all-on-the-floor-that-we-may-redistribute-it inheritance was not well distributed the first time around.
interpretation_gold: Whatever needs to be done again must not have been done well the first time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dùgbẹ̀-dùgbẹ̀ kì í fi ẹyin rẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: The egg-bearing spider never leaves its eggs behind.
interpretation_gold: One does not turn one's back on one's treasure.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ nimú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ fi ńwọgbà.
english_literal: It is bit by bit that the nose of the pig enters the fence.
interpretation_gold: A small problem, if not attended to, becomes unmanageable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dúró o kíkà; bí o ò dúró kíkà, ìkà a ba tìrẹ jẹ́.
english_literal: Stop and say hello to the wicked; if you do not say hello to the wicked, the wicked will find problems for you.
interpretation_gold: One's best defence against the wicked is ingratiation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dídì ní ḿmú abẹ mú.
english_literal: It is wrapping that makes a knife sharp.
interpretation_gold: Only by taking great care of them does one keep one's possessions in good shape.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
interpretation_gold: One should speak to others in a manner that befits one, and that will facilitate one's business with them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ebi ńpa mí ọlọ́ṣẹ ńkiri; ìgbà tí ng ò wẹnú ng ó ṣe wẹ̀de?
english_literal: I am hungry and the soap seller hawks her wares; when I have not washed my inside, how can I wash my outside?
interpretation_gold: One must order one's priorities sensibly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ejò-ó rí ihò tó há ó kó wọ̀ ọ́; ìyá-a rẹ̀-ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àti fà á yọ?
english_literal: A snake sees a tight hole and crawls into it; has its mother hands to pull it out?
interpretation_gold: One had better be certain that one would be able to extricate oneself before one ventures into tight spots.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-fẹ́-obìnrin-tẹ́nìkan-ńfẹ́, olúwarẹ̀ ò níí fẹ́ obìnrin ni.
english_literal: I-will-court-no-woman-being-courted-by-another-man will court no woman at all.
interpretation_gold: A person who wants exclusive rights to a woman (or anything) will look for a long time and in vain.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Eégún tí yó gbeni là ńdáṣọ fún; òrìṣà tí yó gbeni là ńsìn; bi igí bá gbè mí mà kó obì mà bọ igi.
english_literal: It is the masquerader that succors one that one makes shrouds for; it is the god that succors one that one worships; if a tree succors me, I will take kolanuts and worship the tree.
interpretation_gold: One should confine one's efforts to profitable ventures, and one's service to appreciative people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ebi ò pàmọ̀le ó ní òun ò jẹ àáyá; ebí pa Súlè ó jọ̀bọ.
english_literal: The muslim is not hungry and he vows he will not eat a red Colobus monkey; hunger gripped Suleiman and he ate a monkey.
interpretation_gold: A desperate person is seldom finicky.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èrò kì í mọ ibùsọ̀ kọ́rùn ó wọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: A wayfarer does not know the location of the rest stop and yet have his neck crushed from the weight of a heavy load.
interpretation_gold: One measures one's exertions to suit one's capacity.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èyí tó yẹ ará iwájú, èrò ẹ̀hìn fiyè sílẹ̀.
english_literal: (To) what turned out favorably for those going ahead, you coming behind, pay close attention.
interpretation_gold: Learn from the examples of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-ṣu-imí-le-imí, olúwarẹ̀ ó rìn jìnnà ààtàn.
english_literal: I-will-not-defecate-on-existing-excrement will walk a good distance into the bush.
interpretation_gold: People who are too finicky will pay in effort and delay for their habits.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èpè la fi ńwo èpè sàn.
english_literal: Curses are the antidote for curses.
interpretation_gold: One matches the remedy to the affliction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Epo lojú ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: Palm-oil is the countenance of stew.
interpretation_gold: One should be particularly attentive to that one ingredient or thing whose absence mars the entire project.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Elékuru kì í kiri lóko.
english_literal: The seller of steamed ground beans does not hawk her wares on a farm.
interpretation_gold: One wastes one's time attempting to sell things to those who produce them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ ò ṣe-e fiṣu ṣọ́.
english_literal: A goat is not a wise choice as the guard over yams.
interpretation_gold: Do not entrust your affairs to your enemy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èló là ńra adìẹ òkókó, tí à ńgba ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ sìn?
english_literal: How much does a hen cost that one would contract to raise chicks for the owner?
interpretation_gold: Certain obligations are not worth the trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ètò lòfin kìn-ín-ní lóde ọ̀run.
english_literal: Order is the first law in heaven.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one does, one must be orderly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ète lẹ̀gbọ́n; ìmọ̀ràn làbúrò; bí-a-ó-ti-ṣe lẹ̀kẹta wọn.
english_literal: Intention is the eldest, contemplation is the next, and plan of action is the third.
interpretation_gold: First there is the goal, next a contemplation of it, and finally a plan for attaining it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Epo ló ṣeé jẹṣu; àkàsọ̀ ló ṣeé gun àká; obìnrín dùn-ún bá sùn ju ọkùnrin lọ.
english_literal: It is palm oil that goes best with yams; it is a ladder that is best for climbing granaries; a woman is more pleasant to make love to than a man.
interpretation_gold: Certain things are fit for certain purposes; not anything will do anytime.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Fi ìjà fún Ọlọ́run jà, fọwọ́ lérán.
english_literal: Leave the fighting to God, sit back and watch.
interpretation_gold: One should leave those who have injured one to God's judgement and punishment.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Fimí-pamọ́-kí-npa-ọ́ làrùn ńjẹ́.
english_literal: Hide-me-and-I-will-kill-you is the name a disease answers to.
interpretation_gold: A concealed disease is a deadly thing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Gba ọmọ fún mi kí nrèdí”; bí ìdí ò bá ṣe-é re ká gbọ́mọ fọ́lọ́mọ.
english_literal: “Hold my child for me so I may wiggle my buttocks”; if one cannot wiggle one's buttocks one should return the child to its mother.
interpretation_gold: One should not place oneself in difficulty in order to help others out of difficulty.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbọ̀nwọ́ ti kékeré yọké.
english_literal: The elbow develops a hump right from its youth.
interpretation_gold: Said of a precocious person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbín ìbá má mọ̀-ọ́ jẹ̀ kò tó okòó.
english_literal: Had the snail been careless in its foraging it would not “have grown large enough to” be worth twenty cowries.
interpretation_gold: With caution one can offset the effects of any handicap.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Iṣú ta iṣu ò ta, ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńwúṣu lébè.
english_literal: Whether the yams are large or not, it is one by one that one extracts them from the heap.
interpretation_gold: There is no task that is so small or insignificant that it does not deserve care and attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ àmúyọ, a kì í sin kádìí tán.
english_literal: One does not string decorative beads all around one's waist.
interpretation_gold: One should not deploy all one's resources at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìwò-o ọlọgbọ́n ò jọ ti aṣiwèrè.
english_literal: The way a wise person looks at things is different from the way an imbecile does.
interpretation_gold: A wise person considers matter in a more rational way than an imbecile does.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ilẹ̀ nìjòkò ńjókòó de ìdí.
english_literal: It is on the ground that the stool sits to await the buttocks.
interpretation_gold: One should maintain one's place and not, for example, go out of the house to receive a visitor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Iná tó ńlérí omi á kù sọnù.
english_literal: The fire that challenges water will die off.
interpretation_gold: It is foolhardy to take on a power one is no match for.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìtórò tó so lóko tí kò fẹ̀hìntì, afẹ́fẹ́ oko ní ńtú u.
english_literal: The lemon plant that grows in the bush and does not support itself against something will be uprooted by the forest breeze.
interpretation_gold: A weak person who has no support will fall victim to puny forces.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí oyín gbé ńhó, tí àdó ńhó, ìfun ò dákẹ́ lásán.
english_literal: As the bees hum and the small calabash containing charms hums, the intestine does not keep silent.
interpretation_gold: No matter what other people's preoccupations are, one should not ignore one's own problems.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí a ti ńjẹun bí ikun bí ikun, a kì í sọ̀rọ̀ bíi kẹ̀lẹ̀bẹ̀ bíi kẹ̀lẹ̀bẹ̀ níbẹ̀.
english_literal: Where one is eating food like mucus, one should not bring up matters like phlegm.
interpretation_gold: One must be careful not to bring up matters that are too sensitive for present company.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí a bá ńgbé la ti ńgbàwìn; à-rà-àì-san ni ò sunwọ̀n.
english_literal: One's home is a legitimate place to buy things on credit; what is bad is avoiding payment.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing wrong in seeking favors from those close to one; what is bad is not returning favors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Igbá tó gbédè là ḿpè lóṣùwọ̀n.
english_literal: It is a calabash that understands one's language that one describes as a measure.
interpretation_gold: One places one's confidence only in those of the same mind with one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí òjò-ó ti ńpa igún bọ̀-ọ́ jìnnà; ta ní rán igún níṣẹ́?
english_literal: The vulture has endured the drenching rain from a great distance, but who sent the vulture on an errand?
interpretation_gold: If one's choices land one in difficulty, one should not blame others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìlọ-ọ́ ya, oníbodè Atàdí; wọ́n kó o nílé, wọ́n gbà á lóbìnrin, ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ tó ní òun ó fi wádìí ọ̀ràn, ajá gbé e, ọmọ ẹ̀ tó lé ajá láti gba ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀, ó yí sí kàǹga; oníbodè Atàdí wá dáhùn ó ní, “Ìlọ-ọ́ yá.”
english_literal: It is time to get out of here, the gatekeeper of Atadi; his home was burglarized, his wife was taken from him, the divining string he was going to use to investigate matters was snatched by a dog, his son who ran after the dog to retrieve the divining string fell into a well; the gatekeeper of Atadi then spoke up and said, “It is time to get out of here.”
interpretation_gold: When a place becomes too hot for a person, he/she should know it is time to get out.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìyàwó ṣe ọ̀ràn kan tán; ọkọ ẹ̀-ẹ́ ṣe ọ̀ràn-an nkò-jẹ-mọ́.
english_literal: The wife has done the unpardonable; her husband has adopted an I-will-not-eat-any-longer attitude.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who have caused unpardonable offence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìloro là ńwọ̀ ká tó wọlé.
english_literal: One enters the porch first before one enters the house.
interpretation_gold: Everything in its proper order.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbín ìbá má mọ̀-ọ́ jẹ̀ ìbá ti kú síjù.
english_literal: Had the snail been careless in its foraging it would have died in the bush.
interpretation_gold: However disadvantaged one might be, one could still thrive if one took life easy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí òjò-ó bá ọjọ́ ní ńpa á sí.
english_literal: Wherever the rain catches up with the day, there it drenches it.
interpretation_gold: One should do what one has to do as the opportunities present themselves.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ijó ní ḿbọ́ṣọ, ìjà ní ḿbọ́ ẹ̀wù.
english_literal: It is dance that strips one of one's cloth; it is a fight that takes off one's shirt.
interpretation_gold: Different situations call for different responses.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí a ti gùn, ibẹ̀ la ti ńrọ̀.
english_literal: Where one began one's climb, there one effects one's descent.
interpretation_gold: One must not shift the problems originating in one context to another, unrelated context.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìpàṣán tí a fi na ìyálé ḿbẹ láàjà fún ìyàwó.
english_literal: The whip used on the senior wife is resting on the rafters waiting for the new wife.
interpretation_gold: One should not assume that the misfortune that befell those who went before one will pass one over.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí à ńgbé là ńṣe; bí a bá dé ìlú adẹ́tẹ̀ à di ìkúùkù.
english_literal: One should live according to the customs and fashions of the place one finds oneself in; if one lands in the city of lepers, one should make a fist, i.e., conceal one's fingers.
interpretation_gold: While in Rome, do as the Romans do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí o máa sùn lo tẹ́ ọmọ sí.
english_literal: It is precisely where you will eventually have to sleep that you have laid down your child to sleep.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person deceiving himself or herself, in the futile hope that a transparent ruse will work to his/her advantage.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Igbá là ńpa, a kì í pa àwo.
english_literal: It is a calabash that one cuts decorative patterns on; one does not cut patterns on china plates.
interpretation_gold: What is appropriate treatment for one thing may be inappropriate for another.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ibi tí a gbé epo sí a kì í sọ òkò síbẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not throw rocks at the place where one has one's palm-oil stored.
interpretation_gold: One should always protect one's base or where one's best interests lie.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Iná èsìsì kì í jóni lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: The fire of the stinging tragia plant does not burn a person twice.
interpretation_gold: One should learn a lesson from the first bad experience.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìyàwó sọ ọ̀rọ̀ kan tán: ó ní ìyálé òun a-bẹnu-funfun-bí-ègbodò.
english_literal: The junior wife has said what will be her last; she said the senior wife's mouth is as white as the new yam.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who have done the unthinkable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbà ara là ḿbúra.
english_literal: One swears when it is time to swear.
interpretation_gold: Everything in its proper time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìṣeǹṣe ewúrẹ́, kágùntàn fiyè síi.
english_literal: The fate that has befallen the goat, the sheep should bear in mind.
interpretation_gold: One should learn from the fates of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbà òjò ńlọ, ìgbà ẹ̀rùn ńlọ, a ní ká dí isà eku kó le; ìgbà wo la óò tó wá peku náà?
english_literal: The rainy season passes, the dry season passes, and the suggestion is that the rat's burrow be sealed up tight; when will the time be ripe to kill the rat?
interpretation_gold: One must do what needs to be done while there is still time, rather than resort to transparent temporizing ruses.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìdí òwò ni òwòó gbé tà.
english_literal: It is at its home base that a company or trade prospers.
interpretation_gold: One would be wise to protect one's base.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ikúdú pa ẹṣin à ńyọ̀; ó ḿbọ̀ wá pa ọmọ èèyàn.
english_literal: An abandoned well kills a horse and we rejoice; it will in time kill a human being.
interpretation_gold: One should take other people's misfortunes as a reminder that one also is not immune to such misfortunes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìbéèrè kì í jẹ́ kí ẹni ó ṣìnà; ẹni tí kò lè béèrè ní ńnpọ́n ara ẹ̀ lójú.
english_literal: Asking “directions” keeps one from losing one's way; the person who refuses to ask is responsible for his/her own difficulties.
interpretation_gold: One should not be too obstinate or too proud to seek help when one needs it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Isó inú ẹ̀kú, à-rá-mọ́ra.
english_literal: The fart within a masquerader's shroud “is” something to be endured.
interpretation_gold: The insult one cannot escape from, one has to endure.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ilé olóńjẹ là ńdẹ̀bìtì àyà sí.
english_literal: It is in the home of a person who has food that one sets one's chest like a trap.
interpretation_gold: People usually position themselves where they imagine there is something to gain.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìyàwó mi ò sunwọ̀; nítorí ọmọ ni mo ṣe fẹ́ ẹ; ẹni mélòó la ó wìí fún tán?
english_literal: “My wife is not good looking, but I married her for the sake of children”; to how many people will one give that explanation?
interpretation_gold: One should not embark on the endless and futile task of justifying one's decisions to people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Igúnnugún ò torí abẹ párí.
english_literal: The vulture did not go bald for fear of the razor.
interpretation_gold: One's actions are not determined by one's fear of any person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbà tí a bá rẹni lòwúrọ̀ ẹni.
english_literal: Whenever one first sees a person, that is that person's morning.
interpretation_gold: One does what one has to do when it is convenient for one to do it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbà tí a bá dóko làárọ̀ ẹni.
english_literal: The time of one's arrival on the farm is one's dawn.
interpretation_gold: People must not be slaves of time but use time to their own advantage.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ilé ajá là ńwá ìwo lọ?
english_literal: Is a dog's house the place to go in search of horns?
interpretation_gold: One should not bark up wrong trees.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Igbó lẹranko ńgbé.
english_literal: The forest is the home for animals to live in.
interpretation_gold: Everything in its proper place.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Iná kúkú ni yó ba ọbẹ̀ ará oko jẹ́.
english_literal: It is too much fire that will ruin the stew of a bushman.
interpretation_gold: An ignorant person will ruin whatever venture he/she embarks on with his/her ignorance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìjà ní ńpa onítìjú; ogun ní ḿpa alágbára.
english_literal: A street fight is the death of a bashful person; warring is the death of a strong man.
interpretation_gold: One should not rather court danger or disaster simply to avoid losing face.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Já ilé ẹ̀ kí mbá ẹ kọ́ ọ”; ìtẹ́ èèkàn kan ní ńfúnni.
english_literal: “Unroof your house and I will help you re-roof it” usually gives one only one bundle of thatching grass.
interpretation_gold: One relies on other people's promise of help only at one's risk.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Jùrù-fẹ̀fẹ̀ jùrù-fẹ̀fẹ̀, ewúrẹ́ wọ ilé àpọn jùrù-fẹ̀fẹ̀; kí làpọ́n rí jẹ tí yó kù sílẹ̀ féwúrẹ́?
english_literal: Busily wagging tail, busily wagging tail, a goat enters a bachelor's house busily wagging its tail; what does a bachelor have to eat whose left-over the goat can have?
interpretation_gold: One wastes one's time expecting some largesse from a destitute person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kókó ló kọ́kọ́ dé orí, tàbí orí ló kọ́kọ́ dé kókó?
english_literal: Was it the lump that first got to the head, or the head that first got to the lump?
interpretation_gold: A chastisement for someone attempting to reverse the order of precedence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kí ni à ńwọ̀ nínú-u ṣòkòtò mẹ́ta ọ̀ọ́dúnrún?
english_literal: What is there to wear in a pair of trousers bought at three for three hundred cowries, or three a penny?
interpretation_gold: Much ado about a worthless thing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kéré-kéré leku ńjawọ; díẹ̀-díẹ̀ leèrà ḿbọ́ ìyẹ́.
