english_literal: Bit by bit the rat consumes the leather; gently gently the ant sloughs its skin.
interpretation_gold: One should use caution in all one's enterprises.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kì í jẹ́ kí etí ẹni di kì í jẹ kí inú ẹni dùn.
english_literal: Whatever keeps one from being deaf to certain things keeps one from being happy.
interpretation_gold: One should learn to turn a deaf ear to certain things for the sake of one's peace of mind.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kì í ṣe gbogbo ẹni tí ńṣe “Ẹni Ọlọ́rún bùn ó bùn mi” là ńfún ní nǹkan.
english_literal: It is not to every person who says “Whoever has received some bounty from God should give to me” that one gives alms.
interpretation_gold: One should be judicious as to those to whom one shows kindness.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kóǹkólóyo: èyí tó ní tèmi.
english_literal: A rather small thing: this is enough for me.
interpretation_gold: However small it is “usually a child”, one is glad to have it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kàkà kí ọmọdé pàgbà láyò, àgbà a fi ọgbọ́n àgbà gbé e.
english_literal: Instead of permitting defeat by a child in a game, an elder should resort to elderly wiles.
interpretation_gold: An elder should protect his face and standing by all means available.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kò sí ẹni tí kò mọ ọgbọ́n-ọn ká fẹran sẹ́nu ká wá a tì.
english_literal: There is nobody who does not know the trick of putting meat in the mouth and making it disappear.
interpretation_gold: Nobody is a complete fool.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kò sí aláásáà tí ńta ìgbokú; gbogbo wọn ní ńta oyin.
english_literal: There is no snuff seller who will advertise her ware as awful; they all say they are selling honey.
interpretation_gold: Everybody presents himself/herself in the best light.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Kí ni ìyá aláṣọ ńtà tó yọ ẹgba lọ́wọ́? Ewúrẹ́ ńjẹ wúlìnì?
english_literal: What is the cloth-selling woman have to sell that she carries a whip in her hand?
interpretation_gold: One should not engage in meaningless or unnecessary activities.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Lójú òpè, bí-i kọ́lọgbọ́n dàbí ọ̀lẹ.
english_literal: As far as the dunce is concerned, the wise person should rather be shiftless.
interpretation_gold: The worthless person always wishes others were equally worthless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Màá kó ẹrú, màá kó ẹrù” là ḿbá lọ sógun; ọ̀nà lẹnìkẹta ḿbáni.
english_literal: “I will capture slaves and I will capture loot” is what one has in mind on departure for a war; the third one comes upon one only along the way.
interpretation_gold: Too often one is so preoccupied with the good aspects of a proposition that the bad aspects sneak up on one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Máa jẹ́ ǹṣó” lọ̀yà fi ńju ẹmọ́ lọ.
english_literal: “Go on feeding” is what makes the cane rat fatter than the Tullberg's rat.
interpretation_gold: Excessive consideration for others can be disadvantageous.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Mójú-kúrò nilé ayé gbà; gbogbo ọ̀rọ̀ kọ́ ló ṣéé bínú sí.
english_literal: Judicious forebearance is the wise approach to the world; not every matter deserve to be angry at.
interpretation_gold: The best way to live is to ignore petty annoyances.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Màjèṣín dóbò àkọ́kọ́, ó sáré yọ okó síta, ó ní Olúwa-á ṣeun.
english_literal: The tender youth has sex for the first time ever, pulls out his penis prematurely, and says “God be praised!”
interpretation_gold: A novice knows not how to relish good things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ní ìlú tí a ò ti fẹ́ ẹyẹlé, tí a ò fẹ́ adìẹ, irú ẹyẹ wo ní yóò jí wọn lójù orun?
english_literal: In a town that does not tolerate pigeons and does not tolerate chickens, what sort of bird will awaken them from sleep?
interpretation_gold: A person who will not be pleased by anything will simply have to do without everything.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Nítorí èèyàn la ṣe ńní ọwọ́ ọ̀tún; òsì là bá lò.
english_literal: It is on account of people that one has a right hand; one could do with only a left hand otherwise.
interpretation_gold: One must learn the grace that is appropriate for decent company.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Nígbàtí ọwọ́ ò tí ì gbọ́n lojú ńṣepin.
english_literal: It is when the hands have not learned wisdom that the eyes ooze matter.
interpretation_gold: A wise person will know how to manage and conceal his shortcomings.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Nítorí-i ká lè ríbi gbé e la ṣe ńṣe ọyàn sódó.
english_literal: It is so that one would have a means of lifting it that one carves breasts [handles] on the mortar.
interpretation_gold: One should anticipate problems and prepare solutions for them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Níbo ló gbé wà?” nìyájú ẹkùn.
english_literal: “Where is it?” is a great insult to the leopard.
interpretation_gold: One should be smart enough to hide one's ignorance about things one should know.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ní ìlú tí a ò ti fẹ́ ẹyẹlé, adìẹ yóò ṣọ̀wọ́n níbẹ̀.
english_literal: In a town that does not welcome pigeons, chickens will be very scarce there.
interpretation_gold: Onerous things will not be countenanced where easy obligations are not.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Nítorí adití lòjò fi ńṣú; nítorí afọ́jú ló ṣe ńkù.
english_literal: It is for the benefit of deaf people that rain clouds gather; it is for the benefit of the blind that thunder rumbles.
interpretation_gold: The wise person should be able to read portents and take precautions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tó ní òun óò bẹ́ni lórí, bó bá ṣíni ní fìlà, ká dúpẹ́.
english_literal: If a thing that vows to decapitate one only knocks off one's hat, one shounld be thankful.
interpretation_gold: If the misfortune that befalls one turns out to be far milder than one expected, one should give thanks.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olòṣì ọmọ ní ńfọwọ́ òṣì júwe ilé-e baba-a ẹ̀.
english_literal: It is a worthless child that points the way to his father's house with his left-hand fingers.
interpretation_gold: One should show proper regard for one's own patrimony.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Owó tọ́mọdé bá kọ́kọ́ ní, àkàrà ní ńfi-í rà.
english_literal: The first money a youth comes into he spends on bean fritters.
interpretation_gold: The youth seldom know how to manage their wealth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Oko kì í jẹ́ ti baba àti tọmọ kó má nìí àlà.
english_literal: Farms do not, by virtue of belonging to a father and his son, lack boundaries.
interpretation_gold: Even close relatives may benefit from good fences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Owó kì í lóye kọ́mọ kú sẹ́rú.
english_literal: If the amount of money is known, a child cannot die in slavery.
interpretation_gold: One does not endure adverse conditions when one is capable of the effort to escape them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O kò wọ bàtà nínù ẹ̀gún ò ńsáré; o lágbára màlúù?
english_literal: You have no shoes on on the thorny path and yet you are running; do you have a cow's “hoof” power?
interpretation_gold: Unless one is well fortified one should not court danger.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Okotorobo-ó yé ẹyin sílẹ̀, àdàbà ńgarùn wo ẹyin ẹlẹ́yin.
english_literal: Okotorobo the bird lays an egg, and the turtle dove stretches its neck to inspect the egg that does not belong to it.
interpretation_gold: One should mind one's own business.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O fi awọ ẹkùn ṣẹbọ àìkú; ẹkùn ìbá má kùú ìwọ ìbá rawọ ẹ̀ ṣoògùn?
english_literal: You use a leopard's skin as an ingredient for medicine to hold off death; had the leopard not died would you have had access to its hide for the medicine?
interpretation_gold: One should not chase impossible dreams.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ogún mbókòó? Òwe aṣiwèrè.
english_literal: Twenty or a score? An imbecile's puzzle.
interpretation_gold: Trust an imbecile to pose stupid questions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ojú tó rọ̀ nirorẹ́ ńsọ.
english_literal: Pimples attack only faces that are delicate.
interpretation_gold: People always take advantage of gentle people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Orín yí, ìlù-ú yí padà.
english_literal: The song changes, and the drumming changes to suit.
interpretation_gold: One should match one's behavior to one's circumstances.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Ó ṣe mí rí”; ògbó adìẹ-ẹ́ rí àwòdì sá.
english_literal: “I have experienced it before”; a grown chicken flees at the sight of a kite.
interpretation_gold: One learns to run from danger once one has recognized it for what it is.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Onígi ní ńfigi ẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀.
english_literal: It is the firewood seller who sets a low price for his wares.
interpretation_gold: People take their cue from the owner of a thing in placing a value on it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Okotorobo-ó tùyẹ́ sílẹ̀ ọmọ titún ńgbe jó; ó ní ó rọ òun lọ́rùn lòún tu ú?
english_literal: Okotorobo, a bird, casts away a feather, and a young chick picks it up to dance with it; the one who shed the feathers asks, would I have discarded it if it was not a nuisance.
interpretation_gold: One should be careful before taking over things that others have rejected.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Owú pani ju kùm̀mọ̀.
english_literal: Jealousy kills more surely than a cudgel.
interpretation_gold: Jealousy is a dangerous thing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olóhun kì í rí ohun ẹ̀ kó pè é lórò.
english_literal: The owner will not see what he owns and call it a fearful; abomination.
interpretation_gold: One cannot be fearful of what one owns.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olóhun-ún dolè; “Gbà bù jẹ́” dolóhun.
english_literal: The owner becomes a thief; “Take this and eat” becomes the owner.
interpretation_gold: The tables are turned, such that the rightful owner is displaced by a usurper.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Orí ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ popo láwo; bí a wí fọ́mọ ẹni a gbọ́ràn.
english_literal: The squirrel's head sits in a plate like a lump; if one counsels one's child it should listen.
interpretation_gold: Refusal to listen to counsel leads to disaster.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká mu ìṣápá; òùngbẹ kì í gbẹni ká mu ẹ̀jẹ̀.
english_literal: One is never so desperate that one drinks red sorrel juice; one is never so thirsty that one drinks blood.
interpretation_gold: Desperation must never push one beyond the bounds of acceptable behavior.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Oòrùn kì í jẹ iṣu àgbà kó má mọbẹ̀.
english_literal: An elder does not lose his yams to the sun without knowing where the event happened.
interpretation_gold: A grown up person should know where he went wrong and make amends accordingly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òjòwú ò lẹ́ran láyà.
english_literal: The jealous woman lacks flesh on her chest.
interpretation_gold: Excessive jealousy eats up the jealous.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O ní kí ará ọ̀run ṣe oore fún ọ; bẹ́ẹ̀ni o rí ẹni tí eégún ńlé, tó fá lọ́bẹ̀ lá.
english_literal: You pray to the being from heaven to grant you a boon; yet you can see the person being chased by the masquerader and whose stew the masquerader has consumed.
interpretation_gold: One should not expect to receive better treatment from a person who is known to be vicious to others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olówó á wá; aláwìn á wá; ìlú tí à ńgbé la gbé ńgbàwìn; à-rà-àì-san ni ò súnwọ̀n.
english_literal: Those who have money will come, and those who will buy on credit will come; it is in one's town that one buys on credit; failure to eventually pay up is what is bad.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing bad about buying on credit, as long as one eventually pays.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òwú kì í là kínú bí olóko.
english_literal: The cotton seed does not open and thus anger the farmer.
interpretation_gold: The success of one's venture does not make one angry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Ó ḿbọ̀, ó ḿbọ̀!” la fi ńdẹ́rù ba ọmọdé; bó bá dé tán ẹ̀rù a tán.
english_literal: “It's coming! It's coming!” is what one says to frighten a child; after it has arrived it loses all its terror.
interpretation_gold: Looming problems often cause consternation out of all proportion to their real damaging force.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tí kò jẹ́ káṣọ pé méjì ni ò jẹ́ kó dú.
english_literal: The same thing that keeps one from having more than one item of clothing also keeps that one from blackening from dirt.
interpretation_gold: Misfortune teaches one fortitude; scarcity teaches one to be thrifty.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Òkè ìhín ò jẹ́ ká rí tọ̀ún” ò ṣéé pa lówe nílé àna ẹni.
english_literal: “The nearer hill kept one from seeing the farther one” is not a proverb one uses in one's parents-in-law's home.
interpretation_gold: There are some obligations one cannot sidestep with flippant excuses.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Orí tó kọ ẹrù, owó ní ńnáni.
english_literal: A head that refuses “to carry” loads will cost its owner some money.
interpretation_gold: It costs money to get others to do for one what one refuses to do for oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ó ti ojú orun wá ó ńfọ ẹnà; ó ní “ẹ jẹ́ ká máa ji ní mẹ́mu-mẹ́mu.”
english_literal: He woke up from sleep and spoke in scrambled language; he said, “Let us wake it in moos.”
interpretation_gold: An ignorant person will always make stupid suggestions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Orin tí ò ṣoro-ó dá kì í ṣòro-ó gbè; bí ó bá ní “héééé,” à ní “háááá.”
english_literal: A song that is not difficult to lead is not difficult to follow; if the leader sings “haaaay,” one responds “haaaah.”
interpretation_gold: One expends on a task only the amount of effort commensurate with it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O sá fún ikú, o bọ́ sí àkọ̀ idà.
english_literal: You run from death and seek refuge in a scabbard.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who has got himself/herself in a worse predicament from the one he/she was fleeing from.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; adámú fi sàárà san ẹgbẹ̀ta.
english_literal: The goitered person sets a low price on beads; the person with a blocked nose repays six thousand cowries with alms.
interpretation_gold: One usually sets little value on what one cannot use.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ogún kì í pọ̀ ká pín fún aládùúgbò.
english_literal: The inheritance is never so abundant that one shares it with neighbors.
interpretation_gold: However abundantly one is blessed one should manage one's resources wisely.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olóògùn ní ńṣe bí a-láigbọ́-mọ̀ràn; bí ogun ó bàá wọ̀lú ọlọgbọ́n là ńfọ̀rọ̀ lọ̀.
english_literal: The medicine man behaves like a person impervious to wise counsel; if war threatens a town the person to consult for counsel is the sage.
interpretation_gold: Trust rather in wisdom than in magical charms.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olé tó jí kàkàkí, níbo ni yó ti fọn ọ́n?
english_literal: A thief who stole a bugle, where will he blow it?
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's efforts chasing something one can never use.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Odó iyán ò jẹ́ gún ẹ̀lú; odó ẹ̀lú ò jẹ́ gúnyán; àtẹ tá-a fi ńpàtẹ ìlẹ̀kẹ̀, a ò jẹ́ fi pàtẹ ọ̀rúnlá.
english_literal: The mortar used for pounding yams will not do for pounding indigo leaves; the mortar for pounding indigo leaves will not do for yams; the tray on which beads are displayed for sale will not do for displaying dried okro.
interpretation_gold: Each object has its proper uses.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òjòwú ò já gèlè; kooro ló lè já.
english_literal: The jealous woman does not snatch her head gear off; all she can do is threaten a fight.
interpretation_gold: Some people are all mouth and no action.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ó ńti ilé bọ̀ kò ra ẹ̀gbẹ; ó dé oko tán ó ní ẹ̀gbẹ ni oníkú ẹ̀kọ.
english_literal: Leaving the home he did not purchase dried meat; after arriving on the farm he says dried meat is the indispensable thing to eat corn loaf with.
interpretation_gold: One should make provisions against one's future needs.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olóúnjẹ-ẹ́ tó-ó bá kú.
english_literal: Someone who has food is worth dying with.
interpretation_gold: Food is a good enough reason to cast one's lot with another person's.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Onígbèsè tí ńpa àpatà ẹyẹ́lé.
english_literal: Habitual debtor who butchers a pigeon for sale.
interpretation_gold: The debtor is desperate, because there is not much to a pigeon, and few people eat pigeons anyway.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Owó la fi ńlògbà; ọgbọ́n la fi ńgbélé ayé.
english_literal: It is with money that we secure pleasures; it is with wisdom that one secures a good life.
interpretation_gold: Riches are desirable, but wisdom is more valuable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tí a ṣe nílé àna ẹni, “Ojú ńtì mí” kúrò níbẹ̀.
english_literal: What one does in the home of one's parents-in-law leaves no room for “I am bashful.”
interpretation_gold: One must not be reticent in doing whatever one must do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Owó ní ńpa ọjà ọ̀mọ̀ràn.
english_literal: It is money that brings a knowing person's trading to a conclusion.
interpretation_gold: A wise trader knows how to use his money to make his offer successful.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ó di kan-nu-rin kan-nu-rin, agogo Ògúntólú.
english_literal: All one hears is noise without pattern, like that of Oguntolu's bell.
interpretation_gold: The statements being made are senseless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ojú kì í ti eégún kó má mọ̀nà ìgbàlẹ̀.
english_literal: A masquerader is never so shamed that he cannot find his way to the secret grove.
interpretation_gold: One cannot become so shamed abroad that one cannot return to the embrace of one's home.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O kò bá òkun máwo, o ò bá ọ̀sà mulẹ̀; abẹ́rẹ́ ẹ-ẹ́ bọ́ sódò o ní o ó yọ ọ́.
english_literal: You made no secret pact with the lagoon and you entered into no covenant with the ocean; yet when your needle dropped into the stream you proposed to retrieve it.
interpretation_gold: Unless one has extraordinary means one should not attempt the impossible.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tí a ni la fi ńkẹ́ ọmọ ẹni.
english_literal: It is what one has that one uses to spoil one's child.
interpretation_gold: One should not go beyond one's means simply to make a good impression on others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tó ní òun óò ṣeni lẹ́rú, tó wá ṣeni níwọ̀fà, ká gbà á.
english_literal: If whatever promised to make one a slave only makes one a pawn, one should accept one's fate.
interpretation_gold: One should gratefully accept a fate that turns out more merciful than what could have been.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tí a ò rí rí lèèwọ̀ ojú.
english_literal: It is something one has never seen before that is taboo for the eyes.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one has encountered before cannot be too much for one to accommodate.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Oko mímọ́ ṣe-é ro; ọ̀nà mímọ́ dùn-ún tọ̀; gbogbo ìyàwó dùn-ún gbàbálé; aṣọ ìgbà-á ṣe-é yọ.
english_literal: A clean farm is a pleasure to weed; a clean-swept path is a pleasure to trod; all new wives are a pleasure to deflower; the new fashionable cloth of the season is a pleasure to wear.
interpretation_gold: Everybody loves performing the most pleasant of chores.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òmùgọ̀ ní ńgbé ígunnu; ọlọgbọ́n ní ńgbowó.
english_literal: It is the fool that wears the Nupe masquerade; it is the wise person that collects the monetary gifts.
interpretation_gold: The wise person chooses the most profitable option available.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O kò lu òmìrán lóru, ò ńlù ú lọ́sàn-án.
english_literal: You did not hit the giant at night time, but you hit him in daylight.
interpretation_gold: One should court trouble only if and when one has some cover.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O rí etí adẹ́tẹ̀ o fi san okòó; kò nípọn tó ni, tàbí kò rẹ̀ dẹ̀dẹ̀ tọ́?
english_literal: You see a leper's ears and you value it at twenty cowries; does it lack sufficient thickness or is it not red enough?
interpretation_gold: Said of someone who applies the wrong value to things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olówó pèlù o ò jó; ọjọ́ wo lo máa rówó pe tìẹ?
english_literal: A rich person engages a dance band and you do not dance; when will you have the money to hire your own band?
interpretation_gold: One should take advantage of every opportunity to supply one's deficiencies.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Odídẹrẹ́ dawo, ìkó ìdí ẹ̀-ẹ́ dọ̀gbẹ̀rì.
english_literal: The parrot becomes fully initiated into the secrets, his tail feather becomes a non-initiate.
interpretation_gold: The person being propped up achieves great glory, but his backer loses his standing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òjò òì dá a ní kò tó tàná.
english_literal: It has not yet stopped raining and some observe that today's rainfall is not as much as yesterday's.
interpretation_gold: One should not arrive at conclusions until one has all the facts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ò ḿbẹ oníṣègùn, o ò bẹ asínwín; bí oníṣègùn-ún ṣe tí asínwín ò gbà ńkọ́?
english_literal: You are pleading with the medicine man but not with the demented person; what if the medicine man produces the medicine and the demented person refuses it?
interpretation_gold: When two steps are required to accomplish a purpose, one should not take one and slight the other.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òbò ò ṣé ṣe àlejò.
english_literal: The vagina is not a thing for showing hospitality.
interpretation_gold: Good things are not good for all purposes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òkú ẹran kì í ti ajá lójú.
english_literal: A dog is never to squeamish to eat a carcase.
interpretation_gold: If one's means are limited, one cannot be too choosy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Oníṣègùn tó sọ pé díẹ̀ ò tó òun, òfo ni yó fọwọ́ mú.
english_literal: The medicine man who is dissatisfied with a modest payment will wind up with nothing.
interpretation_gold: One should not demand too much from people who are in dire straights.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olórìṣà tó da kiriyó: ọjọ́ tó gbọ́ dùrù orí ijó lẹsẹ̀-ẹ́ kán sí.
english_literal: The idol worshipper who became a Christian; the day he first heard the organ play he lost his legs dancing.
interpretation_gold: Old habits die hard.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Oòrùn kì í là kínú bí olóko.
english_literal: The sun does not shine and cause displeasure in the farmer.
interpretation_gold: Everybody welcomes an auspicious event.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olè tó gbé fèrè ọba ò róhun gbé.
english_literal: The thief who stole the king's bugle could find nothing to steal.
interpretation_gold: There can be no rational explanation for acts of utter senselessness.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun-a-lè-ṣe, tó forí sọ àpò òwú; wọ́n ní ṣe bó rí yangí nílẹ̀, ó ní “Ohun a bá lè ṣe là ńlérí sí.”
english_literal: Ohunalese who dashes his head against a sack of cotton wool; people asked if he did not see the rock nearby; he replied, “One should vow to do only what one can safely accomplish.”
interpretation_gold: One should attempt only feats that will cause one no headache.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òṣùpá lé a ní kò gún; ẹni tọ́wọ́ ẹ̀-ẹ́ bá to kó tún un ṣe.
english_literal: The moon appears and people say it is not straight; whoever can reach it let him go and right it.
interpretation_gold: It is pointless to complain about things one can do nothing about.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ojú àwo làwó fi ńgba ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: It is on its face that a plate accepts soup.
interpretation_gold: One should not delegate crucial matters for oneself to others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fi pọ́nlẹ̀.
english_literal: One should not because of one's suffering try honing one's eyes on the ground.
interpretation_gold: Difficulties should not lead one to foolish behavior.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tí kò jẹ́ kí oko pọ̀ ni ò jẹ́ kó mọ́.
english_literal: Whatever limits the size of a farm is the same thing that makes it overgrown with weeds.
interpretation_gold: A basic defect will manifest itself in sundry ways.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Owó la fi ńfíná owó; bí ẹgbẹ̀rún bá so lókè, igbió la fi ńká a.
english_literal: Money is what one uses to kindle the fire for money; if a thousand cowries grow from the branches above, one uses two hundred cowries to pluck them.
interpretation_gold: Without some expenditure there can be no profit.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òtòṣì ò gbọ́ tìṣẹ́ ẹ̀ ó ní ogún kó àparò; ọdẹ́ rorò.
english_literal: The destitute person does not look to repairing his fortune; he says the partidge has been captured in a war, for the hunter is merciless.
interpretation_gold: Rather than deal with their own problems, people sometimes gloat over the troubles of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O rojọ́ láàárọ̀ o ò jàre, ó dalẹ́ o ní kọ́ba dúró gbọ́ tẹnu ẹ; ohun tó o wí láàárọ̀ náà kọ́ lo máa wí lálẹ́?
english_literal: You state your case in the morning and you are not vindicated, and at nightfall you plead with the king to delay a bit and listen to what you have to say; isn't what you have to say in the evening the same thing you said in the morning?
interpretation_gold: Repeated stating will not make a bad case a good one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohùn àgbà: bí kò ta ìgún, a ta èbù.
english_literal: An elder's voice: if it does not yield yams ready for pounding (for food), it will yield yam seedlings ready for planting.
interpretation_gold: There is some value in whatever comes out of an elder's mouth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ojú la fi ḿmọ àísí epo; ẹnu la fi ḿmọ àìsíyọ̀; ọbẹ̀ tí ò bá lépo nínú òkèèrè la ti ḿmọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: It is with the eyes that one tells the absence of palm-oil; it is with the mouth that one determines the absence of salt; if a stew lacks oil, it is the eyes that will tell.
interpretation_gold: In some matters the evidence of the eyes is enough to tell one all one needs to know.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ojú kì í ti àgbà lóru; jagun a lóṣòó góńgó.
english_literal: An elderly person does not become embarrassed under cover of darkness; the stalwart squats nonchalantly.
interpretation_gold: One can do whatever one pleased when no eyes are watching.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Owó kì í yéye kọ́mọ ó kú.
english_literal: If money is available in abundance, a child does not die.
interpretation_gold: One should spare no expenses to take care of one's children or one's affairs.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Onígbá ní ńpe igbá ẹ̀ ní àíkàrágbá káyé tó fi kólẹ̀.
english_literal: It is the owner of the calabash who first called it a broken piece of gourd before the world used it for scooping dirt.
interpretation_gold: If one does not value what one has, other people will value it even less.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tí a bá pàdé ò jọ ohun tí a rí tẹ́lẹ̀.
english_literal: That which one comes upon is nothing to compare to what one has always had.
interpretation_gold: No new friend or find can be as valuable as that one has had for some time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Obìnrin ò gbé ibi tó máa rọ̀ ọ́ lọ́rùn.
english_literal: A woman never remains where her well being rests.
interpretation_gold: Women seldom know until it is too late which home would best suit them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ó yẹ kí eégún mọ ẹni tó mú àgbò so.
english_literal: It is proper that the masquerader know who tethered the ram.
interpretation_gold: One should acknowledge those who have done one some favor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Orí tí yó jẹ igún kì í gbọ́; bí wọ́n fun ládìẹ kò níí gbà.
english_literal: The head that is destined to eat a vulture cannot be saved; if a chicken is offered to it it will refuse.
interpretation_gold: The person destined to suffer will manage to succumb to the suffering even in spite of efforts by others to save him/her.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ooré pẹ́, aṣiwèrè-é gbàgbé.
english_literal: The favor is long past; the imbecile forgets.
interpretation_gold: Only an imbecile forgets a favor even long after it was done.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O rí ẹsẹ̀-ẹ wèrè o ò bù ú ṣoògùn; níbo lo ti máa rí tọlọgbọ́n?
english_literal: You see the footprint of an imbecile and you do not take soil from it to make a charm; where will you find the footprint of a wise person?
interpretation_gold: One should take advantage of the weak and vulnerable, because one will not be able to take advantage of the strong.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O wà láyé, mo wà láàyè, ò ḿbi mí bí ọ̀rún ṣe rí.
english_literal: You are on earth “alive” and I am on earth, and yet you ask me what heaven is like.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person seeking information from someone in no better position to know than the seeker.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: O fẹ́ joyè o ní o-ò ní-í jà.
english_literal: You aspire to taking a chieftaincy title and you say you will not get into a fight.
interpretation_gold: It is self-deceit to wish for something without being prepared for the struggle it demands.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ohun tó fọ́ni lójú ló ńjúwe ọ̀nà fúnni.
english_literal: Whatever deprives one of one's sight is the same thing that shows one the way.
interpretation_gold: Misfortune teaches those its afflicts how to cope with it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Olówe laláṣẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: A person who knows proverbs has the last word in a dispute.
interpretation_gold: There is no authority like proverbial authority.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ràdà-ràdà-á mọ ibi tí ó ńrè.
english_literal: The meandering person knows where he is headed.
interpretation_gold: A person may seem without a purpose, but he or she is engaged in some thing known to himself or herself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Rírí tí a rí igún la fi ńta igún lọ́fà.
english_literal: It is because one sees the vulture that one shoots arrows at it.
interpretation_gold: If one does not make oneself available, one would not present a target for people's hostility.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Rà á ire, gà á ire; ìpéǹpéjú ni àlà-a fìlà.
english_literal: Press it well on the head; puff it out; the eyebrow is the limit for the cap.
interpretation_gold: One may be free to use one's possession as one pleases, but there are still some conventions one must observe.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Sọ̀rọ̀ kí ọlọ́rọ̀ gbọ́, àbùkù ní ńfi kanni.
english_literal: Spreading rumors into the ears of the subject of the rumor brings disgrace to one.
interpretation_gold: One should refrain from rumor mongering.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Sìn mí ká relé àna,” ó wẹ̀wù ẹtù.
english_literal: “Go with me to my in-laws' home,” and he wore a garment made from rich hand-woven material.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who attempts to steal other people's glory when he/she is supposed to be helping them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tábà tí ò dùn, ẹnu ò tà á.
english_literal: Snuff that is not pleasant, the mouth cannot not sell.
interpretation_gold: No amount of talk will make something unpleasant become pleasant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tẹni ntẹni; bí àpọ́n bá sun iṣu a bù fọ́mọ-ọ ẹ̀.
english_literal: One's own is one's own; when a man without a wife roasts yams he cuts a piece for his child.
interpretation_gold: One makes do with what one has.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ta ní jẹ́ jẹ ọṣẹ kó fògìrì fọṣọ?
english_literal: Who would eat soap and wash clothes with fermented beans?
interpretation_gold: Who would seek unease when ease is available?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tinú ọ̀lẹ lọ̀lẹ ńjẹ; aṣiwèrè èèyàn ni ò mọ èrú tí yó gbà.
english_literal: The lazy person eats the products of his native wisdom; only a fool does not know what devious way will be fruitful.
interpretation_gold: If one lacks industry, one had better be resourceful.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńṣíwájú eré sísa.
english_literal: A child's learning to walk comes before running.
interpretation_gold: One should observe some order in what one does.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tìẹ́ sàn, tèmí sàn, lolókùnrùn méjì-í fi ńdìmú.
english_literal: “Your condition is better; My condition is better,” is what gets two invalids into a fight.
interpretation_gold: Fools will fight over the most stupid things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Tèmi ò ṣòro,” tí kì í jẹ kọ́mọ alágbẹ̀dẹ ní idà.
english_literal: “Mine is not urgent.” which prevents the son of the blacksmith from owning a sword.
interpretation_gold: The person who always yields to others will never get anywhere.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tẹni ní ńjọni lójú; eèrà-á bímọ-ọ ẹ̀ ó sọ ọ́ ní òyírìgbí.
english_literal: One's own thing is what impresses one; the ant has a child and names it The-one-who-rolls-mightily-around.
interpretation_gold: One always tends to overestimate the worth of one's possession.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wò mí lójú, wò mí lẹ́ẹ̀kẹ́; ẹni a bá lọ sóde là ńwò lójú.
english_literal: Keep your eyes on my face, and keep your eyes on my cheeks; one keeps one's eyes on the person with whom one goes visiting.
interpretation_gold: People should not cultivate wandering eyes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wèrè-é dùn-ún wò, kò ṣé-é bí lọ́mọ.
english_literal: An imbecile makes an entertaining spectacle, but one would not want one as one's child.
interpretation_gold: One might be tolerant of simplicity or irresponsibility in other people, but not in one's own relatives.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wèrè-é yàtọ̀ sí wéré; wéré kì í ṣe wèrè; ìjá yàtọ̀ sí eré.
english_literal: Madness differs from the singing of Islamic songs; the singing of Islamic songs is not madness; fighting is different from playing.
interpretation_gold: One should not confuse jesting with quarrelling.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wàrà-wàrà là ńyọ oró iná.
english_literal: When one is on fire one's reaction is extremely agile.
interpretation_gold: One should not delay in exacting vengeance for a wrong.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wéré-wéré lọmọdé ḿbọ oko èèsì.
english_literal: A child's journey home from a nettle bush is fast indeed.
interpretation_gold: Painful problems enforce quick attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wọ́n ní, “Afọ́jú, o ò tanná alẹ́.” Ó ní àtọ̀sán àtòru, èwo lòún rí níbẹ?
english_literal: People said, “Blind man, you did not light a lamp.” He asked, night or day, which one would his eyes register?
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's efforts in procuring things one cannot use.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wọ́n ní, “Afọ́jú, ọmo-ọ̀ ẹ-ẹ́ pẹran.” Ó ní kò dá òun lójú, àfi bí òún bá tọ́ ọ wò.
english_literal: They said to the blind man, “Blind man, you son has killed a game.” He responds that he cannot believe them until he has tasted the meat.
interpretation_gold: Always insist on proof positive.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Wo ọmọ-ọ̀ mi dè mí”: ó ńlo kíjìpá mẹ́ta gbó; mélòó ni ọlọ́mọ-ọ́ máa lò gbó?
english_literal: “Look after the child for me”: she wears three durable hand-loom wrappers to tatters; how many would the mother of the child herself wear out?
interpretation_gold: The caretaker should not use up all his own resources for the benefit of his/her employer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wolé-wolé kì í wolé agbọ́n láì tẹ́.
english_literal: The sanitary inspector does not inspect a wasp's home without coming to grief.
interpretation_gold: One should be cautious in performing one's duties.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀sán ọ̀run ò pọ́n; ẹni tó bá yá kó máa bá tiẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: It is not yet noon time in heaven; whoever is anxious to get there may go ahead by himself/herself.
interpretation_gold: One is not eager to join others in deadly adventures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ iná là ńrán síná.
english_literal: It is the child of fire that one sends on an errand to fire.
interpretation_gold: It is best to match the remedy to the problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ ni ilé ẹ̀rín.
english_literal: The cheeks are the home of laughter.
interpretation_gold: Suit the means to the project.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọkọ́ ọlọ́kọ́ la fi ńgbọ́n èkìtì.
english_literal: It is other people's hoe that one uses to clear a mound of rubbish.
interpretation_gold: One is usually more respectful of one's own property than of others'.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n dùn-ún gbọ́n; ìmọ́ dùn-ún mọ̀.
english_literal: Wisdom is a good thing to have; knowledge is a good thing to have.
interpretation_gold: Always seek wisdom and knowledge.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí kò mọ ọba ní ńfọba ṣeré.
english_literal: Only a person who does not know the king trifles with the king.
interpretation_gold: The wise person recognizes potential danger and avoids it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́gbọ́n jẹni bí ẹmùrẹ́n; aṣiwèré jẹni bí ìgbọ̀ngbọ̀n.
english_literal: The wise person bites one like a mosquito; the mad person bites one like a gadfly.
interpretation_gold: Cautiousness will get one to one's goal far more successfully than brashness.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ la fi ńjẹ omitooro ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: Words are the things with which to savor the delicious broth of words.
interpretation_gold: It is with words that one resolves all problems.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n a-dákọ-kéré ò tó ti a-yọwó-má-rà.
english_literal: The cunning of the person who skimps on the measure of her corn meal is not as great as that of the would-be purchaser who refuses to buy.
interpretation_gold: One does not have to patronize a dishonest trader.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni a óò gbé òkú-u rẹ̀ sin, a kì í sọ pé ó ńrùn pani.
english_literal: One does not complain that a corpse one will have to bury stinks.
interpretation_gold: One should not run down a person or thing that will eventually devolve to one's care.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹbọ díẹ̀, oògùn díẹ̀, ní ńgba aláìkú là.
english_literal: A little sacrifice, a little medicine, is what keeps the one who does not die alive.
interpretation_gold: One should not place all of one's faith in a single solution to a problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní òún lè sín ìlẹ̀kẹ̀; ta ní jẹ́ fi ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sídìí ọmọ-ọ ẹ̀?
english_literal: The toad boasts that it knows how to string beads; who, though, would put a toad's beads around his child's waist?
interpretation_gold: Not just anything will do for discriminating people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ní wọ́n ńjẹ igún, bàbá ẹ̀-ẹ́ ní wọn kì í jẹ ẹ́; ó ní ẹnìkán jẹ ẹ́ rí lójú òun; bàbá ẹ̀-ẹ́ ní ta ni? Ó ní ẹni náà ò sí.
english_literal: A child says that people do eat vultures, and its father says people do not; the child says someone did eat a vulture in its presence; its father asks, who? The child says the person is dead.
interpretation_gold: The youth who attempts to challenge the wisdom of the elders will find himself tripped by his own mouth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ọlọgbọ́n ò jẹ́ ká pe àgbà ní wèrè.
english_literal: Other people's wisdom saves the elder from being called a lunatic.
interpretation_gold: The person who can learn from others will avoid a lot of embarrassment.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́jà kì í wípé kọ́jà ó tú.
english_literal: The owner of the market never wishes the market to be disrupted.
interpretation_gold: People always want the best outcome for their ventures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní gbọ́n juni lọ ní ńtẹni nÍfá.
english_literal: It is someone wiser than one who consults the oracle for one.
interpretation_gold: One receives advice only from those qualified to offer it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni àìgbọ́n pa ló pọ̀; ẹni ọgbọ́n pa ò tó ǹkan.
english_literal: People killed by folly are innumerable; people killed by wisdom are few.
interpretation_gold: Few things kill more surely than folly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó máa tẹ́ òkú ọ̀pọ̀lọ́, yó nìí ilé ògbóni tirẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to lay a dead toad in state will have to build his own cult shrine separately.
interpretation_gold: Whoever wishes to do the absurd should not expect the cooperation or approval of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọsán gbé ojú ọrun le kókó; bó bá wọ odò, a di ọ̀-rọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀.
english_literal: The bow-string is taut while it remains on the bow; dipped into the river it becomes very soft indeed.
interpretation_gold: One thrives on one's home ground where conditions are ideal; in hostile territory one becomes helpless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀bẹ ńwólé ara ẹ̀ ó ní òún ḿba àkọ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: The knife is destroying its own home, it says it is ruining the sheath.
interpretation_gold: Said of people whose actions will hurt them more than they will hurt other people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé kì í ní ina níle kí tòde má jòó o.
english_literal: A child does not have fire at home and therefore escape being burned by the fire abroad.
interpretation_gold: Being secure and well respected in one's home does not save one from vicissitudes outside the home.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá ní igbà-á lò, bí igbà-á bá já, kó dúró so ó.
english_literal: If one must use a tree-climbing rope and it breaks, one must pause to repair it.
interpretation_gold: One must make the time to attend to chores that must be performed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá fi ojù àná wòkú, ẹbọra a bọ́ ọ láṣọ.
english_literal: Whoever looks at the dead with yesterday's eyes will be stripped naked by the spirits.
interpretation_gold: One behaves towards people according to the heights they have attained, not according to the way they used to be.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí a wífún kó gbọ́; ẹni tí kò gbọ́, tara-a rẹ̀ ni yó dà.
english_literal: Let the person one advises heed one; the heedless person places himself at risk.
interpretation_gold: Those who refuse instruction lay the foundation for their own ruin.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé mọ sáárá, ṣùgbọ́n kò mọ àlọ̀yí.
english_literal: A child knows snuff, but does not know how to grind and turn the tobacco.
interpretation_gold: A child is good at consuming, but not at procuring.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó rúbọ tí kò gba èèwọ̀, bí ẹni tó fi owó ẹbọ ṣòfò ni.
english_literal: The person who makes a sacrifice but does not follow the prescribed taboos is just like someone who throws away the money for the sacrifice.
interpretation_gold: A person who knows of the remedy but does not apply it is as badly off as the person who does not know the remedy at all.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣẹ́kẹ́-ṣẹkẹ̀-ẹ́ dára, ṣùgbọ́n alágbẹ̀dẹ ò rọ ọ́ fún ọmọ ẹ̀.
english_literal: Handcuffs are pretty, but the blacksmith does not fashion them for his own child.
interpretation_gold: When trouble is being distributed, one always wishes to exempt one's own people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹnu ehoro ò gba ìjánu.
english_literal: A rabbit's mouth does not accept a leash.
interpretation_gold: Do not adopt an inappropriate remedy for a problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí kò mọ iṣẹ́-ẹ́ jẹ́ ní ńpààrà lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: It is a person who does not know how to carry out instructions that is forced to repeat his or her efforts.
interpretation_gold: One saves time and effort by doing things right the first time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọpẹ́ ló yẹ ẹrú.
english_literal: Gratitude is what befits the slave.
interpretation_gold: People should be grateful for whatever charity they receive.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹjọ́ a-fẹ́ni-lóbìnrin là ńwí; a kì í wíjọ́ a-fẹ́ni-lọ́mọ.
english_literal: One may complain about a person who courts one's wife, but one does not complain about a person who courts one's daughter.
interpretation_gold: One should not pursue causes without good grounds.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹyẹ igbó kì í mọ fífò ọ̀dàn.
english_literal: The bird of the forest does not know how to fly in the grassland.
interpretation_gold: When one is in a strange environment, one becomes a dunce.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó pa kẹ́tẹ́kẹ́tẹ́ yó ru káyá ẹrù.
english_literal: The person who kills the donkey will carry a heavy burden.
interpretation_gold: Whoever is careless with his/her resources will pay dearly in the future.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ ẹní dàra, bí-i ká fi ṣaya kọ́.
english_literal: One's child may be beautiful, but one cannot make her one's wife.
interpretation_gold: Not all attractive propositions can be pursued.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní kéjò máa kálọ; ìjà òún di ojú ọ̀nà.
english_literal: The toad tells the snake to follow it, for it does not fight except by the roadside.
interpretation_gold: Weaklings always make sure that saviors are around before they get into a fight.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ní ńṣẹgun; ìmọ̀ràn ní ńṣẹ́ ẹ̀tẹ̀.
english_literal: Cunning wins battles; knowledge defeats plots.
interpretation_gold: Cunning and knowledge will help one prevail.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n kì í tán.
english_literal: Wisdom is never used up.
interpretation_gold: There will always be a place and some use for wisdom.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀mọ̀ràn ní ḿmọ oyún ìgbín.
english_literal: Only a sage knows the pregnancy of a snail.
interpretation_gold: Deep wisdom is the gift of only a select few.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí ẹ̀gún gún lẹ́sẹ̀ ní ńṣe lákáǹláká tẹ̀lé alábẹ́rẹ́.
english_literal: It is the person with a thorn in his foot who limps to the person with a needle.
interpretation_gold: The person in need of help should make some effort in his own behalf, and not expect his helper to make all the necessary effort.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó mọ ẹtu ní ńkì í ní “òbèjé, ẹlẹ́sẹ̀ ọwọ̀.”
english_literal: It is someone who knows the duiker intimately who can recite its praise, “spindle-legged duiker.”
interpretation_gold: Only those deeply involved in a profession are versed in its jargon.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá yá ìwọ̀fà ẹgbàá, tòun tirẹ̀ ní ńlọ ata kúnná.
english_literal: Whoever hires a pawn for only sixpence will join the pawn in grinding pepper.
interpretation_gold: Whatever comes too cheaply is sure to work unsatisfactorily.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀fẹ̀-ẹ́ dẹ̀fẹ̀ iyán; a paláwẹ́ ẹ̀kọ baálé ilé ní ẹ̀ ńpèun bí?
english_literal: The teasing involves pounded yams; the corn-loaf is unwrapped, and the father of the household asks, “Did someone call me?”
interpretation_gold: A person who wants something badly will not let a little teasing put him or her off taking it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ju agbára.
english_literal: Wisdom is greater than strength.
interpretation_gold: Always prefer wisdom to strength.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọjọ́ tí olówó ńṣẹbọ ni à-wà-jẹ-wà-mu ìwọ̀fà.
english_literal: The day the person who did the hiring makes a sacrifice is the day the hired hand eats and drinks.
interpretation_gold: The poor will eat when the rich provide a feast.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ ẹni ẹlẹni ò jọ ọmọ ẹni; ọmọ eni ì-bá jiyán, ọmọ ẹni ẹlẹ́ni a jẹ̀kọ.
english_literal: Other people's children are not like one's own; when one's child eats pounded yams, other people's children will eat corn meal loaf.
interpretation_gold: One always favors one's own children over those of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ kì í gbórín ká fi ọ̀bẹ bù ú, ẹnu la fi ńwí i.
english_literal: A problem is not so formidable that one attacks it with a knife; one tackles it with the mouth.
interpretation_gold: The weightiest problem is resolvable through discussion and negotiation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọkùnrin jẹ́jẹ́ a-bìwà-kunkun.
english_literal: An easy-going man's gentle mien hides a strong disposition.
interpretation_gold: The quiet type is often a tough customer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ò moògùn ó ńpè é lẹ́gùn-ún.
english_literal: A child does not know medicine and says it is a thorn.
interpretation_gold: The ignorant person knows not the value of anything.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́n-ọn hùn, ọjọ́ náà ni ọ̀rọ̀ ò ti nìun lára mọ́.
english_literal: The pig says since the day it learned to reply to every statement with a grunt it has not got into any trouble.
interpretation_gold: A person who says nothing seldom gets in trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá máa jẹ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ a jẹ èyí tó lẹ́yin.
english_literal: If one must eat a toad one should eat one with eggs.
interpretation_gold: If one must suffer, one might as well do so with panache.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní máa ké ìbòsí á pa baba rẹ̀ jẹ.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to raise an alarm will have to murder his father.
interpretation_gold: Whoever acts without cause will have to justify his action by manufacturing some cause.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá fi orí-i rẹ̀ fọ́ àgbọn ò níí jẹ níbẹ̀.
english_literal: The person on whose head a coconut is broken will not share in eating it.
interpretation_gold: Whoever takes foolhardy risks in pursuit of an end seldom lives to enjoy it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ọmọ ní ḿmú inú-u bàbá ẹ̀ dùn; aṣiwèrè ọmọ ní ḿba inú ìyá ẹ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: A wise child gladdens the heart of his father; an imbecile of a child saddens the heart of his mother.
interpretation_gold: Every parent would prefer a wise child to an idiot.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọjọ́ eré là ńjiyàn ohun.
english_literal: It is on a playful occasion that one argues about matters.
interpretation_gold: Arguments conducted in jest conceal some serious import.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n tí ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ fi pa ẹfọ̀n ló fi ńjẹ ẹ́.
english_literal: The same cunning with which the toad killed the buffalo will show it how to eat the prey.
interpretation_gold: If a person has proved himself capable of doing the impossible, one should not doubt that he can accomplish another.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé kékeré ò mọ ogun, ó ní kógun ó wá, ó ní bógún bá dé òun a kó síyàrá ìyá òun.
english_literal: A small child does not know what war is like, hence, he says that war should break out, for when it does he will go hide in his mother's room.
interpretation_gold: Ignorance often leads people to bite off much more than they can chew.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹyẹ ńwá àtifò, wọ́ ńsọ òkò sí i.
english_literal: A bird is preparing for flight, and people throw stones at it.
interpretation_gold: One needs little encouragement to do what one is determined to do anyway; being forced to do what one wishes to do anyway is no punishment.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹlẹ́nu-ú tóó rí sá.
english_literal: An overly loquacious person is someone to flee from.
interpretation_gold: Be wary of loquacious people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ atiro tó ra bàtà fún bàbá ẹ̀, ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ gbọ́.
english_literal: The child of a cripple who bought shoes for his father is asking for a stern lecture.
interpretation_gold: One must not be thoughtless in one's actions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀fẹ̀-ẹ́ dẹ̀fẹ̀ iyán; ò báà gbémi lulẹ̀ ng ó bàá ọ jẹun.
english_literal: The teasing involves pounded yam; even if you throw me on the ground I will eat with you.
interpretation_gold: No amount of teasing will stop me from doing what I have in mind.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni a wí fún ko gbọ́; ẹni a fọ̀ fún kó gbà; èyí tí ò gbọ́ yó filẹ̀ bora.
english_literal: Whoever people speak to should listen; whoever people instruct should accept instruction; the one who does not listen will be covered by the earth.
interpretation_gold: Refusal to heed advice can be deadly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n tí ahún gbọ́n, ẹ̀hìn ni yó máa tọ ti ìgbín.
english_literal: The cunning that the tortoise has will always rank behind that of the snail.
interpretation_gold: Some people cannot hope to be more cunning than some others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó fò yó bẹ̀rẹ̀.
english_literal: The person who will leap must first crouch.
interpretation_gold: One must make adequate preparations for any project.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó dùbúlẹ̀-ẹ́ ṣe oògùn ìjàkadì tán.
english_literal: The person who remains prone has perfected the charm for wrestling.
interpretation_gold: The wise person forestalls problems.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ èèyàn, bí a ò bá gbé e lulẹ̀, kò níí lè fọhùn ire.
english_literal: A person who is like the divining string: unless you throw him down he will not talk sense.
interpretation_gold: Some people respond only to force.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹnu àìmẹ́nu, ètè àìmétè, ní ḿmú ọ̀ràn bá ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́.
english_literal: A mouth that will not stay shut, lips that will not stay closed, are what bring trouble to the cheeks.
interpretation_gold: The words that the mouth and lips allow to escape usually bring the slap to the cheek; a person who cannot keep his/her mouth shut often lands in trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé yìí, máa wò mí lójú, ẹni (tí) a bá lọ sóde là ńwò lójú.
english_literal: Child, keep your eyes on me; one keeps one's eyes on the person who takes one visiting.
interpretation_gold: Always pay attention to what your guide and instructor does and tells you to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀ràn tí ò sunwọ̀n, konko ǹṣojú.
english_literal: A matter that is unpalatable hardens the eyes.
interpretation_gold: When one is in the wrong one hides behind braggadocio.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀bẹ̀ là ḿbẹ òṣìkà pé kó tún ìlú-u rẹ̀ ṣe.
english_literal: One can only remonstrate with a wicked person to urge him or her to improve his or her town.
interpretation_gold: Gentle pleas are the only likely means of getting contrary people to do what is right.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ńdẹ ihò, ọ̀mọ̀rànán dúró tì í; ọlọgbọ́n ní “Háà, ó jáde!”Ọ̀mọ̀rán ní “Háà, mo kì í!”Ọlọgbọ́n ní “Kí lo kì?” Ọ̀mọ̀rán ní “Kí nìwọ náà-á ló jáde?”
english_literal: The cunning man is watching a hole, and the knowledgeable person is standing by him; the cunning man exclaims, “Ha, it has sprung out!” The knowledgeable person responds, “Ha, I have grabbed it!” The cunning person asks, “What did you grab?” The knowledgeable person asks in turn, “What did you say sprang out?”
interpretation_gold: Two matched wits are in contest.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ò mọ oògùn, ó ńpè é lẹ́fọ̀o?; kò mọ̀ pé ikú tó pa baba òun ni.
english_literal: A child does not know medicine and he therefore calls it vegetables; it does not recognize it as what killed its father.
interpretation_gold: People may call disasters on their own heads out of ignorance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó gbajúmọ̀ tí kò mọ èèyàn-án kí, òun òbúrẹ́wà ẹgbẹ́ra.
english_literal: The dandy who does not know how to extend greetings to people is no different from a boor.
interpretation_gold: Good looks without the social graces amount to nothing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó bọ Ògún, yó ra ọjà-a tirẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
english_literal: The person who will worship Ògun will keep his or her market purchases separate from those of others.
interpretation_gold: If one's priorities are incompatible with those of others, one parts company with them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹgbẹ́ ẹni kì í wọ́n láyé ká wá a lọ sọ́run.
english_literal: One does not upon failing to find suitable company in this world go looking in heaven.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot find what one wants, one should learn to do without it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pá gbóńgbó ní nṣíwájú agbọ́ọni.
english_literal: It is a small walking-stick that goes before the person who walks a path overhung with foliage that is wet with morning dew.
interpretation_gold: One uses the tools or weapons at one's disposal to tackle the challenges that confront one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀rù bíbà ní ḿmúni pe àjẹ́ ní ará ire.
english_literal: It is fear that makes one call witches the good people.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to curry the favor of fearful or malicious people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò mọ̀nà odò, ó dà á sí àwàdà.
english_literal: The toad does not know the way to the stream and turns matters into a jest.
interpretation_gold: When one is stumped, one covers one's embarrassment with laughter.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó mu ẹ̀kọ ọ̀fẹ́ yó bàá ọmọ ẹlẹ́kọ ṣeré.
english_literal: The person who wishes to eat free corn pap will play with the seller's child.
interpretation_gold: Nothing comes free.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá rántí Efuji, kó má fi ore ṣe ẹṣin.
english_literal: Whoever remembers Efuji should show no kindness to any horse.
interpretation_gold: One should remember those who have caused one injury, and remember to show them no favor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni à ńwò kì í wòran.
english_literal: The person people have gathered to watch should not himself or herself be a spectator.
interpretation_gold: One should not ignore one's problems to dwell on others'.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní rúbọ òrìṣà-á gbọ́dọ̀ rú ti èèyàn kí ẹbọ-ọ́ tó gbà.
english_literal: Whoever offers a sacrifice to a deity must also offer a sacrifice to humans in order for the sacrifice to be efficacious.
interpretation_gold: One can please the gods and yet run afoul of humans.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ló lè mọ àdììtú èdè.
english_literal: Only a wise person can decipher the meaning of speech.
interpretation_gold: The deep meanings and nuances of an utterance are for the wise only to understand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńyọ ẹsẹ̀ lábàtà.
english_literal: One at a time is how one extricates one's feet from a mire.
interpretation_gold: The best way to approach a problem is systematically.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó fi irun dúdú ṣeré, yó fi funfun sin ẹniẹlẹ́ni.
english_literal: Whoever plays around with his or her black hair will serve others with his or her white hair.
interpretation_gold: If one wastes one's youth, one spends one's old age struggling for a living.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹbọ ẹnìkan là ńfi ẹnìkan rú.
english_literal: It is a sacrifice on behalf of only one person that demands only one person as offering.
interpretation_gold: Extraordinary problems demand extraordinary solutions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó ńṣápẹ́ fún wèrè jó, òun àti wèrè ọ̀kan-ùn.
english_literal: The person who claps for a mad person to dance to is no different from the mad person.
interpretation_gold: Whoever joins the imbecile in his or her games is himself or herself an imbecile.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní bá tó ẹni-í gbà là ńké pè.
english_literal: One appeals only to those capable of helping one.
interpretation_gold: One should not seek the aid of feckless people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé kì í mọ ori-í jẹ kó má rá a lẹ́nu.
english_literal: A child is never so careful about eating corn meal that it does not smear the meal on its mouth.
interpretation_gold: A youth may be clever, but he will inevitably make some mistakes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣẹ̀kẹ̀rẹ̀ ò ṣéé fọ̀pá na.
english_literal: The beaded musical gourd is not something to play with a stick.
interpretation_gold: Always apply the proper tool to the job.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá rántí ọjọ́ ní ńṣe ọmọ òkú pẹ̀lẹ́; ta ní jẹ́ ṣe ọmọ eégún lóore?
english_literal: Those who gratefully remember past favors extend compassion to the survivors of the deceased; who would rather show compassion to the child of a masquerader?
interpretation_gold: When a good person dies, his or her survivors inherit the good will of those who remember him or her well.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ ni òun ò nílé; ibi tí wọ́n bá rí ni wọ́n ti ńsọ òun.
english_literal: Discourse says it has no home; people engage in it wherever they please.
interpretation_gold: Any place is a good place for an exchange of views.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀sín alátọ̀sí ò sí lọ́wọ́ òkóbó.
english_literal: The ridiculing of the person with gonorrhea does not belong with the eunuch.
interpretation_gold: Do not ridicule a person whose condition is no worse than yours'.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀ràn ọlọ́ràn la fi ńkọ́gbọ́n.
english_literal: From other people's problems one learns wisdom.
interpretation_gold: One should learn from other people's vicissitudes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó torí òtútù fi ọmọrí odó yáná ò gbọdọ̀ retí a-ti-jẹyán.
english_literal: Whoever because of cold weather uses the pestle as kindling to warm him/herself must not expect to eat pounded yams.
interpretation_gold: One should not jeopardize one's long-term interests by indulging in immediate gratifications.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ ẹni kì í gbọnsẹ̀ ká fi eèsún nù ú nídìí.
english_literal: One does not, after one's child defecates, wipe the child's anus with the abrasive elephant grass.
interpretation_gold: One does not deliberately injure those who look to one for protection.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọọgbọ́n làgbàlagbà-á fi ńsá fún ẹranlá.
english_literal: It is with cunning that a grown man runs away from a bull.
interpretation_gold: A grown person should know how to avoid disaster without losing face.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́tí kì í mọ ọmọ ẹ̀ lólè
english_literal: The wine seller never realizes that his child is a thief.
interpretation_gold: One is always blind to the flaws of those one loves.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí kò gbọ́n lààwẹ̀ ńgbò.
english_literal: Only the unwise hungers while fasting.
interpretation_gold: The resourceful person can find a way around any difficulty.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀fàfà fohùn ṣakin.
english_literal: The tree-bear wins renown with its voice.
interpretation_gold: The loud person wins attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá máa lu òṣùgbó a lu ńlá; kékeré ẹgbẹ̀fà, ńlá ẹgbẹ̀fà.
english_literal: Whoever will smite a secret-cult priest had better smite an important one; for a lowly one twelve hundred cowries in fines, and for an important one twelve hundred cowries.
interpretation_gold: If the penalty for a small offence is the same as that for a grievous one, one might as well throw all caution to the wind.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ rere ní ńyọ obì lápò; ọ̀rọ̀ búburú ní ńyọ ọfà lápó.
english_literal: Good talk brings the kola-nut out of the pouch; provocative talk draws the arrow out of th quiver.
interpretation_gold: Judicious language defuses problems, while thoughtless talk aggravates them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́gbọ́n dorí ẹja mú; òmùgọ́ dìrù-u ẹ̀ mú.
english_literal: The wise person grabs a fish by the head; the fool grabs it by the tail fin.
interpretation_gold: The wise person knows better than a fool the best way to handle a situation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó máa yáni lẹ́wù, ti ọrùn-un rẹ̀ là ńwò.
english_literal: If a person offers to lend one a dress, one should consider what he or she has on.
interpretation_gold: One should be discriminating about those from whom one will accept favors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí ó lè jà ni yóò kúnlẹ̀ kalẹ́.
