english_literal: It is the incorrigible fighter who has to remain on his or her knees until nightfall.
interpretation_gold: The person who cannot stay out of a fight will spend his or her time incessantly stating cases.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá máa mú ọ̀bọ a ṣe bí ọ̀bọ.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to catch a monkey must act like a monkey.
interpretation_gold: To succeed against an adversary, or with a person one desires, one must suit one's approach to the other's ways.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńyọ ẹsẹ̀ lẹ́kù.
english_literal: One at a time is how one removes one's legs from a masquerade costume.
interpretation_gold: The best way to approach a problem is systematically.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ tó dojú rú di ti ọlọ́rọ̀, ayé á dẹ̀hìn.
english_literal: A problem that is too complicated to resolve becomes the sole responsibility of the person concerned; the world leaves him/her to his/her devices.
interpretation_gold: People will help one only so far; in the end each person must confront his/her problems alone.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọde kì í mọ ìtàn, kó mọ à-gbọ́-wí, kó mọ ọjọ́ tí a ṣe ẹ̀dá òun.
english_literal: A child does not know so much history and know so much hearsay that it knows the day of its creation.
interpretation_gold: However knowledgeable a youth might be, some deep knowledge would be beyond him.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní léku méjì á pòfo.
english_literal: Whoever chases after two rats will catch neither.
interpretation_gold: If one pursues two or more objectives at once one is liable to achieve neither.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Ọmọ-ọ̀ mi ò yó” la mọ̀; “ọmọ-ọ̀ mí yó, ṣùgbọ́n kò rí sáárá fẹ́,” a ò mọ ìyẹn.
english_literal: “My child did not have enough to eat,” we understand; “My child had enough to eat but had no snuff to snort,” that we do not understand.
interpretation_gold: People should care for their children, not spoil them with over-indulgence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọn la fi ńgbé ayé.
english_literal: One needs wisdom to live in this world.
interpretation_gold: Wisdom is indispensable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá mọ ìdí ọ̀ràn tẹ́lẹ̀ ní ḿbu àbùjá èké.
english_literal: It is a person who has prior knowledge of the facts of a matter that can foil a devious person's attempts to skirt them.
interpretation_gold: Prior knowledge is the surest weapon against lies.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọbẹ̀ tí baálé kì í jẹ, ìyálé ilé kì í sè é.
english_literal: The sort of stew the man of the house will not eat, the woman of the house should not cook.
interpretation_gold: One should not do what one knows one's comrades hate.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní bá ríkun nímú ọlọ́jà ní ńfọn ọ́n.
english_literal: Whoever sees mucus in the nose of the king is the one who cleans it.
interpretation_gold: Tactless or indiscreet people usually rue their bad judgement.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó yàáni lówó, tí kò níí sinni, ohùn ẹnu-u rẹ̀ la ti ḿmọ̀.
english_literal: The person who will lend one money and will not keep pestering one for repayment: one can tell from the tone of his or her voice.
interpretation_gold: The way people talk is a good indication of their character.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá pẹ́ lórí imí, eṣinṣin kéṣinṣin yó ò bá a níbẹ̀.
english_literal: Whoever prolongs his or her defecating will be visited by a host of flies.
interpretation_gold: Nothing good comes of dawdling over what one must do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní du ara-a rẹ̀ lóyè Apènà: kó tó jẹ ẹran ọ̀fẹ́, ó dọ̀run.
english_literal: Whoever deprives himself of the title of Apena will wait until he dies before tasting free meat.
interpretation_gold: If one does not grab opportunities when they present themselves, one is in for a difficult life.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó mi kùkùté, araa rẹ̀ ní ńmì.
english_literal: The person who shakes a tree stump shakes himself.
interpretation_gold: Whoever takes on an invincible adversary fashions his or her own defeat.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni a pé kó wáá wo kọ̀bì: ó ní kí nìyí kọ́bi-kọ̀bi?
english_literal: The person invited to take a look at the palace stateroom: he exclaims, “What a maze of apartments!”
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's breath expressing the obvious.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀wọ̀-ọ kókó la fi ńwọ igi; ọ̀wọ̀ òrìṣà la fi ńwọ àfín.
english_literal: The regard one has for the knob is the one with which one clothes the tree; the regard one has for the gods is the same that one invests the albino with.
interpretation_gold: One extends the same regard one has for certain people to those associated with them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ò mẹ̀fọ́, ó ńpè é légbògi.
english_literal: A child does not recognize a vegetable and calls it medicine.
interpretation_gold: An uninformed person will inevitably make a fool of him/herself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá da omi síwájú á tẹ ilẹ̀ tútù.
english_literal: Whoever throws water ahead will step on cool earth.
interpretation_gold: The future will look kindly on those who look well to the future.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ni yó jogún ògo; aṣiwèrè ni yó ru ìtìjú wálé.
english_literal: The wise child will inherit glory; the idiot child will bring shame home with him.
interpretation_gold: A wise child is to be preferred to an idiot.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ tí ò ní baba kì í jìjà ẹ̀bi.
english_literal: A fatherless child should not engage in an unjust fight.
interpretation_gold: Never provoke trouble unless you have strong backers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá sọ pé ẹsẹ̀ eégún ńhàn ní ńwá abẹ́rẹ́ lọ.
english_literal: Whoever announces that the legs of the masquerader are showing is the one who goes in search of a needle.
interpretation_gold: Some sights the eyes must not acknowledge seeing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹlẹ́jọ́ ṣa èyí tó wù ú wí.
english_literal: The person with complaints selects the most pressing ones to press.
interpretation_gold: One should concentrate on one's most pressing problems.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọjọ́ tíìlù-ú bá ńlu onílù, iṣẹ́ mìíràn-án yá.
english_literal: The day the drum begins to beat the drummer is the day he should seek another employment.
interpretation_gold: One should know when to abandon an unprofitable proposition.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó mu ẹ̀kọ fòrò, yó bàá ọmọ ẹlẹ́kọ ṣeré.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to eat steaming corn pap will play with the child of the seller.
interpretation_gold: One must ingratiate oneself with the person from whom one expects a favor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀ràn kan la fi ńṣòfin ọ̀kan.
english_literal: One problem serves as the basis for a law that will apply to another case.
interpretation_gold: Experience serves as a precedence for future occurrences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Ṣe mí níṣu” ní ńṣíwájú “ẹ kúuṣẹ́” bí?
english_literal: Does “Give me some yam” go before “Hello there, you working man.”?
interpretation_gold: It is bad form to ask people for favors before you say hello to them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá ḿbá nájà là ńwò, a kì í wo ariwo ọjà.
english_literal: One pays attention to the person with whom one is bargaining, not to the commotion of the market place.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's mind on one's business and leave extraneous matters aside.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọwọ́ aṣiwèrè ni a gbé ḿbá apá yíya.
english_literal: It is in the hands of an imbecile that one finds a severed arm.
interpretation_gold: Simple-minded people do not know how to cover their tracks or get rid of the evidence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀ẹ̀kan lejò ńyánni.
english_literal: One gets bitten by a snake only once.
interpretation_gold: The same disaster does not befall one more than once; after the first time one learns to avoid it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ọlọgbọ́n bá sọ, ẹnu aṣiwèrè la ti ńgbọ́ ọ.
english_literal: Whatever a wiseman says will be heard repeated by the nitwit.
interpretation_gold: Romour mongers always distort the news they hear from reliable sources.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó fi owó-o rẹ̀ ra ẹṣin, kò níí jẹ́ kó ṣe àrìnjẹ́.
english_literal: Whoever paid his or her own money for a horse will not let it be sacrificed for a good-luck charm.
interpretation_gold: One guards one's treasures jealously.

yoruba: Akánjú jayé, ọ̀run wọn ò pẹ́.
english_literal: People who live impatiently: their going to heaven is not far off.
interpretation_gold: Reckless living leads to early death.

yoruba: Arọ ò nasẹ̀ kan dí ọ̀nà.
english_literal: A cripple does not block the road with his legs.
interpretation_gold: A person with a handicap should not challenge those who are not handicapped.

yoruba: Àgùntàn ńwò sùn-ùn; ọgbọ́n inú pé egbèje.
english_literal: The sheep stares blankly, but its cunning stratagems number a thousand four hundred.
interpretation_gold: Looks are deceptive.

yoruba: Àdàbà ńpògèdè, ó rò pé ẹyẹlé ò gbọ́; ẹyẹlé gbọ́, títiiri ló tiiri.
english_literal: The dove recites incantations, thinking that the pigeon cannot hear; the pigeon hears; it is only pretending to sleep.
interpretation_gold: Never mistake a person's easygoing demeanor for cowardice or folly.

yoruba: Arọ́basá ò ṣojo.
english_literal: He-who-flees-on-seeing-the-king is no coward.
interpretation_gold: One's safest course is to steer clear of those in authority.

yoruba: Àìgbọ́ràn, baba àfojúdi.
english_literal: Disobedience, father of disregard.
interpretation_gold: To disobey people is to show a lack of regard for them.

yoruba: Alágbàró ò yege; aláṣọ á gbà á bó dọ̀la.
english_literal: She who borrows a wrapper-skirt to wear is not home free; the owner of the cloth will take it back come tomorrow.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing like having one's own.

yoruba: Ajá kì í dán-nu “Kò séwu” lókò ẹkùn.
english_literal: A dog does not boast “No danger” in a leopard's bush.
interpretation_gold: Never sneer at obvious danger.

yoruba: Àkọ̀ tó bá bá ọ̀bẹ dìtẹ̀ á gbọgbẹ́ láti inú.
english_literal: A sheath that engages in a dispute with a knife will suffer an internal wound.
interpretation_gold: Never court the anger of a person in a position to inflict injury on you.

yoruba: Ayáraròhìn, aya ọdẹ, ó ní ọkọ òun-ún pa èkínní, ó pa ẹ̀kẹfà.
english_literal: The-impatient-reporter, wife of the hunter, she says that her husband killed the first and killed the sixth.
interpretation_gold: The impatient reporter is liable to outstrip her report.

yoruba: Àjẹ́ ńké, òkùnrùn ò paradà; ó lówó ẹbọ nílé.
english_literal: A witch proclaims her presence and an invalid does not make away; he must have money for sacrifices at home.
interpretation_gold: One needs not fear a scourge for which one has the remedy.

yoruba: Ajá ilé ò mọdẹẹ́ ṣe.
english_literal: A domesticated dog does not know how to hunt.
interpretation_gold: Pampering kills initiative.

yoruba: Alápàáǹdẹ̀dẹ̀ ńjayé lébé-lébé.
english_literal: The sparrow enjoys life carefully.
interpretation_gold: The best way to live is carefully.

yoruba: Apatapara-á pa ara-a rẹ̀ lájùbà; ẹni tí yó ko là ńwòye.
english_literal: Apatapara kills himself in the wilderness; who will carry him is now the question.
interpretation_gold: One should not to outstrip one's help.

yoruba: Àìlèfọhùn ní ńṣáájú orí burúkú.
english_literal: Inability to speak out precedes misfortunes.
interpretation_gold: A person who will not speak out on his or her own behalf suffers the consequences.

yoruba: Àgbẹ̀ tó bá pẹ́ nílé ò níí kọ oko ọ̀sán.
english_literal: A farmer who tarries in the house will not object to hoeing the farm in the afternoon.
interpretation_gold: He who dallies makes his tasks that much more difficult.

yoruba: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ẹni kì í tanni.
english_literal: One's palm does not deceive one.
interpretation_gold: One's trust is best placed in one's own resources.

yoruba: Àpáàdì ló tó ko iná lójú.
english_literal: Only a potsherd has what it takes to confront live coal.
interpretation_gold: Only a person capable of confronting a situation should take it on.

yoruba: A kì í bú ọba onígẹ̀gẹ̀ lójú àwọn èèyàn-án ẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not insult a king with a goitre in the presence of his people.
interpretation_gold: Never expose yourself to repercussions with careless speech or indiscreet behavior.

yoruba: Àgbà òṣìkà ńgbin ìyà sílẹ̀ de ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A wicked elder sows suffering for his children.
interpretation_gold: One's character often affects the fortunes of one's children.

yoruba: Àlọ ti alábaun; àbọ̀ ti àna-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: To Tortoise belongs the outward trip; to his father-in-law belongs the return.
interpretation_gold: The person in the right in a dispute, if he/she is too vindictive, quickly becomes the one in the wrong.

yoruba: Àmọ̀jù là ḿmọ ẹkùn-un Sàárẹ́.
english_literal: Saare always goes too far in his description of a leopard.
interpretation_gold: An immoderate display of knowledge soon backfires.

yoruba: A kì í rójú ẹni purọ́ mọ́ni.
english_literal: One does not look into the eyes of a person and still tell a lie against that person.
interpretation_gold: It is always easier to do evil to people when they are absent.

yoruba: Aṣòroówọ̀ bí ẹ̀wù àṣejù.
english_literal: Difficult-to-wear like the garment of immoderation.
interpretation_gold: Wearing the cloak of immoderation exposes one to difficulties.

yoruba: A níṣẹ́ iṣẹ́ ẹ, o ní ò ńlọ sóko; bó o bá lọ sóko ò ḿbọ̀ wá bá a nílé.
english_literal: You are told that a job is your responsibility and you say you are on your way to the farm; you may be on your way to the farm, but the job will be there on your return.
interpretation_gold: One may devise stratagems to defer carrying out one's duties, but they are unlikely to make others carry them out.

yoruba: Àkèekèé ta Kindo lẹpọ̀n, ará ilée Labata ńrojú; kí ló kàn án níbẹ̀?
english_literal: A scorpion stung Kindo in the testicle, and a person from Labata's household frowns in dismay; what business is it of his?
interpretation_gold: One should not take on matters that are not one's business.

yoruba: Àdóìṣí loògùn ọrọ̀.
english_literal: Choosing-a-base-and-maintaining-it is the medicine for wealth.
interpretation_gold: One should not be a rolling stone.

yoruba: Àlá tí ajá bá lá, inú ajá ní ńgbé.
english_literal: Whatever dream the dog dreams remains inside the dog.
interpretation_gold: Keep your own counsel.

yoruba: Asárétete ní ńkọjá ilé; arìngbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni yóò rí oyè jẹ.
english_literal: The fast runner will run past his home; the leisurely stroller is the one who will win the title.
interpretation_gold: A fast start does not guarantee success.

yoruba: Àrísá iná, àkòtagìrì ejò; àgbà tó réjò tí kò sá, ara ikú ló ńyá a.
english_literal: Fire, something-one-sees-and-flees, snake, something one sees and jumps; an elder who sees a snake and does not flee flirts with death.
interpretation_gold: Fire and snakes are not things to take lightly; and elder should not be embarrasses to flee from danger.

yoruba: Ajá tí yó sọnù kì í gbọ́ fèrè ọdẹ.
english_literal: A dog destined to be lost does not hear the hunter's whistle.
interpretation_gold: No matter what help one may render, one cannot save an ill-fated person.

yoruba: A kì í sọ̀rọ̀ orí bíbẹ́ lójú ọmọdé; lọ́rùnlọ́rùn ni yó máa wo olúwa-a ẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not speak of a beheading in the presence of a child; otherwise his gaze will be fixated on the neck of the person concerned.
interpretation_gold: Never discuss a secret in the hearing of a person whose behavior will give the secret away.

yoruba: Adìẹ́ ńjẹkà, ó ḿmumi, ó ńgbé òkúta pẹ́-pẹ̀-pẹ́ mì, ó ní òun ò léhín; ìdérègbè tó léhín ńgbé irin mì bí?
english_literal: The chicken eats corn, drinks water, even swallows small pebbles, and yet complains that it lacks teeth; does the goat that has teeth swallow steel?
interpretation_gold: One should be content with one's lot.

yoruba: A kì í bá ẹlẹ́nu jìjà òru.
english_literal: One does not fight at night with a braggart.
interpretation_gold: Never get into a competition with a braggart unless a witness is present.

yoruba: Àgbẹ̀ ò dáṣọ lóṣù, àfọdún.
english_literal: A farmer does not make new clothes monthly, only annually.
interpretation_gold: The reward for one's labor is often a long time coming.

yoruba: Àkèekèé rìn tapótapó.
english_literal: The scorpion travels accompanied by venom.
interpretation_gold: The stalwart is never unprepared to answer a call.

yoruba: Arúgbó ṣoge rí; àkísà-á lògbà rí.
english_literal: The old person was once a dandy; the rag was once in fashion.
interpretation_gold: Those who are favored should remember that times and circumstances do change.

yoruba: Ata-á kéré; ìjá jù ú.
english_literal: Pepper is small; its fight is much bigger.
interpretation_gold: One should not judge people by their size.

yoruba: Àjànàkú tí a gbẹ́ ọ̀fìn sílẹ̀ dè, erin-ín mojú; erin ò bá ibẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: One digs a pit in the path of the elephant, but the elephant can read signs; the elephant does not go that way.
interpretation_gold: The alert person will thwart an enemy's machinations.

yoruba: Marking one's face with kẹ́kẹ́ is a quest for beauty; marking one's face with àbàjà is a quest for beauty.
interpretation_gold: The pains one takes to adorn oneself are for a good end.

yoruba: Ajẹnifẹ́ni, èkúté ilé.
english_literal: One-that-bites-and-blows-on-the-wound, the house-mouse.
interpretation_gold: One should be wary of adversaries who pose as friends.

yoruba: Àgékù ejò, tí ńṣoro bí agbọ́n.
english_literal: Partially severed snake, that stings like a wasp.
interpretation_gold: A wounded adversary is a vicious one.

yoruba: A kì í rídìí òkun; a kì í rídìí ọsà; ọmọ-oní-gele-gele kì í jẹ́ kí wọ́n rídìí òun.
english_literal: One never sees the bottom of the ocean; no one ever sees the bottom of the lagoon; a well-bred woman will never expose her buttocks to anyone.
interpretation_gold: People should not expose their innermost secrets to all and sundry.

yoruba: Àwòfín ní ḿmú ọ̀rẹ́ bàjẹ́; fírí là ńwo ẹni tí ńwoni.
english_literal: Persistent-staring ruins a friendship; one looks only glancingly at those looking at one.
interpretation_gold: A battle of looks does not help a friendship.

yoruba: A ki ẹsẹ̀ kan bọ odò omi fà á; bí a bá wá ti mejèèjì bọ́ ọ́ ńkọ́?
english_literal: One dips one leg into the stream and the water tugs at it; what if one had dipped both legs into it?
interpretation_gold: Repercussions should not be disproportionate to the act.

yoruba: Ajá tó rí mọ́tò tó dúró fi ara-a ẹ̀ bọ Ògún.
english_literal: A dog that sees a motor vehicle and stands in its was makes itself a sacrifice to Ogun.
interpretation_gold: A person who needlessly endangers him/herself deserves his/her fate.

yoruba: Aláwàdà ló lè ṣọkọ òṣónú; ẹni tí kò lẹ́nu mímú tete ò lè ṣọkọ alápẹpẹ.
english_literal: Only a good-humored person can make a good husband for an ill-humored woman; a person whose mouth is not sharp cannot make a good husband for a hyperactive woman.
interpretation_gold: Incompatible natures cannot make a good marriage.

yoruba: Akóbáni lèkúté-ilé; ejò kì í jàgbàdo.
english_literal: The mouse is a bringer of disaster to the innocent; snakes do not eat corn.
interpretation_gold: Bad company brings bad fortune.

yoruba: Afẹ́fẹ́ tó wọlé tó kó aṣọ iyàrá, ìkìlọ̀ ni fún ẹni tó wọ tiẹ̀ sọrùn.
english_literal: The wind that enters into the house and carries off the clothes in the bedroom is a warning to those who wear theirs around their necks.
interpretation_gold: When disaster befalls the most formidable people, those less formidable should take warning.

yoruba: Àgúnbàjẹ́ ni tolódó.
english_literal: Pounding-until-it-is-ruined is the habit of the owner of the mortar.
interpretation_gold: One should exercise restraint in using what has in abundance.

yoruba: Àpò tí a kò fi ọwọ́ ẹni dá ṣòro-ó kiwọ́ bọ̀.
english_literal: A pocket one did not make with one's own hand is a difficult one to dip one's hand into.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's hands to one's own pockets.

yoruba: 1e Atọrọohungbogbolọ́wọ́Ọlọ́run kì í kánjú.
english_literal: The-seeker-of-all-things-from-God does not yield to impatience.
interpretation_gold: The supplicant must be patient for an answer.

yoruba: Aláàárù kì í sọ pé kí ajé ṣe òun pa; ẹlẹ́rù ńkọ́?
english_literal: The hired carrier does not ask to die from his efforts; what would the owner of the merchandise ask?
interpretation_gold: One should not assume other people's responsibilities and risks.

yoruba: A bu omi lámù a rí eégún; kí ni ẹni tó lọ sódò lọ pọnmi yó rìí?
english_literal: We scoop water from the water pot and see a masquerader; what will the person who goes to draw water at the river find?
interpretation_gold: If a person exposed to minimal risk cries disaster, what would the person exposed to much greater risk do?

yoruba: Àgbọ́ká etí ọlọ́ràn á di.
english_literal: The ear that will insist on hearing everything will go deaf.
interpretation_gold: There is some benefit to ignoring certain things.

yoruba: Àṣesílẹ̀ làbọ̀wábá; ẹni tó da omi síwájú á tẹlẹ̀ tútù.
english_literal: What one puts aside is what one returns to find; whoever dumps water ahead of him/her will step on wet earth.
interpretation_gold: One reaps what one sows.

yoruba: Àyé gba ògùnmọ̀ ó ránṣẹ́ sí òdú; àyé gba Tápà ó kọ́lé ìgunnu.
english_literal: The cultivated vegetable is contented, so it sends for its wild variety; the Nupe (Fulani) person is so comfortable that he builds a tall house.
interpretation_gold: When one enjoys a life of ease, one is tempted to overreach.

yoruba: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀wọ́n ológbò ní ńjìyà; bó bá pẹ́ títí a tó eku-ú pa.
english_literal: Only the newly weaned cat suffers; eventually it will learn to kill mice.
interpretation_gold: A child may be helpless today, but not in the future.

yoruba: Àáké tí ńgégi-í kọsẹ̀, gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nà-á bu ètù sórí.
english_literal: The axe that cuts wood stumbles, and the carver anoints his head with medicinal powder.
interpretation_gold: The evil doer's conscience will not let him/her rest.

yoruba: Àgùntàn bọ̀lọ̀jọ̀ ò gbàgbé eléèrí bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: The big, fat sheep does not soon forget the provider of corn bran.
interpretation_gold: One remembers one's benefactor.

yoruba: Aláǹgbá tó fojú di erè, ikùn ejò ni yó bàá ara-a ẹ̀.
english_literal: A lizard that views a python with disregard will find itself in the belly of the snake.
interpretation_gold: Whoever disdains obvious danger will suffer dire consequences.

yoruba: Àìfẹ̀sọ̀ké ìbòsí ni kò ṣéé gbè.
english_literal: It is an alarm that is raised without moderation that finds no helpers.
interpretation_gold: If the person who raises an alarm puts people off by his or her methods, they will not come to his or her aid.

yoruba: Àìsàn là ńwò, a kì í wo ikú.
english_literal: One treats an illness; one does not treat death.
interpretation_gold: If one neglects an illness until death intervenes, the treatment comes too late.

yoruba: Àáyá kan-án bẹ̀ ọ́ wò; igba wọ́n ti rí ọ.
english_literal: If a single Colubus monkey sees you, be sure that two hundred of them have seen you.
interpretation_gold: A secret that one discloses to one person is as good as published for all.

yoruba: Abẹ ní ḿbẹ orí; oníṣẹ́ àtẹ́lẹsẹ̀ ní ḿbẹ ọ̀nà; bèbè ìdí ní ḿbẹ kíjìpá; bí a dáwọ́-ọ bíbẹni, a tán nínú ẹni.
english_literal: The razor begs the scalp; the wayfarer's soles beg the path; waist beads beg the home-woven cloth; when the begging is done, one lets matters drop.
interpretation_gold: It is a person that is close to one that placates one; after such placation, one allows oneself to be appeased.

yoruba: Àgbọ́kànlé ò pani lébi.
english_literal: A thing in which one reposes one's trust does not make one hunger.
interpretation_gold: One's reserve guarantees one's supplies.

yoruba: Àbùlẹ̀ ní ḿmú aṣọ tọ́; ẹni tí kò tọ́jú àbùlẹ̀ yó ṣe ara-a ẹ̀ lófò aṣọ.
english_literal: Patching extends the life of clothes; whoever does not save materials for patching deprives himself or herself of clothing.
interpretation_gold: Everything has its use; conserve your resources.

yoruba: Atẹ̀hìnrọ́gbọ́n agétí ajá; a gé e létí tán ó fabẹ pamọ́.
english_literal: A-creature-that-learns-wisdom-in-reverse-order, dog-with-severed-ears; after its ears have been severed it hides the razor.
interpretation_gold: Prevention makes sense only before the disaster.

yoruba: À-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, à-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-fọ̀ ni ikú awo.
english_literal: Something-seen-but-unmentionable, something-seen-but-unspeakable is the death of a guardian of the mysteries.
interpretation_gold: The eyes sometimes see things that are too sacred for the mouth to mention.

yoruba: Àròkàn ní ḿmú à-sun-ùn-dá wá; ẹlẹ́kún sunkún ẹ̀ ó lọ.
english_literal: Going-from-one-sadthought-to-another results in endless weeping; the person weeping does his weeping and departs.
interpretation_gold: If one keeps thinking sad thoughts one will ever remain miserable; if one must be sad, one must observe some limits.

yoruba: Ará Ìbàdàn kì í ságun; à ó rìn sẹ́hìn ni wọ́n ńwí.
english_literal: Ibadan people do not run from war; what they say is, “We will fall back a little.”
interpretation_gold: There are ways of avoiding battle without seeming to do so.

yoruba: A kì í gbélé gba ọfá láìlọ ogun.
english_literal: One does not sit at home, not go to war, and yet be shot with an arrow.
interpretation_gold: One should be safe in one's own home.

yoruba: Àkàlàmàgbò-ó ṣoore ó yọ gẹ̀gẹ̀ lọ́rùn.
english_literal: The ground hornbill did a favor and developed a goitre.
interpretation_gold: One's good deeds sometimes come back to haunt one.

yoruba: Àlùkẹrẹsẹ ò mọ̀ pé olóko-ó ládàá.
english_literal: The weed did not know that the farmer had a machete.
interpretation_gold: The evil doer does not consider the response of the person wronged.

yoruba: Àkèekèé ò ṣé-é dì níbò.
english_literal: A scorpion is not a thing to close one's palms on.
interpretation_gold: Some matters call for extreme caution.

yoruba: Àìtètèmólè, olèé mólóko.
english_literal: Because of the delay in apprehending the thief, the thief apprehends the owner of the farm.
interpretation_gold: One must be alert in dealing with slippery people; otherwise they turn the tables on one.

yoruba: Arọ tí kò lẹ́sẹ̀ nílẹ̀-ẹ́ lọ́gbọ́n nínú.
english_literal: A cripple who has no legs to stand on has wisdom inside him.
interpretation_gold: Whatever handicaps one might have, one will have some asset.

yoruba: Atàkò fọ́ ẹyin àparò; ohun ojú ńwá lojú ńrí.
english_literal: Person-who-stones-and-breaks-partridge's-eggs; the eyes find what the eyes seek.
interpretation_gold: The culprit is asking for trouble, and he will not be disappointed.

yoruba: A sìnkú tán, alugba ò lọ; ó fẹ́ ṣúpó ni?
english_literal: The funeral is over, but the calabash beater does not take his leave; does he want to inherit a wife?
interpretation_gold: This proverb has the same import as, A kúnlẹ̀, a pàgbò . . .

yoruba: Alárìnjó tí yó jòó, kó ti ìwòyí mú ẹsẹ̀ kó le kó kó kó.
english_literal: The person who will engage in itinerant dancing should look to his legs in good time.
interpretation_gold: Before embarking on a trade, one should hone one's tools.

yoruba: À-gbẹ́rù-àì-wẹ̀hìn lọ̀pálábá fi gbàgbé ìyá ẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: Picking-up-one's-load-without-checking-one's-rear caused the piece of broken bottle to forget its mother on the ground.
interpretation_gold: The broken bottle suffered its fate, perhaps, because it was not careful about what it “carried.” The hasty traveller leaves his goods behind.

yoruba: Àfojúdi ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ní ńjẹ́ “Ẹrú-kò-ní.”
english_literal: It is an impertinent bead that is named “The-slave-does-not-own-its like.”
interpretation_gold: One must be mindful of how one's actions might affect others.

yoruba: Agbójúlógún fi ara-a rẹ̀ fóṣì ta.
english_literal: He-who-places-his-hopes-on-inheritance delivers himself to destitution.
interpretation_gold: One should secure one's own living.

yoruba: Àṣá ḿbá ẹyẹlé ṣeré, ẹyẹlé ńyọ̀; ẹyẹlé ńfikú ṣeré.
english_literal: The kite plays with the pigeon and the pigeon rejoices; the pigeon is courting death.
interpretation_gold: An enemy who pretends friendship is so much more dangerous.

yoruba: A kì í fi ìkánjú lá ọbẹ̀ gbígbóná.
english_literal: One does not eat scalding stew in a hurry.
interpretation_gold: Patience is best in delicate or difficult matters.

yoruba: Ayé ò ṣéé fipá jẹ.
english_literal: Life is nothing to enjoy heedlessly.
interpretation_gold: Life demands caution.

yoruba: Bí ẹnìkán ṣe ohun tí ẹnìkan ò ṣe rí, ojú-u rẹ̀ á rí ohun tí ẹnìkan ò rí rí.
english_literal: If a person does what no one has ever done before, his eyes will see what no one has ever seen before.
interpretation_gold: Those who do unusual things should expect unusual consequences.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá láyà-a rìndọ̀rìndọ̀, a kì í jẹ aáyán.
english_literal: If one's stomach is not immune to nausea, one does not eat roaches.
interpretation_gold: One should avoid things one cannot stomach.

yoruba: Bí a bá wí a dàbí òwe; bí a ò bá wí a dàbí ìjà.
english_literal: If one speaks it sounds as though one was speaking in proverbs; if one does not speak it seems as though one was picking a fight.
interpretation_gold: In certain delicate situations no option is safe.

yoruba: Baálé ilé kú, wọ́n fi olókùnrùn rọ́lé; ẹkún ńgorí ẹkún.
english_literal: The man of the house died and they put an invalid in his place; weeping climbs upon weeping.
interpretation_gold: People known to be unsuitable should not be entrusted with important affairs.

yoruba: Bọ̀rọ̀kìnní àṣejù, oko olówó ni ḿmúni lọ.
english_literal: Excessive devotion to fashion leads one to pawn oneself.
interpretation_gold: Excessive trendiness depletes a person's resources.

yoruba: “Baálé pè mí nkò wá”, ọ̀hànhàn ní ńpa wọ́n.
english_literal: “The patriarch of the compound called me but I did not respond” dies of anxiety.
interpretation_gold: A person who defies his/her main succor heads for ruin.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá lè kú, ìpẹ̀ là ńgbà.
english_literal: If one is unable (or unwilling) to die, one accepts consolation.
interpretation_gold: Unless one would die of grieving, one should allow oneself to be consoled.

yoruba: “Bá mi mádìẹ” kì í fi orúnkún bó.
english_literal: “Help me catch a chicken” does not scrape his knees.
interpretation_gold: Overzealousness in helping others is a fault.

yoruba: Bí a bá bu ìrẹ̀ jẹ, ká bu ìrẹ̀ sápò.
english_literal: If one takes a bite of a cricket, one should put a little in one's pocket.
interpretation_gold: Even if one has only a little, one should still save something for the morrow.

yoruba: Bí aáṣẹ́ bá ti ńfò, bẹ́ẹ̀ la ti ńsọ̀kò sí i.
english_literal: It is according to the flight pattern of the standardwinged nightjar
interpretation_gold: One responds according to the situation one is confronted with.

yoruba: Bí a bá bu ọba tí a sẹ́, ọba a fini sílẹ.
english_literal: If one insults a king and denies doing so, the king leaves one in peace.
interpretation_gold: One should not be held accountable for an insult one recants.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá ṣe fún ilẹ̀, a kì í fi ọwọ́ sọ ọ́.
english_literal: If one has done nothing for Earth, one does not swear by it.
interpretation_gold: One cannot expect sustenance from where one has not cultivated.

yoruba: Bí a bá dákẹ́, tara ẹni a báni dákẹ́.
english_literal: If one keeps silent, what is in one's body keeps silent with one.
interpretation_gold: If one does not disclose one's problems one can expect no help.

yoruba: Bí ògbó ẹni ò bá dánilójú, a kì í fi gbárí wò.
english_literal: If one does not trust one's cudgel, one does not try it on one's own head.
interpretation_gold: One should not swear by something about which one is not certain.

yoruba: Bí a bá fi ọdún mẹ́ta pilẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ẹ wèrè, ọjọ́ wo la ó bunijẹ?
english_literal: If one takes three years to prepare for one's madness, when will one start biting people?
interpretation_gold: Preparations for an action should not be endless.

yoruba: Bí adìẹ́ bá gbélẹ̀ a ya òpìpì.
english_literal: If a chicken always keeps to the ground, it becomes flightless.
interpretation_gold: Whatever endowment one has, one loses it if one neglects it.

yoruba: Bí a bá róbìnrin à lérí ogun; bí a bá róbìnrin à sọ̀rọ̀ ìjà; bí a dé ojú ogun à ba búbú.
english_literal: When one sees women one boasts of war; when one sees women one talks of battle; when one gets to battle, one lies low.
interpretation_gold: Before women one protects one's image; in battle one protects one's life.

yoruba: Bí a bá fi dídùn họ ifàn, a ó họra dé egun.
english_literal: If one scratches an itch as long as the sensation is pleasant, one will scratch down to the bone.
interpretation_gold: Even pleasures should be pursued in moderation.

yoruba: Bí ẹlẹ́hìnkùlé ò sùn, à pẹ́ lẹ́hìnkùlé-e rẹ̀ títí; bó pẹ́ títí orun a gbé onílé lọ.
english_literal: If the owner of the backyard does not sleep, one stays in the backyard for a long time, sooner or later the owner of the house will fall asleep.
interpretation_gold: Patience accomplishes all ends.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá ní èsè ẹ̀fà, a kì í kó iṣu òje.
english_literal: If one does not have twelve hundred cowries in savings, one does not purchase yams worth fourteen hundred cowries.
interpretation_gold: One's aspirations should match one's means.

yoruba: Bánú sọ, má bàá èèyàn sọ; èèyàn ò sí; ayé ti dèké.
english_literal: Counsel with your inside, do not counsel with people; “good” people are no longer to be found; the world has turned false.
interpretation_gold: There are no people to trust, only oneself.

yoruba: Bí ẹjá bá sùn, ẹja á fi ẹja jẹ.
english_literal: If fish sleeps, fish will devour fish.
interpretation_gold: If one does not wish to be taken advantage of, one must be ever watchful.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá rígún, à fàkàlà ṣẹbọ.
english_literal: If one cannot find a vulture, one sacrifices a hornbill.
interpretation_gold: One makes do with what one has.

yoruba: Bí ìdí ìkokò kò bá dá a lójú, kì í gbé egungun mì.
english_literal: If the wolf does not have faith in its anus it does not swallow bones.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt a thing whose repercussions one cannot withstand.

yoruba: Bí a bá ńjà, bí í kákú là ńwí?
english_literal: Even though we are quarrelling, should we wish each other dead?
interpretation_gold: Quarrels should stop short of death wishes.

yoruba: Bí a bá fi ọwọ́ kan fọmọ fọ́kọ, ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá kì í ṣeé gbà á mọ́.
english_literal: If one gives a girl away in marriage with one hand, ten hands will not suffice to take her back.
interpretation_gold: Mistakes made casually are seldom easy to correct.

yoruba: Bí a bá sọ́ pé ẹyẹ ni yó jẹ ojú ẹni, bí a rí tí-ń-tín, a ó máa sá lọ.
english_literal: If one has been told that a bird will eat one's eyes, when one sees the tiniest of birds, one takes to one's heels.
interpretation_gold: If one has prior warning of a peril, one takes extraordinary precautions.

yoruba: Bí a bá ní ká jẹ èkuru kó tán, a kì í gbọn ọwọ́-ọ rẹ̀ sáwo.
english_literal: If one wishes to clean one's plate of dry bean grits, one does not keep scraping the remnants from one's fingers onto the plate.
interpretation_gold: If one wishes a quarrel to end, one does not keep recalling its cause.

yoruba: Bí ọwọ́ ò bá tẹ èkù idà, a kì í bèrè ikú tó pa baba ẹni.
english_literal: If one has not laid one's hand on the hilt of the sword, one does not ask what death killed one's father.
interpretation_gold: Until one is able, one should not attempt to right an injustice.

yoruba: Bí a bá lé ẹni, tí a kò bá ẹni, ìwọ̀n là ḿbá ẹni-í ṣọ̀tá mọ.
english_literal: If one chases a person and does not catch up with the person, one should moderate one's hatred of the person.
interpretation_gold: Envy should not turn into hatred.

yoruba: Bí a ó ti ṣe é ní ńfi ara-a rẹ̀ hàn.
english_literal: How it will be accomplished will reveal itself.
interpretation_gold: The way to accomplish a task will always reveal itself.

yoruba: Bí àjànàkú ò bá gbẹ́kẹ̀lé fùrọ̀, kì í mi òdù àgbọn.
english_literal: If an elephant is not sure of its anus, it does not swallow whole coconuts.
interpretation_gold: Unless one can cope with the consequences, one does not engage in an action.

yoruba: Bí àjẹ́ bá mupo, ojú-u rẹ̀ a rọ̀.
english_literal: When a witch has drunk oil, she calms down.
interpretation_gold: After one has achieved one's goal, one should relax.

yoruba: Bíbi là ḿbi odò wò ká tó wọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: One asks a river before one enters it.
interpretation_gold: One must study well any situation before one involves oneself in it.

yoruba: Bí ekòló bá kọ ebè, ara-a rẹ̀ ni yó gbìn sí i.
english_literal: If a worm makes a heap, it is itself that it will plant in it.
interpretation_gold: The consequences of a person's actions will fall on the person's own head.

yoruba: Bí a bá fa àgbò féégún, à fi okùn-un rẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: If one drags a sheep to present to a masquerader, one lets go of its leash.
interpretation_gold: When one has made a gift of something, one should forget about it.

yoruba: Bí àṣá bá ḿbínú, sùúrù ló yẹ ọlọ́jà.
english_literal: If the kite is displaying anger, the best response for the trader is patience.
interpretation_gold: One must learn forbearance in the face of provocation.

yoruba: Bí a bá sọ̀kò sí àárín ọjà, ará ilé ẹni ní ḿbà.
english_literal: If one throws a stone into the market place, it hits someone from one's household.
interpretation_gold: One's random acts of wickedness are liable to affect those close to one.

yoruba: Bí awó ti ńlù lawó ti ńjó.
english_literal: As the initiate of mysteries drums, so the initiate of mysteries dances.
interpretation_gold: One's actions are best suited to the circumstances.

yoruba: Bí kò bá sí oníṣẹ́ iṣẹ́ ò leè lọ; bí kò bá sí ọlọ́wẹ̀ a kì í ṣọ̀wẹ̀; àkẹ̀hìnsí ọlọ́wẹ̀ là ńṣípá.
english_literal: If the owner of the job is absent the job does not progress; if the person who engaged the help is absent no help is given; when the back of the person who engaged help is turned, one lifts one's hands from the job.
interpretation_gold: The employee is most industrious when under the supervision of the employer.

yoruba: Bí o máa ra ilá ra ilá, bí o máa gba ènì gba ènì; ọmọdé kì í wá sọ́ja Agbó-mẹ́kùn kó wá mú eku.
english_literal: If you wish to buy okro, buy okro; if you wish to receive a gratuity do so; a child does not come to a tiger hunt and catch rats.
interpretation_gold: One's deed's should be appropriate to the location.

yoruba: Bí olówe-é bá mọ òwe-e rẹ̀, tí kò já a, ẹ̀rù ìjà ḿbà á ni.
english_literal: If the butt of a proverb recognizes it but does not acknowledge it, he is afraid of a fight.
interpretation_gold: A person who has reason to take offence but does not is avoiding a fight.

yoruba: Bí a bá fi ojú igi gbígbẹ wo tútù, tútù-ú lè wó pani.
english_literal: If one approaches a dried-up tree as one would a green one, it is liable to crash on one and crush one to death.
interpretation_gold: One should be alive to the peculiarities of whatever situations one finds oneself in.

yoruba: Bí ológbò-ó bá ṣẹ̀ ńpa ẹmọ́, à mọ̀ pé ó máa lọ.
english_literal: When a cat begins to kill guinea pigs, one knows it is ready to go.
interpretation_gold: A person who embarks on improper behavior invites ostracism.

yoruba: Bí ọ̀nà-á dé orí àpáta, níṣe ní ńpin.
english_literal: When a trail comes to a rock, it ends.
interpretation_gold: When an insurmountable obstacle intervenes, matters must come to an end.

yoruba: Bí ìlùú bá dún àdúnjù, yó fàya.
english_literal: If a drum makes too much noise, it breaks.
interpretation_gold: Disaster follows excess.

yoruba: Bí a bá fẹ́ràn ọ̀rẹ́ ẹni láfẹ̀ẹ́jù, bó bá forígbún, ìjà níńdà.
english_literal: If one loves one's friend beyond reason, when that friend bumps his/her head a fight results.
interpretation_gold: Friendship that knows no limits is a burden.

yoruba: Bí alágbára-á bá jẹ ọ́ níyà, fẹ̀rín sí i.
english_literal: If a powerful person mistreats you, burst into laughter.
interpretation_gold: Never protest against victimization by one against whom you can do nothing.

yoruba: Bí ọtí bá kún inú, ọtí á pọmọ; bí oòrùn-ún bá pọ̀ lápọ̀jù a sọ ọmọ di wèrè; bí a bá lọ́ba lánìíjù a sínni níwín; tẹ̀tẹ̀ ẹ̀gún pọ̀ lódò o di olú eri.
english_literal: If wine fills the stomach it intoxicates a child; if there is too much sun it makes a child go insane; if one has too much authority one goes mad; spinach grew in too great abundance by the stream and became ordinary weed.
interpretation_gold: Excess in anything is evil.

yoruba: Bí ojú alákẹdun ò dá igi, kì í gùn ún.
english_literal: If the monkey is not certain about a tree, it does not climb it.
interpretation_gold: One should not embark on projects one cannot accomplish.

yoruba: Bí iṣu ẹní bá funfun, à fọwọ́ bò ó jẹ.
english_literal: If one's yam is white, one eats it furtively.
interpretation_gold: One would be unwise to flaunt one's good fortune.

yoruba: Bí oníṣú bá fi iṣu-u rẹ̀ se ẹ̀bẹ, ọgbọ́n a tán nínú a-tu-èèpo-jẹ.
english_literal: If the owner of the yams cuts them for porridge, the person who gleans what sticks to the peelings is at a loss for what to do.
interpretation_gold: If the perennial victim learns to protect himself, the victimizer is stumped.

yoruba: Bí ẹlẹ́jọ́ bá mọ ẹjọ́-ọ rẹ̀ lẹ́bi, kì í pẹ́ níkùnúnlẹ̀.
english_literal: If the person involved in a case acknowledges his or her guilt, he or she does not last long on his or her knees.
interpretation_gold: Penitence invites leniency.

yoruba: Bí òwe ò bá jọ òwe, a kì í pa á.
english_literal: If a proverb does not apply to a situation, one does not use it.
interpretation_gold: One's comparison's should be apt.

yoruba: Bí a bá ńretí òfò, ká fi ohun tọrẹ.
english_literal: If one expects a loss, one should make a gift of what one has.
interpretation_gold: Rather give things away than lose them.

yoruba: Bí ọmọdé ò rí àjẹkù-u kìnìún nínú igbo, a ní kí ẹran bí ẹkùn ó pa òun.
english_literal: If a child has not seen the leavings of a lion in the forest he prays that he might be killed by an animal like the leopard.
interpretation_gold: One is liable to disdain forces the extent of whose powers one is ignorant of.

yoruba: Bọ̀rọ̀kìnnín lọ̀tá ìlú; afínjú lọba ńpa.
english_literal: The dandy is the enemy of the town; it is the finicky person that the king kills.
interpretation_gold: The people of a town may envy a dandy; but it is the reckless person who comes to grief.

yoruba: Bí alẹ́ bá lẹ́, adẹ́tẹ̀ a rìn, a yan.
english_literal: When night falls, the leper walks and struts.
interpretation_gold: Night is a welcome cloak for blemishes.

yoruba: Bí ojú onísó ò bá sunwọ̀n, a kì í lọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: If the face of the person who farted is baleful, one does not make a big fuss about the fart.
interpretation_gold: One does not incite a person spoiling for a fight.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá lè mú ọkọ, a kì í na obìnrin-in rẹ.
english_literal: If one is no match for the husband, one does not hit the wife.
interpretation_gold: Never provoke a fight you cannot fight.

yoruba: Bí ọmọ ẹní bá dára, ká sọ pé ó dára; bí-i ká fi ṣaya ẹni kọ́.
english_literal: If one's daughter is beautiful, one may acknowledge that she is beautiful, but one may not make her one's wife.
interpretation_gold: However much one might be attracted to a forbidden thing, one must avoid it.

yoruba: Bí ológbò-ó bá pa eku, a fi ìrù-u rẹ̀ dẹlé.
english_literal: When a cat kills a mouse, it uses the tail as a sentry.
interpretation_gold: One should save something of one's fortune for the future.

yoruba: Bí a bá sọ̀rọ̀ fún olófòófó, ajádìí agbọ̀n la sọ ọ́ sí.
english_literal: Whatever one says to a talebearer one says to a basket that has lost its bottom.
interpretation_gold: Words whispered to a talebearer are in effect broadcast.

yoruba: Bí a bá bú ọba, à sẹ́; bí a bá bú ọ̀ṣọ̀run, à sẹ́.
english_literal: If one insults the king, one denies doing so; if one insults the chief minister, one denies doing so.
interpretation_gold: One may disdain authority, but one should not expose oneself to punishment for doing so.

yoruba: Bí ọ̀ràn ò tán, ibì kan là ńgbé; arékété lohun ńṣe.
english_literal: If a problem is not over, one stays in place; it is the over-eager person who comes to grief.
interpretation_gold: One should await the outcome of a confused situation before embarking on further action.

yoruba: Bí ọ̀ràn-án bá ṣú òkùnkùn, à bẹ̀ ẹ́ wò lábẹ́.
english_literal: If a matter is dark, one peeps at it under cover.
interpretation_gold: If the facts of a matter are a close secret, one should quietly investigate it.

yoruba: Bí a kò rówó ra ẹrú, à sọ adìẹ ẹni lórúkọ.
english_literal: If one has no money to buy a slave, one gives one's chicken a name.
interpretation_gold: One should somehow make do with what one has and be content.

yoruba: Bí a kò bá lówó aládìn-ín, à jẹun lójúmọmọ, à gbálẹ̀ sùn wàrà.
english_literal: If one has no money for lamp oil, one eats in the daytime, and one sweeps the house and goes to sleep in good time.
interpretation_gold: One's plans and actions should fit one's resources.

yoruba: Bí ooré bá pọ̀ lápọ̀jù, ibi ní ńdà.
english_literal: If goodness is excessive, it becomes evil.
interpretation_gold: There can be too much of even a good thing.

yoruba: Bí iná bá jóni, tó jó ọmọ ẹni, tara ẹni là ńkọ́ gbọ̀n.
english_literal: If one is on fire and one's child is on fire, one douses one's fire first.
interpretation_gold: Without first attending to one's needs, one cannot attend to others'.

yoruba: Bí a bá perí ajá, ká perí ìkòkò tí a ó fi sè é.
english_literal: If one talks of the dog, one should also talk of the pot one will use to cook it.
interpretation_gold: If one proposes a momentous action, one should also consider the consequences.

yoruba: Bí èṣù ikú bá ńṣe ìgbín nìgbín ńyẹ́yin.
english_literal: It is when the snail wants to invite death that it lays eggs.
interpretation_gold: A person who knows an action will be disastrous but carries it our anyway deserves what he gets.

yoruba: Bí ìfà bí ìfà lọmọdé fi ńdáràn wọlé.
english_literal: As though he were stumbling on treasures, thus a youth brings trouble into the household.
interpretation_gold: A youth seldom realized what actions of his will involve his household in trouble.

yoruba: Bí a bá fi ọdún mẹ́ta ṣánpá, ọdún mélòó la ó fi fò?
english_literal: If one spends three years flapping one's arms, how many years will one take to fly?
interpretation_gold: Preparations for an action should not be interminable.

yoruba: Bí a bá ṣí ìdí ẹni sókè, ọmọ aráyé á rọ omi gbígbóná sí i.
english_literal: If one exposes one's anus to view, people will fill it with hot water.
interpretation_gold: If one exposes one's vulnerability to people, one will be done in.

yoruba: Bí a bá ní ká bẹ́ igi, a ó bẹ̀ẹ́ èèyàn.
english_literal: If one attempts to cut a tree, one will cut people.
interpretation_gold: If one behaved towards certain people as they deserve, one would offend innocent people.

yoruba: Bí òní ti rí, ọ̀la ò rí bẹ́ẹ̀, ni babaláwo-ó fi ńdÍfá lọ́rọọrún.
english_literal: As today is, tomorrow will not be, hence the diviner consults the oracle every five days.
interpretation_gold: Since no one knows the future, one must constantly reassess one's decisions.

yoruba: Bí alágẹmọ-ọ́ bá fẹ́ kọjá, ìjàm̀pere ò ní-í jà.
english_literal: When the chameleon wishes to go by, the black ants refrain from stinging.
interpretation_gold: The cautious person is immune to the dangers that beset others.

yoruba: Dá-ǹkan-dá-ǹkan, tí kì í dáṣọ̀, tí kì í dẹ́wù.
english_literal: Originator-of-problems: he not make a cloth and does not make a dress.
interpretation_gold: What a troublemaker brings is trouble, never anything useful.

yoruba: Dá-mìíràn-kún-mìíràn tí ńpa àpatà ẹyẹlé.
english_literal: One-who-commits-crimes-atop-crimes: he butchers pigeons for sale.
interpretation_gold: The person referred to is a hardened criminal who piles crimes on crimes.

yoruba: Dàńdógó
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limits.

yoruba: Dàda ò leè jà, ṣùgbọ́n ó lábùúrò tó gbójú.
english_literal: Dada cannot fight, but he has a brave younger brother.
interpretation_gold: One may not be able to do much, but one has relatives to take one's cause.

yoruba: Dágun-dágun Kaletu tí ńdá ìbejì lápá.
english_literal: Troublemaker of Kaletu, who breaks the arms of a twin.
interpretation_gold: A person who provokes someone with powerful champions is a trouble maker.

yoruba: Eré-e kí lajá ḿbá ẹkùn ṣe?
english_literal: What sort of sport is it that the dog is engaged in with the leopard?
interpretation_gold: One should know better than to court disaster.

yoruba: Ewú logbó; irùngbọ̀n làgbà; máamú làfojúdi.
english_literal: Grey hair shows age; a beard shows maturity; a moustache shows impudence.
interpretation_gold: One's appearance in a group sometimes indicates one's attitude towards the group.

yoruba: Èèyàn-án ní òun ó bà ọ́ jẹ́ o ní kò tó bẹ́ẹ̀; bí ó bá ní o ò nùdí, ẹni mélòó lo máa fẹ fùrọ̀ hàn?
english_literal: A person vows to disgrace you and you respond that there is no way he can succeed; if he spreads the word that you did not clean yourself after defecating, to how many people will you display your anus?
interpretation_gold: No one is immune to malicious defamation.

yoruba: Èyí ò tófò, èyí ò tófò; fìlà ìmàle-é kù pẹ́tẹ́kí.
english_literal: “This is no great loss; this is no great loss;” the muslim's cap dwindles to almost nothing.
interpretation_gold: If one keeps dispensing of one's property only a little at a time, soon little will be left.

yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ kì í wọlé tọ ìkokò.
english_literal: A goat does not venture into the lair of a wolf.
interpretation_gold: Never knowingly put yourself in harm's way.

yoruba: Èpè-é pọ̀ ju ohun tó nù lọ; abẹ́rẹ́ sọnù a gbé ṣẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ síta.
english_literal: The curse is out of all proportion to the lost article; a needle is lost “the owner” brings out his/her magic wand.
interpretation_gold: One should not overreact to events.

yoruba: Eku tí yó pa ológìnní ò níí dúró láyé.
english_literal: The mouse that attempts to kill a cat will not live long on this earth.
interpretation_gold: It is foolhardy for one to take on powers that can destroy one.

yoruba: Èèyan má-jẹ̀ẹ́-kí-èèyàn-kú ḿbẹ níbòmíràn; bó-le-kú-ó-kú m̀bẹ nílé-e wa.
english_literal: Save-the-person-from-death type of people abounds elsewhere; let-the-person-die-if-he/she-wishes type abounds in our house.
interpretation_gold: It is not our way to stop people bent on destroying themselves. Also, We do have evil people in our home.

yoruba: Èyí ayé ńṣe ng kà ṣàì ṣe; bádìẹ-ẹ́ máa wọ ọ̀ọ̀dẹ̀ a bẹ̀rẹ̀.
english_literal: Whatever the rest of the world does I will not forswear; when a chicken wants to enter the porch it stoops.
interpretation_gold: One should not violate established custom.

yoruba: Eṣinṣin ò mọkú; jíjẹ ni tirẹ̀.
english_literal: The fly does not heed death; all its cares to do is eat.
interpretation_gold: The fly will persist in attacking an open sore, heedless of death; nothing will keep an addict from the thing he/she is addicted to.

yoruba: Èmi ò wá ikún inú agbè fi jiyán; ṣùgbọ́n bíkún bá yí sínú agbè mi mo lè fi jiyán.
english_literal: I will not go looking for a squirrel in my gourd to eat with pounded yam; but if a squirrel falls into my gourd I will eat it with pounded yam.
interpretation_gold: I will not steal, but neither will I refuse a lucky find.

yoruba: Èké tan-ni síjà ẹkùn, ó fi ọrán ṣíṣẹ́ sápó ẹni.
english_literal: The devious person goads one to confront a leopard and fills one's quiver with broken arrows.
interpretation_gold: One risks danger if one follows a devious person's counsel.

yoruba: Èrò kì í; jẹ́wọ́-ọ “Mo tà tán.”
english_literal: The trader never confesses, “I sold all my wares.”
interpretation_gold: People are ever loath to disclose the extent of their good fortune.

yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ jẹ ó relé; àgùntán jẹ ó relé; à-jẹ-ì-wálé ló ba ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: The goat forages and returns home; the sheep forages and returns home; the pig's flaw is its habit of not returning home after foraging.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing wrong with travelling, as long as one knows when to return home.

yoruba: Èṣù ò ṣejò; ẹni tó tẹ ejò mọ́lẹ̀ lẹ̀bá ḿbá.
english_literal: There is no disaster stalking the snake; it is whoever steps on a snake that is in trouble.
interpretation_gold: It is not the snake inadvertently stepped on that is in peril; it is the person who inadvertently steps on the snake.

yoruba: Etí mẹta ò yẹ orí; èèyàn mẹ́ta ò dúró ní méjì-méjì.
english_literal: Three ears are unbecoming for the head; three people cannot stand in twos.
interpretation_gold: Good things are not good in all situations; one can have too much of a good thing.

yoruba: Eku ò gbọdọ̀ ná ọjà tí ológìnní dá.
english_literal: A mouse dares not visit a market established by a cat.
interpretation_gold: One should not deliberately court disaster.

yoruba: Fẹ̀hìntì kí o rí ìṣe èké; farapamọ́ kí; o gbọ́ bí aṣeni-í ti ńsọ.
english_literal: Sit back and you will see how a devious person operates; conceal yourself and you will hear how those who seek others' destruction speak.
interpretation_gold: One must be cagey in order to learn the truth about unreliable people.

yoruba: Fáàárí àṣejù, oko olówó ní ḿmú ọmọ lọ.
english_literal: Intemperate dandyism lands a youth in a creditor's farm as a pawn.
interpretation_gold: Squandered resources bring destitution.

yoruba: Fi ọ̀ràn sínú pète ẹ̀rín;fi ebi sínú sunkún ayo.
english_literal: Keep your troubles inside and laugh heartily; keep your hunger hidden and pretend to weep from satiation.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's woes to oneself and show a happy face to the world.

yoruba: Fò síhìnín fò sọ́hùnún làkèré fi ńṣẹ́ nítan.
english_literal: Jump this way, jump that way is the way a frog breaks its thigh.
interpretation_gold: Restlessness lands people is trouble.

yoruba: Fi ohun wé ohun, fi ọ̀ràn wé ọ̀ràn;fi ọ̀ràn jì ká yìn ọ́.
english_literal: Liken one thing to another, liken one matter to another; forgive and forget and earn people's praise.
interpretation_gold: Rather than permit an offence to recall earlier ones, one should forgive and forget.

yoruba: Fi ẹ̀jẹ̀ sínú, tu itọ́ funfun jáde.
english_literal: Keep your red blood inside and spit out clear saliva.
interpretation_gold: Never show your hand to your enemy; let not your words or action reveal your intentions to your enemy.

yoruba: Gùdùgudu ò túra sílẹ̀ lẹ́ẹ̀kan.
english_literal: Poisonous yam has never lost its skin.
interpretation_gold: A certain person has never been known to be off his or her guard.

yoruba: Gùdùgudu-ú kan légbò kán-ín-kán-ín.
english_literal: Poisonous yam's roots are sour indeed.
interpretation_gold: The subject is something one must stay away from, for encounter with it is unpleasant.

yoruba: Gìdì-gìdì ò mọ́là; ká ṣiṣẹ́ bí ẹrú ò da nǹkan.
english_literal: Scurrying around does not ensure prosperity; working like a slave results in nothing.
interpretation_gold: One does not necessarily prosper by working oneself to death.

yoruba: Gbígbòòrò là ńṣe ọ̀nà igi.
english_literal: The path along which a log will be rolled must be made wide enough.
interpretation_gold: One should make provisions adequate for the task ahead.

yoruba: Gbogbo ajá ní ńjẹ imí: èyí tó bá jẹ tiẹ̀ mẹ́nu laráyé ńpè ní dìgbòlugi.
english_literal: All dogs eat excrement, but only those that smear their mouths with it are described as rabid.
interpretation_gold: No one is without blemish, but one must keep one's flaws within reasonable bounds.

yoruba: “Gbà sókè” ni “Gbà sọ́kọ̀”; ohun tá a bá sọ síwájú là ḿbá.
english_literal: “Put this above (ashore)” equals “Put this in the boat”; it is what one throws ahead that one finds in one's path.
interpretation_gold: One reaps the rewards of the good one sows.

yoruba: Gbẹ́ran-gbẹ́ran ò gbé ẹkùn.
english_literal: No animal pilferer ever pilfers a leopard.
interpretation_gold: There are some risks even the most brazen risk taker would be wise to avoid.

yoruba: Gbéjò-gbéjò ò gbé ọká.
english_literal: No snake dancer dances with a cobra.
interpretation_gold: There are some perils even the bravest of people should not court.

yoruba: Gbogbo ìjà nìjà; bóo gbémi lulẹ̀ mà mọ́ ẹ lójú lákọ lákọ.
english_literal: Every way of fighting is a legitimate way of fighting. If you are strong enough to throw me, I will fight back by looking at you with absolute disdain.
interpretation_gold: One must know one's limitations, especially when up against insurmountable odds.

yoruba: Gbólóhùn kan-án ba ọ̀rọ̀ jẹ́; gbólóhùn kan-án tún ọ̀rọ̀ ṣe.
english_literal: One solitary statement muddies an entire affair; one solitary statement clears all the confusion.
interpretation_gold: A single sentence can cause irreparable damage; a single sentence can also repair the greatest relational damage.

yoruba: Gbogbo obìnrin ló ńgbéṣẹ́, èyí tó bá ṣe tiẹ̀ láṣejù laráyé ńpè láṣẹ́wó.
english_literal: All women are unfaithful; only those who know no moderation are put down as whores.
interpretation_gold: Nobody is without blemish; the important thing is to keep one's from getting out of hand.

yoruba: Gbólóhùn kan la bi elépo; elépo ńṣe ìrànrán.
english_literal: One asks only one question of the palm-oil seller, but she rambles endlessly on.
interpretation_gold: A person plagued by a bad conscience makes endless excuses when asked simple questions.

yoruba: Ìnàkí kì í ránṣẹ́ ìjà sẹ́kùn.
english_literal: The baboon does not send an ultimatum to the leopard.
interpretation_gold: People should not challenge forces they are no match for.

yoruba: Ijó àjójù ní ńmú kí okó-o eégún yọ jáde.
english_literal: Unrestrained dancing is what causes the masquerader's penis to become exposed.
interpretation_gold: One should exercise restraint in performing even pleasurable activities.

yoruba: Ibi tí a gbọ́n mọ là ńṣòwò-o màlúù mọ.
english_literal: One should limit the depth of one's involvement in cattle trading to the extent of one's astuteness.
interpretation_gold: One should be careful not to put at risk more than one can afford, or to get in above one's head.

yoruba: Igúnnugún gbọ́n sínú.
english_literal: The vulture conceals a lot of wisdom in itself.
interpretation_gold: A person may be quite astute even though he/she appears foolish.

yoruba: Ìgbín tó ńjẹ̀ ní màfọ̀n, tí ò kúrò ní màfọ̀n, ewé àfọ̀n ni wọn ó fi dì í dele.
english_literal: A snail that forages at the base of the African breadfruit tree and never leaves the base of the African breadfruit tree will be taken home wrapped in the leaf of the African breadfruit tree.
interpretation_gold: One should know when to quit, or else one would wind up in trouble.

yoruba: Ìgbín ńràjò ó filé-e ẹ̀ ṣẹrù.
english_literal: The snail sets out on a journey and makes a load of its house.
interpretation_gold: Comment on people who are overly possessive of their goods or turf.

yoruba: Ìkòkò ńseṣu ẹnìkan ò gbọ́; iṣú dénú odó ariwó ta.
english_literal: Yams cook in a pot and nobody knows, but when the yams get into the mortar alarms sound.
interpretation_gold: Matters disclosed only to prudent people can be contained, but once they leak to irresponsible persons they become broadcast.

yoruba: Ìyẹ̀wù kan ṣoṣo ò lè gba olókùnrùn méjì.
english_literal: One single room will not do for two invalids.
interpretation_gold: One should make adequate provisions for whatever one contemplates doing.

yoruba: Ìyàwó ò fọhùn, ó fọ́jú.
english_literal: The bride does not speak, and she is also blind.
interpretation_gold: The person newly arrived in a place or a company should shut his/her mouth and open his/her eyes, so that he/she knows the customs before speaking.

yoruba: Ìṣẹ́ kì í pani; ayọ̀ ní ńpani.
english_literal: Misfortune does not kill; it is indulgent happiness that kills.
interpretation_gold: Indulgence kills more surely than want.

yoruba: Ìkánjú òun pẹ̀lẹ́, ọgbọọgba.
english_literal: Haste and patience end up the same.
interpretation_gold: Great haste offers no advantage over patience.

yoruba: Ìbínú lọbá fi ńyọ idà; ìtìjù ló fi ḿbẹ́ ẹ.
english_literal: It is in anger that the king draws his sword; it is shame that makes him go through with the beheading.
interpretation_gold: Once one begins an injudicious action on impulse, one might have to carry it through to avoid embarrassment.

yoruba: Ìyá là bá bú; bí a bú baba ìjà ní ńdà.
english_literal: One would be wiser to insult “another person's” mother; if one insults the father a fight would certainly ensue.
interpretation_gold: One should measure one's insults in order to avoid a fight; a father is valued well over a mother.

yoruba: Ìyàwó la bá sùn; ọkọ ló lóyún.
english_literal: The wife was the one made love to, but it is the husband who got pregnant.
interpretation_gold: The person directly involved in a matter does not make as much fuss as the person only tangentially involved.

yoruba: Ìpàkọ́ ò gbọ́ ṣùtì, ìpẹ̀hìndà ò mọ yẹ̀gẹ̀ yíyẹ̀.
english_literal: The occiput does not recognize contempt; a turned back does not see a disdainful gesture.
interpretation_gold: The best response to insults is to disregard them.

yoruba: Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ òṣì bí ọmọ ọlọ́rọ̀ là ńrí.
english_literal: At the beginning of one's penury one seems like the child of most prosperous parents.
interpretation_gold: A course of action that will lead to disaster often has a pleasant beginning.

yoruba: Ìlara àlàjù ní ḿmúni gbàjẹ́, ní ḿmúni ṣẹ́ṣó.
english_literal: Excessive envy of others causes one to take on witching, and makes one become a wizard.
interpretation_gold: Too much envy leads to antisocial behavior.

yoruba: Ìfunra loògùn àgbà.
english_literal: Wariness is the elders' most efficacious juju.
interpretation_gold: The person who is always wary will avoid much grief.

yoruba: Ibi tí akátá ba sí, adìẹ ò gbọdọ̀ débẹ̀.
english_literal: Wherever the jackal lurks, the chicken must give the place a wide berth.
interpretation_gold: One should keep as clear of known dangers as possible.

yoruba: Ìhàlẹ̀-ẹ́ ba ọ̀ṣọ́ èèyàn jẹ́.
english_literal: Empty boasts ruin a person's reputation.
interpretation_gold: One's mouth should not be more powerful than one's arms.

yoruba: Ibi tí inú ḿbí asẹ́ tó, inú ò gbọdọ̀ bí ìkòkò débẹ̀; bínú bá bí ìkòkò débẹ̀, ẹlẹ́kọ ò ní-í rí dá.
english_literal: The cooking pot must never harbor a grudge to the same extent that the sieve does; if the pot does so, the corn-meal trader will have nothing to sell.
interpretation_gold: The more power one has, the more one should exercise restraint.

yoruba: Ìbínú baba òṣì.
english_literal: Anger “is the” father of hopelessness.
interpretation_gold: Anger achieves no good, but may backfire on whoever expresses it.

yoruba: Itọ́ tí a tu sílẹ̀ kì í tún padà re ẹnu ẹni mọ́.
english_literal: The saliva one has spat out of one's mouth does not return to one's mouth.
interpretation_gold: Once one has said something one cannot take it back.

yoruba: Ibi ìṣáná la ti ńkíyè sóògùn.
english_literal: It is from the time one makes one's boasts that one should begin to mind one's charms (or juju).
interpretation_gold: One should always match one's vows with adequate preparation to effectuate them.

yoruba: Iná ò ṣé-é bò máṣọ.
english_literal: Fire is not something one conceals under one's clothing.
interpretation_gold: One should not hide one's pressing problems but seek help.

yoruba: Ìwà òní, ẹjọ́ ọ̀la.
english_literal: Today's behavior “causes” tomorrow's problem.
interpretation_gold: The foolish behavior of the present sows the seeds of difficulties for the future.

yoruba: Igbá dojúdé ò jọ ti òṣónú, tinú igbá nigbá ńṣe.
english_literal: That a calabash faces downwards is no antisocial sign; the calabash is only acting according to its nature.
interpretation_gold: One should not take read evil intent into others' innocent actions.

yoruba: Ìtọ́jú ló yẹ abẹ́rẹ́.
english_literal: Safe keeping is what is appropriate for a needle.
interpretation_gold: One should pay special attention to matters that are very delicate.

yoruba: Ìfi ohun wé ohun, ìfi ọ̀ràn wé ọ̀ràn, kò jẹ́ kí ọ̀ràn ó tán.
english_literal: Citing comparable things and recalling similar occurrences “in the past” makes ending a quarrel impossible.
interpretation_gold: Refusal to forget the past makes reconciliation impossible.

yoruba: Iyán àmọ́dún bá ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: Next year's pounded yam will still find some stew.
interpretation_gold: Whenever one's good fortune comes, then will be time enough to enjoy it.

yoruba: Ìyàn-án mú, ìrẹ́ yó; ìyàn-án rọ̀, ìrẹ́ rù.
english_literal: A famine rages and the grasshopper grows fat; the famine subsides and the grasshopper grows lean.
interpretation_gold: One should husband one's resources wisely, and save for lean times in times of plenty.

yoruba: Ìgbà ara ḿbẹ lára là ḿbù ú tà.
english_literal: It is when there is a surfeit of flesh on the body that one cuts some of it for sale.
interpretation_gold: One makes a gift only of one's surplus.

yoruba: Ìbínú ò da nǹkan; sùúrù baba ìwà; àgbà tó ní sùúrù ohun gbogbo ló ní.
english_literal: Anger accomplishes nothing; forebearance is the father of character traits; an elder who has forebearance has everything.
interpretation_gold: Forebearance will avail one everything, whereas anger will always prove futile.

yoruba: Ìgbà tí a bá perí àparò ní ńjáko.
english_literal: Just as the talk turns to the partridge it shows up to raid the farm
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who plays into his/her adversary's hand when the adversary most wants to injure him/her.

yoruba: Ìkekere ńfọ̀rọ̀ ikú ṣẹ̀rín.
english_literal: Ikekere (type of fish) is treating a deadly thing as something to laugh about.
interpretation_gold: One should not take serious or deadly matters lightly.

yoruba: Ìpàkọ́ là ńdà sẹ́hìn ká tó da yangan sẹ́nu.
english_literal: One throws back the head first before throwing corn into the mouth.
interpretation_gold: One should not put one's cart before one's horse.

yoruba: Inúure àníjù, ìfura atèébú ní ḿmù wá báni.
english_literal: Too much good will towards others engenders suspicion and attracts insults.
interpretation_gold: One can be too good towards others.

yoruba: Ìgbẹ̀hìn ní ńyé olókùúàdá.
english_literal: It is only at the end that the person with a blunt cutlass realizes his error.
interpretation_gold: Sometimes wisdom comes too late to salvage lost opportunities.

yoruba: Igi ganganran má gùnún mi lójú, òkèèrè la ti ńwò ó wá.
english_literal: “Protruding twig, do not poke me in the eye”; one must keep one's eyes on the twig from a distance.
interpretation_gold: One does not wait until problems arise before one begins preparing to deal with them.

yoruba: Ìbínú ò mọ̀ pé olúwa òun ò lẹ́sẹ̀ ńlẹ̀
english_literal: Anger does not know that its owner has no legs to stand on.
interpretation_gold: Anger does not know prudence.

yoruba: Ibi rere làkàsọ̀ńgbé sọlẹ̀.
english_literal: The ladder always rests on a propitious spot.
interpretation_gold: A prayer that one may always land at a fortunate place.

yoruba: Igbá tó fọ́ ní ńgba kasẹ létí; ìkòkò tó fọ́ ní ńgba okùn lọ́rùn.
english_literal: It is the broken calabash that has iron staples driven into its edges; it is the cracked pot that has its neck tied with a rope.
interpretation_gold: It is the person who makes trouble that is visited with repercussions.

yoruba: Isà tí ò lójú Alalantorí ńdẹ ẹ́, áḿbọńtorí àgbá ikún.
english_literal: Alalantori watches a hole without a visible opening, how much more a squirrel's burrow.
interpretation_gold: A person who watches his/her pennies is not likely to be careless with his/her dollars.

yoruba: Iṣẹ́ tí a kò ránni, òun ìyà ló jọ ńrìn.
english_literal: A task one was not asked to do usually travels in the company of punishment.
interpretation_gold: One usually rues doing things one has no business doing.

yoruba: Ìbọn-ọ́n ní apátí kò lápátí, taní jẹ́ jẹ́ ka kọjú ìbọn kọ òun?
english_literal: Whether a gun has a trigger or not, who would calmly permit the gun to be pointed at him/her?
interpretation_gold: One should not take foolish chances.

yoruba: Ìtọsẹ̀ ló nìlú.
english_literal: Close investigation keeps the affairs of the town in order.
interpretation_gold: Investigating matters well before acting helps maintain harmony in a group.

yoruba: Ìbìsẹ́hín àgbò kì í ṣojo.
english_literal: A ram's stepping backwards is not indicative of cowardice.
interpretation_gold: One should not mistake a person's deliberateness before acting as indecisiveness.

yoruba: Isán ni à ḿmọ olè; ìtàdógún là ḿmọ dọ́kọ-dọ́kọ.
english_literal: The thief is exposed on the ninth day; the woman who sleeps around is exposed on the seventeenth day.
interpretation_gold: Bad habits can be kept secret only so long; they eventually become exposed.

yoruba: Ibi tí ó mọ là ńpè lọ́mọ.
english_literal: Where it stops, there one designates “child.”
interpretation_gold: When one reaches the end of a matter, or the end of a road, one should acknowledge the end.

yoruba: Ìfẹ́ àfẹ́jù lewúrẹ́ fi ḿbá ọko-ọ ẹ̀ hu irùngbọ̀n.
english_literal: It is excessive love that induces the goat to grow a beard in sympathy with her mate.
interpretation_gold: In all things, moderation is advisable.

yoruba: Ìjẹǹjẹ àná dùn méhoro; ehoro-ó rebi ìjẹ àná kò dẹ̀hìn bọ̀.
english_literal: Yesterday's food find so delighted the hare; the hare went to the spot of yesterday's feeding and never returned.
interpretation_gold: Persistence in risky ventures leads to disaster.

yoruba: Ibi tí a ti ńwo olókùnrùn la ti ńwo ara ẹni.
english_literal: Just as one cares for the sick, one should also care for oneself.
interpretation_gold: One should be as solicitous of one's own welfare as one is of others'.

yoruba: Ìkókó ọmọ tó tọwọ́ bọ eérú ni yó mọ bó gbóná.
english_literal: The newborn child who thrusts his/her hand into ashes will find out for himself/herself if it is hot.
interpretation_gold: Experience is the best teacher that one should avoid dangerous ventures.

yoruba: Inú ẹni lorúkọ tí a ó sọ ọmọ ẹni ńgbé.
english_literal: It is inside oneself that the name one will name one's child resides.
interpretation_gold: One should not broadcast one's secrets to the whole world.

yoruba: Ikún ńjọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ikún ńrèdí; ikún ò mọ̀ pé ohun tó dùn ní ńpani.
english_literal: The squirrel is eating a banana and the squirrel is wagging its tail; the squirrel does not know that it is what is sweet that kills.
interpretation_gold: Overindulgence in good things can result in serious problems.

yoruba: Ibi tí à ńlọ là ńwò, a kì í wo ibi tí a ti ṣubú.
english_literal: One should keep one's eyes on where one is going, not where one stumbled.
interpretation_gold: The best course of action is not to dwell on setbacks, but to resolutely face the future.

yoruba: Ìjímèrè tó lóun ò ní-í sá fájá, ojú ajá ni òì tí-ì to.
english_literal: The brown monkey vows it will not run from a dog, only because the dog has not caught a glimpse of it.
interpretation_gold: The coward may boast as much as he/she wishes, until the real test materializes.

yoruba: Iná kì í wọ odò kó rójú ṣayé.
english_literal: Fire does not enter into a stream and yet have the opportunity to live.
interpretation_gold: Whoever ventures into dangerous situations deserves the repercussions.

yoruba: Jẹ ẹ́ kí o yó oògùn ni kò sunwọ̀n.
english_literal: Eat-your-fill-of-it medicine is no good.
interpretation_gold: Anything without measure is dangerous.

yoruba: Jẹ́ kí ọmọ ó ti ọwọ́ ìyá-a ẹ̀ kú wá.
english_literal: Let a child die at his/her own mother's hands.
interpretation_gold: One should not become involved in the affairs of a person intent on his/her own ruin.

yoruba: Já ewé ọ̀pọ̀tọ́ kí o ríjà eèrùn; jáwé bọ ẹnu kóo ríjà odi.
english_literal: Pluck a fig leaf and be attacked by soldier-ants; put a leaf in your mouth and be attacked by the deaf.
interpretation_gold: Whoever takes unnecessary risks will very likely face dangerous consequences.

yoruba: Jayé-jayé fi ẹ̀lẹ̀ jayé; báyé bá já kò ní àmúso.
english_literal: You reveler, do things in moderation; if the string of life is cut there is no retying it.
interpretation_gold: One should observe moderation in all things.

yoruba: Kí á tó mọ̀ pé kíjìpá kì í ṣe awọ, ó di ọdún mẹ́ta.
english_literal: Before one realizes that tough hand-woven cloth is not leather, three years will have passed.
interpretation_gold: It might take time, but one will eventually realize that one is not invulnerable to misfortune.

yoruba: Kí á jìnnà séjò tí a ò bẹ́ lórí; ikú tí yó panni a jìnnà síni.
english_literal: One should stand far back from a snake that has not been beheaded; the death that would kill one deserves a wide berth.
interpretation_gold: One should recognize dangerous situations and keep away from them.

yoruba: Kò sí ajá tí kì í gbó; àgbójù ajá là ńpè ní dìgbòlugi.
english_literal: There is no dog that does not bark; excessive barking by a dog is what makes people say it is rabid.
interpretation_gold: No person is without a flaw; unbounded flaws is what gives people a bad reputation.

yoruba: Kọ́kọ́rọ́ àṣejù, ilẹ̀kùn ẹ̀tẹ́ la fi ńṣí.
english_literal: The key of excess is usually good only to open the door of disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Excess brings disgrace.

yoruba: Kì í bọ́ lọ́wọ́ èèyàn kó bọ́ sílẹ̀; ọwọ́ ẹlòmíràn ní ḿbọ́ sí.
english_literal: It never slips out of a person's hand and fall to the ground; it always drops into someone else's hand.
interpretation_gold: Other people always stand ready to appropriate whatever one carelessly lets slip through one's fingers.

yoruba: Kì í tètè yé oníbúrẹ́dì; ó dìgbà tó bá di mẹ́ta kọ́bọ̀.
english_literal: The bread seller never learns in time, not until his ware has become three a penny.
interpretation_gold: People hardly learn to mend their ways until they have suffered some reverses.

yoruba: Kò sí ohun tó lọ sókè tí kò ní padà wá sílẹ̀.
english_literal: There is nothing that goes up that will not eventually come down.
interpretation_gold: One should not be too impatient in anticipating the inevitable.

yoruba: Kìtì ò mọ́là; ká siṣẹ́ bí ẹrú ò da nǹkan.
english_literal: Sudden pouncing does not capture greatness; working like a slave does not ensure anything.
interpretation_gold: One does not guarantee greatness for oneself by slaving.

yoruba: Kí á lé akátá jìnnà ká tó bá adìẹ wí.
english_literal: One should first chase the jackal away before reprimanding the chicken.
interpretation_gold: One should get rid of the immediate danger before reprimanding those who caused it.

yoruba: Kàkà kí ọmọ ó bẹ̀bẹ̀ ọ̀ràn, òmíràn ni kò ní-í ṣe mọ́.
english_literal: Instead of apologizing for past misbehavior, a child should rather guard against a repetition.
interpretation_gold: One should look to the future and not dwell on past mistakes.

yoruba: Kùkùté kan kì í fọ́ni lépo lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: No one stump can break one's oil-pot twice.
interpretation_gold: The same disaster should not befall a person twice; one usually learns from experience.

yoruba: Kékerè nìmàle-é ti ńkọ ọmọ-ọ ẹ̀ lóṣòó.
english_literal: The muslim teaches his children how to squat from their youth.
interpretation_gold: One should do things in a timely manner.

yoruba: Kí a baà lè mọ̀ pé Wòrú pa awó, wọ́n ní “Káàbọ̀”; ó ní “Kẹnkẹn làpò.”
english_literal: Just so that people might know that Woru killed a partridge, he was greeted “Welcome,” and he responded, “My hunting-bag is full!”
interpretation_gold: Said of people gratuitously proclaiming their accomplishments when no one is interested.

yoruba: Kò sí ohun tí sùúrù-ú sè tí kò jinná.
english_literal: There is nothing that patience cooks that is not well cooked.
interpretation_gold: Forbearance overcomes all things.

yoruba: Kí oníkálùkù rọra ṣe é; ìfẹjú òbò ò lè fa aṣọ ya.
english_literal: Let everybody take matters easy; the vagina cannot tear a cloth by gaping at it.
interpretation_gold: Over-excitement accomplished little; it is far better to take life easy.

yoruba: Kí á ta sílẹ̀ ká ta sẹ́nu, ká má jẹ̀ẹ́ kí tilẹ̀ pọ̀ ju ti inú igbá lọ.
english_literal: Let us place some on the ground and put some in the mouth, but let what is placed on the ground be more than what is left in the calabash.
interpretation_gold: One should do one's duty by others, but not at the expense of one's provision for the future.

yoruba: Kí á siṣẹ́ ká lówó lọ́wọ́ ò dàbí-i ká mọ̀-ọ ná.
english_literal: To work and make a great deal of money is nothing like knowing how to spend it.
interpretation_gold: Riches are nothing if one does not know how to use the wealth.

yoruba: Kòkòrò tó jẹ̀fọ́ jàre ẹ̀fọ́; ìwọ̀n lewéko ńdára mọ.
english_literal: The insect that eats the vegetable wins the case against the vegetable; leaves should observe moderation in their attractiveness.
interpretation_gold: A person enticed to a crime is not as guilty as the person who did the enticing.

yoruba: Kì í tètè yéni: òwe ńlá ni.
english_literal: One never learns in good time: that is a profound proverb.
interpretation_gold: People tend always to learn wisdom too late.

yoruba: Kò sí ohun tí ńle tí kì í rọ̀.
english_literal: There is nothing that gets hard that does not eventually become soft.
interpretation_gold: Every problem eventually becomes solved somehow.

yoruba: Kò sí ohun tó yára pa ẹni bí ọ̀rọ̀ àsọjù.
english_literal: There is nothing that kills faster than talking too much.
interpretation_gold: One should govern one's mouth.
