yoruba: Kí a máa re tábà ká máa wòkè, kọ́jọ́ tó kanrí ká wo oye ìka tí yó kù.
english_literal: Let us keep on cutting tobacco leaves to pieces while looking up, and let us see at day's end how many fingers will be left.
interpretation_gold: One should pay close attention when one is engaged in dangerous work.

yoruba: Kí ni ológìní ńwá tó fi jóna mọ́le? Ṣòkòtò ló fẹ́ẹ́ mú ni, tàbí ẹrù ní ńdì?
english_literal: What was the cat doing that caused it to be burnt in a house fire? Was it looking for its trousers or gathering its property?
interpretation_gold: One should not put oneself in the path of avoidable dangers.

yoruba: Kọkọ-kọkọ ò jẹ́ ká mọ ẹni tí ọ̀ràn ńdùn.
english_literal: The woman who divorces husbands at the least provocation does not allow one to know when a matter really hurts.
interpretation_gold: Habitual overreaction defuses real alarms.

yoruba: Kèrègbè tí kò lọ́rùn ni yóò júwe bí àgbẹ̀ ó ti so òun kọ́.
english_literal: The neckless gourd will itself indicate to the farmer how to tie it up.
interpretation_gold: A difficult person prompts others as to the best way to handle him/her.

yoruba: Kò sí ìgbà tí a dá aṣọ tí a ó rílẹ̀ fi wọ́.
english_literal: There is no time one makes a dress that one lacks opportunities to wear it casually.
interpretation_gold: There will always be time for one to enjoy what one has worked for; one should not be unduly impatient.

yoruba: Kí ni ó yá apárí lórí tó ńmòòkùn lódò?
english_literal: What got into the bald person that made him/her swim under water?
interpretation_gold: One should not unnecessarily endanger oneself.

yoruba: Kì í ṣe ojú-u kọ̀lọ̀kọ̀lọ̀ ladìẹ́ ti ńjẹ̀.
english_literal: It is not in the presence of the fox that the chicken forages nonchalantly.
interpretation_gold: One would be foolish to let down one's guard when one knows that danger is nearby.

yoruba: Kàkà kí ó sàn lára ìyá àjẹ́, ó fi gbogbo ọmọ bí obìnrin; ẹye ńgorí ẹyẹ.
english_literal: Instead of mother-witch's affairs improving, all the children she bears turn out to be female; birds climb upon birds.
interpretation_gold: Despite all efforts the fortunes of a person continue to be bad.

yoruba: Kì í tán nígbá osùn kó má ba àlà jẹ́.
english_literal: The calabash of camwood is never so empty that it can not soil white cloth.
interpretation_gold: Some people or conditions are so unredeemable that no matter what one does they persist in being evil.

yoruba: Kùn yún, kùn wá bí ikọ̀ eèrà.
english_literal: Hurry forth and hurry back like a messenger ant.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who are too restless to stay still.

yoruba: Kí á fọn fèrè, ká jámú sí-i, ọ̀kan yóò gbélẹ̀.
english_literal: Between blowing a flute and wriggling one's nose, one will have to go.
interpretation_gold: One cannot hope to perform two conflicting activities at the same time.

yoruba: Kékeré ejò, má foore ṣe é.
english_literal: However small the snake, show it no mercy.
interpretation_gold: Better be safe than sorry.

yoruba: Kèrègbè tó fọ́ a padà lẹ́hìn odò.
english_literal: The broken gourd ceases plying the river.
interpretation_gold: One should know when to stop pursuing an adversary.

yoruba: Làákàyè baba ìwà; bí o ní sùúrù, ohun gbogbo lo ní.
english_literal: Common sense “is” the father of good character; whoever has patience has everything.
interpretation_gold: Common sense and patience are the chief qualities one must have.

yoruba: Lù mí pẹ́, lù mí pẹ́ làpọ́n fi ńlu ọmọ-ọ ẹ̀ pa.
english_literal: It is by gentle but persistent beating that the bachelor beats his child to death.
interpretation_gold: People not used to caring for delicate articles soon destroy them by their mishandling.

yoruba: Labalábá kì í bá wọn nájà ẹlẹ́gùnún; aṣọ-ọ ẹ̀ á fàya.
english_literal: The butterfly does not join others at a market of thorns; otherwise its cloth
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limitations and act accordingly.

yoruba: Làálàá tó ròkè, ilẹ̀ ní ḿbọ̀.
english_literal: A worrisome problem that soars to the heavens must eventually come down.
interpretation_gold: No difficulty is without its end.

yoruba: Labalábá tó dìgbò lẹ̀gún, aṣọ ẹ̀ á fàya.
english_literal: The butterfly that collides with a thorn with have its cloth shredded.
interpretation_gold: One should be wise enough to know one's nemesis and to avoid it.

yoruba: Má fi iyán ewùrà gbọ́n mi lọ́bẹ̀ lọ sóko ẹgàn.
english_literal: Do not eat up my stew with pounded yam made from wateryams before your trip into the forest farm.
interpretation_gold: Do not use up my meager resources on your way to a place of plenty.

yoruba: Màá jẹ iṣu, màá jẹ èrú, ibi ayo ló mọ.
english_literal: I will eat a whole yam, I will also eat a slice of yam, satiation ends it all.
interpretation_gold: The greediest appetite will not survive satiation.

yoruba: “Méè-wáyé-ẹjọ́” fọmọ ẹ̀ fọ́kọ mẹ́fà. Méèwáyéẹjọ́
english_literal: “I did not come to live a life of litigation” gave his daughter to six suitors all at once.
interpretation_gold: If one wishes to avoid trouble one should avoid actions certain to result in trouble.

yoruba: “Má fi tìrẹ kọ́ mi lọ́rùn” là ńdá fún apèna àti òwú.
english_literal: “Do not hang your trouble around my neck” is the oracle delivered to the shuttle and the weft thread.
interpretation_gold: Do not involve me in your problems as the weft thread got the shuttle entangled in its problem.

yoruba: Má bà á loògùn ẹ̀tẹ̀.
english_literal: Avoiding contact is the only medicine for leprosy.
interpretation_gold: The best way out of trouble is not to get into it in the first place.

yoruba: Má bàá mi ṣeré tí kèrègbè-é fi gba okùn lọ́rùn.
english_literal: Do not ask me to play the sort of game the gourd played and got a rope around its neck.
interpretation_gold: Do not ask me to endanger myself needlessly.

yoruba: “Má fi okoò mi dá ọ̀nà,” ọjọ́ kan là ńkọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: “Do not cut a path through my farm” is a protest one must make some day.
interpretation_gold: Whoever does not take a stand to protest the violation of his/her rights will continue to have them violated.

yoruba: Nítorí ọjọ́ tí ó bá máa dáràn la ṣe ńsọmọ lórúkọ.
english_literal: It is in anticipation of the day a child will get into trouble that one gives it a name.
interpretation_gold: Each individual has a name and is therefore an independent agent responsible for his/her actions.

yoruba: Nítorí ọ̀la la ṣe ńṣòní lóore.
english_literal: Its is with tomorrow in mind that we do favors for today.
interpretation_gold: What one sows determines what one reaps.

yoruba: Nítorí ara ilé la ṣe ńdá ṣòkòtò ará oko dára.
english_literal: It is with the town dweller in mind that one makes the bush person's trousers well.
interpretation_gold: One's products are one's advertisement, regardless of whether the recipient knows its quality.

yoruba: Nǹkan mẹ́ta la kì í pè ní kékeré: a kì í pe iná ní kékeré; a kì í pe ìjà ní kékeré; a kì í pe àìsàn ní kékeré.
english_literal: Three things one must never treat as of little consequence: one must never treat fire as of little consequence; one must never treat a quarrel as of little consequence; and one must never treat an illness as of little consequence.
interpretation_gold: One must attend to every potential problem early before it gets out of hand.

yoruba: “Ng óò wọ́ ọ kágbó,” ẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀ ni yó fi lànà.
english_literal: “I will drag you through the bush” will have to clear a path with his own back.
interpretation_gold: Whoever is determined to make trouble for others must be prepared to take some trouble himself.

yoruba: Nítorí-i ká lè simi la ṣe ńṣe àì-simi.
english_literal: It is so that one would be able to rest that one forgoes rest.
interpretation_gold: One labors in the present to provide for one's future.

yoruba: Nítorí ọlọgbọ́n la ṣe ńdá ẹ̀wù-u aṣiwèrè kanlẹ̀.
english_literal: It is with the wise person in mind that one makes the idiot's garment full length.
interpretation_gold: If one cares about one's reputation, one will perform one's obligations well even when the recipient has no power over one.

yoruba: Olóògbé ò jẹ́wọ́; atannijẹ bí orun.
english_literal: The dozing person does not confess; nothing deceives like sleep.
interpretation_gold: One can always feign sleep to avoid engaging in discussions.

yoruba: O rí àgbébọ̀ adìẹ lọ́jà ò ńta geere sí i; ìba ṣe rere olúwa rẹ̀ ò jẹ́ tà á.
english_literal: You see an adult chicken at the market and you eagerly go for it; if it was of any value would the owner sell it?
interpretation_gold: People should think carefully before they assume obligations.

yoruba: Ó ní ohun tí àgbà-á jẹ tẹ́lẹ̀ ikùn kó tó sọ pé ìyà-á yó òun.
english_literal: There was something the elder ate to line his stomach before he said his/her suffering is enough food for him/her.
interpretation_gold: Even when one is prostrated by grief, one does not ignore one's need to survive.

yoruba: Ohun tí a rí la fi ḿbọ párá ẹni; bí igi tíná ḿbẹ lẹ́nu-u ẹ̀ kọ́.
english_literal: It is whatever one can find that one uses to fill gaps in one's roof; that does not apply to a faggot spewing flames.
interpretation_gold: Every seemingly sensible generalization has exceptions.

yoruba: Onílé ńrelé wọ́n ní oǹdè ńsá; oǹdè ò sá, ilé ẹ̀ ló lọ.
english_literal: The home owner heads for home and they say the guard is on the run; the guard is not on the run, he is merely heading home.
interpretation_gold: A strategic retreat to regroup is not the same as giving up the fight.

yoruba: Òfèèrèfé ò ṣé-é fẹ̀hín tì.
english_literal: A chasm is nothing to lean on.
interpretation_gold: One can should not trust in emptiness.

yoruba: Olójútì logun ńpa.
english_literal: It is those who worry about their image who die in war.
interpretation_gold: Discretion and a thick skin are sometimes much better than valor.

yoruba: Ohun gbogbo kì í tó olè.
english_literal: Nothing ever satisfies a thief.
interpretation_gold: Greed and covetousness are the marks of a thief.

yoruba: Òkò tí ẹyẹ́ bá rí kì í pẹyẹ.
english_literal: A missile that a bird sees will not kill the bird.
interpretation_gold: If one sees danger approaching, one will take precautions.

yoruba: Òjò kan kì í báni lábà ká jìjàdù ọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ sọ; bí ẹgbọ́n bá sọ tán, àbúrò á sọ.
english_literal: When people are trapped in a hut by a downpour there is no sense in fighting to get a word in the discussion; after the older person has spoken, the younger person will speak.
interpretation_gold: When there is a surfeit of a commodity, there is no sense in scrambling to get some of it.

yoruba: Oore ọ̀fẹ́ gùn jùwàásù.
english_literal: The benediction is longer than the sermon.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who are long winded.

yoruba: Òṣé ní ńṣíwájú ẹkún; àbámọ̀ ní ńgbẹ̀hìn ọ̀ràn; gbogbo àgbà ìlú pé, wọn ò rí oògùn àbàmọ̀ ṣe.
english_literal: Hissing goes before crying; had-one-but-known comes at the conclusion of an unfortunate matter; all the elders in the town assembled but they could find no antidote for had-we-but-known.
interpretation_gold: One can only regret an error once it has been committed; there is no undoing it.

yoruba: Ohun gbogbo kì í pẹ́ jọ olóhun lójú.
english_literal: It is never long before a thing becomes invaluable to the owner.
interpretation_gold: A person always attaches excessive value to his or her possessions.(Trust a person to exaggerate the value of his or her possessions, especially when they are damaged or coveted by others.

yoruba: Odídẹrẹ ní wọn ò lè tí ojú òun yan òun mọ́ ẹbọ; bí wọ́n bá ńdÍfá, òun a sá wọlé.
english_literal: The parrot says no one will prescribe it as a sacrifice in its presence; when it sees people consulting the oracle, it will go hide in its closet.
interpretation_gold: The smart person should always distance himself from disaster.

yoruba: Ojúlé ló bá wá; ẹ̀bùrú ló gbà lọ́; ó dÍfá fún àlejò tí ńfẹ obìnrin onílé.
english_literal: He entered through the front door, but it was through a hidden shortcut that he snuck away; it consulted the Ifa oracle for the visitor who has an affair with his host's wife.
interpretation_gold: Whoever abuses his hospitality will depart with disgrace.

yoruba: Ojú kan náà lèwe ńbágbà.
english_literal: It is at the same place that the youth will come up on the elder.
interpretation_gold: Sooner or later the youth becomes an elder; patience is all.

yoruba: Orí ejò ò ṣé-é họ imú.
english_literal: The head of a snake is nothing to scratch one's nose with.
interpretation_gold: Never expose yourself to unnecessary danger.

yoruba: Ojú tí yóò bani kalẹ̀ kì í tàárọ̀ ṣepin.
english_literal: The eyes that will last one until night time will not start oozing matter at the dawn.
interpretation_gold: Relationships that will last will not start becoming onerous right at the start.

yoruba: Ohun gbogbo là ńdiyelé; ṣùgbọ́n kò sẹ́ni tó moye ara-a ẹ̀; ẹ̀jẹ̀ ò fojú rere jáde.
english_literal: Everything has its price, but no one knows his/her own worth; bloodshed never has a good cause.
interpretation_gold: People should not devalue their own lives by exposing themselves to unnecessary danger.

yoruba: Òní, adìẹẹ̀ mí ṣìwọ̀; ọ̀la, adìẹẹ̀ mí ṣìwọ̀; ọjọ́ kan la óò fẹ́ àìwọlé adìẹ kù.
english_literal: Today, my chicken has gone to roost in the wrong place; tomorrow, my chicken has gone to roost in the wrong place; some day soon the errant chicken will disappear permanently.
interpretation_gold: Little errors, if not checked, will result in a major blunder.

yoruba: Òkóbó ò lè fi alátọ̀sí ṣẹ̀sín.
english_literal: The eunuch cannot make fun of the person with gonorrhea.
interpretation_gold: A person with a blemish of his/her own should not make fun of other people's blemishes.

yoruba: Òkèlè gbò-ǹ-gbò-ó fẹ ọmọ lójú toto.
english_literal: A huge morsel forces the child's eyes wide open.
interpretation_gold: A person who bites off more than he can chew will suffer in the process of trying.

yoruba: O bá ẹfọ̀n lábàtà o yọ̀bẹ sí i; o mọ ibi ẹfọ̀n-ọ́n ti wa?
english_literal: You come upon the carcass of a buffalo in the marshes and you pull out your butchering knife; do you know where the bushcow came from?
interpretation_gold: People should not lay claim to things whose procurement they know nothing about.

yoruba: Oyún inú: a kì í kà á kún ọmọ-ọ tilẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not count a pregnancy as a child already delivered.
interpretation_gold: One should not treat anything hoped for as though it was already in hand.

yoruba: Ojú abẹ ò ṣé-é pọ́nlá.
english_literal: The edge of a razor is not a thing to lick.
interpretation_gold: Never engage in dangerous behavior.

yoruba: Olórìṣà-á gbé ààjà sókè, wọ́n ní ire ni; bí ire ni, bí ibi ni, wọn ò mọ̀.
english_literal: The cult priest raises his divining wand and the worshippers proclaim the omen is good; whether it is good or bad they do not know.
interpretation_gold: It is foolhardy to presume to know what is in other people's minds.

yoruba: Ohun tí à bá ṣe pẹ̀sẹ̀, ká má fi ṣe ìkánjú; bó pẹ́ títí ohun gbogbo a tó ọwọ́ ẹni.
english_literal: That which one should do slowly and carefully one should not do in a hurry; sooner or later everything comes within one's reach.
interpretation_gold: One should not shirk one's present responsibilities in the pursuit of a distant goal.

yoruba: Ònímónìí, ẹtu-ú jìnfìń ọ̀lamọ́la, ẹtu-ú jìnfìn; ẹran miìíràn ò sí nígbó ni?
english_literal: Today, the antelope falls into a ditch; tomorrow, the antelope falls into the ditch; is there no other animal in the forest?
interpretation_gold: If the same person gets into trouble every time, the person need to look to himself/herself.

yoruba: Ojú ológbò lèkúté ò gbọdọ̀ yan.
english_literal: It is in the presence of the cat that the mouse must not saunter.
interpretation_gold: One may cannot afford to be careless in the presence of powerful enemies.

yoruba: Ohun tí a fi ẹ̀sọ̀ mú kì í bàjẹ́; ohun tí a fagbára mú ní ńnini lára.
english_literal: Whatever one handles gently will not be ruined; it is what one attempts with force that causes one grief.
interpretation_gold: A gentle approach will accomplish much, while a forceful approach is likely to complicate matters.

yoruba: Ohun tí a ò pé yó dẹrù ní ńdiṣẹ́.
english_literal: It is always something one does not expect to become a load that eventually becomes a huge task.
interpretation_gold: Matters that one considers of little significance have a way of becoming insoluble problems.

yoruba: Obìnrin bẹẹrẹ òṣì bẹẹrẹ.
english_literal: Innumerable wives, innumerable problems.
interpretation_gold: Whoever adds wives to wives adds problems to problems.

yoruba: “Ó ḿbọ̀, ó ḿbọ̀!” ẹ̀wọ̀n là ńso sílẹ̀ dè é.
english_literal: “Watch out, watch out, for here it comes!” For such a thing one would best prepare a snare.
interpretation_gold: If the thought of something fills one with apprehension one should plot to defeat it.

yoruba: Okùn àgbò kì í gbèé dorí ìwo.
english_literal: It is never long before a ram's tethering rope slips to its horns.
interpretation_gold: Seemingly minor difficulties soon become unmanageable problems.

yoruba: Onísùúrù ní ńṣe ọkọ ọmọ Aláhúsá.
english_literal: Only the patient person will win the daughter of the Hausa man.
interpretation_gold: Patience overcomes all obstacles.

yoruba: Owó ò bá olè gbé.
english_literal: Money does not live with a thief.
interpretation_gold: A thief and money are incompatible neighbors; never trust a thief with money.

yoruba: “Ojú ò fẹ́rakù” tó ta ajá-a ẹ̀ lókòó; ó ní bó bá jẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ ni wọ́n ńtà á wọn a máa tún araa wọn rí.
english_literal: “We might see each other again” who sold his dog for twenty cowries; he said if that is how things are sold, they might well see each other again.
interpretation_gold: If someone sells you an item at a ridiculously low price, you might expect to see the person again soon.

yoruba: Òjijì là ńrọ́mọ lọ́wọ́ alákẹdun.
english_literal: It is all of a sudden that one sees a baby in the arms of the colobus monkey.
interpretation_gold: One need not announce ahead of time what feat one will perform.

yoruba: Ó dé ọwọ́ aláròóbọ̀ ó di níná.
english_literal: When goods get into the hands of the retailer they become objects to haggle about.
interpretation_gold: A store minder is a difficult person to obtain a good bargain from.

yoruba: Onígbàjámọ̀ ńfárí fún ọ, ò ńfọwọ́ kàn án wò; èwo ló máa kù fún ọ níbẹ̀.
english_literal: The hair scrapper is scraping your head and you are feeling your scalp with your hand; what do you expect will be left for you there?
interpretation_gold: Once the end is clear, one should stop being anxious about developments.

yoruba: Òkété tó bọ́ ìrù-ú mọ̀ pé ìpéjú ọjà ọrún òun ló sún.
english_literal: The giant bush rat that has its tail stripped by a trap knows that it is its visit to the fifth-day market that was postponed.
interpretation_gold: One should take a near-disaster as a warning.

yoruba: Òòrẹ̀ ní ńṣẹ́gi tí a ó fi wì í.
english_literal: The porcupine itself will procure the wood with which it will be roasted.
interpretation_gold: The incautious person will provide the instrument for his own undoing.

yoruba: Oókan-án sọni dahuń eéjì-í sọni dàpà.
english_literal: One cowrie makes a miser of one; two cowries make a spendthrift of one.
interpretation_gold: When one has little one seems a miser; when one has plenty one becomes careless with money.

yoruba: Ó ní ibi tí tanpẹ́pẹ́ ńgbèjà ẹyìn mọ.
english_literal: There is a limit to the protection black stinging ants can offer palmfruits.
interpretation_gold: There is a limit to the help one can expect from others.

yoruba: Òjò ńrọ̀, orò ńké; atọ́kùn àlùgbè tí ò láṣọ méjì a ṣe ògèdèm̀gbé sùn.
english_literal: The rain is falling, the call of the secret cult is sounding loudly outside; the threading pin that lacks a change of clothing will sleep naked.
interpretation_gold: If one has not made provisions for rainy days, when they come one must suffer the attendant hardship.

yoruba: Òkù àjànàkú là ńyọ ogbó sí; ta ní jẹ́ yọ agada séerin?
english_literal: It is a dead elephant one approaches with a cutlass; who would dare draw a machete to attack an elephant “that is alive”?
interpretation_gold: One dares taunt a powerful adversary when he has been neutralized.

yoruba: Ohun tí a bá tẹjúmọ́ kì í jóná.
english_literal: Whatever one trains one's eyes upon will not get charred.
interpretation_gold: Matters to which one devotes one's undivided attention will not go awry.

yoruba: Oníṣu ní ḿmọ ibi iṣú gbé ta sí.
english_literal: The owner of the yams is the one who knows where the mature yams are.
interpretation_gold: One should not presume to know more about an affair that the person most intimately involved.

yoruba: Ojú ní ńkán ọkọlóbìnrin; àlè méjì á jà dandan.
english_literal: The husband of the wife is only being unduly hasty; in time two concubines will inevitably quarrel.
interpretation_gold: One should not be overly anxious for results that are inevitable anyway.

yoruba: Òkèlè kan ní ńpa àgbà.
english_literal: Only one morsel kills an elder.
interpretation_gold: The smallest thing, if not accorded the proper attention, can be the death of even the most powerful person.

yoruba: Ogun àgbọ́tẹ́lẹ̀ kì í pa arọ.
english_literal: A long foreseen war does not kill a cripple.
interpretation_gold: One must take advantage of foreknowledge to protect oneself.

yoruba: Ojú tí kì í wo iná, tí kì í wo òòrùn; ojú tí ḿbáni dalẹ́ kọ́.
english_literal: Eyes that cannot stand lamplight, and that cannot stand sunlight, are not eyes that will last one until the twilight of one's life.
interpretation_gold: From early indications, one can tell what friendships or possessions will prove lasting.

yoruba: Òrìṣà kékeré ò ṣé-é há ní párá.
english_literal: A small god is not a thing to hang from the rafters.
interpretation_gold: Some things may seem insignificant but yet must not be taken lightly.

yoruba: Ò ḿbá obínrin ẹ jà ò ńkanrí mọ́nú; o máa nà á lóògùn ni?
english_literal: You quarrel with your wife and you put on a baleful look; do you propose to use evil charm on her?
interpretation_gold: One should moderate one's response to annoyances.

yoruba: Ó pẹ́ títí aboyún, oṣù mẹ́sàn-án.
english_literal: The longest respite for the pregnant woman is nine months.
interpretation_gold: Sooner rather than later, the day will arrive when one must fulfil one's obligation or pay one's debt.

yoruba: Oúnjẹ tí a ó jẹ pẹ́, a kì í bu òkèlè-e ẹ̀ tóbi.
english_literal: Food that one expects to last, one does not eat in huge handfuls.
interpretation_gold: Wise husbandry is the medicine for lasting prosperity.

yoruba: Ohun tó bá wu olókùnrùn ní ńpa á.
english_literal: Whatever the invalid craves is what spells his/her death.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one is addicted to is liable to prove one's undoing.

yoruba: Ohun tí a fún ẹlẹ́mọ̀ṣọ́ ní ńṣọ́.
english_literal: It is that which one gives to a caretaker to look after that he looks after.
interpretation_gold: One would best focus on only that task that was assigned to one.

yoruba: Òní, baba-á dákú; ọ̀la, baba-á dákú; ọjọ́ kan ni ikú yóò dá baba.
english_literal: Today, the patriarch collapsed; tomorrow, the patriarch collapsed; one day death will throw the patriarch.
interpretation_gold: Frequent close calls with death will eventually lead to real death.

yoruba: Ohun tí a bá máa jẹ a kì í fi runmú.
english_literal: One does not sniff at what one will eventually eat anyway.
interpretation_gold: One should nor sneer at a thing that one will eventually embrace.

yoruba: Ojú àwòdì kọ́ ladìẹ ńre àpáta.
english_literal: It is not in the watchful presence of a kite that a chicken strolls to a rock.
interpretation_gold: One does not engage in culpable activity in the presence of those charged with upholding discipline.

yoruba: O wà lọ́rùn ọ̀pẹ ò ḿbá Ọlọ́run ṣèlérí.
english_literal: You are perched at the lofty neck of the palm-tree and you are bandying words with God.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who taunts more powerful adversaries even when he/she is in a vulnerable position.

yoruba: Ohun tí ajá rí tó fi ńgbó ò tó èyí tí àgùntàn-án fi ńṣèran wò.
english_literal: That which a dog sees and barks at is nothing compared to what the sheep contemplates in silence.
interpretation_gold: Some people make mountains out of other people's mole-hills.

yoruba: Ojú kan làdá ńní.
english_literal: A machete can have only one edge.
interpretation_gold: One should be true to one calling or relationship, and not philander.

yoruba: Oore-é pọ̀, a fìkà san án.
english_literal: The favor was excessive; it was repaid with wickedness.
interpretation_gold: Too great a favor provokes enmity.

yoruba: Ó ní ohun tí àgbà-á jẹ tẹ́lẹ̀ ikùn kó tó sọ pé èyí yó òun.
english_literal: There was something the elder ate to line his stomach before he said what “little” is before him will suffice to sate his hunger.
interpretation_gold: The prudent person prepares himself or herself for all eventualities.

yoruba: Orin tí a kọ lánàá, tí a ò sùn, tí a ò wo, a kì í tún jí kọ ọ́ láàárọ̀.
english_literal: The song that we sang yesterday, without sleep, without respite; we do not resume singing it in the morning.
interpretation_gold: Yesterday's problems should be gone with yesterday.

yoruba: Òketè baba ogun; bí a ṣígun, olúkúlùkù n í ńdi òketè-e ẹ̀ lọ́wọ́.
english_literal: Large bundle, father of all wars; when preparing for war, each person prepares his bundle to take along.
interpretation_gold: For all tasks, adequate preparations are mandatory.

yoruba: O lọ sÍjẹ̀bú ẹ̀ẹ̀kan, o ru igbá àṣẹ bọ̀ wálé.
english_literal: You made only one trip to Ìjebu and you returned with a calabash of charms.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person on whom the impact of an experience is out of all proportion.

yoruba: Òwúyẹ́; a-ṣòro-ó-sọ bí ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: A hush-hush matter; difficult to utter as speech.
interpretation_gold: The matter under reference is so delicate it almost does not bear speech.

yoruba: Olóòlà kì í kọ àfín.
english_literal: The facial scarifier does not scarify an albino's face.
interpretation_gold: There are some tasks that are beyond the scope of experts.

yoruba: Oore tí igúnnugún ṣe tó fi pá lórí, tí àkàlá ṣe tó fi yọ gẹ̀gẹ̀, a kì í ṣe irú ẹ̀.
english_literal: The sort of favor the vulture did and went bald, the sort of favor the ground hornbill did and developed a goitre, one does not do it.
interpretation_gold: One should not do favors that will result in one's ruin.

yoruba: Omi là ńkọ́-ọ́ tẹ̀ ká tó tẹ iyanrìn.
english_literal: Water is the first thing one's foot encounters before it encounters the sand.
interpretation_gold: One should attend to the most urgent matters first.

yoruba: Òní, ẹṣin-ín dá baba; ọ̀la, ẹṣin-ín dá baba; bí baba ò bá yé ẹṣin-ín gùn, ọjọ́ kan lẹṣin óò dá baba pa.
english_literal: Today, the horse threw the patriach; tomorrow, the horse threw the patriarch; if the patriarch does not stop riding the horse, one day the horse will throw him to his death.
interpretation_gold: One should take warning from little disasters.

yoruba: Oókan ni wọ́n ńta ẹṣin lọ́run; ẹni tí yó lọ ò wọ́n; ṣùgbọ́n ẹni tí yó bọ̀ ló kù.
english_literal: Horses sell for only one cowrie in heaven; there is no shortage of people who will go there, but who ever returns from there?
interpretation_gold: Setting out on dangerous ventures is the easiest thing in the world, but their repercussions prove to be unspeakable.

yoruba: Ó ní ohun tí ìbòsí ràn nínú ìjà.
english_literal: Raising an alarm or calling for help goes only so far to aid someone in a fight.
interpretation_gold: No matter what help a person in trouble receives he/she will still be in for some grief.

yoruba: Orin ní ńṣíwájú ọ̀tẹ̀.
english_literal: Singing goes before plotting.
interpretation_gold: People about to engage in a plot will first spar to sound one another out.

yoruba: Ojú là ńgbó re ọ̀nà Ìbàdàn: ó fi ogún ọ̀kẹ́ gbàdí.
english_literal: “It takes a great deal of fortitude to set out for Ibadan”; he ties his money around his waist.
interpretation_gold: One should take the necessary precautions when one embarks on a dangerous venture.

yoruba: Ó dé orí akáhín àkàràá deegun.
english_literal: In the mouth of a toothless person bean fritters become like bones.
interpretation_gold: To the shiftless person the easiest task is onerous indeed.

yoruba: Òkò àbínújù kì í pẹyẹ.
english_literal: A stone thrown in anger does not kill a bird.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one does in anger is liable to go awry.

yoruba: O kò rí àkàṣù ò ńpata sẹ́fọ̀ọ́.
english_literal: You have not found corn loaf and yet you are readying the vegetable stew.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person too eagerly anticipating a favor that might not materialize.

yoruba: Ohun gbogbo, ìwọn ló dùn mọ.
english_literal: All things are good or pleasing only to a point.
interpretation_gold: One should observe moderation in all things.

yoruba: Ojúkòkòrò baba ọ̀kánjúà.
english_literal: Covetousness “is” the father of envy.
interpretation_gold: The envious and the covetous are similar.

yoruba: O só pa mí mo pọ́nnu lá, o bojúwẹ̀hìn mo dọ̀bálẹ̀, o tiwọ́ bọ̀gbẹ́; o fẹ́ dè mí ni?
english_literal: You foul the air in my face and I lick my lips, you glance back and I prostrate myself before you, and yet you stretch your hand into the bush; would you tie me up?
interpretation_gold: Said by a long-suffering person who has quietly taken a great deal of abuse, when the abuser persists in his/her illtreatment.

yoruba: Ohun tó bá wu ọmọ-ọ́ jẹ kì í run ọmọ nínú.
english_literal: Whatever a child crave will not give him/her stomach ache.
interpretation_gold: One is always willing to endure sacrifices in order to have whatever one craves.

yoruba: Òròmọ-adìẹ ò màwòdì; ìyá ẹ̀ ló màṣá.
english_literal: The young chick does not know the eagle; it is its mother that knows the kite.
interpretation_gold: The young are neither as experienced not as careful as the old.

yoruba: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, ẹní lọ sódò á bọ̀ wálé.
english_literal: It may take a while, but the person who went to the stream will return home.
interpretation_gold: There is no journey that does not end some time.

yoruba: Pẹ̀tẹ̀pẹ́tẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀, a-ta-síni-lára-má-wọ̀n-ọ́n.
english_literal: The soiling caused by speech; it stains a person and cannot be removed.
interpretation_gold: Injury once spoken cannot be recalled.

yoruba: Paramọ́lẹ̀-ẹ́ kọ ọ̀ràn àfojúdi.
english_literal: The serpent refuses to be trifled with.
interpretation_gold: Certain situations are not to be taken lightly, lest they result in painful repercussions.

yoruba: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, agbọ̀n á bo adìẹ.
english_literal: It may take long, but the coop will eventually cover the chicken.
interpretation_gold: One may put it off a while, but one cannot avoid one's fate.

yoruba: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, amòòkùn yó jàáde nínú odò.
english_literal: It may take a while, but the under-water swimmer will eventually surface.
interpretation_gold: If one is patient, what is bound to happen will eventually happen.

yoruba: Pẹ̀lẹ́-pẹ̀lẹ́ lejò-ó fi ńgun àgbọn.
english_literal: It is very carefully and patiently that a snake climbs the coconut palm.
interpretation_gold: Dangerous and difficult tasks should be attempted with care and patience.

yoruba: Pápá tó ní òun ó jòó wọ odò, ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ẹ́ gbọ́.
english_literal: The grassland that proposes to burn into the river is asking for a lecture.
interpretation_gold: Abstain from actions that will provoke others' ire.

yoruba: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, akólòlòá pe baba.
english_literal: It may take long, but the stammerer will eventually manage to say “Papa.”
interpretation_gold: With perseverance the most difficult task will be accomplished.

yoruba: Pala-pálà kì í ṣe ẹran àjẹgbé; ẹ ṣáà máa mu àgúnmu.
english_literal: Stockfish is not a meat one eats without repercussions; keep on drinking herbal remedies.
interpretation_gold: One pays for one's indiscretions by and by.

yoruba: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, èké ò mú rá.
english_literal: It may take a while, but the deceitful person will not be undiscovered.
interpretation_gold: Truth will unfailingly triumph in the end.

yoruba: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, akọ̀pẹ yó wàá sílẹ̀.
english_literal: It may take a while, but the palm-wine tapster will descend from atop the palm-tree.
interpretation_gold: All is takes is patience; what one desires will eventually happen.

yoruba: Sà á bí olóògùn-ún ti wí.
english_literal: Invoke it exactly as the maker of the charm instructed.
interpretation_gold: Always follow instructions, and do not presume to know better than your instructor.

yoruba: Sùúrù-ú lérè.
english_literal: Patience has its profits.
interpretation_gold: Patience is a useful quality to cultivate.

yoruba: Sùúrù loògùn ayé.
english_literal: Patience is the talisman for living.
interpretation_gold: Patience solves all problems.

yoruba: Sùúrù ò lópin.
english_literal: There is no end to the need for patience.
interpretation_gold: One must never tire of exercising patience.

yoruba: Tọ̀sán tọ̀sán ní ńpọ́n ìtalẹ̀ lójú; bílẹ̀-ẹ́ bá ṣú yó di olóńjẹ.
english_literal: It is the persistence of daylight that imposes suffering on the mud-floor worm; when night falls it will find food.
interpretation_gold: Patience will bring what one lacks to one.

yoruba: “Ta á sí i” kì í báni wá ọfà.
english_literal: “Shoot at it” does not help one find arrows.
interpretation_gold: People are ever eager to goad one to action, but never to help one carry out the task.

yoruba: “Tàná là ńjà lé lórí”, ló pa Baálẹ̀ẹ Kòmọ̀kan.
english_literal: “It is yesterday's matter that we are fighting over” is what killed Chief Know-Nothing.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to let the past alone.

yoruba: Tantabùlù, aṣòróówọ̀ bí ẹ̀wù àṣejù.
english_literal: An unbecoming thing, as unpleasant to wear as the garment of disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Disgrace is not a pleasant thing to live with.

yoruba: Wẹ́rẹ́ wẹ́rẹ́ nikán ńjẹlé.
english_literal: Slowly, slowly is the manner in which termites consume a house.
interpretation_gold: Inconspicuos and imperceptible problems in time become huge disasters.

yoruba: Wọ́n torí ajá ńlóṣòó lọ fowó rọ̀bọ.
english_literal: Because the dog sits on its haunches they went and spent their money on purchasing a monkey.
interpretation_gold: One should not pass up something useful for something useless simply because the latter looks better.

yoruba: “Wó ilé ẹ kí mbá ọ kọ”: ẹrù ikán kan ní ńpa fúnni.
english_literal: “Demolish your house and I will help you rebuild it”: he will give one only one bundle of thatching grass.
interpretation_gold: Never trust people who goad you into trouble with promises of help down the road.

yoruba: Wàrà ò sí lónìí, wàrà-á wà lọ́la.
english_literal: No cheese today, but there will be cheese tomorrow.
interpretation_gold: Today's want will be followed by tomorrow's plenty.

yoruba: Wọ́n purọ́ fún ọ, o ò gbà; o lè dé ìdí òótọ́?
english_literal: People lie to you and you do not accept the lie; can you ever know what the truth is?
interpretation_gold: Since one can seldom be sure what the truth is, one would save oneself a great deal of grief by not always insisting on it.

yoruba: Wọ̀bìà-á yó tán, ó pe ẹgbẹ́ ẹ̀ wá.
english_literal: The greedy person fed to satiation, and he summons his friends.
interpretation_gold: The freeloader always seeks opportunities to take as much as possible from his or her benefactor.

yoruba: Wíwò-ó tó ìran.
english_literal: Watching is enough for a spectacle.
interpretation_gold: One would do well to only watch spectacles and avoid becoming part of them.

yoruba: Yọkọlú-yọkọlú, kò ha tán bí? Ìyàwó gbọ́kọ ṣánlẹ̀, ọkọ-ọ́ yọké.
english_literal: All your strutting and bragging, where is it now? The wife threw the husband down so hard that he grew a hump on his back.
interpretation_gold: Said of braggarts who have been taken down a few notches.

yoruba: Yíyọ́ ẹkùn, tojo kọ́; ohun tí yó jẹ ní ńwá.
english_literal: The leopard's stealthy gait is not a result of cowardice; it is simply stalking a prey.
interpretation_gold: Do not mistake people's gentle nature for spinelessness.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá ḿmú ìyàwó bọ̀ wá fún kì í garùn.
english_literal: The person to whom a bride is being brought does not strain his neck (to see her from a distance.)
interpretation_gold: One should not be unduly impatient for what is coming one's way anyway.

yoruba: Ẹní bá mọ iṣin-ín jẹ a mọ ikú ojú-u rẹ̀-ẹ́ yọ̀.
english_literal: Whoever knows how to eat Akee Apple must know how to remove its deadly raphe.
interpretation_gold: One should be sure of one's capabilities before one attempts dangerous feats.

yoruba: Ọ̀pá àgbéléjìká, a-tẹ̀hìn-lójú.
english_literal: The walking-stick that is carried on the shoulder, which has its eye pointed backward.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who pay no attention to their future.

yoruba: Ẹní kánjú jayé á kánjú lọ sọ́run.
english_literal: Whoever is in a hurry to enjoy life will go to heaven in a hurry.
interpretation_gold: Patience is what life calls for.

yoruba: Ẹyẹ kí lo máa pa tí ò ńfi àkùkọ ṣe oògùn àtè?
english_literal: What sort of bird do you hope to kill that you use a cock in the birdlime charm?
interpretation_gold: It is unreasonable to expend something of great value in pursuit of something of lesser value.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà baba olè; àwòròǹṣoṣò-ó wo ohun olóhun má ṣèẹ́jú.
english_literal: Covetousness, father of thievery; bug-eyed greedy person stares at another person's property without blinking.
interpretation_gold: Covetousness leads to stealing.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó bá obìnrin kó lọ sílé-e rẹ̀ yó sùn nínú ẹ̀rù.
english_literal: A man who goes with a woman to her house will sleep in fear.
interpretation_gold: Illicit acts carried on indiscreetly are attended by great anxiety.

yoruba: Ọgbọ́n pẹ̀lú-u sùúrù la fi ḿmú erin wọ̀lú.
english_literal: It is with cunning and patience that one brings an elephant into town.
interpretation_gold: The most difficult tasks can be accomplished with wisdom and patience.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ tí a ó bàá nù, gágá lara ńyáni.
english_literal: The day one is destined to be lost one is never able to contain one's excitement.
interpretation_gold: Disaster attends over-enthusiasm.

yoruba: Ọ̀ràn ọkà-á ní ìba; ayé ní òṣùwọ̀n.
english_literal: There matter pertaining to corn has a limit; life has its measure.
interpretation_gold: To everything there is a proper limit.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a ò lè mú, Ọlọ́run là ńfi lé lọ́wọ́.
english_literal: An adversary over whom one cannot prevail, one leaves to God's judgement.
interpretation_gold: If an adversary is too much for one, one sets God at him or her.

yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ọdúnnìí, wèrè ẹ̀míì.
english_literal: Today's wisdom, next year's madness.
interpretation_gold: What seems wise now may appear like lunacy in hindsight.

yoruba: Ọ̀mùtí ò mu agbè já.
english_literal: The drunkard does not drink the gourd through.
interpretation_gold: There is a limit to the pleasure a drunk can get from a bottle.

yoruba: Ọ̀gá-a má fi ẹsẹ̀ yí ẹrẹ̀, gbogbo ara ní ńfi yí i.
english_literal: The never-soil-your-foot-with-mud dandy eventually soils his whole body.
interpretation_gold: Too much squeamishness is its own undoing.

yoruba: Ẹ̀sọ̀ ẹ̀sọ̀ la fi ńlá ọbẹ̀ tó gbóná.
english_literal: Slowly, slowly is the way to eat soup that is scalding hot.
interpretation_gold: The more dangerous the task, the greater care one must take.

yoruba: Ẹṣin iwájú ni ti ẹ̀hìn ńwò sáré.
english_literal: The leading horse is the one by which the followers set their pace.
interpretation_gold: One takes one's examples from those that have gone before.

yoruba: Ọ̀bẹlẹ̀wò bẹlẹ̀wò; bí ewúrẹ́ yó bàá dùbúlẹ̀ a bẹ ilẹ̀ ibẹ̀ wò.
english_literal: Inspector of the ground inspects the ground; if a goat wishes to lie down it first inspects the ground.
interpretation_gold: Look well at the lay of the land before engaging in any new venture.

yoruba: Ẹgbẹ́ ẹja lẹja ńwẹ̀ tọ̀; ẹgbẹ́ ẹyẹ lẹyẹ ńwọ́ lé.
english_literal: Fish swim in a school of their own kind; birds fly in a flock of their own kind.
interpretation_gold: One should seek and keep the company of people of one's own station.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó bá wọ odò ni àyà ńkò, àyà ò fo odò.
english_literal: It is the person who enters a river who is terrified, not the river.
interpretation_gold: It is the person who takes on an invincible adversary who has a problem, not the adversary.

yoruba: Ọ̀gbágbá wọlẹ̀, ó ku àtiyọ.
english_literal: The iron stake has been driven into the ground; the problem now is how to pull it out.
interpretation_gold: Some ventures easy at the start prove mightily intractable down the line.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà èèyàn-án dé àwùjọ, ó wòkè yàn-yàn-àn-yàn.
english_literal: The covetous person arrives in a gathering, and his eyes dart about restlessly.
interpretation_gold: The covetous person is always on the lookout for something.

yoruba: Ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńgbẹ̀hìn aláṣejù.
english_literal: Disgrace is the reward of excess.
interpretation_gold: Lack of moderation results in disgrace.

yoruba: Ẹní bá fẹ́ arúgbó gbẹ̀hìn ni yó sìnkú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: The last spouse of an old person will bury him or her.
interpretation_gold: One should weigh the obligations an enterprise will entail before one embarks on it.

yoruba: Ọ̀bọ ni yo para ẹ̀.
english_literal: The monkey will be its own death.
interpretation_gold: Fools will bring their own undoing upon themselves.

yoruba: Ọkọ̀ ńjò, ọkọ̀ ńjò! Ìgbà tó bá rì, kò parí ná?
english_literal: The boat is leaking, the boat is leaking! After it sinks won't matters end?
interpretation_gold: There is little one can do about a problem whose outcome is inevitable.

yoruba: Ọkùnrin tó fẹ́ òjòwú méjì sílé ò rẹ́ni fi ṣọ́lé.
english_literal: A man who marries two jealous women has no one to tend his home in his absence.
interpretation_gold: Jealousy is a terrible quality in a spouse.

yoruba: Ọ̀ràn ò dun gbọ̀ọ̀rọ̀; a dá a láàárọ̀, ó yọ lálẹ́.
english_literal: Problems have hardly any effect at all on the pumpkin shoot; broken off in the morning, it reappears the following night.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who are unimpressed by correction or punishment.

yoruba: Ẹní bẹni-í tẹ́ni.
english_literal: Whoever pleads with one makes one lose face.
interpretation_gold: A person who beseeches one places one at risk of losing face.

yoruba: Ẹnu òfòrò ní ńpa òfòrò; òfòrò-ó bímọ méjì, ó kó wọn wá sẹ́bàá ọ̀nà, ó ní “Ọmọ-ọ̀ mí yè koro-koro.”
english_literal: The squirrel's mouth summons its death; the squirrel has two children, takes them to the edge of the path, and says, “My children are hale and well indeed.”
interpretation_gold: Excessive boasting about one's good fortune invites predators.

yoruba: Ọwọ́-ọ baba lẹ wò, ẹ ò wo ẹsẹ̀-ẹ baba.
english_literal: Your eyes are on the patriarch's hand, but they ignore his feet.
interpretation_gold: People who do not pay attention to details are liable to go astray.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ púpọ̀ ò kún agbọ̀n; irọ́ ní ḿmú wá.
english_literal: A lot of words will not fill a basket; it will only lead to lies.
interpretation_gold: Brevity is wise in discussions; wordiness leads to invention.

yoruba: Ṣe-ǹ-ṣe dìwọ̀fà, bó ṣe é yó dẹrú-u wọn.
english_literal: The habit that made a person a pawn: if the person persists in it it will make him or her a slave.
interpretation_gold: One should desist from pursuits that have proved unprofitable.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó ba ogún-un baba rẹ̀ jẹ́, ó ja òkú ọ̀run lólè, yó sì di ẹni ìfibú.
english_literal: Whoever ruins his or her father's bequest robs the dead, and becomes a person of reproach.
interpretation_gold: One must keep faith with one's ancestral heritage.

yoruba: Ẹ̀rù kọ́ ní ḿba ọ̀pẹ tó ní ká dá òun sí, nítorí ẹmu ọ̀la ni.
english_literal: It is not out of fear that the palm-tree pleads to be allowed to stand; it is on account of tomorrow's palm-wine.
interpretation_gold: What we have the good sense to preserve today will yield benefits for us in the future.

yoruba: Ẹrẹ̀ òkèọ̀dàn ni yó kìlọ̀ fún a-l-áròó-gbálẹ̀ aṣọ.
english_literal: The mud on the plains will teach a lesson to the person whose loincloth has a train sweeping the ground.
interpretation_gold: The thoughtless person will learn wisdom when his or her thoughtlessness comes to roost.

yoruba: Whoever follows the river without turning back will come face to face with Oluwẹri.
interpretation_gold: Whoever persists in courting danger will eventually find it.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà-á pín ẹgbàafà nínú ẹgbàaje; ó ní kí wọ́n pín ẹgbàá kan tó kù, bóyá igbiwó tún lè kan òun.
english_literal: The insatiable person receives twelve thousand cowries out fourteen thousand; he asked that the remaining two thousand be shared, perhaps two hundred of them will come to him.
interpretation_gold: Greed knows no limits.

yoruba: Ẹni méjì kì í bínú egbinrin.
english_literal: Two people do not hold a grudge and refuse reconciliation.
interpretation_gold: If there is to be any hope of ending a quarrel, one of the parties at least must be willing to make up.

yoruba: Ẹ̀hìn ní ńdun ol-ókùú-àdá sí.
english_literal: It is the back of the man with a blunt cutlass that suffers.
interpretation_gold: A person who does not make adequate preparations for a task or test will rue his or her negligence.

yoruba: Ẹní gúnyán kalẹ̀ yóò júbà ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: A person who has made pounded yams must pay homage to the stew.
interpretation_gold: The prudent person cultivates the source of what he/she needs.

yoruba: Ẹní bá mọ ayé-é jẹ kì í gun àgbọn.
english_literal: Whoever knows what makes for a good life never climbs coconut palms.
interpretation_gold: Whoever cares about his or her welfare does not live dangerously.

yoruba: Ṣe-ká-rí-mi, alájá tó so ẹ̀gi mọ́rùn.
english_literal: Exhibitionist, a dog owner who ties a sheep's mane around his own neck.
interpretation_gold: Do not go to too great lengths to call people's attention to yourself.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá ti rí kì í tún ba mọ́lẹ̀ mọ́.
english_literal: A person who has been seen has no further need of hiding.
interpretation_gold: Once the damage is done, prevention comes too late.

yoruba: Ọ̀ràn ńlá-ńlá ní ḿbá àpá; ọ̀ràn ṣẹ́kú-ṣẹ́kú ní ḿbá oṣè.
english_literal: Only huge problems befall the mahogany bean tree; only minor problems befall the baobab tree.
interpretation_gold: Different people have different levels of vulnerability.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ò ní ohùn fífọ̀, dídákẹ́ ló yẹ ẹ́.
english_literal: A matter that does not have a means to voice itself had better be silent.
interpretation_gold: Matters that should not be mentioned should be left unbroached.

yoruba: Ẹ̀bìtì tí ò kún ẹmọ́ lójú, òun ní ńyí i lẹ́pọ̀n sẹ́hìn.
english_literal: It is a trap that the giant rat disdains that wrenches its testicles backwards.
interpretation_gold: Dangers that one belittles are liable to cause great havoc.

yoruba: Ọmọ orogún ẹ-ẹ́ kú, o ní ẹní rí ẹ lọ́run ò purọ́; bí tìẹ́ bá kú ńkọ́?
english_literal: The child of your rival-wife dies and you say the person who saw you in heaven did not lie; what if your own child dies?
interpretation_gold: One should not go overboard in sharing other people's sorrow.

yoruba: Ẹní bá mọ ayé-é jẹ kì í jà.
english_literal: Whoever knows how to enjoy life does not enter into a fight.
interpretation_gold: The best way to enjoy life is to avoid conflict.

yoruba: Ẹnu iná ní ńpa iná; ẹnu èrò ní ńpa èrò..
english_literal: The mouth of the louse is its death; the mouth of the nit is its death.
interpretation_gold: The reckless person brings disaster on his or her head by his or her own actions.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ lọmọ etí ńjẹ.
english_literal: Words are what the child of the ear eats.
interpretation_gold: People who misbehave must endure tongue-lashes.

yoruba: Ẹní bá fẹ́ abuké ni yó ru ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ dàgbà.
english_literal: Whoever marries a humpbacked woman will carry her child on his back until the child is weaned.
interpretation_gold: If one knowingly gets oneself into a difficulty, one will bear the consequences oneself.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà ò ṣé-é fi wá nǹkan.
english_literal: Impatient envy is not a good state in which to seek anything.
interpretation_gold: One should be patient in seeking one's fortune.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́jọ́ kú sílé, aláròyé kú síta gbangba.
english_literal: The person involved in an affair dies at home; the spokesperson dies out in the open.
interpretation_gold: The busybody's fate is worse than that of the person involved in the affair.

yoruba: Ọgbọ́n àgbọ́njù ní ńsọ ẹni diwin; bí oògún bá pọ̀ lápọ̀jù a sọni di wèrè; bóbìnrín bá gbọ́n àgbọ́njù, péńpé laṣọ ọkọ-ọ ẹ̀ ḿmọ.
english_literal: Excessive cleverness turns one into a phantom; if there is too much magical charm it turns the owner into an imbecile; if a woman is too cunning her husband's clothes wind up ill-fitting.
interpretation_gold: People who are too cunning are headed for trouble; a man who married too cunning a woman is headed for trouble.

yoruba: Ọ̀dárayá tí ńfi ẹ̀gbẹ́ na igi.
english_literal: Sprightly person who hurls himself sidewise against a tree.
interpretation_gold: Said of a too-cheerful person whose excess energy is getting on others' nerves.

yoruba: Ẹnu-ù mi kọ́ ni wọ́n ti máa gbọ́ pé ìyá ọba-á lájẹ̀ẹ́.
english_literal: It is not from my mouth that people will learn that the king's mother is a witch.
interpretation_gold: I will not place myself in jeopardy by speaking dangerous truths; one should not acknowledge or comment on everything one sees.

yoruba: Ẹnu ẹyẹ ní ńpẹyẹ; ẹnu òrofó ní ńpòrofó; òrofó bímọ mẹ́fà, ó ní ilé òun-ún kún ṣọ́ṣọ́ṣọ́.
english_literal: The bird's mouth is its death; the green fruit pigeon's mouth is its death; the pigeon hatches six chicks and boasts that its house is bursting at the seams.
interpretation_gold: To boast about one's good fortune is to invite predators.

yoruba: Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ḿbàjẹ́, a ní ó ńpọ́n.
english_literal: The banana is rotting, people say it is ripening.
interpretation_gold: It does not help to rationalize a brat's behavior with silly explanations.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó mú u lórí ní ó kú, ìwọ tí o mú u lẹ́sẹ̀-ẹ́ ní ó ńjòwèrè.
english_literal: The person holding it by the head says it is dead; you who are holding it by the feet say it is going through death throes.
interpretation_gold: Novices should not presume to be more knowledgeable than the experts.

yoruba: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan lọwọ̀ ńyọ.
english_literal: Broom sticks drop off one by one.
interpretation_gold: Huge problems usually build up gradually.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà àgbẹ̀ tí ńgbin òwú sóko àkùrọ̀.
english_literal: “It is” an insatiable farmer who plants cotton on a farm by the stream.
interpretation_gold: Greed sometimes makes people work against their own interests.

yoruba: Ọ̀gán ìmàdò ò ṣé-é kò lójú.
english_literal: A full-grown warthog is not something to confront.
interpretation_gold: One would be wise to avoid dangerous people.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà kì í mu ẹ̀jẹ̀ ẹlòmíràn; ẹ̀jẹ̀ ara ẹ̀ náà ní ḿmu.
english_literal: The greedy person does not drink other people's blood; he drinks only his own.
interpretation_gold: Greed recoils on the greedy.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà ológbò tó jókòó sẹ́nu ọ̀nà; ṣé eku eléku ló fẹ́ pa jẹ?
english_literal: The insatiable cat that sits in the doorway, does it want to kill cats in another house?
interpretation_gold: Greedy people are never satisfied with what they have.

yoruba: Ọdẹ a-fi-fìlà-pa-erin, ọjọ́ kan ni òkìkí-i ẹ̀ ḿmọ.
english_literal: The hunter who would kill elephants with his cap; his fame lasts only one day.
interpretation_gold: Whoever promises to do the impossible enjoys fame only as long as it takes for the impossibility to be manifest.

yoruba: Ẹni àjò ò pé kó múra ilé.
english_literal: The person for whom the journey has not been profitable should prepare to return home.
interpretation_gold: One should know when it is time to go home.

yoruba: Ẹnu ni àparò-ó fi ńpe ọ̀rá; a ní “Kìkì ọ̀rá, kìkì ọ̀rá!”
english_literal: With its own mouth the partridge invites its own ruin; it cries, “Nothing but fat, nothing but fat!”
interpretation_gold: Conspicuous display of one's good fortune invites predators.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó yá ẹgbàafà tí kò san án, ó bẹ́gi dí ọ̀nà egbèje.
english_literal: The person who borrows twelve hundred cowries and does not pay them back blocks the path of fourteen hundred cowries.
interpretation_gold: A person who defaults in little things does himself or herself out of the opportunity for larger ones.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó jìn sí kòtò-ó kọ́ ará ìyókù lọ́gbọ́n.
english_literal: The person who falls into a ditch teaches others a lesson.
interpretation_gold: One learns from the experiences of those who have gone before.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ tí àgbẹ̀ ṣíṣe-é bá di kíyèsílẹ̀, ká ṣíwọ́ oko ríro.
english_literal: The day farming entails being careful not to hurt the soil, one should stop farming.
interpretation_gold: If the basic condition for a trade is interdicted, one should no longer engage in the trade.

yoruba: Ọgbọ́n àgbọ́njù ní ńpa òdù ọ̀yà.
english_literal: It is excessive cunning that kills the mature cane rat.
interpretation_gold: Too much cleverness brings trouble.

yoruba: Ọ̀nà ni yó mùú olè; ahéré ni yó mùú olóko.
english_literal: The road will eventually expose the thief; the farm hut will eventually expose the farmer.
interpretation_gold: When the habitual wrongdoer comes to grief, it will be in the course of his wrongdoing.

yoruba: Ọ̀wọ́n yúnlé, ọ̀pọ̀-ọ́ yúnjà.
english_literal: Expensive commodities come to the home; inexpensive ones go to the market.
interpretation_gold: If one overprices one's goods one will find no takers.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ò fẹ́-ẹ́ wọ àkísà kì í bá ajá ṣe eré-e géle.
english_literal: A person who does not wish to wear rags should not engage in rough play with a dog.
interpretation_gold: People should avoid situations that might earn them disgrace.

yoruba: Ṣe-ǹ-ṣe ewúrẹ́ làgùntàn ńfiyè sí.
english_literal: The habit of the goat is what the sheep pays attention to.
interpretation_gold: One would be wise to learn from the behaviour and plight of fools.

yoruba: Ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ là ńtẹ ẹrẹ̀; ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ là ńtẹ eruku.
english_literal: One step after the other is the manner to walk through mire; one step after the other is how one walks through dust.
interpretation_gold: With great care, one can extricate oneself safely from any problem.

yoruba: Ẹní bá rọra pa eèrà á rí ìfun inú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: Whoever takes great care in killing an ant will see its innards.
interpretation_gold: One must handle delicate matters with great care.

yoruba: Ẹní gbé adíẹ òtòṣì-í gbé ti aláròyé.
english_literal: Whoever steals a poor person's chicken steals from an incessant complainer.
interpretation_gold: One should choose one's adversaries with prudence.

yoruba: Ẹní bá pé kí àkàlà má jòkú, ojú-u rẹ̀ lẹyẹ ńkọ́kọ́ yọ jẹ.
english_literal: Whoever says the ground-hornbill should not eat carrion, he or she will be the first to lose his or her eyes to the bird.
interpretation_gold: Whoever tries to prevent the inevitable will be trampled in the process of its occurring.

yoruba: Ẹ̀ẹ̀kan ṣoṣo lọmọ ńsín tí à ńní “à-sín-gbó, à-sín-tọ́.”
english_literal: It is when a child sneezes only once that one wishes the child “sneeze and grow old, sneeze and live long.”
interpretation_gold: Casual responses are appropriate only for minor difficulties; if the difficulties grow serious more appropriate measures must be adopted.

yoruba: Ọ̀nà ọ̀fun, ọ̀nà ọ̀run: méjèèjì bákannáà ni wọ́n rí.
english_literal: The pathway of the throat, the pathway to heaven: the two are very much alike.
interpretation_gold: One's throat may lead to one's death.

yoruba: Ẹnu tí ìgbín fi bú òrìṣà ní ńfi-í lọlẹ̀ lọ bá a.
english_literal: The same mouth with which the snail insults the god is the one on which it crawls to the god.
interpretation_gold: The person who insults a powerful person will in time eat his or her words before the person insulted.

yoruba: Ọ̀bánijà ní ḿmọ ìjagun ẹni.
english_literal: Only those who struggle with one know one's strategies.
interpretation_gold: Only through close association does one know other people.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó bá mu ọtí ogójì á sọ̀rọ̀ okòó.
english_literal: Whoever drinks forty cowries worth of wine will talk twenty cowries worth of talk.
interpretation_gold: A little wine opens the way for only a little information.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ò tóni-í nà ò gbọdọ̀ ṣe kọ́-ń-dú síni.
english_literal: A person who is not strong enough to beat one up should not adopt a threatening pose towards one.
interpretation_gold: People should not challenge forces they cannot withstand.

yoruba: Ọbẹ̀ tóo sè tílé fi jóná wàá sọ ọ́.
english_literal: The sort of stew you cooked and set the house on fire, you will explain.
interpretation_gold: You must explain your unheard-of behavior that resulted in such a disaster as has occurred.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ńsáré kiri nínú-u pápá ńwá ọ̀nà àti jìn sí kòtò.
english_literal: The person who runs about in the bush courts the danger of falling into a ditch.
interpretation_gold: Reckless action leads to disaster.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ tí a to ọkà a ò to ti èkúté mọ́ ọ.
english_literal: The day one arranged one's corn in the granary, one did not think in terms of the rat.
interpretation_gold: One hardly ever plans for trouble.

yoruba: Ọ̀làjà ní ńfi orí gbọgbẹ́.
english_literal: It is the person who separates two fighters who gets gashed on the head.
interpretation_gold: The peace maker is liable to suffer for his pains.

yoruba: Ẹ̀bi alábaun kì í gbèé dẹ̀bi àna-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: The Tortoise's guilt is not long in becoming that of his parent-in-law's.
interpretation_gold: Incommensurate retaliation soon transfers public sympathy from the aggrieved person to the culprit.

yoruba: Ọmọdé jí ti ojú orun wá, ó ní “Àkàrà kéjìkéjì”; wọ́n ti ḿmú u kẹ́ẹ̀ kó tó jí, ì ká ká níkẹ̀?
english_literal: A child wakes from sleep and says in code, “Bean fritters two-by-two.” Had the others been taking them thus before he woke would any have been left?
interpretation_gold: Never misuse what those before you made available to you by their wise husbandry.

yoruba: Ẹní dáríjiní ṣẹ̀tẹ́ ẹjọ́.
english_literal: Whoever forgives one defuses the dispute.
interpretation_gold: Once the aggrieved person is pacified, there is no further point in pursuing the case.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a lù lógbòó mẹ́fà, tí a ní kó fiyèdénú: ìgbà tí kò fiyèdénú ńkọ́?
english_literal: A person is hit with a cudgel six times and then urged to learn forbearance; what other option does he or she have?
interpretation_gold: A victim with no access to any remedy needs no advice to let matters drop.

yoruba: Ọlọ́dẹ kì í torí atẹ́gùn yìnbọn.
english_literal: A hunter does not fire off his gun because of the wind.
interpretation_gold: One should be deliberate and attentive in pursuing one's profession.

yoruba: Ẹ̀hìn àjànàkú là ńyọ ogbó; ta ní jẹ́ yọ agada lójú erin?
english_literal: It is after the demise of the elephant that one brandishes a cudgel; who dares draw a scimitar in the face of an elephant?
interpretation_gold: One can be brave after the danger has been removed.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá ḿbá ṣiṣẹ́ kì í ṣọ̀lẹ; bórí bá túnni ṣe a kì í tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: The person being lent a hand does not malinger; if Providence favors one, one is not easily disgraced.
interpretation_gold: One should make the most of unexpected good fortune, and not squander the opportunity it presents.

yoruba: Ọ̀ràn kì í yẹ̀ lórí alábaun.
english_literal: The responsibility for trouble never fails to fall on the head of the tortoise.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who are invariable the source of problems.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ tó kú légbodò ló ní ká fòun jẹyán.
english_literal: It is a pig that dies at the time of the harvesting of new yams that asks to be eaten with pounded yam.
interpretation_gold: If one puts oneself in harm's way one deserves what one gets.

yoruba: Ẹ̀lúlùú, ìwọ ló fòjò pa ara-à rẹ.
english_literal: Larkheeled Cuckoo, it was you that got yourself drenched in the rain.
interpretation_gold: Whatever your difficulty is, you brought it on yourself.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́rù ní ńgbé ẹrù ká tó ba ké ọfẹ.
english_literal: The owner of the load must first lift it before one lends one's encouragement.
interpretation_gold: Only those who make an effort on their own behalf deserve help from others.

yoruba: Ẹnìkan kì í fi ọ̀bẹ tó nù jẹṣu.
english_literal: No one eats yams with a lost knife.
interpretation_gold: People are loath to admit they are at fault in any matter.

yoruba: Ẹyin adìẹ ò gbọdọ̀ forí sọ àpáta.
english_literal: A chicken egg should not strike its head against a rock.
interpretation_gold: It is unwise to take on forces one cannot withstand.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ tí elétutu-ú bá máa fò, ìjàm̀pere kì í rìn.
english_literal: On the day the white flying ants wish to swarm, the worms that prey on them keep still.
interpretation_gold: Only cunning will deliver one's prey into one's hands.

yoruba: Ẹní bá sọ púpọ̀ á ṣìsọ.
english_literal: Whoever talks a lot will misspeak.
interpretation_gold: It is best to be of few words.

yoruba: Ẹkùn kì í yan kí ajá yan.
english_literal: A leopard does not strut and be answered by strutting from a dog.
interpretation_gold: One should recognize danger and avoid it.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà pẹ̀lú olè, déédé ni wọ́n jẹ́.
english_literal: Covetousness and thievery are similar to each other.
interpretation_gold: Covetousness is as bad as stealing.

yoruba: Ọ̀kùn-ún mọ̀nà tẹ́lẹ̀ kójú ẹ̀ tó fọ́.
english_literal: The millipede knew the way before it went blind.
interpretation_gold: The old knew how to live before they became frail.

yoruba: Ẹni òyìnbó fẹ́ràn ní ńtì mọ́lé.
english_literal: It is the person the white man likes that the white man incarcerates.
interpretation_gold: Whoever becomes too friendly with a white man deserves what the white man does to him. A favorite, being more likely to take liberties with his or her benefactor, is more likely to get in trouble than the unfavored.

yoruba: Ẹ̀kọ tí kò bá léwé làgbà ńgbà.
english_literal: It is corn-loaf that has no leaf wrapping that the elder takes.
interpretation_gold: If one is careless with one's property one is liable to lose it.

yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀ oògùn ní ńru ọmọ gàle-gàle.
english_literal: It is a great deal of medicine that possesses a child and robs it of all self-control.
interpretation_gold: A person who lacks moderation is like someone overpowered by bad medicine.

yoruba: Ọ̀nà là ńṣì mọ̀nà; bí a ò bá ṣubú, a kì í mọ ẹrù-ú dì.
english_literal: It is by missing one's way that one learns the way; if one does not fall one does not learn how to tie one's load properly.
interpretation_gold: Errors and failures are opportunities to learn.

yoruba: Ọmọrí odó pani lọ́tọ̀, ká tó wí pé ká kùn ún lóògùn.
english_literal: A pestle is a lethal weapon in itself, let alone after rubbing poison on it.
interpretation_gold: Overkill is pointless. Also, if a situation is dangerous enough as it is, one should not aggravate it by acting provocatively.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a fẹ́-ẹ́ sunjẹ kì í fepo para lọ jókòó sídìí iná.
english_literal: A person being eyed for barbecuing does not baste himself with oil and sit by the fire.
interpretation_gold: One should not facilitate one's own undoing.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà-á bu òkèlè, ojù ẹ̀-ẹ́ lami.
english_literal: A greedy person takes a morsel of food and tears gush from his eyes.
interpretation_gold: Greed has its pains also.

yoruba: “Ọla ni mò ńlọ,” tí ńfi koto ṣe àmù.
english_literal: “Tomorrow I take my leave,” who uses a shallow pot as his water jar.
interpretation_gold: Short-sighted people make little provision for the future.

yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ lejò ḿbùjẹ, tí à ńwí pé ilẹ̀-ẹ́ rorò?
english_literal: Is it because a snake is biting a toad that one says the earth portends disaster?
interpretation_gold: Do not make too much of insignificant events.

yoruba: Ẹní dúró de erín dúró dekú; ẹní dúró dẹfọ̀n-ọ́n dúró dèjà; ẹní dúró de eégún alágangan, ọ̀run ló fẹ́-ẹ́ lọ.
english_literal: Whoever waits in a charging elephant's path waits for death; whoever waits in a buffalo's path waits for an attack; whoever tarries before a fleet-footed masquerader hankers for a trip to heaven.
interpretation_gold: Whoever sees trouble approaching and does not flee courts disaster.

yoruba: Ọ̀daràn ẹyẹ tí ńmusàn.
english_literal: Habitual criminal bird that eats oranges.
interpretation_gold: Addressed to any person whose actions are likely to lead to some disaster.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a ò lè mú, a kì í gọ dè é.
english_literal: One does not lie in ambush for an adversary one is no match for.
interpretation_gold: One should pick fights only with those over whom one can prevail.

yoruba: Ẹ̀bìtì ò peèrà tó ṣe pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́; ẹnu ẹni níńpani.
english_literal: A trap does not kill an ant that is cautious; it's one's mouth that turns out to be one's death.
interpretation_gold: The cautious will live long on the earth; the incautious engineers his or her own death.

yoruba: Ọ̀kánjúwà baba àrùn.
english_literal: Covetousness, father of all diseases.
interpretation_gold: There is no disease like greed.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ ò pọ̀, àkàwé-e ẹ̀ ló pọ̀.
english_literal: The matter in question is not overwhelming; it is the elaboration for it that is almost forbidding.
interpretation_gold: Creating a problem is easy; explaining it is not quite as easy.

yoruba: Ẹyin lọ̀rọ̀; bó bá balẹ̀ fífọ́ ní ńfọ́.
english_literal: Words are eggs; when they drop on the floor they shatter into pieces.
interpretation_gold: Words are delicate things; once spoken, they cannot be retrieved.

yoruba: Ọmọ adìẹ-ẹ́ fò, a ní “Ẹrán lọ àkẹ́ẹ̀!”
english_literal: A chick flies up, and we exclaim, “A game animal has escaped, alas!”
interpretation_gold: Do not blow matters out of all credible proportion!

yoruba: Ẹní fi ìpọ́njú kọ ẹyìn á kọ àbọ̀n; ẹní fi ìpọ́njú rojọ́ á jẹ̀bi ọba; ẹní fi ìpọ́njú lọ gbẹ́ ìhò á gbẹ́ ihò awọ́nrínwọ́n.
english_literal: Whoever gathers palm fruits in desperation will gather unripe ones; whoever states his or her case in desperation will be adjudged at fault by the king; whoever digs a hole in desperation will dig out an iguana lizard.
interpretation_gold: Nothing turns out well if done in desperation. Easy does it.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́kún sunkún ó bá tirẹ̀ lọ; aláròpa ìbá sunkún kò dákẹ́.
english_literal: The person with a cause to cry cries and departs; if it were a person whose mind never leaves a problem he or she would never have stopped crying.
interpretation_gold: One should not keep harping on one's injuries.

yoruba: Ọlọ́gbọ́n bẹẹrẹ-ẹ́ pète ìgárá.
english_literal: The excessively cunning person is trying his hand at stealing.
interpretation_gold: Too much cunning is like thievery.

yoruba: Ọ̀nà ẹ̀bùrú dá ọwọ́ olúwa-a ẹ̀ tẹlẹ̀.
english_literal: A short cut causes a person to land on his palms.
interpretation_gold: There are perils to taking paths one is not familiar with.

yoruba: “Ṣé kí nfìdí hẹ?” làfòmọ́ fi ńdi onílé.
english_literal: “May I perch here awhile?” is the ruse by which the climber-parasite becomes a permanent resident.
interpretation_gold: Give people an inch, and they are liable to take several miles.

english_literal: The problem posed by the banana tree is nothing that calls for a machete.
interpretation_gold: Do not make too much of a minor crisis.

yoruba: Ọ̀gọ̀ ńgbé ọ̀gọ rù.
english_literal: A fool carries a cudjel around.
interpretation_gold: A person is cultivating the means to his/her own ruin.

english_literal: A subordinate military officer who is audacious is the equal of his superior.
interpretation_gold: Audaciousness will get one one's way.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Alára ní ńgbára-á ga;bádíẹ́ bá máa wọ̀ọ̀dẹ̀ a bẹ̀rẹ̀.
english_literal: It is the owner of the body that elevates the body; when a chicken wishes to enter the porch it stoops.
interpretation_gold: One should sound one's own trumpet and not be unduly humble.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring

english_literal: The aftertaste of the bitterleaf is sweet.
interpretation_gold: Sweetness and pleasure come after bitter exertions.

yoruba: Àìtó ehín-ín ká ni à ńfọwọ́ bò ó.
english_literal: It is not-having-attained-the-age-for-losing-one's-teeth that makes one cover (the mouth) with one's hand.
interpretation_gold: One should not be reticent in asserting oneself.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring

english_literal: The cock crows, and the lazy person hisses.
interpretation_gold: The coming of the morning is an annoyance to the lazy person.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àgbàbọ̀-ọ ṣòkòtò, bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a ṣoni; rẹ́mú-rẹ́mú ni ohun ẹni ḿbani mu.
english_literal: Borrowed trousers, if they are not too tight around the legs, they will be too loose; one's own things fit one exactly.
interpretation_gold: Borrowed articles are never like one's own.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: “A ò mọ̀yí Ọlọ́run yó ṣe” kò jẹ́ ká bínú kú.
english_literal: “We know not what God will do” keeps one from committing suicide.
interpretation_gold: Often it is hope that keeps people going.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Apárí ní ńfojú di abẹ.
english_literal: It is a bald person that may be disdainful of the razor.
interpretation_gold: The bald person has no use for razors.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Apẹ́ẹ́jẹ kì í jẹ ìbàjẹ́.
english_literal: A person who waits patiently for a long time before eating will not eat unwholesome food.
interpretation_gold: Those who are patient will have the best of things.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àgbàká lẹsẹ̀ ńgba ọ̀na.
english_literal: It is completely that the feet take over a path.
interpretation_gold: Indulge not in half measures.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Ajé sọ ọmọ nù bí òkò.
english_literal: Wealth throws a person away like a stone.
interpretation_gold: The search for wealth takes one into distant lands.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Aboyún bí, ìhá tù ú.
english_literal: The pregnant woman delivered; her sides are much eased.
interpretation_gold: Relief comes in time to the persevering sufferer.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Abiyamọ ọ̀tá àgàn; ẹní ńṣiṣẹ́ ọ̀tá ọ̀lẹ.
english_literal: Nursing mother, enemy of the barren woman; working person, enemy of the idler.
interpretation_gold: The mother incurs the envy of barren woman; the hard worker incurs the hatred of the idler.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Ajá wo ẹyẹ láwòmọ́jú.
english_literal: The dog looks at birds with eyes full of disdain.
interpretation_gold: Against adversaries beyond one's powers, one must be satisfied with futile gestures.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Ajìnfìn, má ta ojú ilé; ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ jìnfìn má ta ojú àtijáde.
english_literal: You who have fallen into the dungeon, do not be impatient to arrive home; when the toad drops into a pit it cannot be impatient to get out.
interpretation_gold: Certain predicaments one does not get out of in a hurry.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Ariwo àjìjà ní ńdọ́run.
english_literal: It is only the noise of the whirlwind that reaches heaven.
interpretation_gold: One's enemies may be clamorous, but all they are capable of is noise.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Abẹ̀wẹ̀ ńwá ọ̀tá fúnra ẹ̀.
english_literal: He who summons others to render him communal help seeks enemies.
interpretation_gold: It is best to be self-sufficient.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: A-fàkàrà-jẹ̀kọ́ ò mọ iyì ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: He-who-eats-corn-meal-with-bean-fritters does not know the virtues of stew.
interpretation_gold: Whoever leads a sheltered life misses out on some great experiences.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Ara kì í wúwo kí alára má lè gbe.
english_literal: A body cannot be too heavy for the owner to lift.
interpretation_gold: Whatever others might feel, a person is never put off by himself or his own habits.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Alágẹmọ-ọ́ ti bímọ-ọ rẹ̀ ná; àìmọ̀-ọ́jó kù sọ́wọ́-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: The chameleon has given birth to its young; inability to dance is the responsibility of the child.
interpretation_gold: A parent has done his/her part by having a child; the child's fortunes are the child's responsibility.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àgbinsínú legbin ńgbin; àkùnsínú lẹkùn ńkùn; hùn hùn hùn ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ inú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ní ńgbé.
english_literal: Groaning-internally is how an antelope groans; rumbling-internally is how a leopard rumbles, the grunts of a pig stay inside the pig.
interpretation_gold: People may grumble, but they dare not voice their complaints openly.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: A hán ìkokò lọ́wọ́ ọ̀tún, a hán ìkokò lẹ́sẹ̀ òsì; ó ku ẹni tí yó kò ó lójú.
english_literal: We lop off the hyena's right fore limb; we lop off the hyena's left hind limb; the question is, who will face it now?
interpretation_gold: Inflicting such injuries on the hyena is no victory; it only makes the animal more dangerous.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Afẹ́fẹ́ kì í fẹ́ kí omi inú àgbọn dànù.
english_literal: The wind does not blow against the liquid inside a coconut and cause it to spill.
interpretation_gold: Certain people are not susceptible to certain disasters.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àfẹjútoto ò mọ ọkùnrin.
english_literal: Glaring wildly does not bespeak manliness.
interpretation_gold: Action is more persuasive than appearance.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: A kì í sọ pé ọjà-á nígbà; bó bá nígbà, kíníṣe tí wọ́n tún ńná a?
english_literal: One does not say there is a time for the market; if it were so, why would people continuously patronize it?
interpretation_gold: Any time is a good time to trade.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àjà kì í jìn mọ́ ológbò lẹ́sẹ̀.
english_literal: The snare does not snare a cat's paw.
interpretation_gold: Some people are immune to certain perils.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àgbàká lèéfí ńgba igbó.
english_literal: It is completely that smoke fills the forest.
interpretation_gold: Whatever is worth doing is worth doing diligently and thoroughly.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Agẹmọ ò ṣé-é jẹ lẹ́nu.
english_literal: The chameleon is not a thing to eat in one's mouth.
interpretation_gold: Certain propositions are beyond the pale.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: A kì í fi ojoojúmọ́ rí olè jà kó dà bí-i tọwọ́ ẹni.
english_literal: One is never so fortunate at daily thievery that it matches owning one's own things.
interpretation_gold: Self-sufficiency is far better than fortunate opportunism.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àṣá wo ìgbín kọ̀rọ̀; ìkaraun-un rẹ̀ ò jẹ́ kó gbé e.
english_literal: The kite looks slyly at the snail, but its shell stops the bird from snatching it.
interpretation_gold: This is a more mundane version of the previous entry.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àpáàdì-í gbóko kò rà.
english_literal: The potsherd lives on the farm but does not decay.
interpretation_gold: Resilience is a fortunate quality to have.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: À ńpòyì ká apá, apá ò ká apá; à ńpòyì ká oṣè, apá ò ká oṣè; à ńpòyì ká kànga, kò ṣé bínú kó sí.
english_literal: We make circles round the mahogany bean tree, but it is too much to handle; we make circles around the baobab tree, but it is too much to handle; we makes circles around the well, but it is nothing to jump into in anger.
interpretation_gold: The three items listed are formidable in their different ways, and have nothing to fear from people.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: A kì í dùbúlẹ̀ ṣubú.
english_literal: One does not fall from a prone position.
interpretation_gold: Hunger cannot make one faint and fall if one goes to sleep.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Asúrétete ní ńwojú ọjọ́.
english_literal: It is the person in a hurry who studies the complexion of the day.
interpretation_gold: When one has important tasks in hand one pays particular attention to impinging conditions.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àgbàbọ́ ò di tẹni.
english_literal: A foster child does not become one's own child.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing like having one's own.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àṣá ò gbádìẹ níkọ̀kọ̀; gbangba làṣá ńgbádìẹ.
english_literal: The kite does not snatch chicks in secret, it snatches them openly.
interpretation_gold: What one dare do, one does openly.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: A kì í gbọ́ “gbì” ìràwé.
english_literal: One does not hear the thud of a falling leaf.
interpretation_gold: Incantatory assertion that an accident will not befall the subject.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àṣá wo ahun títí; àwòdí wo ahun títí; idì baba àṣá, kí ló lè fi ahun ṣe?
english_literal: The kite looks long at the tortoise; the eagle looks long at the tortoise; what can the hawk, father of the kite, do to the tortoise?
interpretation_gold: When the prey's defences are impenetrable, the predator can only glare.

part_theme: perseverance, industry, resilience, self-confidence, self-reliance, resourcefulness, daring
yoruba: Àgùdà ò jẹ lábẹ̀-ẹ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì.
english_literal: The Catholic missionary is not in the pay of the British administration.
