english_literal: A ram is too much to give; a gelded animal is too much to give; everything is excessive in the sight of a miser.
interpretation_gold: Expect no favor from a miser.

yoruba: Aṣiwèrè ló bí ìyá ọ̀bọ.
english_literal: It was an imbecile that gave birth to the mother of the monkey.
interpretation_gold: The fool belongs in the same lineage as the imbecile.

yoruba: A-ti-ara-ẹni-roni, ajá ọdẹ.
english_literal: A-creature-that-applies-other's-circumstances-to-itself, a hunter's dog.
interpretation_gold: The hunter's dog would do well to place itself in the shoes of the animals it hunts.

yoruba: Aláràjẹ ò mọ ọdún; a-biṣu-úta-bí-igi.
english_literal: He who purchases the food he eats cares not what the season is; his yams always flourish like trees.
interpretation_gold: The consumer does not know what the producer goes through.

yoruba: Bí a bá gé igi nígbó, ká fi ọ̀ràn ro ara ẹni wò.
english_literal: When one fells a tree in the forest, one should apply the matter to oneself.
interpretation_gold: Whenever one does something to another, one should put oneself in that person's shoes.

yoruba: Bí a bá rí òkú ìkà nílẹ̀, tí a fi ẹsẹ̀ tá; ìkà-á di méji.
english_literal: If one sees the corpse of a wicked person on the ground and one kicks it, there are then two wicked people.
interpretation_gold: If one returns evil for evil, one joins the ranks of the evil.

yoruba: Bí o ṣe rere yó yọ sí ọ lára; bí o kò ṣe rere yó yọ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: If your deeds are good the benefits return to you; if your deeds are not good they will be apparent to all.
interpretation_gold: Neither good nor evil goes for nought.

yoruba: Bí ó ti ńdun ọmọ ẹyẹ, bẹ́ẹ̀ ló ńdun ọmọ èèyàn
english_literal: As the young of birds hurt, so the young of humans hurt.
interpretation_gold: Others feel hurt, just as one does.

yoruba: “Èrò tètè jí;” “Èrò jẹ́ ilẹ̀ ó mọ́”; tèrò là ńrò.
english_literal: “Traveller, get up early”; “Traveller, wait until light”; it's all out of solicitousness for the traveller's welfare.
interpretation_gold: Good intention does not guarantee good reception; the person of whose welfare one is being solicitous may resent one's attention.

yoruba: Ìyàwó jẹ ọkà jẹ igbá.
english_literal: The wife ate the yam-flour meal and ate the calabash with it.
interpretation_gold: One should show consideration, and exercise care, in using others' property.

yoruba: Inú búburú, oògùn òṣì.
english_literal: Ill will “is the” medicine that ensures misfortune.
interpretation_gold: Misfortune will surely attend a person who harbors ill will towards others.

yoruba: Igbá onípẹ̀lẹ́ kì í fọ́; àwo onípẹ̀lẹ́ kì í fàya.
english_literal: The calabash belonging to a patient person never breaks; the china plate belonging to a patient person never cracks.
interpretation_gold: Patient people never come to grief.

yoruba: Inúure kì í pani, wàhálà ní ńkó báni.
english_literal: Good will towards others does not kill; it only gets one into trouble.
interpretation_gold: One should be wary of kindness to others.

yoruba: Ilé ọ̀ṣọnú àyàyó; ta ní jẹ́ yalé ahun-káhun?
english_literal: To visit the home of a generous person is to be plied with food aplenty; who would think of visiting a miser?
interpretation_gold: One's generosity or miserliness makes one friends or loses one friends.

yoruba: Igbá olóore kì í fọ́; àwo olóore kì í fàya; towó tọmọ ní ńya ilé olóore.
english_literal: The calabash of a kind-heated person never breaks; the china plate of a kind-hearted person never cracks; both riches and children ever converge in the home of a kind-hearted person.
interpretation_gold: Good always attends those who are good.

yoruba: Ilé olóore kì í wó tán; tìkà kì í wó kù.
english_literal: The home of a kind-hearted person never collapses completely; the home of a wicked person always collapses, leaving nothing standing.
interpretation_gold: Good will attract good, and evil will attract evil.

yoruba: Ìbàjẹ́ iṣu nìbàjẹ́ ọ̀bẹ; ẹni tó ṣe ìbàjẹ́ èèyàn-án ṣe ìbàjẹ́ ara ẹ̀.
english_literal: The blemish of the yam is the blemish of the knife; whoever besmirches other people's names besmirches his/her own.
interpretation_gold: How one treats others reflects more on oneself than on the others.

yoruba: Kò sí kò sí; bẹ́ẹ̀ni ọmọ wọn ńyó.
english_literal: “We have nothing, we have nothing!” Yet their children always have full stomachs.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who are too tight-fisted to help others.

yoruba: Kò mú ti ọwọ́ ẹ̀ wá ò gba tọwọ́ ẹni.
english_literal: He-will-not-bring-what-he-has will not have what one has.
interpretation_gold: A person who will not share what he/she has will not have a share of others' possessions either.

yoruba: “Kiní yìí ò pọ̀; ng ò lè fún ọ níbẹ̀”: olúwarẹ̀ ahun ni.
english_literal: “This thing is not plentiful; I cannot give you some of it”: the person is a miser.
interpretation_gold: However little one has one should be willing to spare some for others.

yoruba: “Kiní yìí tí o fún mi ò pọ̀”: ahun ní ńjẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
english_literal: “This thing that you have given me is not plentiful”: that statement indicates a greedy person.
interpretation_gold: One should not be too demanding of one's benefactors.

yoruba: Kò tó ǹkan ní ńsọni dahun.
english_literal: “There is not much of it” is what turns one into a miser.
interpretation_gold: Only a miser does not have enough to share with others.

yoruba: “Mú wá, mú wá” lapá ẹyẹlé ńké.
english_literal: “Bring! Bring!” is the sound of the pigeon's wings.
interpretation_gold: Some people know only how to take, never how to give.

yoruba: “Má bàá mi jẹ ìdùn,” ẹran ní ńlé lọ.
english_literal: “Do not share in my delicious meal,” chases away the animal.
interpretation_gold: The selfish person would rather ward off good fortune than allow others to share it with him.

yoruba: “Má fẹ̀ẹ́ ọwọ́-ọ̀ mi kù” tí ńyan gúgúrú fún eégún; eégún náàá ní “Má fẹ̀ẹ́ ọwọ́-ọ̀ mi kù”; ó fún un ní ọmọláńgidi.
english_literal: “Just so you won't find my hand empty” roasted popcorn for the masquerader; the masquerader also responded with “Just so you won't find my hands empty” and gave him a wooden doll.
interpretation_gold: Stinginess will not win generosity in return.

yoruba: Náwó-náwó kì í ṣàpà.
english_literal: The big spender is not a prodigal.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing wrong with spending one's money.

yoruba: Ògún
interpretation_gold: One should appreciate people for their efforts, and not belittle their accomplishments.

yoruba: Òkulú ní ta ni òun ó ro tòun fún? Ta ní wá ro tiẹ̀ fun Òkulu?
english_literal: Òkulu asks to whom should he lodge his complaint? Did anybody lodge his complaint with Òkulu?
interpretation_gold: If one has been unhelpful to others, one should not expect any help from them.

yoruba: Owó ló ńpe ìná owó.
english_literal: Money is what calls for spending money.
interpretation_gold: The availability of money creates the need to spend it.

yoruba: Obì kékeré kọjá òkúta ńlá.
english_literal: A small kolanut is superior to a large stone.
interpretation_gold: A small gift is better than none at all.

yoruba: Òjò pa ewé-e kòkò; bó lè ya kó ya.
english_literal: The rain beats the coco-yam leaf; if it will tear, let it tear.
interpretation_gold: When one has no investment in some property one is liable to be careless in using it; also, One will do what one pleases, and damn the consequences.

yoruba: Òṣónú ò bí èjìrẹ́; onínúure ní ḿbí ẹdun.
english_literal: An ill-natured woman will not give birth to twins; only good-natured people give birth to twins.
interpretation_gold: Only good people are fortunate enough to have twins.

yoruba: Obínrin-ín bímo fún ọ o ní o ò rínú ẹ̀; o fẹ́ kó o nífun ni?
english_literal: A woman has a child by you and you still say you do not see her inside “know her mind”; would you have her expose her intestines?
interpretation_gold: People's actions are enough, without accompanying words, to prove the extent of their commitment to one.

yoruba: “Ó kún mi lójú,” ẹ̀kọ Arogun; ọ̀kan ṣoṣo ni mo rà, igba ènì ló fi sí i.
english_literal: “Its impression on me is tremendous,” such is Arogun's corn meal; I bought only one, but she gave me two hundred as makeweight (or extra measure).
interpretation_gold: Said of people who have gone well beyond the call of duty.

yoruba: Ojú la rí là ńkọrin òkú, òkú ò forin sáyé kó tó lọ.
english_literal: It is out of regard for onlookers that one sings in praise of the dead; the dead did not prescribe a song before departing this life.
interpretation_gold: One does certain things out of a sense of propriety, not because one must.

yoruba: Oore kì í gbé; ìkà kì í dànù; à-ṣoore-jindò ní mmúni pàdánù oore.
english_literal: A good deed does not go for nought; a wicked deed is never lost; drowning while doing a favor is what makes the good person lose out on the rewards for his goodness.
interpretation_gold: Every kindness, like every wickedness, is rewarded; one should be prudent, though in doing favors.

yoruba: Obìnrin tó bímọ tó bí olómitútù, wàhálà ọkọ ẹ̀-ẹ́ dínkù; kò ní já ewé mọ́, bẹ́ẹ̀ni kò ní wa egbò.
english_literal: A woman who bears a child that requires only cold water for all cures has saved her husband much worry; he will never again go searching for medicinal leaves, nor will he go digging roots.
interpretation_gold: A considerate woman is the joy of her husband.

yoruba: “O kú iṣẹ́” ò lè bí aráyé nínú.
english_literal: “Greetings to you at work” cannot invite people's anger.
interpretation_gold: A courteous act does not expose one to trouble.

yoruba: Onígẹ̀gẹ̀ ìṣájú ba tìkẹhìn jẹ́.
english_literal: The goitered person going in front ruins the fortunes of the one coming behind.
interpretation_gold: A person's misdeeds compromises those coming after him.

yoruba: Ohun tí ḿbá ahun náwó ẹ̀ ḿbẹ lápò-o ẹ̀.
english_literal: What will help a miser spend his money is right there in his/her pocket.
interpretation_gold: The person who does not willingly share what he/she has will somehow find him/herself being deprived of it.

yoruba: O jẹbẹ, o mubẹ, o babẹ jẹ́.
english_literal: There you ate, there you drank, and there you fouled.
interpretation_gold: One should not besmirch a place that has been good to one.

yoruba: Ojú ọba ayé ló fọ́; tọ̀rún là kedere, ó ńwo aṣebi.
english_literal: Only the king of this earth is blind; that of heaven is wide-eyed, watching evil doers.
interpretation_gold: God sees all acts of wickedness that may be hidden from earthly authorities.

yoruba: Ojú ní ńrójú ṣàánú.
english_literal: Eyes are what see look on eyes and fill with kindness.
interpretation_gold: When the eyes actually see suffering, they cannot avoid compassion.

yoruba: Oore tí a ṣe fádìẹ ò gbé; bó pẹ́ títí a ṣomi tooro síni lẹ́nu.
english_literal: The favor one does a chicken is not for nought; in due course it will make stew to delight one's mouth.
interpretation_gold: There will always be a return for whatever favor one does others.

yoruba: Pẹ̀gàn-pẹ̀gàn-án bọ́ sóde kò ní láárí; ẹni tí ò rówó ṣe fújà ní ńpẹ̀gàn ẹni.
english_literal: He who derides others steps outside and does not amount to much; it is he who has no basis for bragging that derides others.
interpretation_gold: People who belittle others are themselves worthless.

yoruba: Tìkà toore, ọ̀kan kì í gbé.
english_literal: Wickedness or kindness, neither goes for nought.
interpretation_gold: Wickedness and kindness will be rewarded unfailingly.

yoruba: Tútù ní ńtẹnu ẹja wá.
english_literal: Only coolness come out of the fish's mouth.
interpretation_gold: Permit your mouth to say only soothing things.

yoruba: Tigi tọ̀pẹ̀ ní ńṣàánú àfòmọ́.
english_literal: Both trees and palms take pity on the climbing plant.
interpretation_gold: A plea for mercy from all and sundry.

yoruba: Tewé tegbò ní ńṣàánú àfòmọ́.
english_literal: Both the leaf and the root take pity on the climbing parasite.
interpretation_gold: A pleas for consideration from all and sundry.

yoruba: Tigi tọ̀pẹ̀ ní ńsàánú ìyèré lóko.
english_literal: Both trees and palms extend kindness to the African black pepper plant.
interpretation_gold: A pleas for kindness from others.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó ṣe ìbàjẹ́ èèyàn-án ṣe ìbàjẹ́ ara-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: Whoever defames others defames himself or herself.
interpretation_gold: The evil one does to others reflects on oneself.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó bá máa bímọ á yọ̀ fọ́lọ́mọ.
english_literal: Whoever would have children of her own must rejoice with those who already have.
interpretation_gold: Those who seek good fortune must not begrudge those who are already fortunate.

yoruba: Ṣìkà-ṣìkà-á gbàgbé àjọbí, adánilóró gbàgbé ọ̀la.
english_literal: The wicked forgets kinship; the person who hurts others forgets tomorrow.
interpretation_gold: People who inflict injury on others forget that the gods of kinship will inflict punishment on them, and that they too might be at the receiving end in the future.

yoruba: Ọ̀ràn-an-yàn ò sí nínúu iyánrán.
english_literal: There is no compulsion in voluntary work.
interpretation_gold: Volunteering is not an obligation.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a ṣe lóore tí kò dúpẹ́, bí ọlọ́ṣà-á kóni lẹ́rù ni.
english_literal: A person whom one does a favor but who shows no gratitude is like a robber who has stolen one's goods.
interpretation_gold: Ingratitude is comparable to robbery.

yoruba: Ẹ ní ká má tafà; kí ni a ó fi lé ogun? Kànnà-kànnà la fi lé Boko.
english_literal: You forbid us to shoot arrows, so with what shall we repel invaders? In the past the Boko were repelled with catapaults.
interpretation_gold: It is unhelpful to deprive people of the tools they need for what they must do.

yoruba: Ọtí gbélé ahun ó kan.
english_literal: Wine stays in the home of the miser until it goes sour.
interpretation_gold: The miser would rather see things go bad than share them with others.

yoruba: Ṣe sílẹ̀: ẹrù-u ẹ̀ kì í pẹ́ níbodè.
english_literal: He who extends kindness beforehand: his goods will not stay long at the frontier.
interpretation_gold: The generous person will always find helpers to ease his passage.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó so ìlẹ̀kẹ̀-ẹ́ parí ọ̀ṣọ́; ẹni tó fúnni lọ́mọ-ọ́ parí oore.
english_literal: The person who adorns herself with beads has done the ultimate in self-beautifying; the person who gives one a child (in marriage) has done the ultimate in favor.
interpretation_gold: There are certain gestures that cannot be surpassed.

yoruba: Ẹní fowó lògbà ló káyé já.
english_literal: It is the person who uses his/her money to enjoy life that lives well.
interpretation_gold: Money is to be used to enjoy life.

yoruba: Ṣìkà-ṣìkà ò jẹ́ pe ara ẹ̀ níkà.
english_literal: The wicked person will never describe himself as wicked.
interpretation_gold: The wicked always strive to appear as decent, kind people.

yoruba: Ṣìkà-ṣìkà-á fi díẹ̀ ṣe ara ẹ̀.
english_literal: The wicked person does a little wickedness to himself or herself.
interpretation_gold: Wickedness has some adverse effect on the perpetrator.

yoruba: Ẹyẹlé fi ẹ̀sín-in rẹ̀ pamọ́, ó ńṣe ẹ̀sín adìẹ.
english_literal: The pigeon hides its own disgrace and goes ridiculing the chicken.
interpretation_gold: A person full of flaws insists on finding fault with others.

yoruba: Ẹní mọ owó-ó lò lowó ḿbá gbé.
english_literal: It is the person who knows how to use wealth that wealth attaches to.
interpretation_gold: Wealth attaches only to those who know how to use it.

yoruba: Ṣẹ̀gàn-ṣẹ̀gàn ò láṣọ méjì; pé-ń-pé laṣọ abúni ḿmọ.
english_literal: The detractor of others does not possess a change of clothing; the garment of the insulter of people is always skimpy.
interpretation_gold: People who make a habit of cutting others down never prosper either.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó bèèrè ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ ìdí-i rẹ̀ ẹ́gbọ́.
english_literal: Whoever asks about a matter genuinely wishes to know its causes.
interpretation_gold: If a person asks about a problem, one should appreciate the gesture and comply.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ó gòkè, kó fa ọ̀rẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ lọ́wọ́; ẹni tó rí jẹ, kó fún ọ̀rẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ jẹ.
english_literal: Whoever has reached the top, let him or her pull his or her friend by the hand; whoever has food to eat, let him or her share it with his or her friend.
interpretation_gold: If one has succeeded, one should give aid to those still struggling.

yoruba: Ọ̀tọ̀ niṣẹ́ olókùnrùn.
english_literal: The assignment for an invalid must be different from everybody else's.
interpretation_gold: People should be employed only according to their capabilities.

yoruba: Ọ̀mùtí kì í ṣàpà; owó ẹ̀ ló ńná.
english_literal: The drunkard is not a prodigal; it is his money that he is spending.
interpretation_gold: One can spend one's money as one wishes.

yoruba: Ẹní lówó kó ṣe bí ọba; àrà wo lahún fẹ́ fi owó dá?
english_literal: Whoever has riches should act like a king; what kind of feat can a miser perform with money?
interpretation_gold: The best thing to do with wealth is to use it to live well.

yoruba: Ọwọ́ híhá àhájù ní ńdínà ire mọ́ni.
english_literal: Excessive stinginess is what slams the door of fortune in one's face.
interpretation_gold: Miserliness will divert good fortune from the miser's direction.
